# Contracts workstream decisions (CT)

Finer decisions of `whombat-contracts`, under the managed-appliance blueprint (MA-01, MA-02, MA-05…MA-11).

## CT-01 Build with tsc to `dist/`, explicit `.js` relative imports (2026-09-25)

Each package compiles `src/` (minus tests and `__fixtures__`) with `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` to ESM JS and
`.d.ts`. Relative imports in sources name their emitted file (`./common.js`, `./domain/index.js`), so the output
runs unbundled in Node ESM and typechecks under `moduleResolution: nodenext`, while sources still resolve under
`Bundler`. No bundler: per-subpath bundles would duplicate modules (and Zod schema instances) across subpaths.
Dependents build against `../core/dist` via `paths` in their build tsconfig.

## CT-02 Workspace resolves sources, tarballs resolve `dist` (2026-09-25)

`exports` in the repository points at `src/*.ts` (tests and typecheck need no build; a linked checkout serves
TypeScript sources); `publishConfig.exports` points at `dist/*.{js,d.ts}` and is what `pnpm pack` writes.
Packages stay `"private": true` so nothing is published to a registry by accident; `pnpm pack` ignores it.

## CT-03 One version for all packages, immutable release directories (2026-09-25)

All publishable packages share one version and one tag `contracts-vX.Y.Z`; `scripts/release.ts` refuses a dirty
tree, a mismatching tag, or an existing `dist-release/X.Y.Z/`. `RELEASE.json` records the commit so the
integration manifest can cite it. Consumers pin transitive `@whombat/*` dependencies with pnpm `overrides`
pointing at the vendored tarballs (otherwise pnpm would look for `@whombat/core@X.Y.Z` in a registry).

## CT-04 Development override swaps `node_modules/.pnpm` entries for symlinks (2026-09-25)

`scripts/link-contracts.sh` (a template consumers copy) replaces installed `@whombat/*` packages with symlinks
to `$WHOMBAT_CONTRACTS_DEV/packages/<pkg>`. Alternatives rejected: `pnpm link` and `overrides` edit committed
files; a `.pnpmfile.cjs` hook changes the lockfile checksum. Any `pnpm install` undoes the link.

## CT-05 Session frames carry a u32 length prefix (2026-09-25)

The Noise channel is a byte stream (Noise messages may split or join frames), so MA-08's
`[u8 type][u32 streamId][payload]` is prefixed with `u32 length` (= 5 + payload). The body layout is unchanged.
Limits: CONTROL and DATA payloads ≤ 64 KiB, CREDIT window ≤ 16 MiB, 32 open streams, 64 in-flight requests. Client
streams are odd, appliance streams even.

## CT-06 Operation names are the `api` key paths (2026-09-25)

`request.op` for an existing REST contract is `<area>.<action>`, the key path in `api` (not `Endpoint.id`; the two
differ once: `packs.agentPacks` vs id `packs.agent`). `API_OPERATIONS` is derived from `api`, so the input is
`{params, query, body}` with the endpoint's own schemas and the output is `response`. The default allowlist drops
`auth.*` (the Noise identity replaces cookie, magic-link and Tailscale sign-in) and `devices.vapidKey`. Unknown
names in `createOperationAllowlist({only, exclude})` throw.

## CT-07 Enrollment, recovery and endpoint trust are session-native operations (2026-09-25)

`enroll.claim`, `enroll.pair.request/status/approve`, `enroll.invite.create/accept`,
`recovery.kit.register/confirm`, `recovery.enroll` and `endpoints.list/revoke` are defined in
`@whombat/protocol/session`, not as REST contracts. Only `enroll.claim`, `enroll.pair.request`,
`enroll.pair.status`, `enroll.invite.accept` and `recovery.enroll` are open to unenrolled endpoints. These
operations bind the session's Noise static identity, so no key travels in the input. Recovery signatures are
Ed25519 over canonical JSON of a statement bound to purpose, appliance PeerId, endpoint PeerId, time and nonce.

## CT-08 Cross-language schemas are a checked Zod subset; times are epoch seconds (2026-09-25)

See `docs/cross-language.md`. Strict objects, ASCII-only anchored patterns on every string, bounded integers, no
floats, no transforms/refinements/defaults/formats. `checkSubset` enforces it, so JSON Schema and Go accept
exactly what Zod accepts. Device, release and relay schemas use integer epoch seconds instead of ISO strings.

## CT-09 Go bindings: hand-written generator from Zod; validation through embedded JSON Schema (2026-09-25)

Off-the-shelf JSON Schema → Go generators (`go-jsonschema` and others) handle discriminated `oneOf` and named
reuse poorly, and none of them enforce patterns or bounds identically. The generator (`conformance/src/gen-go.ts`,
about 250 lines) reads the Zod definitions, reuses exported names (enums become typed string constants), and emits
`Parse<Name>`/`Validate`. Validation delegates to the maintained `santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6` over the
embedded exported schemas, so the bounds are identical by construction. Canonical JSON in Go uses
`gowebpki/jcs` (RFC 8785). Generated files are committed; `pnpm gen:check` guards them. The Go module copies the
schemas and vectors (`go/internal/schemas/json`, `go/testdata/vectors`), so a vendored `go/` directory is
self-contained.

## CT-10 Device requests are signed envelopes with audience, time and nonce (2026-09-25)

`POST /v1/device/<op>` carries `{v, aud, device, op, ts, nonce, body, sig}`, where
`sig = Ed25519(canonicalJson({purpose: "whombat-device-request/v1", v, aud, device, op, ts, nonce, body}))`. `aud` is
`whombat-api:<env>` (was `whombat-control:<env>` before 0.6.0, CT-57), the skew limit is ±300 s, and nonces are single-use for 600 s. The nonce is spent only
after the signature and time checks pass. Device bodies are field-allowlisted: enums, counters and ids, no free
text. Provisioning registration proves possession of the management key with a signature over the registration
(purpose `whombat-device-registration/v1`).

## CT-11 Push goes to opaque handles (2026-09-25)

A client registers its APNs/FCM token with control (`push.register`) and receives an opaque `PushHandle`, which
it gives to its appliance. The appliance's `push.send` names handles, a `PushKind` and an opaque `ref`: no
content and no local account ids. Control never learns which local account a handle belongs to. Limits: 50
handles per request, 60 requests per minute per device, 120 pushes per hour per handle.

## CT-12 Assignments are sequence-numbered signed documents; hold never downgrades (2026-09-25)

`SignedAssignment = {payload, keyId, sig}` over canonical JSON. The payload has purpose, env, device, a
per-device sequence (strictly increasing), action `install` (release id + tuple digest) or `hold` (pause or
emergency stop), rollout, cohort, `issuedAt`/`notBefore`/`expiresAt` (≤ 7 days). The manager must also find the
release and tuple digest in verified TUF metadata. The tuple digest is `sha256:` of the tuple's canonical JSON.
Session protocol ranges in tuples and manifests are integers `major * 1000 + minor`.

## CT-13 Update journal states use the MA-11 names verbatim (2026-09-25)

`UpdateJournalState` values are `Assigned`, `Downloading`, `Verified`, `Staged`, `WaitingForSafeBoundary`,
`Activating`, `Verifying`, `Healthy`, `Failed`, `RolledBack` and `Quarantined`. `UPDATE_JOURNAL_TRANSITIONS`
(also generated for Go) allows superseding an assignment before activation and forbids leaving
`Activating`/`Verifying` except forward or to `RolledBack`/`Failed`.

## CT-14 Forward compatibility within a major: tolerant wire, strict commands (2026-09-25)

This supports the N/N-1 protocol policy (R-68). Within one major:

- **Wire messages and responses** are `z.object` and strip unknown members. This covers relay messages, session
  CONTROL messages (including stream specs and metadata), session operation outputs, device API responses and
  control API responses. Unknown session message types are skipped.
- **Command inputs** are `z.strictObject` and reject unknown members. This covers session operation inputs,
  device request bodies and control request bodies.
- **Signed, hashed and security documents** stay strict: admission header and claims, JWKS, device envelope,
  registration, release tuple, manifest, journal record and assignment. A verifier never accepts what it doesn't
  understand; adding a member there means a new purpose or a new major.

Semantics-changing additions are negotiated through capabilities, never inferred from a member's presence.
TypeScript strips via Zod. The JSON Schema is exported with `io: 'input'`, so `z.object` leaves
`additionalProperties` open. Go (`internal/schemas.Decode`) drops members the Go type doesn't declare, with
exact-case matching, before `encoding/json`, so an unknown `KID` can't replace `kid`. Vectors: `schemas.json`
cases with `output`, and `session.json`. This supersedes CT-08's "strict objects only".

## CT-15 Strict Ed25519 everywhere by default (2026-09-25)

`verifyEd25519Strict` (`@whombat/core/audit`) applies RFC 8032 with `zip215: false`. It rejects a non-canonical
S, R and public-key encoding, and small-order public keys. `verifyBytes` and every exported verifier use it
(`verifyAdmissionTicket`'s `verify` is now optional and defaults to it). Go uses `internal/ed25519strict`, which
is `crypto/ed25519` plus a `filippo.io/edwards25519` canonical-key and small-order check. `crypto/ed25519` on its
own accepts forgeries for the identity key, and the vectors show it. `signed.json` → `ed25519` covers S + L, a
small-order key, a non-canonical key and an order-2 key; admission vectors include an S + L ticket.

## CT-16 Session identity is the account (2026-09-25)

Endpoints bind to an account (MA-03). `PrincipalSummary` is `{accountId, name, owner,
principals?: [{burrowId, principalId}] ≤ 256}`. `EnrolledOutput` extends it with `endpoint` and
`authzGeneration`, and `EndpointSummary` carries `accountId` and `revocation` (`none|pending|applied`).
`RecoveryStatement` names the owner `accountId` being recovered. No N-1 shim: pre-1.0, no customers.

## CT-17 Appliance extension operations (2026-09-25)

Added session-native operations, shaped after the managed runtime (`apps/server/src/managed/ops.ts`,
`trust.ts`):

- `push.handles.set {handle}` and `push.handles.clear {}` → `{ok}`;
- `admins.list` → `{admins: [{accountId, email, name, since}]}`, `admins.grant` and `admins.revoke {accountId}`
  → `{changed}` (owners only, last owner protected);
- `endpoints.rename {endpointId, label}` → `{ok}`;
- `enroll.invite.revoke {inviteId}` → `{ok}`;
- `endpoints.list {all?}`;
- `appliance.status` → `{claimed, claimReported, recovery{enrolled, kitVerified}, revocationsPending,
  revocationsApplied, owner, draining, policy{…: {available, reason}}, backup{state, lastSuccessAt, ageS,
  coverage, unprotected, lastFailure, recoverable}, update{state, current, candidate, lastCheckedAt,
  deferredReason, failure} | null}`.

`subscribed.denied` lists `{topic, reason: not_member|forbidden|not_found}`. `event` is discriminated by
`ephemeral`: durable events have a cursor, ephemeral ones (typing, presence) don't.

## CT-18 Provisioning proves both device keys (2026-09-25)

`DeviceRegistration` carries `contentPublicKey` and `contentProof`: the content key signs the same canonical
statement as the management key (`proof`). `contentPeerId` must equal `peerIdFromEd25519PublicKey(contentPublicKey)`
(base58btc identity multihash, the same as libp2p; checked against `@libp2p/peer-id`), and the two keys must
differ.

## CT-19 Admission: worker binding, optional org, close-code mapping (2026-09-25)

`VerifyAdmissionOptions.worker` (Go: `Worker`) makes a ticket for another worker fail with `wrong_worker`, which
closes with 4421 (`RELAY_CLOSE.wrongWorker`, reason `wrong_worker`). `org` is optional in `AdmissionClaims`:
absent means an unclaimed appliance, which is still reachable on the enrollment channel and uses the relay's
"unclaimed" quota bucket. `ADMISSION_ERROR_CLOSE` / Go `AdmissionError.CloseCode()` map failures: `wrong_role` →
4403, `wrong_worker` → 4421, everything else → 4401. Some close codes carry more than one meaning: 4409 also
closes an appliance control connection superseded by a newer one for the same `apl` (reason `superseded`), and
4404 also closes a data connection whose session id is unknown or expired. `hello.class` stays required and is
ignored on an appliance control connection, which sends `interactive`.

## CT-20 `@whombat/secure-channel` is released with the other packages (2026-09-25)

Merged from branch `secure-channel` in 0.3.0 and versioned in lockstep. Its ADR
(`docs/decisions/secure-channel.md`) keeps its own status.

## CT-21 Application error codes ride in `error.details.code` (2026-09-25)

`error.code` stays one of `SessionErrorCode`. The application's specific code, when there is one, is
`error.details.code` (`APP_ERROR_CODES`: transfer, claim/enrollment, recovery, owner, and `managed.<capability>`
refusals). The set is open, and `appErrorCode(details)` reads it. `unsupported_version` carries
`details {supported: {min, max} majors, appliance: {major, minor}}`, and `whoMustUpdate` interprets it. A
`result`/`outcome` over 64 KiB is answered with `error{too_large, details.code: use_export_stream}`. A `preview`
download is either a real derived preview or `stream_refused` with `details.code: variant_unavailable`, never
the original.

## CT-22 Collab streams frame Yjs messages inside the DATA byte stream (2026-09-25)

The DATA of a `collab` stream is a byte stream of `[u32 len][message]` (1 byte to 16 MiB). Messages may span
frames. Credit counts DATA bytes, prefixes included; the receiver grants credit as it consumes rather than per
message, and buffers at most one incomplete message. The codec is `@whombat/protocol/collab`
(`encodeCollabMessages`, `collabDataPayloads`, `CollabMessageDecoder`), with vectors in `collab.json`
(TypeScript only, like the session).

## CT-23 Appliance-local IPC is a contract (2026-09-25)

Runtime↔manager and runtime↔backup are specified in `@whombat/control-contracts/local` / Go `local` (see
`docs/local-ipc.md`), cross-language. The manager socket takes ticket, claimed, revocations and push calls from
the runtime. The admin socket takes health, drain (lease, scopes `all`/`writes`, 409 busy), resume,
claim-window and facts from the manager and the backup service. Where the existing implementations differed,
the contract keeps the manager's admin shapes and the runtime's manager-port calls; `docs/local-ipc.md` lists
what each side changes. `claim.claimed` loses `claim`/`org` (control resolves the pending claim). Revocations
reach control as `revocationRef(peerId)`. Local IPC times are RFC 3339 strings and free text is printable
ASCII, so the text stays in the cross-language subset (CT-08).

## CT-24 `appliance.status` names providers and the appliance; backup uses the service's vocabulary (2026-09-25)

`providers: [{provider, authMode, ownerAccountId, state, explanation}]`, where `state` is one of `ready`,
`not_signed_in`, `owner_departed`, `quota_exhausted`, `auth_expired`, `auth_revoked`, `outage`,
`version_drift`, `gated`, and members see their own rows. `appliance: {peerId, runtimeVersion,
schemaVersion, protocol}` is also added. `backup` now uses the backup service's states
(`unprotected|pending|protected|stale|failing`), coverage class ids, `relogin`, and
`lastFailure{at, stage, reason}`. This replaces 0.3.0's provisional vocabulary.

## CT-25 Operation flags: exportable, export ops, ephemeral (2026-09-25)

`OperationSpec.exportable` marks every non-mutating operation and the `exportOp`s (`EXPORT_OPS`:
`packs.export`); these can be read through `open{spec: {kind: 'export', op, input}}`. `ephemeral` marks
`presence.typing {conversationId, threadRootId?}` and `presence.set {state}` → `{ok}`. Ephemeral operations
have no `accepted`, no receipt and no idempotency; clients never queue or resend them; and they are
rate-limited (`EPHEMERAL_MAX_PER_MINUTE` = 120 per endpoint).

## CT-26 Team-agent credential owner and provider sign-in ops (2026-09-25)

`AgentRuntime.credentialOwnerAccountId` (optional, nullable) names whose provider sign-in a non-personal agent runs
on. It is set through `agents.setCredentialOwner` (a REST contract, burrow owners, a Keys event). Personal agents
never carry it. `DispatchContext.credential` gives the runner `{credentialOwnerAccountId, ownerName, ownerPresent,
personal, provider, authMode, requestedByAccountId}`, and the runner uses only that owner's sign-in, never a
fallback. The `providers.*` session operations are adopted from the runtime's providers workstream. Submitting a
secret is a `secret` operation.

## CT-27 The claim id travels through the ceremony (2026-09-25)

`enroll.claim` carries control's `claimId`. The runtime passes it to the manager (`/v1/runtime/claimed`), which
reports `claim.claimed {claimId, claimedAt}`, and control completes exactly that claim. This closes the race of
CL-09/G-04, where an expired claim of one org and a newer claim of another looked the same to control.

## CT-28 The assignment poll says none or unchanged (2026-09-25)

`update.assignment` answers `{result: assigned | unchanged | none, assignment, nextCheckS}`. The assignment is
present exactly when `result` is `assigned` (`assignmentResultValid`).

## CT-29 The claim secret has one normalization and one hash (2026-09-25)

Normalization follows provisioning NX-24: ASCII upper-case; remove Unicode White_Space, U+FEFF and `-`; map
`0/1/8` to `O/I/B`. The result is valid only if it matches `^[A-Z2-7]{26}$`. The stored hash is
`base64url(SHA-256("whombat-claim-secret/1\n" + deviceId + "\n" + normalized))`. TypeScript
(`normalizeClaimSecret`, `claimSecretHash`) and Go (`protocol.NormalizeClaimSecret`, `ClaimSecretHash`) are
checked by `claim.json`.

## CT-30 Backup ops and the checkpoint API (2026-09-25)

The owner operations `backup.status|configureDestination|recoveryMaterial|runNow` use the MR-19 shapes, and
their `details.code` values are `backup_*`. The backup service's status document and its checkpoint API
(`CheckpointRequest {reason, releaseId?, migrations?, underDrain?}` → `CheckpointResult`) live in
`@whombat/protocol/session` and are re-exported by `local`. Errors are `LocalError` (with `stage`).

## CT-31 Forward repair is its own journal state (2026-09-25)

`ForwardRepairRequired` means the candidate is running and can't be rolled back, so it keeps running, nothing is
rewound, and only a fix-forward assignment leaves the state. It is reached from `Activating`/`Verifying` and
replaces the manager's `RolledBack → Quarantined` + failure mapping. It uses PascalCase like the other MA-11
states; the failure code `forward_repair_required` may still accompany it.

## CT-32 Push refs are random or keyed hashes (2026-09-25)

`PushRef` is 22–43 base64url characters: ≥ 128 random bits or HMAC-SHA256 with an appliance-local key
(`pushRefFor`). It reaches Apple and Google, so it must never be an id, a name or an unkeyed derivation.

## CT-33 Control API: precise reasons in the body, extensions adopted (2026-09-25)

`ControlErrorBody.error.details.code` carries the precise reason (`CONTROL_REASONS`, open set). This replaces the
`x-whombat-reason` header. Also added:

- the `entitlement_withheld` code;
- passkeys and sign-out-everywhere;
- invitations (accept, list, revoke), member removal or leaving, the org list and the org audit log;
- `claims.get`;
- `operatorApi`: release registration and list, rollout list, get, stop and manual wave promotion; devices, the
  internal flag, retire and release; relay drain and undrain; entitlements; audit; retention;
- `Wave.observingSince`;
- `type` exports for `EmergencyStop`, `EntitlementState`, `ReleaseStatus` and `RolloutState`.

## CT-34 Pinned assignment keys document (2026-09-25)

`AssignmentKeys {v, env, keys[{kid, publicKey, state: active|next|retired, notAfter}]}` is pinned in the appliance
image. `assignmentKeyMap` (Go `AssignmentKeyMap`) refuses another environment and duplicate kids, and drops keys
past `notAfter`. Control serves the same document for monitoring only.

## CT-35 Compatibility checks in Go (2026-09-25)

`release.CheckActivation`, `UpdateClass`, `ServesClient` and `ProtocolOverlap` mirror the TypeScript functions,
and `compat.json` checks both.

## CT-36 Upload pipelining (2026-09-25)

Chunk announcements may run ahead of acknowledgements, bounded by credit and 256 queued, but must be contiguous.
A gap or an overlap is `RESET protocolError`. Acknowledgements are sent in order, and DATA may span chunk
boundaries. No codec change.

## CT-37 Local IPC 0.5: manager endpoints, runtime facts, backup socket (2026-09-25)

The manager's `update/status`, `maintenance/lock|unlock` and `network/candidates|status` (MG-11, MG-15), the
runtime's `GET /facts` (`RuntimeFacts`, including `quarantined`) and the backup service's socket are contract
types in `local`. `docs/local-ipc.md` lists what each side changes.

## CT-38 Control conventions: emergency-stop read, more reasons, status codes, audit filters (2026-09-25)

- `rolloutApi.emergencyStopStatus` is `GET /operator/emergency-stop`.
- New `CONTROL_REASONS`: `already_claimed`, `invitation_email_mismatch`, `device_exists`, `bad_time` and
  `too_large`.
- `ControlEndpoint.status` is the success status: `201` for a call that creates something (device registration,
  release registration) and `200` for an idempotent repeat of the same creation; otherwise `200`.
- `operator.customerAudit`'s `device` filter matches events whose `target` is that device id.

This covers control R-01…R-04.

## CT-39 Credential sources: personal or organization (MA-17) (2026-09-25)

`AgentRuntime.credentialSource` is `{kind: 'account', accountId} | {kind: 'org', credentialId: 'orgc_…'} | null`. A
member's own sign-in serves only that member's requests and their own automations. Team agents run on
organization credentials.

`credentialOwnerAccountId` and `agents.setCredentialOwner` stay as deprecated aliases until 1.0, so the runtime and
app can move at their pace; `credentialSourceOf` reads either.

`DispatchContext.credential` gains `source` and `automationPublisherAccountId`, replacing the claim answer's
`credentialExtension`. `agents.setCredentialSource` is a REST contract (`PUT
/burrows/:burrow/agents/:agent/credential-source {source}`), so its session op input is `{params, body}`.

Also added:

- the session ops `providers.org.list|login.start|remove` (owners); organization rows (`credentialId`, `label`,
  `ownerAccountId: null`) in `ProviderStatus`/`ProviderSignIn`; `ProviderStatus.expiresAt`/`verified`;
- the runner sign-in routes `signin.poll|answer|event` in `runnerApi`, with `SIGNIN_METHODS` typing each method's
  params and result;
- the error codes `managed.provider_gated`, `managed.provider_excluded` and `provider.*`;
- `APPLIANCE_EVENT_TYPES`, including `provider.signed_in`/`provider.signed_out`, with `ProviderAuditPayload`.

## CT-40 Go FrameDecoder in linear time (2026-09-25)

The Go decoder consumes by offset and moves only the unconsumed tail. Before, it copied the whole buffer on every
push, the same quadratic accumulation that review L-6 found in the TypeScript decoder (SC-07). A test that feeds
two maximal frames byte by byte bounds the allocation.

## CT-41 Assignment-key states and rotation (2026-09-25)

Each key in `AssignmentKeys` has `notBefore` and `notAfter`, both nullable. The key states are:

| State | Accepted | Required window | Otherwise invalid |
|---|---|---|---|
| `active` | always | both null | `active_with_window` |
| `next` | from `notBefore` on; never when `notBefore` is null (pinned, waiting for a later document) | `notAfter` null | `next_with_not_after` |
| `retired` | while `now ≤ notAfter` | `notAfter` set, `notBefore` null | `retired_without_not_after`, `retired_with_not_before` |

A document also needs at least one `active` key (`no_active_key`), unique kids (`duplicate_kid`) and its own
environment (`wrong_env`). A manager refuses an invalid document as a whole (`AssignmentKeysError` in TS, Go
`*AssignmentKeysError`). It never falls back to a partial key set.

Rotation with a grace period:

1. Image N pins `{k1 active, k2 next notBefore: T}`.
2. Control signs with k2 from T (plus clock skew), and devices on image N accept it without an update.
3. Image N+1 pins `{k2 active, k1 retired notAfter: T + grace}`, so assignments signed before the switch stay
   valid during the grace period. The grace is at least 90 days, for long-offline devices.

An emergency revocation of a key ships an image without it. The key vectors in `compat.json` cover every state and
error in both languages. This supersedes the `notAfter`-only rule of CT-34 and closes the manager's MG-21 gap.

## CT-42 Browser push through control (MA-18) (2026-09-25)

`PushPlatform` gains `webpush`. `push.register` takes `PushRegistration`, which is one of:

- `NativePushRegistration {platform: apns|fcm, token, appId}`. `token` is now printable ASCII and `appId`
  `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`.
- `WebPushRegistration {platform: 'webpush', subscription}`, where `subscription` is the browser's
  `PushSubscription.toJSON()`:
  - `endpoint`: `https://` printable ASCII, at most 2048 characters;
  - `keys.p256dh`: 87 and `keys.auth`: 22 base64url characters, without padding;
  - `expirationTime`: epoch ms or null. It is always present because `toJSON()` always includes it, and the
    cross-language subset has no optional-nullable.

`push.vapid` (`GET /v1/push/vapid`, no auth) returns control's per-environment VAPID public key `{publicKey}` (87
base64url characters, the uncompressed P-256 point) for `PushManager.subscribe`. The returned handle goes to the
appliance through `push.handles.set` as before. Device push requests are unchanged (content-free); control
encrypts a generic payload to the subscription (RFC 8291). The registration schemas are cross-language (Go
`device`) with vectors.

## CT-43 Claim proof (MA-19d, review M-3) (2026-09-25)

`claimVerifier(deviceId, normalized) = base64url(SHA-256("whombat-claim-control/1\n" + deviceId + "\n" + normalized))`
(TS `claimVerifier`, Go `protocol.ClaimVerifier`). The value is domain-separated from the appliance's
`claimSecretHash`.

Control assigns the device id at `devices.register`, so provisioning registers the verifier in a second call,
`devices.registerClaimVerifier` (`POST /provisioning/devices/:device/claim-verifier {claimVerifier}`, provisioning
credential; the same value again answers 200, a different one 409 `claim_verifier_exists`). Only after that does it
write `claim.json` and print the card.

`claims.start` requires `claimProof`, the same value computed by the client from the card (device id + secret).
Control compares it in constant time with the stored verifier and never sees the secret. It refuses a claim on a
device without a verifier (`claim_verifier_missing`) or with a wrong proof (`claim_proof_invalid`). A valid proof
replaces another org's pending claim, and the per-device rate limit counts only valid proofs.

## CT-44 Secret ops keep no digest and no result (MA-19f, review L-1/L-2) (2026-09-25)

`OperationSpec.secret` now covers both input and result. The receipt stores neither an input digest
(`receiptDigest` covers the op only) nor the result (only `{state, kind}`), and nothing of either is logged. A retry
with the same request id after a lost answer gets `error{code: 'unknown_outcome'}` instead of a stored result. The
client then asks `status` (`outcome{state, redacted: true}`) and fetches state, or repeats the op with a new id.

Secret ops:

- `enroll.invite.create` (returns the secret) and `enroll.invite.accept`;
- `enroll.pair.request` (returns the code);
- `recovery.kit.register` and `recovery.kit.rotate`;
- `providers.login.start`, `providers.login.submit` and `providers.org.login.start`;
- `backup.configureDestination`;
- the `api` ops `packs.setSecret`, `connectors.setGoogleApp`, `canvases.collabToken`, `devices.register` and
  `devices.update` (`SECRET_API_OPS`).

## CT-45 Recovery rotation and the kit owner (MA-19a, review H-1) (2026-09-25)

`recovery.kit.register` works only while no recovery key exists (`recovery_key_exists`). Replacing a key is
`recovery.kit.rotate {newRecoveryPublicKey, currentKeySignature}`. The signature is by the current recovery key over
`RecoveryRotation {purpose: 'whombat-recovery-rotate/1', appliance, newRecoveryPublicKey}` (canonical JSON), and a
bad one is `recovery_rotation_invalid`. The new key stays pending until its kit is confirmed, and every owner is
notified.

The kit owner is the owner who registered or last rotated the kit. `appliance.status.recovery` now reports it as
`ownerAccountId`, together with `rotationPending`. A recovery statement enrolls only into the kit owner's account
(`recovery_not_kit_owner`), only while that account is still an owner, and only with a confirmed kit
(`recovery_kit_unverified`). Invites create new accounts only (`invite_account_exists`, MA-19b).

## CT-46 Pairing look-up and fingerprint (MR-32, review L-4) (2026-09-25)

`enroll.pair.lookup {code}` → `{pairingId, label, platform, fingerprint, expiresAt}` (app channel, a query).
`pairingFingerprint(peerId)` is the first 6 bytes of `SHA-256("whombat-pairing-fingerprint/1\n" + peerId)`,
formatted as `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX` upper-case hex. The new device shows it next to its code. `enroll.pair.approve` now
requires the looked-up `fingerprint` and refuses a different one (`pairing_fingerprint_mismatch`). Look-ups and
approvals share the runtime's per-account budget. The vectors are in `session.json` → `pairingFingerprints`.

## CT-47 `hello.cachedAccountId` (I-3) (2026-09-25)

`hello.cachedAccountId` is optional: the account the client's cached content belongs to. `welcome.clearCache` is
also true when it isn't the session's account. The runtime's appliance-wide generation sequence (MR-36) stays the
safe default.

## CT-48 Magic-link `next` is a same-origin path (control R-05, review L-5) (2026-09-25)

`SAFE_NEXT` / `isSafeNext` accept one leading `/`, not followed by `/`, `\` or an encoded slash (`%2f`/`%5c`), and
no backslash anywhere. Only URL path and query characters are allowed, so no scheme, fragment or whitespace. This
matches control's check. The limit is 300 characters.

## CT-49 `push.resolve` (MA-20) (2026-09-25)

`push.resolve {ref: PushRef}` → `{burrow, link: LinkRef}` (a query). The appliance maps its keyed ref back to the
item when the member may see it, and answers `not_found` otherwise, the same for unknown and forbidden refs.
`PushRef`/`pushRefFor` moved to `@whombat/protocol/session`; `@whombat/control-contracts/device` re-exports them.

## CT-50 `CredentialMeta` as the runner keeps it (2026-09-25)

`CredentialMeta` gains `creatorAttested`, `login` and `signal {state: quota_exhausted|auth_expired|auth_revoked|
outage, at, until}` (null once a good run clears it). All three are required. The secure-channel replay fix
(`sc-replay-fix`, SC-11) is merged without a wire change.

## CT-51 Owner-assisted re-enrollment of an existing account (MR-23) (2026-09-25)

An account that lost every device had no way back: pairing needs one of its own trusted devices, invites create new
accounts only (MA-19b) and recovery serves only the kit owner (MA-19a). The ceremony is owner-assisted and
fingerprint-confirmed:

1. `enroll.reenroll.create {accountId}` (owners, a `secret` op) → `{reenrollId, secret, expiresAt, account {accountId,
   name}}`. The secret (≥ 128 bits, the invite format) is shown once and stored as a hash; it expires after 24 h
   (`REENROLL_TTL_S`). A new one for the same account revokes the open one.
2. `enroll.reenroll.accept {secret, endpoint}` (enrollment channel, a `secret` op) → `{reenrollId, state:
   'pending_confirmation', account {name}, fingerprint, expiresAt}`. The device shows `pairingFingerprint` of its own
   PeerId. Failed attempts share the unenrolled budget (`rate_limited`). Refusals: `reenroll_invalid`,
   `reenroll_expired`, `reenroll_used`, `reenroll_revoked`, `endpoint_enrolled`.
3. `enroll.reenroll.confirm {reenrollId, fingerprint, approve}` (owners): only now is the endpoint bound to the
   account (`reenroll_fingerprint_mismatch`, `reenroll_not_pending`). The device polls `enroll.reenroll.status
   {reenrollId}` (enrollment channel, answered only to the accepting endpoint) and reconnects for `app`.
4. `enroll.reenroll.list` (open, pending, and ended within 7 days, with the pending device's label, platform and
   fingerprint) and `enroll.reenroll.revoke {reenrollId}` (owners).

Why a confirmation step beyond the task's create/accept: the secret travels out of band (a link), so a leaked link
alone must not bind a stranger's device; the owner compares the fingerprint with the person, as in CT-46. Any owner
may confirm or revoke.

The account's existing endpoints stay; an owner revokes lost ones with `endpoints.revoke`. Any account may be
re-enrolled, owners included. A single owner session can therefore reach another account, which is inherent in an
owner-assisted ceremony; the mitigations are the fingerprint check, the 24 h one-time secret, signed events
(`reenroll.created|accepted|completed|denied|revoked`, `ReenrollAuditPayload`: ids, the acting owner, the
fingerprint), and content-free `security` pushes to every owner and to the account's own endpoints on create and
on completion, so a person who still has a device sees it and can revoke. It gives no recovery-key authority
(CT-45 is unchanged).

## CT-52 Customer-approved diagnostic bundles (assignment §12) (2026-09-25)

Owners generate, read, download and delete bundles over the session; nothing is ever uploaded to Whombat's cloud,
and the customer sends the file themselves.

- `diagnostics.create {scopes}` → `DiagnosticBundleSummary {bundleId, scopes, createdAt, expiresAt, createdBy, size,
  sha256, downloads, lastDownloadedAt}`. At most 10 bundles (`diagnostics_limit`); each expires after 7 days.
- `diagnostics.preview {bundleId}` → `{summary, bundle}` (a query): the stored document unchanged, and
  `sha256(diagnosticBundleBytes(bundle)) === summary.sha256`, so the preview is provably what a download contains.
- `diagnostics.download {bundleId}`: a session export op (mutating, `transfer: 'export'`), read only through an export
  stream; DATA is `diagnosticBundleBytes(bundle)` (UTF-8 canonical JSON), `stream_done.sha256` equals the summary.
- `diagnostics.list`, `diagnostics.delete {bundleId}` → `{deleted}`.
- Signed events `diagnostics.created|downloaded|deleted|expired` (`DiagnosticsAuditPayload`: id, scopes, size,
  sha256, acting owner). A preview is a query and writes no event: the `created` event already fixes the content by
  its hash, and `downloaded` records each time it left the appliance.

Scopes: `versions`, `health`, `updates`, `backup`, `connectivity`, `errors` (`DIAGNOSTIC_SCOPES`). Each has a strict
schema that is its field allowlist, and every string is an enum, a version, a release id, an operation name or a
code, matched by a pattern without spaces or `/`. Message content, prompts, file paths, SQL, environment,
names, emails, labels, account ids and free-text details (health `detail`, backup `reason`, update `explanation`)
therefore can't be expressed. The runtime stores a bundle only if `DiagnosticBundle` parses it and
`diagnosticBundleProblems` is empty (sections match the chosen scopes, ≤ 256 KiB). Vectors: `session.json` →
`diagnosticBundles`.

## CT-53 Client security floor (assignment §12) (2026-09-25)

`ReleaseTuple.clientFloor {web, android, ios, desktop, cli}` gives the lowest client build number each platform may
run against this release (`0`: no floor). Build numbers are integers (`ClientBuildNumber`, 0…2^31−1: Android
`versionCode`, the iOS build counter, the hosted web UI's build counter), not semver strings, so the comparison is
trivial and identical in Go and TypeScript. All five `ClientInfo` platforms are listed now so a later desktop floor
doesn't need another change to the tuple.

- `hello.client.buildNumber` (optional; absent counts as 0).
- The runtime gets the running tuple's floor from the manager in `FactsRequest.update.clientFloor` (`UpdateFacts`,
  optional) and keeps the last value across restarts. Below the floor (`clientBelowFloor`, Go
  `release.ClientBelowFloor`) it answers `error{unsupported_version, details: {supported, appliance, code:
  'client_below_security_floor', floor: {platform, minBuild}}}` and closes; `whoMustUpdate` answers `client`. It
  applies on both channels.
- `appliance.status.clientFloor` (optional, nullable) lets the hosted UI and the apps show the floors.
- The floor follows the running tuple and does not ratchet: a rollback to known-good restores that release's floor,
  so release custody keeps floors monotonic across releases it approves.
- The floor protects honest clients from running a withdrawn build; it isn't authentication (a client can claim any
  build).

`clientFloor` is optional in the tuple so tuples without it keep their digest (`compat.json` → `digests`). A tuple
that carries it is refused by helpers and managers built from contracts < 0.5.3 (an unknown member of a strict
document, CT-14), which is fail-closed. Rollout order: the first release whose manager and helper use contracts ≥
0.5.3 is published without a floor; floors start with the next one.

## CT-54 Reproducible release artifacts (2026-09-25)

`git archive` of `HEAD:go` stamped every entry with the current time, so the Go tarball changed on every build.
`scripts/release.ts` now archives tree objects (the `go` tree, and a `git mktree` tree holding exactly `schema/` and
`vectors/`) with `--mtime=@499162500` (pnpm pack's fixed time), `tar.umask=0022` and git's internal gzip (no
timestamp). Entries are in tree order, uid/gid 0. `pnpm pack` output was already deterministic (fixed mtime, gzip
without a timestamp). The release builds every artifact twice from scratch and refuses (and removes the directory)
unless both builds are byte-identical. `RELEASE.json` records `reproducible {archiveMtime, trees}`; the tree ids let a
consumer check a vendored copy with `git write-tree`. The rebuild recipe is in `docs/publishing.md`.

## CT-55 Pack archives travel as upload streams (parity G-04) (2026-09-26)

`packs.upload` sends the archive as one base64 request, which a 64 KiB CONTROL message caps at ≈ 48 KiB. Over the
session an archive is now staged, uploaded and imported, reusing the attachment upload machinery (per-chunk and
whole-file sha256, resume by reopening, CT-36 pipelining):

1. `packs.stage {burrow, fileName, size, sha256}` → `{stagedArchiveId, expiresAt, maxBytes}`. Anyone who may import
   into the burrow can stage. `size ≤ PACK_ARCHIVE_MAX_BYTES` (= `PACK_LIMITS.maxArchiveBytes`, 4 MiB, the runtime's
   own cap; `pack_archive_too_large` otherwise). A staged archive expires after an hour, and an account may hold 5.
2. `open{upload, target: {type: 'pack-archive', burrow, stagedArchiveId}, size, sha256, chunkSize}` must have the
   staged size and sha256 (`stream_refused`, `pack_staged_mismatch`). `stream_done.output` is
   `PackStagedUploadOutput`.
3. `packs.import {burrow, stagedArchiveId}` → `{version, created}`. It is mutating and goes through the same validation,
   authorization and keys engine as `packs.upload`, so it may answer `approval_required`. It consumes the staged
   archive. Refusals: `pack_staged_not_found|incomplete|expired|used`.

These are session-native operations, not REST contracts: staging only exists on the session. Self-hosted REST keeps
`packs.upload`. Session clients use the staged path for every archive regardless of size. There is no new capability:
an older runtime answers `unknown_op` to `packs.stage`, so it never receives the new upload target (which it would
reject as an invalid message).

## CT-56 Bundled packs install from the running release (parity G-05) (2026-09-26)

`packs.importBundled {burrow, name, version}` → `{version, created}` installs a pack shipped with the running release.
The runtime resolves it only in the release's own bundle directory, which is part of the TUF-verified runtime
component, never from a host path or an input path. `version` must equal the bundled version `packs.list` showed
(`pack_bundled_version_mismatch`), so an update between listing and installing can't swap the content; an unknown
name is `pack_bundled_not_found`. A separate operation replaces an input guard on `packs.importLocal`: managed runtimes
keep excluding `packs.importLocal` wholesale, and its `{bundled}` form stays self-hosted only.

## CT-57 The control service's repository is control (2026-09-26)

John renamed the control service's repository from `whombat-control` to `whombat-api`, since it serves
`api.<env>`. The name is also a wire value, so it changes there too. Device requests now carry `aud =
whombat-api:<env>`, and the product manifest's `RepositoryName` is `control`. This is a breaking change, so the
version goes to 0.6.0. No appliance was ever enrolled against a live control service, so nothing needs to migrate:
an 0.6.0 control service refuses `whombat-control:<env>` (`wrong_audience`), and every consumer moves to 0.6.0
together. The component itself is still called "control", and so are `@whombat/control-contracts`,
`ControlApi…`, the `control-stack` infrastructure module and the CL-nn decisions. Only the repository/service name
changes.

## CT-58 The console claim code (MA-22 CC-01) (2026-09-26)

The claim code's primitives live in a new subpath, `@whombat/protocol/claim`, which the package root also exports.
Go has the same functions in `protocol`.

- `ClaimLookup` (`^[0-9]{4,6}$`) is a **string**, so leading zeros are allowed (`0042`) and a number never changes its
  length. Control decides which numbers it hands out. `ClaimLetters` is four letters of `CLAIM_CODE_ALPHABET`
  (`ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRTVWXY`), and `ClaimCode` is the display form `KX-4821-QM` (`formatClaimCode`).
- `normalizeClaimCode(input)` returns `{kind: 'letters', letters}`, `{kind: 'code', letters, lookup}` or
  `{kind: 'invalid'}`. It upper-cases ASCII `a–z` and drops the same characters as `normalizeClaimSecret` (Unicode
  White_Space, U+FEFF, `-`), and it maps nothing: `KO-4821-QM` is invalid, and so are full-width letters. Where the
  dashes were doesn't matter (`KX4821QM`, `KX-4821-QM-`). The letters of a full code are `L1L2L3L4` in order.
- `generateClaimLetters(randomBytes)` samples without modulo bias and gives the same result in every language: it
  consumes bytes in order, a byte `b < 240` gives `ALPHABET[b % 20]`, and a byte `≥ 240` is skipped. It asks for 4 bytes,
  then for as many as letters are still missing. Go: `GenerateClaimLetters(io.Reader)`. Vectors: `claim.json` →
  `codes`, `formats`, `letters`.
- The alphabet, `CPaceSuite` and the tags are generated into Go's `constants_gen.go` from the TypeScript constants,
  so the two languages can't drift.

## CT-59 CPace suite and the claim binding (CC-06) (2026-09-26)

CPace is `CPACE-RISTR255-SHA512` in the initiator–responder setting, exactly as draft-irtf-cfrg-cpace-21. TypeScript
uses `@noble/curves` `ristretto255` with `ristretto255_hasher.deriveToCurve` (RFC 9496 element derivation) and
`@noble/hashes`. Go uses `github.com/gtank/ristretto255` v0.2.0 (`SetUniformBytes`, `SetCanonicalBytes`). The
spec is silent on some points; they are settled as follows:

- **Scalars**: the draft's recommended `sample_scalar` (32 random bytes, the bits above 252 cleared). A zero scalar is
  drawn again. Randomness is injected (`randomBytes(n)` / `io.Reader`), and the implementation reads exactly 32 bytes
  per scalar.
- **`scalar_mult_vfy`** returns `G.I` for anything that isn't a canonical ristretto255 encoding, and for the identity.
  Both sides abort on `G.I` (`CpaceError` / `ErrCPaceInvalidShare`). K is never exposed.
- **Inputs**: `PRS` is the UTF-8 password (the 4 letters, or for `card` since 0.7.1 the card's `claimSecretHash`, CT-66). `CI` is
  `lv_cat("whombat-claim/1", method, deviceId, appliancePeerId, clientPeerId)` over the UTF-8 strings. PeerIds use their
  `12D3KooW…` text form, as each side sees them in its own Noise handshake. `deviceId` is control's directory id
  (`claim.device`). `sid` is the UTF-8 of control's claim id, and `ADa` = `ADb` = empty. The client is the initiator.
- **Key confirmation**: `k = HKDF-SHA512(salt = none, IKM = ISK, info = "whombat-claim-confirm/1", L = 64)`. The transcript
  is the draft's `transcript_ir(Ya, b"", Yb, b"")`. `tagClient = HMAC-SHA512(k, "client" ‖ transcript)[0..32]` and
  `tagAppliance = HMAC-SHA512(k, "appliance" ‖ transcript)[0..32]`, as ASCII labels. Shares and tags go on the wire as
  base64url without padding (43 characters, `ClaimPakeShare`, `ClaimConfirmTag`). Decoding is strict, so non-canonical
  trailing bits are refused.
- The appliance keeps both tags (not ISK) with the claim id and method. That is equivalent to CC-07's `{ISK,
  transcript}` and simpler. `claimConfirmEqual` compares in constant time and is false for anything that isn't a tag.
- **High-level API**: TS `claimPakeInitiator(ctx, randomBytes)` → `{share, state}`, `claimPakeInitiatorFinish(state,
  applianceShare)` → `{client, appliance}`, `claimPakeResponder(ctx, clientShare, randomBytes)` → `{share, tags}`,
  `claimConfirmEqual`; Go `NewClaimPakeClient` / `(*ClaimPakeClient).Finish`, `ClaimPakeRespond`, `ClaimConfirmEqual`.
  Errors are `ClaimPakeError{code: invalid_share | invalid_password}` and `ErrClaimPakeInvalidShare|InvalidPassword`.
- **Vectors** (`cpace.json`): the draft's Appendix A and B.3 values (generator string and generator, Ya, Yb, K,
  transcript, ISK_IR, `scalar_mult` and both invalid points), transcribed once and checked by both languages. Our own
  cases, generated by TypeScript and checked by Go: code and card agree; a wrong password, a relay's key on either side
  (MITM), swapped PeerIds, another claim id, another device id and another method all disagree; the identity, a
  non-encoding, a non-canonical or negative field element, non-canonical base64url and malformed shares are refused.

## CT-60 Claim attempt counting (CC-07) (2026-09-26)

`claimBackoffSeconds(failuresInWindow)` gives the appliance's policy as a pure function. `failuresInWindow` counts the
failures in the rolling 24 h window, including the one that just happened. The first 3 cost 0; after that, `begin` is
refused for 60, 120, 240, … seconds, counted from the latest failure and capped at 3,600. In the steady state that is at
most 24 guesses a day, as CC-07 estimates. The constants are `CLAIM_FREE_FAILURES`, `CLAIM_FAILURE_WINDOW_S`,
`CLAIM_BACKOFF_BASE_S` and `CLAIM_BACKOFF_MAX_S`. `ENROLL_CLAIM_BEGIN_TTL_S` (120, Go `EnrollClaimBeginTTLS`) is how
long a begin lives.

## CT-61 The claim session operations (CC-07) (2026-09-26)

- `enroll.claim.begin {claimId, method, share}` → `{share}` is **ephemeral**, like `presence.*`: there's no `accepted`
  and no receipt, it is never resent, and it isn't exportable. It commits nothing, and a retried begin must use a fresh
  share anyway. A new begin replaces the session's previous one.
- `enroll.claim {claimId, method, confirm, account, endpoint}` → `EnrolledOutput + {recoveryKitRequired, confirm}`.
  `method` is repeated, so the appliance matches the begin on `(session, claimId, method)`. Without a live begin it
  answers `claim_begin_missing`. A wrong `confirm` is `claim_invalid`, counts as a failure and uses up the begin.
  `enroll.claim` stays a normal mutating op that is **not** `secret`: a tag reveals nothing beyond the one guess it was
  computed for, so a retry after a lost answer gets the stored result, including the appliance's tag, which the
  client can still check.
- App codes (`error.details.code`, with `error.code`): `claim_invalid` (`forbidden`), `claim_backoff` (`rate_limited`,
  `ClaimBackoffDetails {code, retryAt}`), `claim_not_ready` (`unavailable`: no code on the console, or `card` without
  a card secret), `claim_used` (`conflict`), `claim_begin_missing` (`conflict`), and the new `claim_share_invalid`
  (`validation_failed`). A malformed or identity share isn't a guess, so it is refused without counting.
- `normalizeClaimSecret`, `claimSecretHash` and `claimVerifier` stay: the card secret is `card`'s PAKE password and
  control's `claimProof`.

## CT-62 Control: claims by code, nearby devices, self-registration, lookup leases (CC-03…CC-05, CC-10) (2026-09-26)

- The `claims.start` body is `ClaimStartBody`, a union of `ClaimStartCard {method: 'card', device, claimProof}`,
  `ClaimStartCodeNearby {method: 'code', device}` and `ClaimStartCodeLookup {method: 'code', lookup}`, each with
  `class` (default `interactive`). The two `code` forms share a discriminator value, which Zod's `discriminatedUnion`
  refuses, so this is a plain `z.union` of strict objects. `device` together with `lookup` matches neither. The
  response is unchanged, and `PendingClaim` now carries `method`.
- `claims.nearby` (`GET /orgs/:org/claims/nearby`, session) → `{devices: NearbyDevice[] ≤ 20}` (`{device, model,
  registeredAt, lastSeenAt}`, most recently seen first, never the lookup number). Control must route it before
  `/orgs/:org/claims/:claim`; claim ids have at least 8 characters, so `nearby` can never be one.
- `devices.selfRegister` (`POST /devices/self-register`, `auth: 'none'`, which already existed for JWKS) takes
  `DeviceRegistration` with `model` fixed to `SELF_INSTALLED_MODEL` (`self-installed`, Go `device.SelfInstalledModel`)
  and answers `DeviceRegistrationResponse` (201, or 200 for an identical repeat). `DirectoryDevice.origin` is
  `factory | self` (`DeviceOrigin`).
- The device op `claim.lookup {}` → `{lookup, expiresAt, renewAfterS}` has `renewAfterS` in 30…86,400 (control sends
  300). Its Go types are `device.ClaimLookupRequest`/`Response`.
- The new reasons are `device_not_nearby`, `lookup_not_found` and `self_registration_disabled`, and `already_claimed`
  also covers `claim.lookup`. `CLAIM_CODE_LIMITS` records CC-03…CC-05's and CC-10's numbers (renewal, release, the
  4-digit pool, the nearby window, the budgets and the self-registration limits) for control. Paths are relative to
  `CONTROL_PREFIX` (`/v1`), like every endpoint.

## CT-63 The lookup lease on the admin socket (CC-03) (2026-09-26)

`POST /claim-lookup` (`ADMIN_PATHS.claimLookup`, Go `AdminPathClaimLookup`) takes `ClaimLookupLeaseRequest {v, lookup:
ClaimLookup | null, expiresAt?}` and answers `AdminOk`. The name differs from the assignment's `ClaimLookupRequest`
because the registry already uses that name for the device op `claim.lookup`'s body (registry name = JSON Schema
file = Go type). `expiresAt` accompanies a number and nothing else (`claimLookupLeaseValid`, Go
`ClaimLookupLeaseValid`). A refinement isn't allowed in the cross-language subset, so this is a helper, like
`assignmentResultValid`. The manager pushes the lease on every change and at runtime start, as it does with the facts.

## CT-64 The console file (CC-08) (2026-09-26)

`ConsoleState {v: 1, state: ConsoleClaimState, code?: ClaimCode, url, retryAt?: Rfc3339}` is in
`@whombat/control-contracts/local` and Go `local`. It is a tolerant `z.object` with the helper `consoleStateValid` (Go
`ConsoleStateValid`: `code` exactly in `claimable`, `retryAt` exactly in `backoff`), not a discriminated union: union
options must be strict objects, and a strict document would break an older console reading a newer runtime's file.
`url` is the absolute `WHOMBAT_APP_URL/claim` (printable ASCII, no spaces), and the console strips the scheme
(`consoleDisplayUrl`, Go `ConsoleDisplayURL`). `CONSOLE_FILE_ENV` / `CONSOLE_FILE_DEFAULT` (`WHOMBAT_CONSOLE_FILE`,
`/run/whombat/console.json`) are generated into Go.

## CT-65 Contracts 0.7.0 (MA-22, CC-12) (2026-09-26)

The claim code is a breaking change, so the version goes to 0.7.0. `EnrollClaimInput` loses `claimSecret` and gains
`method` and `confirm`, and `EnrollClaimOutput` gains `confirm`. The `claims.start` body is a union with a required
`method`, and `DirectoryDevice` requires `origin`. There are new ops, endpoints and admin/IPC paths
(`enroll.claim.begin`, `claims.nearby`, `devices.selfRegister`, `claim.lookup`, `/claim-lookup`, the console file).
No appliance was ever claimed against a live control service, so nothing needs to migrate. Every consumer (control,
runtime, app, manager, console, provisioning) moves to 0.7.0 together, as with 0.6.0 (CT-57). The Go module gains the
dependency `github.com/gtank/ristretto255` v0.2.0.

## CT-66 The card password is the stored claim-secret hash (0.7.1) (2026-09-26)

In 0.7.0 the claim PAKE's `card` password was the normalized 26-character secret. But the appliance never stores that
secret: provisioning keeps only `claim.json` `secretHash = claimSecretHash(deviceId, normalized)` (NX-24), so the
appliance could not run the responder for a card claim. From 0.7.1 the `card` password is that hash, exposed as
`claimCardPassword(deviceId, normalizedSecret)` (Go `ClaimCardPassword`), 43 base64url characters. The client
computes it from the card; the appliance reads it from `claim.json`. It is as strong as the secret (a 128-bit preimage),
it only lives on the device's encrypted `/persist` and in the client's memory during the claim, and it is
domain-separated from control's `claimVerifier`, so control still can't run a card PAKE. Only the password's shape
check changes (`card`: `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$`); the `card` vectors are regenerated. 0.7.0 was never adopted by a
consumer, so this is a patch release that every consumer takes instead of 0.7.0.

## CT-67 Claiming by code only from the box's own network (0.8.0) (2026-09-26)

John decided (claim-code CC-13) that a console code can only be used from the same network as the box, and that the
console shows only the four letters. `claims.start` loses the `{method:'code', lookup}` form (and the reason
`lookup_not_found`); the body is now a discriminated union of `card` and `code` with `device` (the one
`claims.nearby` lists). `ConsoleState.code` is the four letters (`ClaimLetters`, e.g. `KXQM`), no longer
`KX-4821-QM`. The lookup lease (`claim.lookup`, `/claim-lookup`) stays unchanged as the box's internal "waiting to
be claimed" presence: control's `claims.nearby` still requires a live lease and the runtime shows `waiting` without
one. `ClaimLookup`, `normalizeClaimCode` and `formatClaimCode` stay exported (the lease still carries a number, and
typed letters still normalize through `normalizeClaimCode`). Breaking for control, the runtime's console file and the
app, so 0.8.0; every consumer moves together.

## CT-68 Onboarding has four steps: “Set up your AI” replaces “Connect your code” (SUB-08) (2026-09-26)

`ONBOARDING_STEP_COUNT` is 4: 0 “Name your burrow”, 1 “Set up your AI” (`ONBOARDING_PROVIDER_STEP`), 2 “Meet your
agents”, 3 “Invite your team”. The step copy (`ONBOARDING_STEPS` in fixtures) replaces “Connect your code” with
`{t: 'Set up your AI', d: 'Pick and sign in', …}`. A step stored by an earlier server maps 0→0, 1→1, 2→1, 3→2, 4→3.

- `OnboardingState.clients: LiveProvider[]` (≤ 2, default `[]`) are the clients the owner chose, in the order picked.
  `onboarding.update` takes `clients` (unique). Choosing a client doesn't install it: the server calls
  `clients.install` (CT-72). `provider` stays and names the first agents' provider.
- `githubConnected` and `repos` are deprecated. They get `.default(false)` / `.default([])`: the output type still
  has them, so writers keep sending them and readers before 0.9.0 still parse; new readers accept their absence.
  `OnboardingRepo` is deprecated with them. All three are removed before 1.0.
- The complete body's comments name the steps instead of numbers. In managed mode the agents it creates get the
  source `{kind: 'requester', fallback: null}` (CT-69).

## CT-69 The `requester` credential source (SUB-04) (2026-09-26)

`CredentialSource` gains `{kind: 'requester', fallback: {kind: 'org', credentialId} | null}` (the org member is now
exported as `OrgCredentialSource`). Each turn runs on the sign-in of the person the work is for, and nobody's
subscription answers someone else.

- `DispatchCredential.onBehalfOfAccountId` (required, nullable) is that person. It is who asked; for an automation, its
  publisher; for an agent-to-agent handoff, a follow-up or a retry, the person who started the chain; and null for
  work that is for nobody (system work, a website visitor's feedback report). The server sets it for every source,
  next to `requestedByAccountId`, which stays the direct requester only.
- The runner resolves a `requester` source exactly: with a person, only that account's credential home for the
  agent's provider. If the person has no sign-in for that provider, the turn is refused with
  `provider.requester_not_signed_in`, whose explanation is meant for them. The fallback never stands in for a
  person. Without a person, the turn runs on `fallback`'s organization home, or is refused with
  `provider.no_requester` when there is none. No other fallback exists. For this source, `ownerName`/`ownerPresent`
  describe the person the work is for.
- `fallback` is required (`null` for none), so choosing “no fallback” is explicit, and it can only be an organization
  credential.
- `DEFAULT_TEAM_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE = {kind: 'requester', fallback: null}`: in managed mode the server creates team
  agents (onboarding, hiring) with it. An absent or null source still means none chosen (`provider.owner_required`).
  The runtime may backfill existing team agents. `agents.setCredentialSource` (REST and over the session) accepts the
  new kind, and applies wherever people sign in themselves, including self-hosted servers with per-person sign-ins.
- Compatibility: a reader before 0.9.0 refuses a runtime (and so the agent) that carries a `requester` source (an
  unknown union member), so the server must only write it once the app and the runner are on 0.9.0.
  `onBehalfOfAccountId` is required because the runner and the server ship in one runtime bundle.

## CT-70 Provider sign-ins are a REST contract too (`api.signins`) (2026-09-26)

Self-hosted servers need the same sign-ins as managed appliances (SUB-01), and the web UI already reaches every
`api` endpoint over the session (CT-06). So each capability is now a REST contract. The session reaches it as an
`api` op, so one client code path serves both modes. The shapes move to `@whombat/core`, and
`@whombat/protocol/session` re-exports them under the same names:

- `@whombat/core/domain` (`signins.ts`): `SignInProvider`, `AuthModeName`, `ProviderLoginId`, `ProviderLogin`,
  `ProviderSignIn`, `OrgCredentialProvider`, `OrgCredential`, `SignInVerified`, `SignInError`, and
  `ProviderSignInState`, the appliance's credential states. The protocol's `ProviderState` is now an alias of the same
  enum instance. The name differs because core already has `ProviderState`, the runner's host-check enum.
- `@whombat/core/contracts` (`providers.ts`): `api.signins.list|loginStart|loginStatus|loginSubmit|loginCancel|logout|
  orgList|orgLoginStart|orgRemove`, under `/sign-ins`. The bodies are the same strict schemas as the native inputs.
  Ids the native inputs carry (`loginId`, `provider`, `credentialId`) are path params. `ProvidersListOutput` gains
  `consoles` (CT-71, default `[]`, so a runtime before 0.9.0 still parses).
- The area key is `signins` (lower case), so the op name equals the endpoint id (`^[a-z]+\.[a-zA-Z]+$`). `signIns` as
  an area would break that rule, and `providers` would collide with the native `providers.list`/`providers.logout`.
- The session-native `providers.*` ops stay, with unchanged inputs and the same output schema objects.
  `PROVIDER_OP_EQUIVALENTS` maps each one to its `signins.*` op, and a test checks that the output, the mutating flag
  and the secret flag match. They are deprecated for new clients and removed before 1.0. The runtime serves both
  names from one handler.
- `SECRET_API_OPS` gains `signins.loginStart`, `signins.loginSubmit` and `signins.orgLoginStart` (as their native twins,
  CT-44), plus `signins.consoleRead` and `signins.consoleWrite` (CT-71). Over REST the same rule holds: the server logs
  neither the body nor the answer of these endpoints.
- The organization endpoints are for owners on a managed appliance, and for admins of this Whombat when self-hosted.

## CT-71 The Claude sign-in console (SUB-02, SUB-03) (2026-09-26)

The Claude subscription sign-in is the CLI's own `claude auth login --claudeai`, running in a PTY with the person's
credential home. The web UI shows that console and forwards keystrokes. The person signs in on claude.ai, and
Whombat never reads the credential. The contract:

- **Fixed command, no shell.** `PROVIDER_CONSOLE_COMMANDS['claude:subscription_cli']` is the only program. It follows
  from `{provider: 'claude', authMode: 'subscription_cli'}` alone (literals in `ProviderConsoleStartBody`), and no
  input names a program, an argument or an environment variable. Only people own consoles: a subscription is
  personal, so there is no organization console.
- **Ops** (`api.signins`, the session's or the cookie's own account):
  - `consoleStart {provider, authMode, cols, rows}` → `ProviderConsole` (id prefix `pcn_`, `ProviderConsoleId`). A
    running console of the same account and provider is cancelled first, so a second tab takes over.
  - `consoleRead` (`GET`, query `{cursor, waitMs ≤ 25 s}`) → `{console, from, data, next, more}`.
  - `consoleWrite {seq, data}` → `ProviderConsole`.
  - `consoleResize {cols, rows}` → `ProviderConsole`.
  - `consoleCancel` → `ProviderConsole`.

  States are `running|completed|failed|cancelled|expired`, and a console also carries `exitCode`, `expiresAt`
  (`PROVIDER_CONSOLE_TTL_S` = 600), `outputBytes` and `inputSeq`. `providers.list`/`signins.list` include the
  account's consoles, so a reloaded page resumes one.
- **Output is a long-poll read with a byte cursor, not a session stream.** A session stream would need a new
  `open` spec. An older runtime treats an unknown spec as an invalid message and closes the session, so a stream
  would need its own capability, and REST would still need a read. A read op works the same over REST and the
  session. The output is small: a login writes a few KB.
  - `data` is base64 of the raw PTY bytes (terminal escapes included; UTF-8 may split across reads), at most 16 KiB.
  - The server keeps the newest 64 KiB. A cursor older than that is answered from `from` (later than the cursor),
    not with an error.
  - Over the session, `deadlineMs` must exceed `waitMs`.
- **Input** is text as the terminal emulator produced it (control characters and escape sequences included), at
  most 4 KiB of UTF-8 (`ConsoleInputText`, checked with `utf8ByteLength`, which doesn't need `TextEncoder`).
  - `seq` numbers the writes of a console from 1. A repeated `seq` is answered without typing it again, so a client
    resends safely after a lost answer (a secret op's retry gets `unknown_outcome`, CT-44). A gap is refused
    (`provider.console_input_gap`, `details.inputSeq`).
  - Read and write are `secret`: the output may echo what the person typed (the code from claude.ai), so neither is
    logged or kept in a receipt.
- **Completion:** after exit 0 the runner asks the CLI's own status (`claude auth status`). Only when that says
  signed in is the console `completed`, and the sign-in appears in `signins.list` as a normal `ProviderSignIn`
  (`claude`/`subscription_cli`). Exit 0 without a sign-in is `failed` with `provider.login_missing`.
- **Runner relay**, mirroring `signin.poll|answer|event` (PV-12):
  - `SIGNIN_METHODS.consoleStart|consoleInput|consoleResize|consoleStop` are queued by the server through
    `signin.poll` and answered through `signin.answer`. `consoleStart` carries `expiresAt`, and the runner stops the
    process on its own at that time too.
  - The runner reports `ConsoleSignInEvent`s (`output {offset, data}` in order, then one `exit {exitCode, state,
    error}`) with the new `signin.console` (`runnerApi.signinConsole`, `POST /internal/runner/signin/console`). It
    answers `unknown` consoles, which the runner stops.
  - `offset` makes a repeated report harmless.
- New codes: `provider.console_not_found`, `provider.console_ended` and `provider.console_input_gap`.

## CT-72 AI clients install on demand at the latest tested version (SUB-09) (2026-09-26)

`ClientStatus` (`@whombat/core/domain`, per `LiveProvider`) has these members:

- `installed {version, installedAt, source: whombat|host} | null` and `latest {version, publishedAt} | null` (the
  latest tested version for this machine);
- `state`: `not_installed|installing|installed|updating|failed`;
- `progress` (0–100 | null) and `error {code, message} | null`.

`source: 'host'` is self-hosted only: a CLI found on the host's PATH, which Whombat neither updates nor removes.
`installedAt` is null for it, which is why it is nullable.

The operations are REST contracts in `api.clients`, and so session ops with the same names (CT-06), like
`agents.setCredentialSource` (CT-39):

- `clients.list` (`GET /clients`, everyone signed in) → `{clients, checkedAt, canManage}`;
- `clients.install` (`POST /clients/:provider/install`) → `ClientStatus`;
- `clients.remove` (`DELETE /clients/:provider`) → `ClientStatus`.

Install and remove are for owners who are admins, like `host.recheckAgents`. Install answers at once
(`installing`) and is idempotent. Remove stops an install in progress and keeps sign-ins. There is no update call,
because clients update themselves to newer tested versions. An update installs next to the running version and
switches between turns, so no turn is cut off. Over the session the input is `{params: {provider}}`.

The new codes are `client.unavailable`, `client.busy`, `client.install_failed`, `client.digest_mismatch`,
`client.host_managed` and `client.not_installed` (a turn refusal). The manager side is CT-73, and bundles and the
channel are CT-74.

## CT-73 The manager installs the AI clients (local IPC) (2026-09-26)

The manager socket gains `GET /v1/clients` → `LocalClientsStatus`, `POST /v1/clients/install` (`ClientInstallRequest
{v, provider}`, 202 `LocalClient`) and `POST /v1/clients/remove` (`ClientRemoveRequest`). The admin socket gains
`POST /clients` (`ClientsPushRequest`, the same members as `LocalClientsStatus`, strict at the top). With the push the
runtime learns about updates without polling, and with the `GET` it catches up at start.

- `LocalClient.installed` carries `executable {path, sha256}` and `fixturesDigest`. The runner runs exactly that
  path and checks that hash, so the bundle's pin replaces the image's (SUB-09 refines PV-01).
- The runtime tells the manager which bundles fit it through `RuntimeFacts.clientAdapters {claude, codex}`
  (optional; a tolerant response the manager already reads). Putting the levels in the release tuple instead was
  considered and rejected. A new tuple member makes every older helper and manager refuse the tuple (CT-53's
  rollout constraint). Also, the runtime is the one that knows which adapter it implements, and a wrong claim only
  picks a bundle that still has to pass TUF and the digests.
- Install is idempotent: the manager selects the version, and the request can't name one. Remove stops an install.
  The previous version stays for at least 24 hours after an update, so running turns finish.
- Paths are absolute and made of plain segments (no `..`, no spaces). The pattern avoids nested counted repeats,
  which RE2 limits to 1000.

## CT-74 Client bundles and the signed client channel (`@whombat/release`) (2026-09-26)

A CI job publishes tested client versions within about a day of upstream (SUB-09), independently of appliance
releases. `@whombat/release`, cross-language, with Go and vectors in `clients.json`:

- `ClientBundle` (strict) has these members:
  - `provider` (`claude|codex`), `version`, `os` (`linux`) and `arch` (`x86_64|aarch64`);
  - `publishedAt` (upstream), `testedAt` (≥ `publishedAt`), and `fixturesDigest` (`sha256:` of the provider
    fixtures regenerated from this executable, which the tests ran against);
  - `adapter: IntRange`, the runtime adapter levels the tests passed with;
  - `artifact {target, sha256, size, path}`, the TUF target `clients/<provider>/<version>/<os>-<arch>.tar.gz`
    (`clientBundleTarget`);
  - `source {url, sha256, size, format: binary|tar.gz, path}`, the publisher's own download for self-hosted
    installs;
  - `executable {sha256, size}`, which is identical either way because the binary is unmodified (SUB-02).
- `ClientChannelPayload` has `{purpose: 'whombat-client-channel/v1', env, sequence, issuedAt, expiresAt ≤ 14 days,
  bundles ≤ 64}`. The bundles are in order of preference, newest first per provider. It is signed as
  `SignedClientChannel` (`signedDocument`).
- `verifyClientChannel` / Go `VerifyClientChannel` fail with `bad_schema`, `unknown_key`, `bad_signature`,
  `wrong_env`, `bad_lifetime`, `expired`, `not_yet_valid`, `rolled_back`, `bad_bundle` or `duplicate_bundle`. A
  channel with the same sequence as the last one accepted passes, since a channel is re-read, unlike an assignment,
  which is applied once. A lower sequence is a rollback.
- `selectClientBundle` / Go `SelectClientBundle` pick the first bundle for the provider, os and arch whose adapter
  range contains the runtime's level. `ClientAdapterLevel` is the runtime adapter's version per provider.
- Signing: the channel is signed with a key from a pinned key document shaped like `AssignmentKeys` (CT-41 states,
  `assignmentKeyMap`). On an appliance it is also the TUF target `clients/channel.json` of a delegated targets role
  `clients`, restricted to `clients/*`. That role's key is held by the CI job (online, 1 of 1), so the channel
  advances without the offline 2-of-2 release keys, and the key can never approve a release tuple or a runtime or
  host artifact. The signature lets a self-hosted server, which has no TUF, verify the same document. On an
  appliance, TUF adds freshness and snapshot consistency.
- The product manifest and the release tuple are unchanged. For a runtime that installs bundles, the tuple's
  `providers` may stay empty: the release no longer has to pin client versions.

## CT-75 Contracts 0.9.0 (provider subscriptions, SUB-01…SUB-11) (2026-09-26)

0.9.0 is a minor release before 1.0. It has additive members, one new union member and a few changed shapes, and every
consumer moves to it together. What each side has to watch:

- **Readers before 0.9.0 break on:**
  - an agent runtime with a `requester` source (CT-69). The server writes it only once the app and the runner are on
    0.9.0.
  - an onboarding `step` above 3 written by an older server. The server maps stored steps (CT-68).
- **Tolerated both ways:**
  - `ProvidersListOutput.consoles` (default `[]`);
  - `OnboardingState.githubConnected`/`repos`/`clients` (defaults);
  - `RuntimeFacts.clientAdapters` (optional, in a tolerant response).
- **Strict at the top level:**
  - `ClientsPushRequest` is new and only sent to a runtime that serves `POST /clients`. A manager learns that from
    `clientAdapters` in `GET /facts`.
  - `DispatchCredential.onBehalfOfAccountId` is required (the runner and the server ship together).
- **Unchanged:** the session protocol version (1.0) and capabilities. The console is ordinary request/response and
  needs no new stream kind. The release tuple, the product manifest and the assignment are unchanged too.

Every package is 0.9.0.

## CT-76 The signed appliance licence: token, pinned key set, state (LC-01…LC-04, LC-09) (2026-09-26)

`@whombat/protocol` (`licence.ts`, also the subpath `@whombat/protocol/licence`) and Go `protocol` (`licence.go`), with
cross-language vectors in `licence.json`:

- **Token.** A compact JWS with header `LicenceHeader {alg: 'EdDSA', kid, typ: 'whombat-licence+jwt'}` (`LICENCE_TYP`)
  and strict `LicenceClaims {iss, aud, sub, org, plan, state, limits, iat, nbf, exp, jti}`.
  - `aud` is `LicenceAudience` (`whombat-appliance:<env>`).
  - `sub` is the device id. It uses `OpaqueId`, which is the same pattern as control's `DeviceId`.
  - `plan` is `LicencePlan` (`^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$`) and `state` is `EntitlementState`.
  - `limits` is `LicenceLimits {devices, members, agents, connectors}`, where `null` means unlimited for the last
    three.
  - `jti` is 22 to 64 base64url characters.
  - A token is at most `LICENCE_MAX_BYTES` (4096) long. `LicenceToken` is its string shape.
- **Constants (LC-02).**

  | Constant | Value |
  |---|---|
  | `LICENCE_LIFETIME_S` (also the maximum) | 1,209,600 |
  | `LICENCE_RENEW_S` | 86,400 |
  | `LICENCE_RENEW_UNPAID_S` | 3,600 |
  | `LICENCE_GRACE_S` | 2,592,000 |
  | `LICENCE_CLOCK_SKEW_S` | 300 |

  The Go constants are `LicenceTyp`, `LicenceAlg`, `LicenceAudiencePrefix`, `LicenceLifetimeS`, and so on.
- **`EntitlementState` moves** from `@whombat/control-contracts` to `@whombat/protocol`. Billing re-exports it, so
  existing imports keep working. Go gets `protocol.EntitlementState`, which is new in Go.
- **Key set (LC-03).** `LicenceKeySet {v: 1, env, keys: Ed25519Jwk[1…8]}` is strict. The helper `licenceAudience(env)`
  (Go `LicenceAudience`) gives the audience its tokens must carry. `Ed25519Jwk` is factored out of the admission JWK.
  `AdmissionJwk` is now the same schema object, and in Go `type AdmissionJwk = Ed25519Jwk`, an alias. So the two stay
  identical and existing code compiles unchanged. `ed25519Jwk(kid, publicKey)` builds one, and `admissionJwk` is the
  same function.
- **Verification.** `verifyLicenceToken(token, {keySet, device, now, verify?})` / Go `VerifyLicenceToken(token,
  VerifyLicenceOptions{KeySet, Device, Now})` follow the admission model:
  - structure (`malformed`);
  - header (`bad_header`, which is also where an admission ticket fails);
  - `kid` in the set (`unknown_kid`);
  - strict Ed25519 (`bad_signature`);
  - claims schema (`bad_claims`);
  - audience equal to `licenceAudience(keySet.env)` (`wrong_audience`);
  - `sub` equal to `device` (`wrong_device`);
  - `bad_lifetime` (`nbf < iat`, `exp ≤ nbf`, or `exp − iat` over 14 days);
  - `not_yet_valid` (`iat` or `nbf` later than `now` + 300 s, where `now` is the caller's effective time).

  **Expiry is not a verification error.** The runtime keeps reading an expired token to compute its grace. There
  is no issuer check: the pinned key set is the trust root. `signLicenceToken(header, claims, sign)` is for control
  and tests.
- **State (LC-09).** `licenceStatus({claims, now, highWater, clockMark, claimedAt, graceS?})` / Go
  `LicenceStatus(LicenceStatusParams)` return `LicenceStatusResult {state, reason, plan, limits, renewedAt, expiresAt,
  graceEndsAt, effectiveAt}` in epoch seconds, or null.
  - `LicenceState` is `licensed|grace|lapsed`.
  - `LicenceReason` is `active|trial|past_due|payment|not_renewed|no_licence|cancelled|expired`.
  - The effective time t is max(now, highWater, clockMark).
  - The branches are exactly LC-09's.
  - Decisions beyond LC-09:
    - **Without a token, the reason is `no_licence` in both phases** (grace, then lapsed). It says why better than
      `expired` does, and the lapsed banner reads the same either way.
    - Without a token, `expiresAt` is null and `graceEndsAt` is the claim time plus the grace. There is no token
      expiry to show, and “Agents keep working until …” uses `graceEndsAt`.
    - `cancelled` has `graceEndsAt: null`, since there is no grace.
    - `limits: null` means no token, so no count limits are known.
    - The input interface is named `LicenceStatusParams`, because the session op's input schema is
      `LicenceStatusInput`. The Go function takes `GraceS: 0` to mean the default.
- **Vectors.** `licence.json` holds 33 token cases: valid tokens, the next key, expired-but-valid tokens, a cancelled
  org, the skew edge, a tampered payload and signature, non-canonical S, a wrong device, a wrong audience or key-set
  env, an unknown kid, the admission key under both kids, an admission ticket, an admission `typ`, a lifetime over 14
  days, `nbf < iat`, `exp = nbf`, a future token, extra, missing or malformed claims, and oversize input. It also
  holds 20 `licenceStatus` cases covering every branch, clock rollback (`now < highWater`), `clockMark`, a cancelled
  org, no token, an unclaimed box and a shorter grace. The TypeScript test checks that every state and reason pair
  is covered. The keys come from the public vector seed (`licence-1`, `licence-2`), labelled TEST and bound to
  `whombat-appliance:test`.

## CT-77 Licence renewal, local IPC and session ops (LC-05…LC-08, LC-10, LC-13) (2026-09-26)

- **Device op `licence.renew`** (`LicenceRenewRequest {}` → `LicenceRenewResponse {token, expiresAt, renewAfterS 60…86400,
  now}`). Its documentation follows LC-05. It refuses `device_unclaimed`, `device_revoked`, `devices_allowed_reached`
  (LC-16) and `rate_limited` (12 per hour). A cancelled org still gets a token.
- **`licenceApi.keys`** is `GET /v1/licence/keys`, with auth `none`, and serves the `LicenceKeySet`. It is for
  operators and the dev harness only. Devices never fetch it; they trust the set pinned in their image. `controlApi`
  gains the area `licence`.
- **Local IPC.**
  - The manager socket gains `MANAGER_PATHS.licenceRenew = '/v1/licence/renew'`: `LicenceRenewNowRequest {v}` →
    `LicenceRenewNowResult {v, renewed, error?}`. It answers after the attempt, and answers 429 `busy` within 60 s of
    the last forced renewal. The names carry `…RenewNow…` because the device op already takes `LicenceRenewRequest`
    in the cross-language registry, the same reason as CT-63's `ClaimLookupLeaseRequest`.
  - The admin socket gains `ADMIN_PATHS.licence = '/licence'`: `LicencePushRequest {v, token | null, highWater:
    Rfc3339}` → `LicencePushResponse {v, licence: LocalLicenceStatus | null}`.
    - `LocalLicenceStatus` is `{state, reason, plan, expiresAt, graceEndsAt, effectiveAt}` in RFC 3339. It is enough
      for the manager's log, without usage.
    - The runtime answers 409 `stale` for an older `iat` and 400 `bad_request` for a token that doesn't verify.
    - `token: null` means the manager holds none yet. The runtime keeps the token it stored and takes only
      `highWater`.
- **Session.**
  - `licence.status` (a read, every member) and `licence.refresh` (owners and admins; the runtime checks the role)
    both answer `{licence: LicenceStatusView | null}`. `licence.refresh` is mutating, like `backup.runNow`: it writes
    the renewed token, has a receipt and is idempotent per request id. It isn't `secret`.
  - `LicenceStatusView` is `licenceStatus`'s answer with session `Timestamp`s, plus `usage {members, agents,
    connectors}` and `checkedAt`.
  - `ApplianceStatusOutput.licence` is `LicenceStatusView.nullable().optional()`: null when unclaimed, and absent
    from older runtimes and self-hosted servers.
- **Codes.** `APP_ERROR_CODES` gains:
  - `licence.lapsed` (`not_allowed`);
  - `licence.limit` (`not_allowed`, with `details` `LicenceLimitDetails {code, limit: members|agents|connectors,
    allowed}`);
  - **`licence.renew_failed`** (`unavailable`, `details.reason` = the manager's error). This one is a decision beyond
    LC-08. A “Check again” that couldn't reach control must say so. Answering the unchanged state as if the check had
    succeeded would mislead the owner.
- **Events.** `APPLIANCE_EVENT_TYPES` gains `licence.state_changed`. Its payload is `LicenceAuditPayload {from, to:
  {state, reason} | null, plan, jti}`, written on every change of state or reason.

## CT-78 Terms at claim, plan limits, account deletion (LC-11, LC-15…LC-18) (2026-09-26)

- **Terms.**
  - `APPLIANCE_TERMS_VERSION = '2026-09-26-draft'`, and `ClaimTerms = {version: TermsVersion}` (strict).
