    `TermsVersion` is a date with an optional qualifier: `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}(-[a-z0-9]{1,16})?$`.
  - Both `ClaimStartCard` and `ClaimStartCodeNearby` require `terms`. The schema accepts any well-formed version, and
    control refuses every one but the current version (`terms_required`, 400). This way a newer control can move to
    a new version without a client that sends it being refused by schema.
  - `PendingClaim` gains `termsVersion?` and `termsAcceptedAt?` (control's clock), optional for claims made before.
  - The `claims.start` summary names `terms_required`, `self_install_not_allowed` and `devices_allowed_reached`
    (atomic, and pending claims count).
- **Entitlement.**
  - `Entitlement` gains `limits: EntitlementLimits {members, agents, connectors}` (`PlanLimit`: an integer 0…100,000
    or null) and `selfInstall: boolean`.
  - The operator's `SetEntitlementBody` gains `limits?: {members?, agents?, connectors?}` and `selfInstall?`. It keeps
    the body's existing rule: an **absent member keeps the org's current value**. For an org without a row, the
    limits default to null (unlimited) and `selfInstall` to control's `DEFAULT_SELF_INSTALL`. An explicit null sets
    unlimited. The spec's “default null” is read as the default for a new row, because treating an absent member as
    null would silently clear limits on every partial update.
- **Account deletion.** `authApi.deleteAccount` is `{id: 'accounts.delete', method: 'DELETE', path: '/me', auth:
  'session'}`, with the body `DeleteAccountBody {email}`, the typed confirmation, and the answer `{ok: true}`.
  - `ControlEndpoint` already allows a body on any method, and control's JSON parser handles DELETE bodies, so it
    stays `DELETE /me`.
  - It refuses `last_owner` (409: the sole owner of an org with other members), `org_has_devices` (409: the sole
    member of an org that still has a claimed appliance) and `email_mismatch` (400).
  - Data on appliances belongs to the org and is never touched. Exactly what control deletes is control's to decide
    (CL).
- **`CONTROL_REASONS`** gains `terms_required`, `self_install_not_allowed`, `org_has_devices` and `email_mismatch`.
  `devices_allowed_reached` also covers `licence.renew`, and `last_owner` also covers `accounts.delete`.

## CT-79 Contracts 0.10.0 (the appliance licence, LC-01…LC-18) (2026-09-26)

0.10.0 is a minor release before 1.0, and every consumer moves to it together, as with CT-67 and CT-75. What each
side has to watch:

- **Breaks readers and writers before 0.10.0:**
  - `claims.start` requires `terms`. A client before 0.10.0 can't claim against a 0.10 control, and a 0.10 client
    sends a member an older control refuses (strict body). Control and the app ship together.
  - `Entitlement` requires `limits` and `selfInstall`. A reader before 0.10.0 strips them, but a 0.10 reader refuses
    an older control's entitlement. Control moves first, or together with the app.
  - Go: `protocol.AdmissionJwk` is now an alias of `protocol.Ed25519Jwk`. It is source compatible, but reflection or
    `%T` output shows the new name.
- **Tolerated both ways:**
  - `ApplianceStatusOutput.licence` (optional);
  - `PendingClaim.termsVersion` and `termsAcceptedAt` (optional);
  - the new app error codes and the `licence.state_changed` event (open sets);
  - the new ops. An older runtime answers `unknown_op`, so the app should hide the Subscription section when
    `appliance.status` has no `licence`.
- **Strict at the top level:**
  - `LicencePushRequest` is sent only to a runtime that serves `POST /licence`. A manager should treat a 404 as an
    older runtime and retries with the facts re-send.
  - `LicenceRenewNowRequest`, the device op body `{}`, `SetEntitlementBody` and `DeleteAccountBody`;
  - the licence header, claims and key set are signed and security documents, so they reject unknown members, and a
    new member needs a new `typ` or a new major.
- **Unchanged:** the session protocol version (1.0) and capabilities, the release tuple, the product manifest, the
  assignment and the admission ticket format.

Every package is 0.10.0.

## CT-80 The `guide` card (assistant-guides.md AG-02, AG-16…AG-18) (2026-09-26)

`@whombat/core/domain` (`guides.ts`):

- **`GuideCard`** `{kind: 'guide', guide: GuideTopic, node: GuideNodeId, step: GuideStep | null, title ≤ 120, body ≤ 1200
  (plain text, default ''), blocks ≤ 6, state: GuideState (open|done|expired), answer: GuideAnswer | null}`.
  - It is in `MessageCard` and `StoredCard` (stored as it is, no references) and in `CARD_KINDS`, never in
    `PostableCard`, so `post_card` can't forge one.
  - `GuideAnswer {actionId, optionIds | null, label ≤ 200, at}`. `label` is plain words and never a secret (“Client ID
    1234567890ab… saved”).
  - `GuideStep {index, total}`, 1…20, `index ≤ total`.
- **Blocks** (`GuideBlock`, on `type`):
  - `choices {id, mode: single|multi (default single), options 1…8, submitLabel | null}`. An option is `GuideOption
    {id, title ≤ 80, description ≤ 200, icon, badge: GuideBadge {label ≤ 24, tone: Tone} | null, disabled}`.
  - `actions {actions 1…4}`, where a `GuideAction` is `{id, label ≤ 40, style: primary|secondary|quiet (default
    secondary), href | null}`.
  - `copy {rows 1…8 of {label ≤ 60, value ≤ 2048}}`.
  - `links {links 1…8 of {label ≤ 80, url}}`.
  - `form {id, fields 1…6, submitLabel}`, where a `GuideField` is `{id, label ≤ 60, kind: text|secret|json_file,
    placeholder | null, optional}`.
  - `connect {provider: ConnectorProvider, services 1…6 (preticked), reconnect, returnTo: ReturnPath}`.
  - `status {rows 1…8 of {label ≤ 80, state: ok|warn|bad|mut, detail ≤ 200 | null, href | null}}`.
- **Ids.** Action, option, block and field ids are `GuideElementId` (`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`, ≤ 40), the same
  ids `guides.act` takes. A `choices` or `form` block's own `id` is the `actionId` it acts with.
- **Links.** `links[].url` is `GuideUrl`, https only. `href` is `GuideHref`: a `ReturnPath` on this Whombat or an
  https URL. An action with `href` is a link; the client navigates and sends nothing.
- **`connect.returnTo`** is set by the server: the DM path with its guide marker. The client passes it unchanged to
  `connections.startGoogle`, so the marker's format stays the server's (AG-08).
- **Icons.** `GuideIcon` is `{brand: GuideBrand}` (google, microsoft, mail, claude, openai, github; `mail` is the
  generic “Other email” mark) or `{icon: GuideIconName}`. The Lucide subset uses current Lucide names: mail,
  calendar, folder, file-text, sun, clock, sparkles, key, link, shield-check, circle-help (formerly help-circle),
  user-plus, bell, settings.
- **Open where a newer server may add things.**
  - `GuideTopic` is an open set: any `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` of up to 40 characters. `GUIDE_TOPICS` /
    `KnownGuideTopic` list this release's topics, and `isKnownGuideTopic` narrows.
  - A block `type` this release doesn't know is dropped on read, and an unknown icon reads as `null`. A newer
    server's card still renders from the blocks it knows.
  - A known block must still be valid. `GuideState`, the block field enums and the brands stay closed.
- **Helpers.** `guideCardLabel(card)` gives the label row (`SET UP · EMAIL · STEP 2 OF 6`, `GUIDE` for an unknown
  topic). `guideCardText(card)` gives the runner's history text (`[guide: {title}; you chose {answer.label}]`,
  AG-18). There is also `guideCardOpen`, and `GUIDE_TOPIC_SERVICES` maps a topic to its services (email → mail,
  calendar → calendar, files → files, docs, sheets).

## CT-81 `guides.act`, `connections.finishGoogle` and the guide refusals (AG-03, AG-08, AG-14) (2026-09-26)

- **`api.guides.act`** is `{id: 'guides.act', method: 'POST', path: '/burrows/:burrow/messages/:messageId/guide'}`
  and answers `OkResponse`.
  - The URL is AG-03's. The parameter is named `messageId` like every other message route.
  - The body is `GuideActBody {actionId, optionIds? 1…8, values?}`. `values` is a record of `GuideElementId` → string
    ≤ `GUIDE_VALUE_MAX` (8192, which fits a dropped client JSON), with at most `GUIDE_VALUES_MAX` (6) entries. The
    values are not trimmed.
- **Refusals** follow CT-21: a generic `ErrorCode` with `error.details.code`, the same over REST and over the session.
  `GUIDE_ERROR_STATUS` maps each code to its generic code, and `GuideErrorDetails` is `{code}`. The codes are
  `GuideErrorCode`, an open set in `APP_ERROR_CODES`:

  | Code | Generic code |
  |---|---|
  | `guide_closed` | `conflict` |
  | `not_yours` | `forbidden` |
  | `invalid_values` | `validation_failed`; `error.fields` is keyed by field id |
  | `google_admin_only` | `forbidden` |
  | `google_app_in_config` | `conflict` |
  | `google_unavailable` | `not_allowed` |

  The `google_*` codes are the refusals of the app guide's form, `saveGoogleApp` in chat. Those are the only Google
  failures `guides.act` can have.
- **`api.connections.finishGoogle`** is `{id: 'connections.finishGoogle', method: 'POST', path:
  '/me/connections/google/finish'}`.
  - The body is `FinishGoogleBody {code? ≤ 2048, state ≤ 200, error? ≤ 200}`. It is deliberately lenient: the server
    checks the state.
  - The answer is `FinishGoogleResponse {returnPath: ReturnLocation}`.
  - It is the browser callback's JSON twin, and it **always answers the return path** with
    `connected=google` or `connect_error=<ConnectErrorCode>` (`CONNECTED_PARAM`, `CONNECT_ERROR_PARAM`), exactly as
    the callback redirects. Consent failures (`access_denied`, `invalid_state`, `exchange_failed`, `no_app`) are
    therefore not HTTP or session errors, and there are no `google_*` codes for it.
  - With a guide marker in the path, the server has also posted the result or the troubleshooting in the DM (AG-08).
- **`ReturnPath` moves** to `domain/connectors.ts`. `contracts/connectors.ts` re-exports it, so imports are unchanged.
  `ReturnLocation` is the same rule at 1000 characters, which leaves room for the result parameters.
- **Managed redirect.** `managedGoogleRedirectPath = '/connect/google'` and `managedGoogleRedirectUri(appUrl)` are the
  hosted-UI route of AG-14. On a managed appliance, `googleSetupFacts.redirectUri` returns it.
- **Session.** Both are `api` ops, derived from `api`. `createOperationAllowlist()` includes them by default. A
  runtime that narrows its allowlist with `only` must name them.
  - Both are in `SECRET_API_OPS`: a guide form carries the Google client secret, and `finishGoogle` carries an
    authorization code. So there is no input digest in receipts and no logging, and a retry after a lost answer gets
    `unknown_outcome`.
  - `managed.google_connect` stays for a managed policy that turns Google off. Its text no longer says “yet”.

## CT-82 Assistant preferences, the `briefing` trigger and the assistant's tools (AG-09…AG-12, AG-18) (2026-09-26)

- **`Preferences.assistant?`** is `AssistantPreferences {suggestions: boolean (default true), dontAsk: GuideTopic[] ≤
  16 (default [])}`. `DEFAULT_ASSISTANT_PREFERENCES` holds the defaults. `dontAsk` takes open topics, so a newer
  topic survives a round trip. `me.updatePreferences` (a partial of `Preferences`) replaces `assistant` whole, so the
  client sends both members.
- **`DispatchTrigger`** gains `briefing`, and the owner is `causedById`. `PERSONAL_TRIGGERS` is the server's, not a
  contract.
- **The briefing.** `BriefingTime` is 24-hour `HH:MM` in the person's time zone. `BriefingDays` is `weekdays |
  every_day`, the two choices of AG-09, with `BRIEFING_DAYS_LABELS`. `BriefingSchedule {enabled, time, days,
  timeZone}` is what the agent sees.
- **MCP tools** (`contracts/mcp-guides.ts`, `GUIDE_MCP_TOOLS`, spread into `MCP_TOOLS`). Both need no key.
  - `start_guide({topic: StartableGuideTopic})` → `commitOutcome({messageId})`. The topics are welcome, email,
    calendar, files, briefing and google_app. `repair` stays the server's, because it follows a connection's
    state. The tool is in `MCP_POSTING_TOOLS`: the server posts the first card as the agent, which stamps `postedAt`,
    so a retried turn doesn't start the guide twice.
  - `briefing_set({enabled, time?, days?})` → `commitOutcome({briefing: BriefingSchedule})`. A missing `time` or
    `days` keeps the current value. A new briefing is 08:00 on weekdays.
- **Personal-agent-only tools.** `McpTool.personal?: boolean` marks both tools, next to `connector` for connector
  tools. There are also `mcpToolPersonalOnly(name)` and `PERSONAL_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES`.
  - `WHOMBAT_TOOL_NAMES` (every agent) no longer contains them.
  - A server that lists `MCP_TOOL_NAMES` itself must filter `mcpToolPersonalOnly` for agents that aren't personal,
    and refuse such calls.

## CT-83 Contracts 0.11.0 (guided setup in the assistant's DM, AG-01…AG-18) (2026-09-26)

0.11.0 is a minor release before 1.0, and every consumer moves to it together, as with CT-75 and CT-79. What each side
has to watch:

- **Breaks readers before 0.11.0:**
  - a message with a `guide` card. `MessageCard` is a closed union, so an older web or mobile client refuses the
    message, and a list or event that carries it. The server posts guide cards only once the clients it serves are on
    0.11.0. The server, the web app and the mobile app ship together.
  - a dispatch with trigger `briefing`: an older runner refuses it. The runner and the server ship together.
- **Tolerated both ways:**
  - `Preferences.assistant` (optional). An older server strips it from a PATCH, so an older server doesn't save the
    toggle.
  - the new endpoints and ops. An older server answers 404, and an older runtime answers `unknown_op`.
  - the new app error codes (an open set).
  - within 0.11 and later: unknown guide topics, block types and icons (CT-80).
- **Changed for consumers:**
  - `WHOMBAT_TOOL_NAMES` excludes the personal tools, so the server's tool list must filter `mcpToolPersonalOnly`.
  - `SECRET_API_OPS` gains `guides.act` and `connections.finishGoogle`.
- **Unchanged:** the session protocol version (1.0) and capabilities, the release tuple, the product manifest, the

Every package is 0.11.0.

  `PLAN_STEP_LABELS` holds the default words. `canvas-schema` `PLAN_STEP_STATES` and `PLAN_STATE_LABELS` follow.

  `createdAt`, `source {messageId, threadRootId}` and `messageId` (the card). All default to null, so stored plans and

  person's step in progress), `createCanvas`. Audit type `plan.created`.
- **`mergePlanEdits`** never removes a started step (it is kept; the server re-syncs the block).
- **MCP**: `plan_create`, `plan_update`, `plan_start_step` (key `tasks.create`), `plan_read` (read), `canvas_create`
  (`canvas.write`, optional `planId`), and `start_run.planStep`. `plan_create` and `plan_start_step` are posting tools.
- **`DispatchContext.planStep`** (`PlanStepContext`) tells the agent which step it was handed.

## CT-89 Contracts 0.12.1: routine bookkeeping folds, connector tools in plain words (Whombat WS-52, WS-54) (2026-09-26)

- `ROUTINE_WHOMBAT_TOOLS` (`run_step`, `run_log`, `run_files`, `set_status`, `read_conversation`, `canvas_read`,
  `plan_read`, `recall`, `read_attachment`): `describeActivity` marks their finished rows not important, and
  `collapseActivity` folds them with reads and searches (“Read 2 files and made 9 routine updates”). A failure or an
  interruption still stands out; decisions (`finish_run`, `request_approval`, posting) stay rows of their own. A live run
  wrote ~30 bookkeeping rows per turn, which buried its failures and made “Updated status” a finished run's latest row.

  calendar”), never what was searched or sent.

Every package is 0.12.1.

## CT-90 Contracts 0.12.2: images in messages (Whombat MPO-01) (2026-09-27)

- `Inline` gains `{ type: 'image'; alt; src }` for `![alt](src)` (also `(<src>)` and `(src "title")`, parentheses in
  the source balanced). `src` must pass `isSafeImageSrc`: `https://…`, `http://…`, or `data:image/(png|jpeg|gif|webp|
  svg+xml)[;charset=…][;base64],…` (mime case-insensitive, no whitespace or `<>"` in the URI). Anything else stays
  literal text as before (`![x](mailto:…)` is still a “!” and a link). Images are parsed before links, and an image
  inside a link (`[![CI](badge)](url)`) is that link's content.
- An SVG document an agent writes as a paragraph of its own (lines from `<svg` or an `<?xml` prolog to the `</svg>`
  that closes the root element and ends its line, blank lines and nested `<svg>` allowed, ≤ 256 KB) is a
  `{ type: 'code', lang: 'svg' }` block, and a fenced block in `xml`, `html` or no language holding just an SVG
  document gets `lang: 'svg'` (`SVG` too). No new block type, so an older client shows the code. Unclosed markup, or
  text after `</svg>` on its line, stays a paragraph.
- `@whombat/core/text` exports `isSafeImageSrc(src)`, `isSvgDocument(text)`, `svgImageDocument(text)` (the document
  with the SVG/xlink namespaces added when missing, for an SVG view such as react-native-svg) and
  `svgImageSrc(text)` (a percent-encoded `data:image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8,…` URI for `<img src>`, or null), and
  `SVG_IMAGE_MAX` (256 KB). An `svg` code block is shown as an image only when `svgImageSrc` accepts it. A DOCTYPE with
  an internal subset (entity definitions) is refused. Pure: no Buffer, btoa or DOM.
- Clients show images only through an image element (`<img>`, an RN image, an SVG view that runs no script), never
  as DOM; http(s) images are subject to the client's CSP and may show as a link where remote images are blocked.
- `plainMessageText`/`inlineText`: an image reads as its alt text, or `[image]`; an `svg` code block that is an image
  reads `[image]`.
- Patch release: `Inline` gains a member, so a renderer with an exhaustive switch needs a case; no schema, endpoint or
  protocol changes.

Every package is 0.12.2.

## CT-91 The encrypted feedback drop: `@whombat/core/feedback/drop` (Whombat feedback-drop FD-07 … FD-16) (2026-09-27)

- A new subpath, also re-exported from `@whombat/core/feedback` and the root. It imports no Zod at runtime (types only),
  so the widget frame can bundle it: `@noble/curves` (x25519, ed25519), `@noble/hashes` (sha256, HKDF) and WebCrypto
  AES-GCM. Base64url and UTF-8 are its own strict codecs (no Buffer, atob or TextDecoder).
- **HPKE** (RFC 9180 base mode, `DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256)` / `HKDF-SHA256` / `AES-128-GCM`) is composed as the RFC
  writes it: `deriveKeyPair`, `hpkeSetupBaseS(pkR, info, ikmE?)`, `hpkeSetupBaseR(enc, skR, info)`,
  `hpkeContextSeal/Open(ctx, seq, aad, data)`, `hpkeExport`, and the single-shot `hpkeSealBase`/`hpkeOpenBase`
  (sequence 0). The low-level functions exist so the whole of Appendix A.1.1 (key pairs, key schedule, six sequence
  numbers, three exports) is checked, not only sequence 0. The ephemeral key is always `DeriveKeyPair(ikmE)`, with 32
  random bytes unless the caller passes `ikmE` (vectors only). The all-zero DH output and low-order points are
  refused (`HpkeError` `invalid_key`).
- **Sealing and opening are async** (WebCrypto has no synchronous AES-GCM) and need `crypto.subtle`; without it they
  throw `HpkeError` `unsupported`, never a misleading `undecryptable`. Everything else (cards, fingerprints, headers,
  padding, the reference) is synchronous and runs in React Native too (noble needs `crypto.getRandomValues`, as for
  any key generation). No consumer seals or opens in React Native.
- `FeedbackDropError` codes are exactly the runtime's refusal codes for the crypto layer: `malformed`, `unknown_key`,
  `undecryptable`, plus `too_large` when sealing would exceed the card's `maxEnvelopeBytes`. An unknown version or suite
  is `malformed` (control answers `invalid` for all of them).
- Keys: `siteKeyFingerprint` (`fbk_` + 22), `dropKeyId` (`fdk_` + 16) accept bytes or base64url;
  `generateDropKeyPair`, `generateSiteSigningKey`, `siteSigningKeyOf(seed)`, `dropPublicKeyOf(sk)`. Lifecycle
  constants `FEEDBACK_DROP_KEY_ROTATE_S` (30 d), `FEEDBACK_DROP_KEY_RETAIN_S` (22 d), `FEEDBACK_CARD_REISSUE_S` (7 d).
- `feedbackReferenceFor(site, submissionId)`: FD-16's hash, each of the first 8 bytes mapped by its low 5 bits to
  `FEEDBACK_REFERENCE_ALPHABET` (now exported from `install.ts`, the alphabet `newFeedbackReference` uses).

## CT-92 Site cards (FD-10, FD-12) (2026-09-27)

- Zod in `domain/feedback.ts`: `FeedbackSiteKey`, `FeedbackDropKeyId`, `FeedbackDropSuite`, `FeedbackDropPublicKey`
  (43 base64url characters with canonical trailing bits), `FeedbackCanonicalOrigin` (a string `normalizeOrigin`
  leaves unchanged: a signed document is checked, never normalized), `FeedbackSiteCardLimits` (the bounds of
  `FeedbackLimits`, `maxEnvelopeBytes` up to the hard cap), `FeedbackSiteCard` (strict; `config` is
  `FeedbackPublicConfig`), `SignedFeedbackSiteCard` (strict, adds the ≤ 14-day lifetime check).
- `signSiteCard(card, seed)` refuses a malformed card, a `signingKey` that isn't the seed's, and a result above
  `FEEDBACK_CARD_MAX_BYTES`. `sig` is Ed25519 over the UTF-8 of `canonicalJson(card)`, base64url.
- `verifySiteCard(signed, expectedKey?, {site?, now?})` → `{ok, card} | {ok: false, error}`, in this order: `bad_card`
  (the shape as the Zod schema, exact members at every level, unique canonical origins, `issuedAt < expiresAt ≤
  issuedAt + 14 d`, `kid = dropKeyId(publicKey)`, key and signature lengths), `too_large` (UTF-8 of
  `canonicalJson({card, sig})` above 16 KiB: the size is of the signed document, as control stores it), `wrong_key`
  (pin), `wrong_site`, `bad_signature` (`verifyEd25519Strict`: ZIP-215-only signatures such as a small-order key with
  identity R and S = 0 are refused), `expired` (only with `now`; the frame passes none, FD-28). `config` is only checked
  to be an object: control and the runtime parse the card with `SignedFeedbackSiteCard`, the frame checks the config
  with its own checker as in direct mode. Member order of the received JSON doesn't matter; the signature covers the
  canonical form.

## CT-93 Envelope v1 (FD-14, FD-15) (2026-09-27)

- The AAD is the header bytes alone (not the `u16be` length before them; the header's canonical form fixes its length).
- `parseDropHeader(envelope)` → `{header, headerBytes, enc, ciphertext}` checks everything readable without a key, so
  control can refuse cheaply: `16 ≤ H ≤ 512`, the header is exactly `canonicalJson({kid, site, suite, v: 1})` (strict
  UTF-8, known suite, patterns), and the ciphertext length minus the tag is a padding bucket (≥ 4 KiB, `padLength(x) =
  x`). `encodeDropHeader` builds it.
- `openDropEnvelope(envelope, privateKeyFor, {site?})` checks in FD-23's order: framing and header (`malformed`), the
  key (`unknown_key`; `privateKeyFor` may be async), the AEAD (`undecryptable`), then the header's site and the padding
  (`malformed`). It returns the JSON text unparsed (the runtime runs `scanJsonShape` first).
- `encodeDropPlaintext`/`decodeDropPlaintext`: the padded length must be exactly `padLength(4 + L)` and the padding
  all zero.
- **Room for the wrapper.** The plaintext is `{v, submission, frame}`, slightly larger than the submission body the
  integration's cap is computed for. `dropEnvelopeCap(bodyCap) = 562 + padLength(4 + bodyCap + 4096)`
  (`FEEDBACK_DROP_WRAPPER_BYTES`; 562 = length prefix, longest header, `enc`, tag), so
  `FEEDBACK_DROP_MAX_ENVELOPE_BYTES = 33,817,138`. `FeedbackDropFrame` bounds the frame evidence well inside it:
  `bridgeOrigin` ≤ 255, `ancestorOrigins` ≤ 8 entries of ≤ 255 or null, `widget` `^[0-9A-Za-z.+-]{1,32}$`, `cardSeq`.
- `FeedbackDropPlaintext` (strict), `FeedbackDropHeader`, `FeedbackDropRefusalCode` (FD-23's codes plus `too_large` and
  `unsupported_attachment`, which the shared filing path can also give) and `FeedbackDropOutcome` (`filed`,
  `duplicate`, `refused` with a code).

## CT-94 Delivery device ops and manager paths (FD-19 … FD-21) (2026-09-27)

- `DEVICE_OPS` gains `feedback.cards.sync`, `feedback.drops.pull`, `feedback.drops.ack` (`device/feedback.ts`,
  `FEEDBACK_DEVICE_OPS`), Go `device.FeedbackCardsSyncRequest` … and `local.RuntimeFeedback*` aliases;
  `MANAGER_PATHS.feedbackCards|feedbackPull|feedbackAck` (`/v1/runtime/feedback/cards|pull|ack`).
- **The card is opaque in the device API** (`FeedbackCardWire {card: object, sig}`, Go `json.RawMessage`): a card holds
  free text (labels, paths, a privacy URL) the cross-language subset can't describe, and nothing in Go reads it. This is
  the one exception to CT-10's “no free text in device bodies”: the text is the owner's public widget configuration,
  signed by the runtime and published on purpose (FD-02). Canonical JSON over non-ASCII text agrees between Go and
  TypeScript; `signed.json` has such a request and Go re-signs it to the same signature.
- **Per-op request size.** 200 cards of up to 16 KiB don't fit `DEVICE_REQUEST_MAX_BYTES` (64 KiB):
  `deviceRequestMaxBytes(op)` (Go `DeviceRequestMaxBytesFor`) is `FEEDBACK_CARDS_SYNC_MAX_BYTES` (4 MiB) for
  `feedback.cards.sync` and 64 KiB for every other op; `verifyDeviceRequest` uses it.
- `feedback.cards.sync {seq, cards ≤ 200}` → `{accepted: site[], refused: [{index, site | null, code, seq?}]}`: a
  refusal names the card's position because a `bad_card` may have no readable site; `stale_seq` carries the seq control
  holds so a runtime whose counter is behind (a restored replacement) raises it and re-issues. The sync's own `seq` is
  the runtime's counter (≥ every card's, fresh for an empty set); a sync not above this device's last applied one
  changes nothing and refuses every card `stale_seq`.
- `feedback.drops.pull {max 1…20, maxBytes 1…47 MiB}` → `{drops, pending, expired ≤ 200, nextPullS 2…3600}`;
  `FeedbackDrop {dropId fdr_…, site, receivedAt (epoch s), origin, bytes, envelope (base64url)}`. `maxBytes` stops at
  47 MiB (not FD-20's 48) so the largest answer, 4/3 of it plus JSON, stays under `FEEDBACK_PULL_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES`
  (64 MiB), what the manager and runtime must accept (FD-21).
- `feedback.drops.ack {dropIds 1…100}` → `{ok: true}`.
- Constants (Go too): `FEEDBACK_DROP_TTL_S`, `FEEDBACK_DROP_LEASE_S` (120), `FEEDBACK_DROP_MAX_ENVELOPE_BYTES`,
  `FEEDBACK_CARD_MAX_BYTES`, `FEEDBACK_CARD_MAX_LIFETIME_S`, `FEEDBACK_CARDS_MAX`, `FEEDBACK_CARDS_SYNC_MAX_BYTES`,
  `FEEDBACK_PULL_MAX_DROPS`, `FEEDBACK_PULL_MIN_BYTES`, `FEEDBACK_PULL_MAX_BYTES`, `FEEDBACK_PULL_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES`,
  `FEEDBACK_PULL_BUSY_S` (2), `FEEDBACK_PULL_S` (30), `FEEDBACK_ACK_MAX`.
- Unsupported: an older control rejects the unknown op name as 400 `bad_envelope`; a control with the drop off answers
  404 with the new reason `feedback_drop_off`. The manager reports both as 501 `unsupported` for these paths.

## CT-96 Contracts 0.13.0 (the feedback drop) (2026-09-27)

A minor release; every consumer that uses the drop moves together (as CT-88).

- **Breaks readers before 0.13.0:** closed unions widened — `DeviceOpName` (three ops), `FeedbackHealthWarning.code`
  (four codes; only a managed runtime in drop mode sends them, and the hosted UI deploys first, FD order step 3).
- **Type-level:** `FeedbackIntegrationHealth`'s output type now has `delivery`: code that builds a health object adds
  `delivery: null` (the runtime's `read.ts`). `ControlEndpoint.status` widens to `200 | 201 | 202`.
- **Tolerated both ways:** the new optional snippet inputs, the defaulted `delivery`, the new schemas, endpoints,
  manager paths and constants. `verifyDeviceRequest` still refuses every other op above 64 KiB.
- **Tooling:** `buildVectors()` and `generate()` are async (sealing uses WebCrypto). New vector file
  `feedback-drop.json` (RFC 9180 A.1.1, envelopes per padding class with a fixed `ikmE`, tampered envelopes, cards incl.
  ZIP-215-only and non-canonical signatures, references, padding), three new `signed.json` device requests, schema
  cases for the new ops. Go gains no dependency.
- **Unchanged:** the session protocol, the release tuple, the product manifest and the licence.

Every package is 0.13.0.

## CT-98 Where an entry may connect (VT-10…VT-13, VT-59) (2026-09-27)

- **Addresses.** `parseIpv4` (strict dotted quad, no leading zeros), `parseIpv6` (every RFC 4291 form, an embedded IPv4
  tail, no zone id), `parseIp`, `ipv4MappedOf`, `formatIpv6` (RFC 5952). `classifyAddress` → `public|private|loopback|
  link_local|metadata|multicast|unspecified|reserved|documentation`; an IPv4-mapped address is classed as its IPv4.
  `addressIsPublic` mirrors the server's `isPublicAddress` range for range, and is stricter in four places the runtime
  should adopt: metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254, 169.254.170.2, 100.100.100.200, 168.63.129.16, fd00:ec2::254),
  IPv4-compatible `::/96`, and `3fff::/20` documentation space are never public.
- **The home network list.** `parseCidr` / `canonicalCidr` (a bare address is a /32 or /128; host bits are cleared, so
  `192.168.1.7/24` is `192.168.1.0/24`). `vaultNetworkProblem(cidr, ports)` → `{code, field, message}`: a network must lie
  inside 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 100.64/10 (shared space, Tailscale) or fc00::/7, be at most a /16 or /48, hold no
  metadata address (`100.100.0.0/16`, `fd00:ec2::/48` are refused), not be written as IPv4-mapped IPv6 (`mapped`), and
  list 1–16 different ports. Codes and copy in `VAULT_NETWORK_PROBLEM_TEXT`. `vaultNetworksFile(networks)` is VT-59's
  hand-over document (`{version: 1, networks}` sorted, ports ascending, no notes).
- **Entry URLs.** `parseVaultUrl` (no WHATWG `URL`): http or https, no credentials, query or fragment, a strict host
  (a name ending in a number such as `127.1` or `0x7f.0.0.1` is refused), a safe path (`vaultPathProblem`: no `.`/`..`,
  `//`, backslashes, encoded dots or slashes, broken escapes). It returns `origin`, `port`, `path` and `basePath` (the
  path without a trailing slash). `vaultEntryAddress` is the card's “host:port”.
- **Destinations.** `vaultDestinationProblem({url, resolved, networks, at})` → null or `{code, message, suggestion?}`:
  every address public → https only (`http_public`); any address loopback, link-local, metadata, multicast, reserved,
  documentation or unspecified → `never`; public and private at once → `mixed` (VT-12's “every address”); a private
  address outside a listed network with the port → `not_listed` with VT-13's copy and `suggestion {cidr, port}` (the
  listed network when only the port is missing, else the address's /24 or /64); no address → `unresolved`. With
  `at: 'call'` every refusal reads “This Vault entry’s address isn’t allowed any more.” The caller passes the addresses
  it will dial (DNS pinned), so rebinding can't slip past.

## CT-99 Safe requests and bridged tools (VT-40…VT-44) (2026-09-27)

- **`vault_request` paths.** `normaliseVaultPath(basePath, path)`: `path` is relative to the entry's base URL and
  appended to its base path (`https://api.example.com/v1` + `/users/7` → `/v1/users/7`), so it can't leave it; refused:
  no leading `/`, `?`/`#`, and everything `vaultPathProblem` refuses. `vaultRequestQuery` encodes the query (RFC 3986)
  and refuses the parameter a `query` entry signs in with; `vaultRequestTarget` composes origin, path and query;
  `vaultRequestWhat` is the use's `METHOD /path` without the query.
- **Headers.** `vaultRequestHeaders(agentHeaders, auth)` → `{headers, refused}`: `Accept`, `Content-Type`,
  `If-None-Match`, `If-Modified-Since`, `Prefer`, `X-Requested-With` and `X-*` except the entry's own header, values
  without line breaks or control characters, canonical capitalisation. A call with anything refused is refused
  (`vaultRefusedHeadersText`), not sent without it.
- **Credentials.** `vaultCredential(auth, secret)` → the header to add last (`Bearer`, the named header, `Basic` of
  `username:password`) or the query pair to append (`withCredentialQuery`); `vaultBase64` is a pure UTF-8 base64.
- **Responses.** `filterVaultResponseHeaders(headers, base, requestPath?)` keeps `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`,
  `ETag`, `Last-Modified`, `Retry-After`, `Link`, `X-RateLimit-*`, and `Location` only when it stays under the base
  (same origin; a relative reference resolves against the request path's directory), else `"elsewhere"`.
- **Scrubbing.** `scrubSecret(text, secret, username?)` and `scrubSecretDeep(value, …)` replace every form in
  `vaultSecretForms` with `[secret]`: the value, its URL encodings (upper- and lowercase escapes, `+` for spaces), its
  JSON-escaped form, standard and URL-safe base64 with and without padding, and a login's `username:password` base64.
  Short secrets are scrubbed too, whatever that costs the output.
- **Failures.** `VAULT_FAILURES` `timeout|unreachable|too_large|not_allowed|protocol|tool_error|busy|invalid_request`
  with `VAULT_FAILURE_TEXT` (“It didn’t answer within 30 seconds.”, “Couldn’t reach it.”) and `vaultStatusText`
  (“The server answered 401.”). The remote side's words are never quoted.
- **Bridged tools.** `vaultEntryKey(entryId)`: 8 lowercase letters, each of the first 8 bytes of
  `sha256("whombat-vault-entry-key:" + id)` mod 26. `vaultToolMcpName(key, tool)` → `vt_<key>__<tool>` or null when the
  whole name doesn't fit `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$` (51 characters are left for the tool); `parseVaultToolMcpName`,
  `isVaultToolName`, `isVaultActivityTool` (any runner prefix). `vaultToolDescription(owner, entry, remote)`: “From
  Mara’s Vault entry “Home Assistant”: ” + the server's text with line breaks as spaces, other control characters,
  bidirectional overrides and BOMs removed, ≤ 1 000 characters. `vaultToolHash` covers name, title, description, input
  and output schemas and annotations (canonical JSON). `mergeVaultTools(key, stored, listed, firstCheck)` applies VT-44:
  the first check turns everything on; later an unchanged hash keeps its switch and badge, a new or changed tool is off
  with “New”, a gone tool goes, a repeated name keeps its first, and tools beyond 64 are counted as `ignored`.

- `EVENT_TYPES`: `vault.entry.added|changed|secret_replaced|removed`, `vault.key.given|changed|taken`, `vault.used`
  (Vault) and `vault.refused` (Blocked). Asking and deciding are the approval events with VT-51's texts.
- `AuditEvent.vault` (`AuditVaultDetail {entryId, entryName, what | null, outcome | null}`), optional, outside the signed
  envelope, filled only for the entry's owner. `auditFields` adds a `VAULT` row with `vaultAuditDetailText`;
  `AUDIT_CSV_COLUMNS` gains a trailing `vault` column for everyone, filled only on the owner's rows. The pill is
  unchanged (`BLOCKED` for `vault.refused`, none for Vault rows).

## CT-104 Managed mode and fixtures (VT-58, VT-70) (2026-09-27)

- `SECRET_API_OPS` gains `vault.create` and `vault.setSecret` (no input digest, no stored result, `unknown_outcome` on a
  replay); the conformance list follows and `vectors/session.json` (and Go's copy) are regenerated. Every other Vault
  op is ordinary and allowlisted by default; `vaultNetworks.*` are account-level ops. `docs/session-protocol.md` has

## CT-105 Contracts 0.14.0 (the Vault) (2026-09-27)

A minor release; every consumer that uses the Vault moves together (as CT-88, CT-96).

- **Breaks readers before 0.14.0:** closed unions widened —
  - `AuditKind` (`Vault`): an older client refuses an audit page or `audit.appended` frame that holds a Vault event;
  - `RealtimeEvent` (`vault.updated`);
  - `ApprovalAction` (`vault_use`, with `keyId: null`): an older client refuses the approval, its card and its frames;
  - `DispatchTrigger` (`vault_pass`): an older runner refuses the dispatch;
  - `AuditKindFilter` (`vault`): an older server refuses `kind=vault`.

  The server, the web app, the mobile app and the runner ship together.
- **Type-level:** `Approval.keyId` is nullable and `actionKey(ApprovalAction)` may answer null (the server's “keys still
  turn” check skips `vault_use`, and its `approvals.key_id` column must allow null); `SessionParts` requires `vault`;
  `PackSecretView`'s output has the four binding fields; `AuditCounts` has `vault`; `request_approval` and
  `perform_action` take `AgentApprovalAction`; `ApprovalView` has `declineCta`; `AUDIT_CSV_COLUMNS` ends with `vault`.
- **Tolerated both ways:** the new endpoints (an older server answers 404, an older runtime `unknown_op`), the new
  refusal codes (an open set), the optional `DispatchContext.vault`, `AuditEvent.vault` and `Approval.vault`, the
  defaulted `PackSecretView` fields and `AuditCountsSchema.vault`, the new MCP tool (the server lists tools).
- **Tooling:** the conformance secret-op list and the regenerated `session.json` vectors (TypeScript and Go). No schema
  or other vector changes.
- **Unchanged:** the session protocol version and capabilities, the release tuple, the product manifest, the licence and
  the Go module's API.

Every package is 0.14.0.

## CT-106 Plans, the Billing view and the billing endpoints (Whombat billing.md BL-01, BL-02, BL-11, BL-13, BL-15…BL-18) (2026-09-27)

- **Plans.** `PlanId` (`^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$`, the same shape `Entitlement.plan` always had, which now uses it; `none` is
  an entitlement's “waiting for a plan” and has no row). `Plan {id, name (PlanName, 1…64), amountCents (0…100,000,000),
  currency 'eur', interval 'month', limits: EntitlementLimits, selfInstall, public}`. `SignupPlan` is `Plan` without
  `selfInstall` and `public`, exactly BL-25's list.
- **`BillingView`** for `billing.view` (`GET /orgs/:org/billing`, any member): `org`, `provider`, `plan {id, name} |
  null`, `state`, `trialEndsAt`, `currentPeriodEnd`, `cancelAtPeriodEnd`, `whombats {claimed, paid}` (`paid` =
  `devicesAllowed`), `setupRequired`, `trialAvailable`, `manual`, `canManage`.
  - `plan` is **null while waiting for a plan** (`setupRequired`), rather than `{id: 'none', name: …}`: the UI shows
    plan cards then, and there is no name to show.
  - `trialEndsAt` is set only while trialing and equals `currentPeriodEnd` then (BL-16 stores the trial end as the
    period end); it saves the UI a state check.
  - `org` is included like `Entitlement.org`.
- **Endpoints** (all `auth: 'session'`, bodies strict):
  - `billing.checkout` `POST /orgs/:org/billing/checkout {plan, whombats 1…50}` → `BillingRedirect {url}`;
  - `billing.portal` `POST /orgs/:org/billing/portal {}` → `{url}`;
  - `billing.whombats` `POST /orgs/:org/billing/whombats {count 1…50}` → `BillingView` (applied at once);
  - `billing.startNow` `POST /orgs/:org/billing/start-now {}` → `BillingView`.
  - `billing.entitlement` is unchanged.
- `BillingRedirect.url` is `http(s)://` printable ASCII, ≤ 2,048 characters (Stripe's Checkout URLs are long and carry
  a fragment); `http` only so a local Stripe fake works. The client navigates to it and nothing else.
- **The Stripe webhook** (`POST /v1/billing/stripe/webhook`, BL-16) is control-internal: Stripe is its only client, the
  body is Stripe's raw JSON verified by signature, and nothing Whombat builds calls it. It is not in `controlApi` and
  has no schema here.

## CT-107 Signups: the signup info, the waitlist, signup codes and terms at org creation (BL-21…BL-25) (2026-09-27)

- `SignupMode` = `open | waitlist | invite`; `BillingProviderName` = `manual | stripe`; `TrialDays` 1…60.
- **`SUBSCRIPTION_TERMS_VERSION = '2026-09-27-draft'`** and `SubscriptionTerms {version: TermsVersion}` (strict), the
  pattern of `APPLIANCE_TERMS_VERSION` (CT-78): the schema accepts any well-formed version and control refuses every
  one but the current one with `terms_outdated` (409); a missing `terms` is a schema failure (400).
- **`orgs.create`** takes `CreateOrgBody {name, terms, code?}` (strict).
- **Codes.**
  - `SIGNUP_CODE_ALPHABET` is Crockford base32.
  - `normaliseSignupCode(input)` → the 8 canonical characters without the dash, or null. It upper-cases, removes every
    whitespace character and dash, maps O→0 and I/L→1, then requires exactly 8 alphabet characters (so U and anything
    else fails). Input over 64 characters is null. It is idempotent, and **control hashes the canonical form**.
  - `formatSignupCode` → `XXXX-XXXX`.
  - `SignupCodeInput` (what `orgs.create` accepts) is an already normalised code with or without the dash. It is not a
    transform: the client sends `normaliseSignupCode`'s or `formatSignupCode`'s output, and control normalises again
    before hashing. A raw lower-case code is a schema failure, which tells a client that forgot to normalise.
  - `SignupCodeDisplay` is the dashed form and `SignupCodeHint` the last 4 characters.
- **Public endpoints** (`auth: 'none'`, like `auth.requestMagicLink`), in `controlApi.signup`:
  - `signup.info` `GET /signup` → `SignupInfo {mode, billing, trialDays, termsVersion, plans: SignupPlan[] ≤ 20}`;
  - `signup.waitlist` `POST /waitlist` `WaitlistBody {email, company? (trimmed, 1…120), note? (trimmed, 1…500)}` →
    `{ok: true}` with 200, for a repeat as well.

## CT-108 Billing and signup refusals (BL-13, BL-15…BL-18, BL-21, BL-23, BL-27, BL-28) (2026-09-27)

- `CONTROL_REASONS` stays an open set and gains:
  - from the spec: `billing_setup_required` (403), `trial_used_device` (409), `subscription_exists` (409),
    `subscription_live` (409), `manual_billing` (409), `signup_code_required` (403), `signup_code_invalid` (403),
    `terms_outdated` (409), `waitlist_closed` (409);
  - decided here: `no_subscription` (409: no Stripe customer or subscription for the portal, the Whombats change,
    start-now, cancel or sync), `not_trialing` (409: start-now, trial extension), `plan_unavailable` (400: checkout for
    an unknown or non-public plan), `plan_not_found` (404, operator), `whombats_below_claimed` (409: BL-18's “≥ the
    number of claimed Whombats”), `billing_provider_error` (502 with `error.code: 'internal'`: Stripe refused or
    didn't answer), `invalid_credentials` (401: panel sign-in), `operator_session_invalid` (401),
    `panel_header_required` (403: CSRF), `account_not_found`, `waitlist_entry_not_found`, `signup_code_not_found`
    (404) and `waitlist_entry_not_waiting` (409).
- Every endpoint's summary names its refusals.
- **`ControlErrorBody.error.details`** gains two optional members:
  - `canStartNow: boolean`, with `trial_used_device` (BL-17);
  - `allowed: 0…10,000` (the plan's `devicesAllowed`), with `devices_allowed_reached`. BL-18's “entitlement_withheld
    with details.allowed” is the coarse code `entitlement_withheld` with this reason.

  Before this, `details` was `{code}` and a reader stripped anything else, so the UI lost `canStartNow`.

## CT-109 The operator panel and the customer API (BL-27…BL-29) (2026-09-27)

- **Auth.** `auth: 'operator'` means an operator bearer token on the operator listener, or the `wb_op` panel session
  cookie plus `X-Whombat-Panel: 1` on non-GET requests on the panel listener. Both listeners serve the same endpoints.
  - **Sign-in is a username and a password** (John, 2026-09-27, replacing BL-27's operator token), from an address on
    control's panel IP allowlist. `operator.signIn` is `POST /operator/session` with `OperatorSignInBody {username
    (OperatorUsername, ^[a-z0-9._-]{1,64}$), password (1…256, never trimmed)}`. It is `auth: 'none'`, because the
    body carries the credential, as with `auth.verify`, and it works on the panel listener only.
  - It refuses `invalid_credentials` (401, the same answer for an unknown username and a wrong password) and
    `rate_limited` (429).
  - A caller outside the allowlist gets a **bare 403** on every panel request. It has no `ControlErrorBody` and no
    reason, and the panel shows it as “not allowed from this network”.
  - `operator.session` (GET) answers `OperatorSession {operator, username, permissions}`; for a bearer token,
    `username` is the operator id. `operator.signOut` (DELETE) answers `{ok}`.
  - There is no `via`, expiry or Access identity in the answer. The first draft of this entry had a Cloudflare Access
    `via` and an `access_required` reason, which were dropped with the token sign-in. Control keeps any Access check
    to itself.
  - Constants: `OPERATOR_SESSION_COOKIE = 'wb_op'`, `OPERATOR_PANEL_HEADER = 'X-Whombat-Panel'` and
    `OPERATOR_SESSION_TTL_S = 43200`.
- **Permissions.** `OPERATOR_PERMISSIONS` lists what control knows, the nine existing ones plus `customers.read`,
  `customers.write`, `signup.write`, `plans.write` and `settings.write`. `OperatorPermission` is that enum, for
  `operators.json`. Answers use `OperatorPermissionName`, an open dotted lower-case name, so an older panel doesn't
  refuse a newer control's session. Reads (overview, orgs, accounts, settings, waitlist, codes, plans) need
  `customers.read`.
- `OperatorId` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`, what `operators.json` allows) is the operator in sessions. It also
  replaces `Ident` in `OperatorAuditEvent.operator`, which refused an id with a dot. This widens that type.
- **Paging.** `Page(item)` = `{items, next}` with an opaque `cursor` query. Orgs and accounts are newest first, 50 per
  page. The waitlist is a queue, oldest first, 100 per page. Codes are newest first, 100 per page. Every date is
  `EpochSeconds`, unlike the older `Org.createdAt`.
- **Customers.**
  - `OperatorOverview {at, accounts {total, new7d, new30d}, orgs {total, byState (every state), byPlan, waitingForPlan},
    trialsEndingSoon, waitlistWaiting, whombats {claimed, seen24h}}`.
  - `OperatorOrgRow {org, name, ownerEmail, createdAt, plan, planName, state, provider, trialEndsAt,
    currentPeriodEnd, whombats {claimed, allowed}, lastSeenAt, flags {sameNetworkAs: OrgRef[] ≤ 10,
    trialEndedEarly}}`, with the query `{q?, state?, plan?, cursor?}`.
  - `OperatorOrgDetail` = the row plus `members`, `devices`, `entitlement`, `billing {stripeCustomerId,
    stripeSubscriptionId, customerUrl, subscriptionUrl, cancelAtPeriodEnd}`, `trialMarks` and `terms` (≤ 100 each), and
    `audit` (≤ 50).
  - Trial marks show `{kind, label, createdAt, alsoUsedBy}`. The label is the account's email or the device id. **The
    card fingerprint and the network tag are never sent** (label null).
  - Every org action (`extendTrial {days 1…30}`, `setPlan {plan, whombats 0…10,000, state?}`, `cancelSubscription {at:
    now|period_end}`, `syncBilling {}`) answers the fresh `OperatorOrgDetail`, so the panel replaces its state
    without a second call.
  - `OperatorAccountRow {account, email, name, createdAt, orgs (with role), lastSignInAt, disabled}`. `disableAccount`
    and `enableAccount` (`{}`, idempotent) answer the row.
- **Settings.** `ControlSettings {signupMode, selfRegistration, feedbackDrop (a boolean; control maps it to
  `FEEDBACK_DROP`'s on/off), trialDays}`. `PUT` takes `ControlSettingsUpdate`: partial, strict and not empty. Absent
  members keep their value, so two operators changing different settings don't overwrite each other.
- **Waitlist.** `WaitlistEntry {id, email, company, note, status, createdAt, invitedAt, codeHint, sameNetworkAs}`, with
  the query `{status?, cursor?}`. `approveWaitlist` and `removeWaitlist` (`{}`) answer the entry. The code an approval
  creates is only emailed; the panel never sees it.
- **Signup codes.**
  - `SignupCode {id, hint, note, plan, whombats, maxUses, uses, expiresAt, createdBy, createdAt, revokedAt,
    waitlistEntryId, status}`. `status` (`active|used|expired|revoked`) is derived by control, revoked winning over
    expired over used. `createdBy` is the operator, or `waitlist` for an approval. A listed `note` may be up to 500
    characters (control writes the note of an approval's code), while an operator types at most 200.
  - `createSignupCode` (201) takes `{note 1…200, plan?, whombats? 1…1,000, maxUses? 1…1,000, expiresInDays? 1…365}`
    and answers `CreatedSignupCode`, which is the code plus `code` (`XXXX-XXXX`) and `link`. This is the only answer
    that holds the code. The defaults are 30 days, 1 Whombat and 1 use. `whombats` only matters with a plan.
  - `revokeSignupCode` is idempotent and answers the code.
- **Plans.** `OperatorPlan` = `Plan` plus `sort`, `stripeLookupKey`, `stripePriceId` (null before `stripe:setup`) and
  `updatedAt`. `updatePlan` (`PUT /operator/plans/:plan`) takes `PlanUpdate {name?, amountCents?, limits? (partial,
  null = unlimited), public?}`, which is strict and not empty. The currency, interval and id can't change.

## CT-110 Contracts 0.15.0 (accounts, signups, trials and Stripe; BL-01…BL-30) (2026-09-27)

A minor release. Control and the hosted UI move together; the new admin app ships with them.

- **Breaks readers and writers before 0.15.0:**
  - `orgs.create` **requires `terms`** (strict body). A client before 0.15.0 can't create an org against a 0.15
    control, and a 0.15 client sends `terms` and `code`, which an older control refuses. The hosted UI and control ship
    together.
- **Type-level:**
  - `OperatorAuditEvent.operator` widens from `Ident` to `OperatorId`;
  - `ControlErrorBody.error.details` has two optional members;
  - `Entitlement.plan` is the named `PlanId` (the same schema).
- **Tolerated both ways:**
  - the new endpoints (an older control answers 404; the UI hides Billing when `GET /signup` is 404);
  - the new refusal codes (an open set; the Android app only has to fall back to `error.code`) and the optional
    `details` members;
  - the open permission names in `OperatorSession`.
- **Operator panel sign-in** is username and password (CT-109), so `OperatorSignInBody` has no `token`. Bearer tokens on
  the operator listener are unchanged.
- **Strict at the top level:** every new request body (`CreateOrgBody`, `WaitlistBody`, the billing and operator
  bodies, `ControlSettingsUpdate`, `PlanUpdate`). A newer member needs a contracts release.
- **Tooling:** none. The control API isn't in the cross-language registry, so there are no schema, vector or Go
  changes.
- **Unchanged:** the appliance, the runtime and the device API (`DEVICE_OPS`, the manager paths), the session protocol
  version and capabilities, the licence token and `EntitlementState`, the release tuple and the product manifest.

Every package is 0.15.0.

## CT-111 Contracts 0.15.1: operators delete an org or an account (control BL-31, BL-32) (2026-09-27)

John asked to be able to remove organizations and users from the admin panel, on dev and prod.

- `operator.deleteOrg` (`POST /operator/orgs/:org/delete`, `customers.write`): body `DeleteOrgBody {name}`, the org's
  name as a typed confirmation; answers `OperatorOrgDeleted {ok, devicesReleased}`. Refusals `org_not_found`,
  `name_mismatch`, `subscription_live`.
- `operator.deleteAccount` (`POST /operator/accounts/:account/delete`, `customers.write`): body
  `OperatorDeleteAccountBody {email}`; answers `OperatorAccountDeleted {ok, orgsLeft, orgsDeleted, devicesReleased}`.
  Refusals `account_not_found`, `email_mismatch`, `last_owner`, `subscription_live`.
- POST with a `/delete` suffix, like the other operator actions (`/disable`, `/revoke`), rather than a DELETE with a
  body.
- A patch release: only additions (an older control answers 404 to the new endpoints; the panel ships with control).
  No schema, vector or Go changes; the runtime, relay, device API and licence are unchanged.

Every package is 0.15.1.

## CT-112 Contracts 0.15.2: the Appliance Terms version `2026-09-27-draft` (appliance LC-20) (2026-09-27)

John asked for full Appliance Terms next to a new Terms of Service. The rewritten draft
(`appliance/docs/legal/appliance-terms.md`) keeps every commitment of `2026-09-26-draft` and adds the licence
check's numbers, updates, hardware, the keys only the customer holds, agents and AI providers, resets, and warranty
and liability. LC-18 says a change of the terms is a new id, so `APPLIANCE_TERMS_VERSION` is `2026-09-27-draft`.

- Control accepts only the new id in `claims.start` (`terms_required` otherwise), so control and the clients that

## CT-113 Contracts 0.16.0: handoffs, structured delegation between people and agents (Whombat delegation DG-01…DG-27) (2026-09-27)

Whombat's `docs/decisions/delegation.md` makes a handoff a plan step with a brief, an owner, a lane (its own thread),
limits and a typed result. The contracts carry the shapes and the pure rules, so the server and both prompt builders
decide the same way.

- **Plan steps.** `PlanStep.handoff: PlanHandoff | null` (default `null`, so every stored plan parses unchanged):
  `brief`, `deliverable`, `outputSchema` (a JSON Schema object), `dueAt`, `budget {tokens?, minutes?}`,
  `delegatedById`, `delegatedAt`, `laneRootId`, `depth` (1…2), `parentStepId`, `result {status: done|blocked|declined,
  summary, data, dataDropped, messageId, at}`, `declineReason`, and `used {tokens, reported}` (resolved when read,
  like `refs`). Limits are constants: `HANDOFF_MAX_DEPTH` 2, `HANDOFF_OPEN_PER_PLAN` 8, `HANDOFF_PER_TURN` 4,
  `HANDOFF_LANE_AGENT_TURNS` 12, brief 2 000, deliverable 500, summary 2 000, schema 8 KB, data 16 KB, and the
  default budgets `HANDOFF_TOKENS_DEFAULT` 2 M and `HANDOFF_PLAN_TOKENS_DEFAULT` 10 M.
- **Rules** (`domain/handoff.ts`, pure): `decideHandoff` (depth, cycles up the chain, one plan per chain, busy owners,
  8 open per plan, 4 per turn, 30 steps, the plan's token cap, licence, readiness, workspace; refusal codes
  `HandoffRefusalCode` with `handoffRefusalText`), `handoffOpen` / `handoffAcceptsReport` / `handoffAwaitingResult`,
  `handoffAncestors`, `checkOutputSchema` and `validateHandoffResult` (a checked subset of JSON Schema; unknown
  keywords are refused rather than ignored), `laneAgentTurns` / `laneAllowsTurn`, `projectHandoffStep` (finished work
  waits for the owner's report; a turn that ended without one is “Replied”; a recorded result is final), the copy
  (`handoffLaneText`, `handoffRetryText`, `handoffNudgeText`, `handoffReportText`, `handoffResultStep`,
  `HANDOFF_STOP_LABELS`, `handoffStopNote`, `formatHandoffDue`, `formatTokens`), readiness (`TeammateReadyCode`,
  `readyReasonText`) and `HANDOVER_KEYS` / `handoverLabels`.
- **Step actions.** `PlanStepAction` gains `open_lane`, `ask_for_report` and `report_back`; `planStepActions` gives a
  handoff step its lane's actions. A closed union widens, so web, mobile and the runtime move together (CT-83).
- **Dispatches.** `DispatchTrigger` gains `handoff` (the owner's turn in the lane) and `handoff_result` (the delegating
  agent woken by a report or a stop).
- **Runner context.** `DispatchContext.teammates: Teammate[]` (≤ 40, default `[]`): id, kind, name, handle, role,
  title, job, status, doing, `here`, `ready` with `readyCode` / `readyReason`, `can` (≤ 8) and `asks` (≤ 4) handover
  key labels, `skills` (≤ 12), `workdir`, `openHandoffs`. `DispatchContext.handoff: HandoffContext` (the owner's or
  the delegator's turn in the lane, `as`) and `DispatchContext.handoffResult: HandoffResultContext` (what came back,
  with the plan's thread and source). Optional, so older runners and servers keep working.
- **MCP.** `delegate` (key `tasks.create`; input `DelegateBody`; answers `ok {planId, stepId, laneRootId,
  dispatchId}`, the commit outcomes, or `refused {code, reason}`) and `report_back` (no key; `{stepId, planId?,
  status: done|blocked|declined|progress, summary, data?}`; answers `ok {planId, stepId, messageId}`, the commit
  outcomes, or `invalid {problems}`). Both are posting tools (`MCP_POSTING_TOOLS`); activity copy “Handed work over”,
  “Reported back”.
- **REST.** `plans.delegate` (`POST /burrows/:burrow/plans/delegate`, 201 `DelegateResponse`; a refusal is 409
  `conflict` with `details HandoffRefusal`), `plans.reportBack` (`POST …/steps/:stepId/report`, bad data is 400 with
  `details {problems}`), `plans.askReport` (`POST …/steps/:stepId/ask-report`). Retry, Reassign and Cancel stay
  `plans.startStep` and `plans.updateStep`.
- **Work view.** `WorkItem.handoff: WorkHandoff | null` (default `null`) and `WorkAction` `ask_for_report`.

## CT-116 Contracts 0.17.0: the console file carries the burrows (appliance CG-08) (2026-09-27)

John wants the graphical console of a claimed box to show the burrow's name, “+ N more burrows” when the box holds
more than one, and wombat facts (`appliance/docs/decisions/console-gui.md`, CG-08). The console knows nothing
but the console file, so the runtime puts the names there.

- `ConsoleState.burrows` (`ConsoleBurrows {first, more}`), optional, **only in `claimed`** (`consoleStateValid`, Go
  `ConsoleStateValid`): `first` is the name of the oldest live burrow, `more` the number of the other live burrows
  (0…9999). The runtime leaves it out when there is no burrow. A `claimed` file without it stays valid, so a runtime
  older than 0.17 still passes, and an older console strips the member (the schema is tolerant, CC-08).
- `first` is `ConsoleDisplayText`: 1–64 code points, no control (Cc), format (Cf: bidi overrides like U+202E,
  zero-width characters like U+200B, the BOM), surrogate (Cs) or separator (Z: U+2028, U+2029 and every space) except
  U+0020, and no space at either end. Burrow names are user input in any script, so ASCII (the rule for every other
  console string) is not an option; the refused categories are exactly what could move the cursor, reorder or hide
  text, or break the line on tty1 or in the kiosk. The ConsoleState doc comment's “printable ASCII” sentence now
  carves `burrows.first` out and says consumers must still strip control and format characters themselves (defence
  in depth: their Unicode tables may be newer than the validator's) and render the name as text only.
- The cross-language subset admits this one Unicode pattern by name (`CONSOLE_DISPLAY_TEXT_RE`, flag `u`,
  `conformance/src/subset.ts`). It carries its length in the pattern because `.min`/`.max` count UTF-16 units in Zod
  and code points in JSON Schema; a string with it may not also carry `.min`/`.max`. The general category tables of
  ECMAScript (Node 24, Unicode 17) and Go RE2 (Go 1.26, Unicode 15) agree today for these categories; rather than
  assume it, `local.json` → `displayText` lists every code point the pattern refuses on its own and the Go test
  compiles the pattern with RE2 and compares all of them (surrogates aside). A toolchain update that moves a code
  point fails the test.
- The name is local only: the runtime never sends it to control or the relay (managed-runtime MR-78).
- Version: 0.16.0 is reserved by the handoffs work (CT-113…CT-115), which is not on main yet. This release is built
  from main without it, so 0.17.0 does not contain handoffs; the handoffs release that lands after it takes the next
  version.

A minor release: an additive member and one new schema, with schema, vector and Go changes (`ConsoleBurrows`,
`ConsoleState.Burrows`, `ConsoleStateValid`).

Every package is 0.17.0.

## CT-117 Contracts 0.18.0: handoffs and the console's burrows together, after the delegation reviews (2026-09-27)

0.16.0 (CT-113…CT-115, handoffs) and 0.17.0 (CT-116, the console file's burrows) were released side by side from
`3327cae`; neither contains the other. 0.18.0 is both, so every consumer moves to one version. Changes to handoffs
since 0.16.0, from Whombat delegation's security and product reviews:

- **No `pattern` in output schemas.** `validateHandoffResult` ran the delegator's regular expression on the owner's
  data inside the commit, under the burrow lock; `^(a+)+$` against 40 characters backtracks for hours (security F1).
  `checkOutputSchema` now refuses `pattern` like any keyword Whombat can't check. `required` checks own properties
  (`toString` isn't always present).
- **Actions** (`planStepActions` for handoff steps): a declined handoff offers Reassign before Retry; `mark_done` joins
  `report_back` on unfinished handoffs (clients offer `report_back` to the owner, `mark_done` and `ask_for_report` to
  everyone else); a gate waiting on a linked approval, run or automation run offers no Retry (it would unlink it).
- **Copy**: a declined step's note is the owner's reason alone (the label says “Declined”); `handoffReportText` doesn't
  lead with “I can’t take this.” when the summary already says so; `handoffLaneText` takes `ownerKind`, and a person's
  lane ends “When it’s done, use Report back on the plan.”; the budget stop's note says what Retry does.

A minor release: additions and copy; no schema, vector or Go change beyond 0.17.0's. Every package is 0.18.0.

## CT-121 The content scan (skills-library.md SL-08) (2026-09-28)

`scanPackContent(files: {path, text}[]) → PackScan {verdict: safe | caution | dangerous, findings}` in
`packs/scan.ts`, pure; a finding is `{category: exfiltration | injection | destructive | persistence, severity: caution
| dangerous, path, line, excerpt, message}`. `validatePack` runs it over every UTF-8 text file of the pack (the
manifest, instructions, SKILL.md, skill files and unused files; binary files are skipped), puts `scan` in its success
result, turns a `dangerous` verdict into a problem with the new code `scan` (`scanRefusalText`: the first three
dangerous findings “path line n: message”, then “(and n more)”) and carries `scan` on the failure too when it got that
far. `scanSkillProposal({name, description, body, files})` scans a proposal with the same rules (its SKILL.md is the
front matter from the name and description plus the body).

Decided here (the header of `scan.ts` is the reference):

- **Severities.** `dangerous` is what would harm or leak if an agent ran it as written and a skill has no good reason
  to do: every instruction-injection phrase (ignore/disregard/forget previous or your instructions, another identity
  without rules, asking for or replacing the system prompt, getting around approvals, keys, sandboxes or the scan,
  hiding actions from people), imitated chat delimiters (`<|im_start|>`, `[INST]`, `<<SYS>>`) and Whombat's own
  (`[[pack`, `[[memory`, `[[web`, `[[vault`, `[[untrusted`, `[[handoff`, `[[assessment`, `[[skill`, any `[[/…]]`,
  `<system>`/`</system>`), Unicode tag characters and bidi controls, a secret, the environment or a credential file on
  a network call, the environment piped into one, DNS exfiltration, paste and request-capture sites, a decoded payload
  run, `rm -r` of `/`, `~`, `$HOME`, `*` or a system folder (or `--no-preserve-root`), `mkfs`, `dd of=/dev/…`, disk
  tools on `/dev`, `chmod -R … /`, fork bombs, `find / … -delete`, writing `authorized_keys`, cron, systemd units,
  launch agents and autostart entries, `curl | sudo sh`. `caution` has legitimate uses and is shown, not refused:
  `rm -r` of an absolute, `..` or variable path, force pushes, `DROP TABLE` / `TRUNCATE`, base64 runs of 200+ and hex
  runs of 128+ characters (inline images excepted), a lone `curl | sh`, shell rc edits, git hooks, chat webhooks,
  invisible characters (zero-width space, word joiner, a BOM inside the text), “don’t tell the user”, the word
  “jailbreak”. The verdict is the worst severity found.
- **Code and prose.** Code blocks count. Every line of a file that isn't prose is code; in prose files (Markdown, text,
  and the manifest, whose strings are descriptions) fenced blocks are code and everything else, inline code spans
  included, is prose. In prose the exfiltration, destructive and persistence rules find at most `caution`: “never run
  rm -rf /” explains, and a security pack may describe what it audits. Injection, hidden Unicode and delimiters are
  judged the same in prose and code, with two exceptions for honest skills: an injection phrase inside quotation marks
  (“…”, "…", ‘…’, «…») is mentioned, not said, and is `caution` (anti-injection skills quote what to refuse; inline
  code is not a quotation), and hiding actions from people (“without telling the user”) doesn't count after a negation
  earlier in the same sentence (“Never delete a file without telling the user.”). Phrases common in honest skills are
  left out on purpose (“ignore previous context”, “get around filters”, “without user consent”).
- **Secrets that sign in.** A named secret in an `Authorization`/API-key header or `-u user:password` authenticates the
  call to the API it names: `caution` (“Signs in to a web API with a secret: check where it goes.”). A secret anywhere
  else in a network call (body, query, upload), the whole environment or a credential file stays `dangerous`.
- **Calibration.** Run over the 31 skills of Anthropic's official Claude Code plugins on 2026-09-28: 24 safe, 6 caution
  (a Homebrew `curl | bash`, `rm -rf $TEMP_DIR`, a Bearer header, quoted injection phrases in an anti-injection skill),
  1 dangerous (a hook-development example whose code block holds `rm -rf /` in a test string: code blocks count).
- **Categories for the in-between.** Running a script from the internet (`curl | sh`, `bash <(curl …)`, `iex (iwr …)`)
  is filed under `persistence` (it installs whatever the server sends); a decoded payload run and encoded blobs under
  `exfiltration` (SL-08's “encoded payloads”).
- **Matching.** Per line, after removing invisible characters and NFKC folding (so a zero-width space or full-width
  letters can't break a phrase); phrases also with Markdown emphasis, ticks and HTML tags removed and across one line
  break (a match counts for the line it starts on). Named-secret detection looks at variable names token by token
  (`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `api_key`, `DB_PASSWORD`, not `$AUTHOR` or `$PORT`). Lines longer than 4 096 characters are scanned
  in overlapping chunks and every gap in a pattern is bounded, so a 256 KB line can't run away. Wiki links
  (`[[project overview]]`) are not delimiters.
- **Findings.** One per rule and line; dangerous first, then by file order and line; at most `SCAN_FINDINGS_MAX` 50
  (the verdict counts them all). Excerpts are at most `SCAN_EXCERPT_MAX` 120 characters around the match, with secrets
  redacted by the new `redactSecrets` (`packs/secrets.ts`: the credential shapes `literalSecretKind` knows, random-looking
  and long hex runs, values after secret-named keys, `Bearer …`, passwords in URLs and `-u user:password`; `$VARIABLES`
  and `${secret:NAME}` stay) and hidden characters shown as `⟨U+202E⟩`, tag characters as the text they hide
  (`⟨hidden: ignore previous instructions⟩`). `SCAN_CATEGORY_LABELS` and `SCAN_VERDICT_LABELS` are the UI's words.

## CT-122 Agents propose skills: `propose_skill`, the `skill` card, skill proposals over REST, skill hints on messages (skills-library.md SL-06, SL-07, SL-09, SL-D01, SL-D03) (2026-09-28)

- **Ids.** `SkillProposalId` (`skp_…`, `ID_PREFIXES.skillProposal`).
- **Limits** (SL-D03, `domain/skills.ts`): `SKILL_PROPOSALS_PENDING_MAX` 5 per agent, `OWN_PACK_SKILLS_MAX` 20,
  `SKILL_BODY_MAX_BYTES` 32 KB of UTF-8, `SKILL_DESCRIPTION_MAX` 300, `SKILL_REASON_MAX` 500, `SKILL_FILES_MAX` 8 and
  `SKILL_FILES_MAX_BYTES` 64 KB together, `SKILL_PROBLEMS_MAX` 10, `SKILL_DECISION_NOTE_MAX` 500.
- **Tool** (`contracts/mcp-skills.ts`, `SKILL_MCP_TOOLS` spread into `MCP_TOOLS` after memory): `propose_skill`, key
  `skills.propose`, input `SkillProposalInput` `{name: SkillName, description, body (Markdown, no front matter needed),
  files?: {path, text}[], reason, supersedes?: SkillName}`. A file path follows the pack path rules two levels less
  deep (the skill lives in `skills/<name>/`), is unique, isn't `SKILL.md` and is no hook or plugin file. Output
  `ProposeSkillOutput`: the commit outcomes with `{proposalId, messageId}`, `invalid {problems ≤ 10}` (the server's
  limits: pending, pack size, a name taken without `supersedes`) and `refused {reason, findings}` (a `dangerous` scan;
  nothing is stored). It is a posting tool (`MCP_POSTING_TOOLS`): the server posts the card as the agent.
- **Views.** `SkillProposalSummary` (id, agent `{id, name, handle}`, name, description, reason, supersedes, files
  `{path, size}`, scan, status `proposed | approved | rejected`, createdAt, `decidedBy` (a name), decidedAt, `note`,
  versionId, version, conversationId, messageId, `canDecide`) for lists and the card; `SkillProposalView` adds `body`
  and each file's `text`, both nullable for a viewer who may know the proposal exists but not read it.
  `SKILL_PROPOSAL_STATUS_LABELS`.
- **Card.** `SkillCard {kind: 'skill', proposalId, proposal: SkillProposalSummary | null}` joins `MessageCard` and
  `CARD_KINDS`; `StoredSkillCard {kind: 'skill', proposalId}` joins `StoredCard`; never `PostableCard`. Like report and
  approval cards it is resolved on read per viewer; `proposal: null` is a viewer outside the audience (“A skill
  proposal”, `SKILL_CARD_HIDDEN`). The card never carries the body or files: they are an agent's words, kept out of
  other agents' windows; `skillCardText` (“[skill proposal: invoice-check; waiting for approval]”) gives name and
  status only. `skillCardLabel`: `SKILL PROPOSAL · WAITING FOR APPROVAL`.
- **REST** (`api.skills`): `skills.proposals` `GET /burrows/:burrow/skill-proposals?status=&agent=` (summaries,
  absent status = all), `skills.proposal` `GET …/skill-proposals/:proposalId` (`{proposal: SkillProposalView}`),
  `skills.decide` `POST …/:proposalId/decision` `{decision: approve | reject, note?}` (same answer; a proposal that can
  no longer be built is 409 `conflict`), `skills.uses` `GET /burrows/:burrow/agents/:agent/skill-uses` →
  `{uses: {pack, skill, count, lastAt}[]}`.
- **Hints.** `SkillHint` = `{kind: 'use', name}` | `{kind: 'learn'}`. `SendMessageBody.skillHint?`,
  `Message.skillHint?: SkillHint | null` (optional, so older servers parse). `parseSkillCommand(text)` reads a leading
  `/name` (`{name, rest}`; clients send `rest` when it isn't empty, else the text as typed), `skillHintText` gives the
  prompt's line for `use` (“The person asked you to use the skill {name} for this.”).
- **Uses.** `SkillUses {count, lastAt | null}` and `skillUsesText` (“Used 12 times, last Tuesday”, “Used 3 times, last
  at 09:12”, “Used once, yesterday”, “Not used yet”).
- **Events** (`EVENT_TYPES`): `skill.proposed`, `skill.approved`, `skill.rejected`, `pack.skill_switched` (Keys) and
  `pack.role_packs_dismissed` (System); ids, names, statuses and scan verdicts only, never a body (BP-06).
