## CT-125 The Vault's `login` kind and Test sign-in (Whombat vault.md VT-D28…VT-D33, browser.md BT-06) (2026-09-28)

Agents sign in to websites in the browser Whombat runs with logins kept in the Vault; they never see the password.

- **Kind and sign-in.** `VAULT_ENTRY_KINDS` is `mcp|http|login|secret`. A `login` entry's `url` is the sign-in page
  (`parseVaultUrl`'s rules: http or https, no credentials, query or fragment); its `auth` is `form {username
  (VaultUsername: no colon, no control characters, ≤ 200), usernameSelector?, passwordSelector?, submitSelector?}`
  with `VaultCssSelector` (1–200 characters, not only spaces, no C0, DEL or C1 characters: the host uses it as a
  locator, nothing is evaluated); the password is the secret. `vaultEntryShapeProblems`: a login needs the URL, `form`
  and, on create, the password (“Paste the password.”); `form` belongs to `login` alone and `login` takes nothing else.
  `vaultSecretProblem` refuses line breaks and control characters in a password (a password input never takes them).
  The destination rule is `vaultDestinationProblem` unchanged (VT-12/VT-13). A login has no tools and no
  `vault_request`: `vaultCredential` throws for `form`.
- **Templates** (VT-D29): `VAULT_TEMPLATES` `mcp|token|basic|login|secret`. `basic` “Basic auth” is the former `login`
  template (`http` + basic, unchanged underneath, `vaultTemplateOf(http, basic)` → `basic`); `login` “Login” is the new
  kind with `form`. Templates are derived, never stored, so nothing persisted changes; a client offering “Login” now
  sends `login` + `form`.
- **`totp`**: `VaultEntry.totp` (`VaultSecretState`, defaulted to `VAULT_TOTP_UNSET` `{set: false, setAt: null}`, a
  fresh copy per parse) is the reserved one-time-code slot. No body sets it in this version.
- **Test sign-in** (VT-D31): `vault.testSignIn` `POST /burrows/:burrow/vault/:entryId/test-sign-in` (no body) answers
  `VaultTestSignInResponse {entry, result: VaultSignInResult}`: `{outcome: signed_in|still_asks|no_form|not_allowed|
  unreachable|timeout|unavailable, summary, screenshot: {mimeType: 'image/png', data (base64, ≤ 2 MB decoded)} | null,
  checkedAt}`. It answers the entry as well, as `vault.check` does, because the outcome is recorded as the entry's
  check and the card changes. `vaultSignInCheck` maps signed_in → reached, still_asks → rejected, no_form →
  bad_answer, the rest by name (failing), and `unavailable` → null: a browser that is down says nothing about the
  entry, so its check stays. `vaultSignInSummary` writes “Signed in”, “The page still asked for the password.”,
  “Couldn’t find a sign-in form on that page.”, “Not allowed: …”, the Vault's failure texts, and “The browser isn’t
  available on this Whombat right now.”; `vaultCheckSummary` reads a login's check in the same words. `vault.check` on
  a login and `vault.testSignIn` on anything else answer `wrong_kind`. Constants: `VAULT_SIGN_IN_WAIT_MS` 15 s,
  `VAULT_SELECTOR_MAX` 200, `VAULT_SIGN_IN_SCREENSHOT_MAX` 2 MiB, `VAULT_BROWSER_SIGN_IN_WHAT` “Browser sign-in” (the use's
  `what`, VT-D33). Copy: `VAULT_COPY.testSignIn`, `signInScreenshotNote`, `selectorsHint`.
- **Over a session** `vault.testSignIn` is an export op (`EXPORT_OPS`, with `packs.export`): its answer is larger than
  one CONTROL message and a mutation's result must be small, so it is read through an export stream (the web client
  already does that for export ops and parses the JSON). An export stream has no receipt, so nothing stores the
  screenshot and a retry signs in again, which is harmless. It is not a secret op: its input holds no secret.
- **Agents** (VT-D30): `VaultContextEntry.site` (≤ 253, optional and nullable, so the context builders for `mcp` and
  `http` entries compile unchanged): a `login` entry's registrable domain, computed by the server, in every turn (the
  site is needed to sign in and is not the entry's name); `baseUrl` carries its sign-in page in the owner's own turn
  only (VT-D27), `tools` is empty, and `VaultDispatchContext.tools` gains nothing (`browser_sign_in` is one of
  Whombat's own tools). `SetVaultSecretBody.username` also replaces a login's username;
  its selectors stay.
- **Fixtures**: every entry has `totp`; `createFixtureFetch()` serves `vault.testSignIn` (no browser: an allowed
  address signs in, with the 1×1 PNG `FIXTURE_SIGN_IN_SCREENSHOT`) and refuses `vault.check` on a login. `vaultShopLogin`
  (Shop admin, Pippa's key at Asks) is opt-in like the handoff fixtures (CT-114), not in `VAULT_ENTRIES`, so the seeded
  Vault page is unchanged. The printer entry now reads “Basic auth · 192.168.1.20 · no agents”.
- **Older readers.** `VaultEntryKind`, `VaultAuth` and `VaultTemplate` are closed unions and widen. The policy for
  closed unions (CT-83, CT-88, CT-105) applies: an app before 0.20 refuses a `vault.list`, `vault.get` or
  `vault.agentKeys` answer holding a login, and a runner before 0.20 a dispatch whose Vault context holds one, so the
  server, the web and mobile apps and the runner ship together. They are not made tolerant: a catch-all kind would show
  a login as something it isn't. In practice a login exists only once a 0.20 web client created one.

## CT-126 Where the browser may go: `@whombat/core/browser` (Whombat browser.md BT-05) (2026-09-28)

- A new subpath, also re-exported from the root. Pure (no `URL`, no DNS) like the Vault's rules, which it reuses.
- **URLs an agent opens.** `parseBrowserUrl` / `browserUrlProblem(url)` → null or `{code: invalid|scheme|credentials|
  host|port, message}` (`BROWSER_URL_PROBLEM_TEXT`): `http:` or `https:` followed by `//`, any path, query and fragment;
  the host by the Vault's rules (dotted-quad IPv4, bracketed IPv6, or an ASCII name not ending in a number, so `127.1`,
  `0x7f.0.0.1`, `2130706433` and percent-encoded or non-ASCII names are refused: write punycode); no credentials, no
  control characters anywhere, no backslash before the query (a browser reads it as `/`), at most
  `BROWSER_URL_MAX` 4 096 characters. Every other scheme is `scheme` (“The browser opens only http and https pages.”):
  `file:`, `data:`, `javascript:`, `blob:`, `chrome:`, `about:`, `view-source:`, `ws:`, extension and intent schemes.
  `about:blank` (`BROWSER_BLANK_PAGE`) is the one exception.
- **What may be shown.** `stripUrlForActivity(url)` drops credentials, query and fragment (and cuts at the first `?`
  or `#` of anything that isn't a clean URL); `browserUrlHost(url)` is the host a person reads (“example.com”,
  “192.168.1.10:8123”: the port only when written and not the default), null for anything but http(s).
- **Destinations.** `browserDestinationProblem({scheme, host?, port, resolved, networks})` → null or `{code: scheme|
  port|never|not_listed|mixed|unresolved, message, suggestion?}`, checked on every address the proxy may dial: all
  public → ports 80 and 443 only (`BROWSER_PUBLIC_PORTS`; http and https alike, `ws`/`wss` read as them); any address
  `classifyAddress` doesn't call public or private (loopback, link-local, metadata, multicast, reserved, documentation,
  unspecified, IPv4-compatible, NAT64, 6to4, Teredo; an IPv4-mapped address as its IPv4) → `never`, even inside a
  listed network; public and private at once → `mixed`; private (RFC 1918, 100.64/10 shared space incl. CGNAT and
  Tailscale, fc00::/7 unique local) → only inside a listed network whose ports include the port, else `not_listed`
  with the Vault's suggestion; nothing resolved → `unresolved` (an IP-literal `host` is its own address). This is the
  Vault's matching: CGNAT and ULA are home-network space an admin may list, as for Vault entries (CT-98), not a
  separate “never” class. `never` says only “That address can’t be reached from the browser.”: the text may reach a
  shared room, so it doesn't name the address.
- **Shared with the Vault** (`vault/network.ts`, behaviour unchanged): `parseUrlAuthority(scheme, authority)` (the
  authority rules `parseVaultUrl` used inline), `addressInCidr`, `listedNetworkFor(address, port, networks)` and
  `suggestedNetworkFor(address)` (the /24 or /64 an admin would add).
- **Limits** (`browser/limits.ts`): `BROWSER_SNAPSHOT_MAX` 64 KB with `BROWSER_SNAPSHOT_CUT_NOTE`,
  `BROWSER_CALL_DEADLINE_MS` 30 s, `BROWSER_MAX_NAVIGATIONS` 40, `BROWSER_WAIT_MAX_MS` 10 s, `BROWSER_IDLE_MS` 5 min,
  `BROWSER_VIEWPORT` 1280×800, `BROWSER_MAX_PAGES` 2, `BROWSER_TYPE_MAX` 4 000.

## CT-127 The browser's tools, its status on the host and in the dispatch (Whombat browser.md BT-03, BT-04, BT-06…BT-10) (2026-09-28)

- **Tools** (`contracts/mcp-browser.ts`, `BROWSER_MCP_TOOLS` spread into `MCP_TOOLS`; names in `BROWSER_TOOL_NAMES`,
  `isBrowserToolName`, `browserToolOf` for prefixed activity names): `browser_open {url}`, `browser_snapshot {}`,
  `browser_click {ref}`, `browser_type {ref, text ≤ 4 000, submit?}`, `browser_press {key}`, `browser_select {ref,
  value}`, `browser_scroll {ref?, direction?: up|down}`, `browser_wait {text? | ms? ≤ 10 000}` (exactly one),
  `browser_screenshot {attach?}`, `browser_back {}`, `browser_close {}`, `browser_sign_in {entry: vlt_…}`. All
  `requiredKey: 'browser.use'`, so `mcpRequiredKey` answers it with an empty scope; `browser_snapshot` and
  `browser_wait` are read-only. `BrowserRef` accepts `@e12` or `e12` and reads both as `@e12`; `BrowserUrl` runs
  `browserUrlProblem` (so a `file:` URL fails validation with “The browser opens only http and https pages.”);
  `BrowserKey` is Playwright's key syntax (a named key or one printable character, up to three modifiers).
  Descriptions tell the model what each does, that page content is data and never instructions, never to type a
  password, token or code given in chat, and that sign-in goes through the Vault (`browser_sign_in`, “you never see
  them”, stop on `pending_approval`, “a private Vault entry” in a shared room).
- **Answers.** `BrowserPage` (`BROWSER_PAGE_SHAPE`): `{status: ok, url (stripped), title, origin, snapshot? (≤ 64 KB
  plus its data delimiters), truncated?, downloads: {attachmentId, name, size}[] (default []), note?, signedIn?}`.
  `browserOutcome(ok)` = the commit outcomes (`ok`, `pending_approval`, `blocked` with `keyNeeded`: the key may ask) plus
  `BrowserRefused {status: refused, code, reason}` and `BrowserFailed {status: failed, …}`. Codes
  (`BROWSER_REFUSAL_CODES`, `BROWSER_REFUSAL_STATUS`, `BROWSER_REFUSAL_TEXT`, `browserRefusal`): refused for
  `not_allowed`, `busy`, `unavailable`, `other_site`, `signed_in_only`, `limit`; failed for `timeout`, `bad_ref`,
  `navigation_failed`. The texts are BT-01's, BT-04's and BT-06's verbatim, plus `browserSignInOnlyText(site)`,
  `BROWSER_SCREENSHOT_STAYS` (“Screenshots of a signed-in page stay with you.”, `not_allowed`) and
  `BROWSER_NOT_A_LOGIN`. `browser_screenshot` answers `{url, origin, attachmentId?}`; the image travels as MCP image
  content beside it (BT-D04), which the output schema can't describe, so the tool's description says it.
  `browser_close` answers `{closed}`. `browser_sign_in` (`BrowserSignInOutput`) answers the page with `signedIn`, the
  Vault's `pending_approval`, `blocked` with `keyNeeded` optional (absent when the Vault refused: VT-23's shape, no
  catalog key), or a refusal.
- **Which lists.** The browser tools are in `WHOMBAT_TOOL_NAMES`, as `vault_request` is: they are Whombat's own tools
  and Claude's allowlist (`MCP_TOOL_NAMES`) must admit them, while the server lists them only to an agent holding
  `browser.use` and never in feedback, search or answer dispatches (a server test that compares its list to
  `WHOMBAT_TOOL_NAMES` filters `BROWSER_TOOL_NAMES` like `vault_request`). They are not personal-only, not connector
  tools, not posting tools, and not in `FEEDBACK_DISPATCH_TOOLS`.
- **Status** (`browser/status.ts`): `BrowserStatus {state: available|off|unavailable, reason | null}`
  (`off`: switched off or not installable, `unavailable`: should run but its host is down), `BROWSER_STATE_LABELS` and
  `browserStatusLine` (“Web browser: Available”, “Web browser: Off · {reason}”, “Web browser: Not available right
  now”). It is on both `HostInfo.browser` and `AgentSetupStatus.browser`, optional (older servers leave it out), with
  the same value. Settings → General reads `host.agents` (`AgentSetupStatus`) already, polled every 5 s while open, and
  both are session ops, so it reaches the line in self-hosted and managed mode without a second request. Hire and
  Configure already read `host.info` (the working directory), so they can say beside “Use a web browser” that the
  browser is off without another request.
- **Runner** (`DispatchContext.browser`, `BrowserContextInfo`, optional and nullable): `{state, reason, logins:
  {entryId, site}[] (default [])}`, null when the agent doesn't hold `browser.use` (and in feedback, search and answer
  turns). `logins` are the agent's own keys to `login` entries, so the host can refuse those sites to a plain session.
- **Audit**: `EVENT_TYPES['browser.used']` is `System`: the hidden event (`text: null`) every browser call signs, payload
  `{tool, origin, dispatchId}` (BT-03). A sign-in signs `vault.used` as well (VT-D33).
- **Fixtures**: `FIXTURE_HOST.browser` is available.

## CT-128 The browser in the activity feed (Whombat browser.md BT-03, vault.md VT-D33) (2026-09-28)

- **`describeActivity`** reads a browser tool by its name, whatever kind the row has (`web` as BT-03 says, or `whombat`
  / `tool` from a runner that doesn't know the browser yet), and wherever the runner prefixed it (`browserToolOf`):
  `browser_open` and `browser_back` (`BROWSER_OPENING_TOOLS`) read “Opening / Opened / Couldn’t open example.com”; every
  other tool “Using / Used / Couldn’t use the browser on example.com”. The host is `browserUrlHost(object)` (a URL or an
  origin; the port only when written and not the default), so no path or query ever reaches a title; with no object
  the rows read “Opened a page”, “Went back a page”, “Used the browser”. The detail is the usual failure detail, never
  the object; every browser row is important, like web rows. `waiting` and `blocked` read as for every tool
  (“Waiting for approval”, “Blocked · needs Use a web browser”).
- **`browser_sign_in` is a Vault row** (VT-D33): `isVaultActivityTool` now also answers true for it, so the runner and
  the server (which both call it already) store it as the neutral Vault row (`whombat.vault_request`, no object,
  evidence or approval) and it reads “Used a private Vault entry”, with no site. `isVaultToolName` is unchanged (the
  server routes by it).
- **What the runner sends** for browser tools: kind `web`, tool `whombat.<name>`, no evidence (like Whombat's other
  tools), and as object `browserActivityObject(tool, input)`: `browser_open`'s URL without credentials, query and
  fragment (`stripUrlForActivity`), null for every other tool (a click's page isn't known when the call starts, and
  typed text or selected values never reach a row). The server should strip a stored browser row's object with
  `stripUrlForActivity` again, whatever a runner sent. A runner may later fill the object of other rows from an
  answer's `origin`; the copy already reads it.

## CT-129 Spend: the overview and the agent's week (Whombat spend.md SP-01, SP-02, SP-D01) (2026-09-28)

- **Arithmetic** (`domain/spend.ts`, pure): `SpendUsage` (a turn's `{inputTokens, outputTokens, costUsd?}`, as
  `CompleteBody.usage`), `SpendTotals {turns, inputTokens, outputTokens, costUsd | null, costTurns, unreportedTurns}`,
  `emptyTotals`, `addUsage(totals, usage | null)` (no usage: a turn with 0 tokens and `unreportedTurns + 1`; a reported
  cost adds to `costUsd` and `costTurns`; `costUsd` stays null until a turn reports one; sums rounded to micro-dollars
  so many small costs don't drift), `mergeTotals`, `spendTokens`. `SpendWindows {today, week, month}`:
  `spendWindowsOf(finishedAt, now, timeZone)` counts a turn in `today` on the same calendar day in the burrow's zone and
  in `week` / `month` when it finished less than 7 / 30 days before now (rolling windows, `SPEND_WINDOW_DAYS`); a turn
  stamped slightly after now counts. `addTurn` and `spendWindowsFrom(turns, now, timeZone)` fold turns into windows.
- **Views.** `SpendOverview {scope: burrow|own, generatedAt, timeZone, totals: SpendWindows, byAgent: {agentId, name,
  handle, role, personal, windows}[], byPerson: {personId | null, name, windows}[], handoffs: {open, budgetTokens,
  usedTokens}, plans: {planId, title, budgetTokens | null, usedTokens}[] ≤ SPEND_PLANS_MAX 5}`; rows by 30-day tokens,
  “Nobody” (`SPEND_NOBODY`, `personId` null) last. `SpendAgentWeek {scope: all|yours, week}`. Endpoints (`api.spend`):
  `spend.overview` `GET /burrows/:burrow/spend` and `spend.agent` `GET /burrows/:burrow/agents/:agent/spend`; the
  visibility is SP-01's (owners everything; a member their own turns and their personal agent's, `own` / `yours`).
- **Words.** `formatTokenCount` (900, 1.2k, 340k, 1.2M, 12M, 1.5B: one decimal below 10 of a unit, whole above, `.0`
  dropped) — not `formatTokens`, which is handoffs' “12k tokens” (CT-113) and keeps its meaning; `formatCost` (“about
  $3.40”, “about $1,204.00”, “under $0.01” below a cent, null without a reported cost); `spendSummary` (“1.2M tokens ·
  about $3.40”) and `spendLine(week)` (“This week: 1.2M tokens · about $3.40”, “This week: 1.2M tokens”, and “This
  week: no turns” for an agent that did nothing, which SP-02 didn't word).
- **Fixtures** (`spend.ts`): `SPEND_TURNS`, 30 days of the crew's turns with plausible usage (Clover's provider reports
  no cost, two of Dusty's scheduled turns no usage), summed by core's helpers into `spendOverview()` (Mara, an owner:
  scope `burrow`) and `spendAgentWeek(handle)`; `createFixtureFetch()` serves both endpoints. No open handoffs, as in
  the seeded world; the invoice-PDF plan is the one plan.
- **No Go, JSON Schema or vector changes** for CT-125…CT-129: none of these types is in the cross-language registry
  (the Vault, MCP tools, dispatch contexts and Spend have no Go bindings, as CT-105 and CT-115). The session vectors'
  secret-op list is unchanged (`vault.testSignIn` is an export op, not a secret op).
- **Tolerated both ways**: the new endpoints (an older server answers 404, an older runtime `unknown_op`), the optional
  `HostInfo.browser`, `AgentSetupStatus.browser`, `DispatchContext.browser`, `VaultContextEntry.site`, the defaulted
  `VaultEntry.totp`, and the new MCP tools (an older server doesn't list them). **Type-level**: `VaultEntry`'s output
  type has `totp` (code that builds an entry adds `totp: {set: false, setAt: null}`); `vaultCredential` throws for
  `form`. Breaking readers: the closed unions of CT-125.

One release for Whombat's agent-capabilities workstream (`docs/decisions/browser.md`, `skills-library.md`,
`agent-roles.md`, `spend.md` and `vault.md` VT-D28…VT-D33 in the Whombat repository): CT-119 (roles, keys, hire keys by
role), CT-120…CT-124 (manifest roles and requirements, the content scan, skill proposals and the `skill` card, skill
switches, role packs on hire, skill hints, scratch turns, the `skills` guide) and CT-125…CT-129 (the Vault's `login`

A minor release. Closed unions grow (`AGENT_ROLES`, `KEY_IDS`, `VAULT_ENTRY_KINDS`, `VAULT_TEMPLATES`, `CARD_KINDS`,
guide topics, event types), so older apps and runners refuse answers that carry a new member: runtime, web, mobile and
the appliance candidate ship together, as with CT-110 and CT-117. *Superseded by CT-136 (0.22): unions still grow in
minors, and clients decode with `decodeTolerant`, leaving out what they don't know.* The template id `login` now means the website login;
the HTTP basic-auth template is `basic`. No Go, schema or vector change (`pnpm gen:check` clean). Every package is

## CT-131 Contracts 0.20.1: the capabilities security and product-review fixes (2026-09-28)

A patch over 0.20.0 (CT-130) closing findings from the `capabilities` security review and product review. Behaviour
changes and additive exports only — no shape change except an optional parameter and an optional field, both defaulted
so 0.20.0 callers compile and behave as before. The lead bumps and releases; runtime, web and mobile pick it up when
they choose (nothing forces a joint ship, unlike a minor).

Security findings:

- **M3, the content scan (`packs/scan.ts`).** The scan was per line and blind to several writings of the same attack.
  Now: it joins `\`-continued lines before matching (a split command is judged whole; a finding keeps the first
  physical line's number). Environment reads are broadened (`process['env']`, `__import__('os').environ`,
  `vars(os)['environ']`, `getattr(os, …environ…)`, `os.getenv`, `Deno.env`, `$ENV{…}`, `printenv`) and network sinks
  too (`/dev/tcp`, `/dev/udp`, `socket.create_connection`, `socket.socket`, `urllib.request`). Obfuscated command
  names (`c''url`, `cu""rl`, `c\url`, `/usr/bin/cu*`, `$(printf '\x63…')`, `${IFS}`) are `caution` alone and
  `dangerous` next to a secret. `eval "$(… base64 -d)"` and `eval`/`bash`/`sh -c`/`python -c` of `$(curl …)` or
  `<(curl …)` are `dangerous`; `shutil.rmtree` of the home folder or root, and `at`/`batch` scheduling, are added.
  HTML entities are decoded and Cyrillic/Greek confusables folded before injection phrases and delimiters are matched,
  so `&#91;&#91;pack` and `Іgnоrе previous instructions` are caught. One file-wide rule correlates a credential-file
  read with any network sink, or a secret/environment read with a raw channel (a socket, `/dev/tcp`, `nc`, an
  obfuscated tool), across lines; a named env var with an HTTP client is left to the per-line rule and `secret-to-api`
  (broadened to recognise any `…-Token`/`…-Key` header, so a vendor token stays `caution`), so honest API clients are
  not flagged. The false-positive rules are unchanged; the new `dangerous` rules are code rules, so quoting or negation
  can't downgrade them in a code block. The table-driven test carries every bypass from the review as a true positive
  and new prose false positives. Calibrated over ~260 third-party skills: no `safe`→`dangerous` regression; the
  thirteen shipped packs still scan `safe`.
- **M4, nested `SKILL.md` (`packs/validate.ts`, `domain/skills.ts`, BP-D20).** `validatePack` refuses a `SKILL.md`
  (any case) below a skill's own directory root — which also stops skill directories from nesting — and checks the
  front matter (name and description only) of every other `SKILL.md` in the pack, at any depth. A proposal's `files`
  refuse `SKILL.md` at any depth, and hook files, MCP configs, plugin and provider folders (`.claude-plugin`,
  `.codex-plugin`, `.claude`, `.codex`) and `agents/*.yaml` at any depth.
- **M13, hire keys by role (`keys/grants.ts`).** `hireGrants(agentId, selected, channelIds, role?)` — the new
  optional `role` — grants `cannot` for a locked row whose key (or an umbrella above it) is in
  `ROLE_DEFAULT_KEYS[role].cannot`, so a hired Lead, Tester or Writer gets Deploy `cannot`, as when onboarded (AR-05).
  `hireKeyOptions(role)` shows that row locked at `cannot` with the note `ROLE_LOCKED_NOTE` (“not for this role”).
  Without `role` (older callers) every locked row keeps its cap, so behaviour is unchanged. The runtime's hire command
  should pass the role to get this (and its `roles.int.test.ts` deploy expectation for lead/tester/writer follows).
- **L4, `stripUrlForActivity` (`browser/destination.ts`).** Returns the empty string (callers store null) for any URL
  that isn't an absolute http(s) URL once cut at the first `?`/`#`, or that holds a username or password in any form
  (`https:\\user:pass@host`, `//user:pass@host`, `user:pass@host/a`, `https://user:pa/ss@host`); `about:blank` stays.
  The return type is unchanged (string). `browserActivityObject` answers null for it.

Product-review fixes (same release):

- **M3, role grammar (`domain/roles.ts`, `text/copy.ts`, `packs/roles.ts`).** `ROLE_NOUNS: Record<AgentRole, string>` —
  a noun phrase with its article — reads “a product agent”, “a security agent”, “a support agent”, “a finance agent”,
  “a legal agent”, “a sales agent”, “a marketing agent”; the mock's roles keep “an architect”, “a developer” …
  `roleNoun(role)`, `roleNounForLabel(label)` and `roleDutiesLabel(name)` (“What Bolt does”) are exported. `dmIntro`
  (unchanged shape: name, roleLabel, job — so web and mobile need no edit) and `rolePackSuggestionText` read the noun.
- **S1 (`keys/grants.ts`).** When a role's default key is brought in by a fixed bundle row (Tester's `tests.run` under
  “Run tests and CI”), `hireKeyOptions` replaces that row in place with the narrower key, on, instead of appending it,
  so no “off” row sits beside a near-identical “on” one. A role's other extras come before the locked Merge/Deploy
  rows, which stay last as in the mock.
- **S2 (`keys/catalog.ts`, `keys/grants.ts`).** `impliedBy(keyId, onKeys)`, `keysImpliedBy(keyId)`, `includedNote` and
  `impliedWithNote` express bundles. `hireKeyOptions` shows a key a bundle brings in (“Browse the web” under “Use a
  web browser”) on and locked “included with the browser” via the new optional `HireKeyOption.includedWith`; it grants
  nothing of its own (`hireGrants`/`configureGrants` skip it — the bundle key implies it). `impliedKeyRows(grants)`
  lists such keys for the profile (“Browse the web · with the browser”); `keyRows` is unchanged.

No Go, JSON Schema or vector change (`pnpm gen:check` clean). Versions stay 0.20.0 until the lead's 0.20.1 commit.

## CT-134 Contracts 0.21.0: a migrating candidate is judged by the schema it migrates to (appliance MG-43, Whombat MD-12) (2026-09-28)

Production, 2026-09-28: box `wb-old0-prod-0001` on `pve-20260928.4` (schema 48) quarantined `pve-20260928.5` (schema
49, `0048_capabilities`, an `expand` whose floors are `0047_delegation`) with `schema_incompatible`. The manager called
`CheckActivation(current, candidate, 48)` with the **pre-migration** schema; Whombat tuples read only their own newest
schema (`schemaReads {49..49}`), so `candidate_cannot_read_schema`, and rollback judged by the tuples alone
(`current.schemaReads ∋ candidate.schemaWrites`) is false for every new schema, so every migration would have needed a
backup checkpoint. No release with a migration could install.

`checkMigratingActivation(current, candidate, dbSchema, migration)` (Go `CheckMigratingActivation`, `SchemaMigration`)
is the check for a candidate whose own schema check answered *migration required* — that answer is the proof it
migrates from `dbSchema`. `migration` is what the runtime's `whombat.schema-check/1` says (Whombat MD-12): `target`
(the schema its migrations produce), `readers`/`writers` (that schema's floors: the oldest binary schema that can read
/ write it; `null` from runtimes before MD-12) and `needsCheckpoint` (the contract/incompatible migrations it names).

- With floors: `candidate_cannot_read_schema` when the candidate's `schemaReads` doesn't include `target`;
  `schema_downgrade` as before (`schemaWrites < dbSchema`); `schema_target_mismatch` when `target` isn't the
  candidate's `schemaWrites` (the tuple and the runtime disagree about what it writes); `host_abi_unsupported` as
  before. The current runtime's access after the migration (`rollbackAccess`): `read-write` when its schema
  (`current.runtime.schemaWrites`, the binary's own version) ≥ `writers`; else `read-only` when ≥ `readers`; else
  `none`. The floors decide even where the current tuple's `schemaReads` claims the target: the runtime's own check
  judges a newer schema by its recorded floors (Whombat MD-02, MD-04), so the tuple can't promise more. `rollbackCompatible` = `read-write`. `requiresCheckpoint` when
  the runtime names migrations or a rollback wouldn't be `read-write` (a read-only rollback leaves the appliance unable
  to write until a fix-forward: the checkpoint is the way back, as for a contract).
- Without floors: exactly `checkActivation(current, candidate, dbSchema)` (so an older runtime that must migrate is
  still refused, as before), with `requiresCheckpoint` also set for migrations the runtime names.

`ActivationCheck` gains `rollbackAccess` (`'read-write' | 'read-only' | 'none'`; `checkActivation` answers
`read-write` or `none`). `compat.json` gains `migrating` (tuples `schema48`/`schema49` model the production pair,
`wideReader` a current tuple that claims to read the target) and every `activation` expectation carries
`rollbackAccess`; the Go module checks both. A minor release: a new function and an added output field; no schema or
wire change. Only the appliance's manager uses it (the Go module); Whombat, control and the harness need not move.
Every package is 0.21.0.

## CT-135 Version order and the exit-0 floors check, in both languages (robust updates UP-A1, UP-A2, UP-B2) (2026-09-28)

`compareVersions(a, b)` (`@whombat/release`, Go `release.CompareVersions`) is the appliance helper's `CompareVersions`
(`helper/pkg/trust/forward.go`) line for line, so control (`notOlder` by versions, UP-X03), the pipeline (UP-A3) and
the manager order components the same way: build metadata after the first `+` ignored; core and pre-release split at
the first `-`; dotted segments with a missing one counting as `0`, two numeric segments numerically, a numeric one
before an alphanumeric one, otherwise by bytes; a pre-release before its release. TypeScript reads a segment as a
number exactly when Go's `ParseUint(s, 10, 64)` does (ASCII digits within 64 bits, compared as `bigint`; a longer
run of digits is text, after every number) and compares text by code point (= UTF-8 byte order). `compat.json` →
`versions` pins semver basics, host ids (`pve-20260928.5` < `.6` < `.10` < `pve-20260929.1`, `pve-dev-…` alike), the
text trap of the old runtime versions (`0.1.0-e847497` > `0.1.0-195421a`, `0.1.0-a2abeeb.p26a328c` >
`0.1.0-843d1ba`), the transition (UP-A2: each of `0.1.0-a2abeeb.p26a328c`, `0.1.0-843d1ba`, `0.1.0-2be6fc1`,
`0.1.0-e847497`, `0.1.0-195421a`, `0.1.0`, `0.0.48-2be6fc1` is older than `0.2.0-20260928190000.abcdef1` and than
`0.2.0-dev`, both directions) and the new scheme (commit time, then rev; `.p<digest>` and `.<label>` sort after their
base; a release build before `0.2.0-dev`, which sorts before `0.2.0`).

`checkCompatibleActivation(current, candidate, dbSchema, floors)` (Go `CheckCompatibleActivation`, `SchemaFloors
{Readers, Writers}`) is the check for a candidate whose own schema check answered exit 0 **and** reported the live
schema's floors (UP-B2). With `own = candidate.runtime.schemaWrites`: `own ≥ dbSchema` → `checkActivation`'s candidate
check (its `schemaReads` includes `dbSchema`); `own < dbSchema` → the floors decide (`own ≥ writers` ok, `readers ≤ own
< writers` `candidate_read_only`, below `candidate_cannot_read_schema`), with no `schema_downgrade` and no
`schemaReads` check; `host_abi_unsupported` as always. `rollbackAccess` is `current.runtime.schemaWrites` against the
same floors, `rollbackCompatible` = read-write, `requiresCheckpoint` false (nothing migrates). The forward check
(`allowDowngradeFrom`) is separate and unchanged, as are `checkActivation` and `checkMigratingActivation`. The manager
picks the function from the exit code and whether floors were reported, never from the tuple. `compat.json` →
`compatible`: the custody rollback (current 49, candidate 48, db 49, floors {47, 48} → ok, read-write), the contract
cases ({48, 49} → `candidate_read_only`, {49, 49} → `candidate_cannot_read_schema`), the current schema (the same
answer as `checkActivation`), a newer candidate, an installed runtime below the floors (`none`) and a host ABI
refusal.

## CT-136 Clients tolerate version skew: tolerant decoding, API levels, runtime features (UP-B3) (2026-09-28)

This replaces CT-130's closed-union policy. Unions (`CARD_KINDS`, `WorkItemKind`, `AGENT_ROLES`, event types, …) still
grow in minors; clients no longer refuse an answer that carries a member they don't know. Signed, hashed and
security documents and command inputs stay strict (CT-14 unchanged).

- **`decodeTolerant(schema, value, {maxRepairs?})`** (`@whombat/protocol`) → `{ok: true, data, skipped}` or `{ok:
  false, error}` (the plain parse's error). When a parse fails only on tolerable issues (`isTolerableIssue(issue,
  input)`: zod 4's `invalid_value` on a string — an enum member or string literal it doesn't know — and `invalid_union`
  with an unknown string discriminator; a plain union when every option failed only on such issues), it repairs at
  the nearest place walking up from the unknown value: a list element is dropped, an optional member unset, a nullable
  member set to null. A repair reaching the top of the value, any other issue, more than `TOLERANT_MAX_REPAIRS` (256)
  repairs or eight rounds fail as before. `skipped: [{path, value, action: 'dropped'|'unset'|'nulled'}]` locates each
  item in the value as given (repairs are decided before any is applied, drops last-first), so a client can put
  “This needs a newer version of the app.” where it was. A record keyed by an enum (`unrecognized_keys`) is not
  repaired: the only one in a response is the operator overview's `byState`. The core schemas have no `unknown`
  placeholder member, so UP-B3b's placeholder is the client's, from `skipped`. `parseRealtimeEvent` now decodes
  tolerantly (a `message.created` with a new card kind keeps the message, card null); `decodeApplianceMessage` is
  unchanged (a control message with an unknown value still fails; unknown message types were already skipped).
- **`SESSION_API_LEVEL = 22`** (`session/version.ts`, Go `protocol.SessionAPILevel`): bumped by every contracts minor
  that changes a session op, output, frame or union (the release checklist in `docs/publishing.md`); `LEGACY_API_LEVEL
  = 21` for runtimes that don't say; `apiLevelWindow(level)` = `{level − 2, level + 1}`; `runtimeSkew(client,
  runtime?)` → `ok | runtime_too_old | client_too_old`.
- **`RUNTIME_FEATURES`** (`session/features.ts`), each with the version that brought it: `diagnostics` (0.5.3),
  `packs` (0.5.4), `signins`, `clients.install` (0.9), `licence` (0.10), `guides` (0.11), `work` (0.12),
  `messages.images` (0.12.2), `feedback` (0.13), `vault` (0.14), `delegation` (0.16/0.18), `roles`, `skills`,
  `vault.login`, `browser`, `spend` (0.20) — together `LEGACY_FEATURES`, what every runtime before the advertisement
  (every box in the field) has — and `backup.destinations` (0.22, CT-142). `RuntimeFeature` is the known names;
  `runtimeHasFeature(runtime?, name)` answers from the list or `LEGACY_FEATURES`.
- **`Welcome.runtime`** (optional, `WelcomeRuntime {version: VersionString, apiLevel, features ≤ 128}`); older
  clients strip it. `FeatureName` (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]*$`, ≤ 64, an open string: unknown names are ignored) and
  `ApiLevel` (0…100 000) live in `@whombat/core/contracts` (re-exported by the protocol), because the runtime's
  release manifest (`ReleaseManifest`, `distribution.ts`) also gains optional `apiLevel` and `features` (Whombat
  writes `SESSION_API_LEVEL` and its list there; the pipeline reads them for notes and release records).

Tests feed the 0.21 schemas a 0.22-shaped answer (a new card kind: the message stays with `card: null`; a new work item
kind and work action; an agent with a new role; a new event type) and the 0.22 schemas a 0.20-era answer (a welcome
without `runtime`, update facts without the 0.22 members).

## CT-137 Update failure detail (UP-E3) (2026-09-28)

`UpdateFailureDetail {stage: UpdateJournalState, code: Ident, reasons: Ident[] ≤ 8, release, schema?: {database,
target: int | null, candidateWrites, candidateReads}, rollbackAccess?, failedChecks: (HEALTH_CHECKS)[] ≤ 8, at}` —
codes, ids and numbers only (the device report allowlist, assignment §12; the box keeps its message). It is defined in
`@whombat/release` (`failure.ts`), not `device/status.ts`, because `appliance.status.update` (`@whombat/protocol`)
mirrors it and the protocol can't depend on control-contracts; `@whombat/control-contracts/device` re-exports it. It
is a tolerant `z.object`: it travels in facts, session answers and control responses that an older reader may get
from a newer writer. Device bodies are commands (CT-14), so `DeviceStatusReport.update.failureDetail` and
`UpdateProgressReport.failureDetail` carry `UpdateFailureReport = z.strictObject(UpdateFailureDetail.shape)`; in Go the
two structs have the same fields (`device.UpdateFailureReport(detail)` converts a `release.UpdateFailureDetail`).
`DeviceStatusReport.runtimeVersion` (optional) names the running runtime. The brief's `.nullable().optional()` is
`.optional()` in every cross-language schema (the subset has no optional-nullable, CT-08): absent means none.
`HEALTH_CHECKS` names the health checks once (`HealthEvidence.check`, `failedChecks`).

`describeUpdateFailure(detail)` renders one or two sentences for operators and owners from a catalogue of the manager's
codes (`manager/internal/update`: `schema_incompatible` with `candidate_cannot_read_schema`, `candidate_read_only`,
`schema_downgrade`, `schema_target_mismatch`, `host_abi_unsupported`, `protocol_no_overlap`; `unhealthy` with the
failed checks in words, `boot_fallback`, `reboot_timeout`, `manager_recovery`, `download_corrupt`,
`verification_failed`, `no_space`, `incompatible`, `downgrade`, `not_assigned`, `not_staged`, `activation_failed`,
`activation_deferred`, `boundary_lost`, `checkpoint_required`, `checkpoint_stale`, `checkpoint_failed`,
`migrate_failed`, `forward_repair_required`; a helper's `helper_<code>` reads as `<code>`). The 2026-09-28 failure
reads “pve-20260928.5 couldn’t start on this Whombat’s database: it reads schema 49 only and the database is at 48.
Nothing was changed.” An unknown code reads “<release> couldn’t be installed (<code>).”, followed by “Nothing was
changed.” before activation or “This Whombat went back to the release it ran before.” during and after it.

## CT-138 What the owner sees of updates (UP-E4) (2026-09-28)

`UpdateFacts` (local, tolerant) gains `failureDetail`, `waiting: UpdateWaiting {reason: UpdateWaitReason, since,
blockers: [{kind, count}] ≤ 16}` and `lastUpdate: LastUpdate {release, from: ReleaseId | null, at}`, all optional
(absent when there is nothing to say; older runtimes strip them). `UpdateWaitReason` (`@whombat/release`) is
`boundary | checkpoint | window | hold | lock | metadata`. `UpdateStatus` (`appliance.status.update`) mirrors them with
ISO times; `summarizeUpdate` passes them through. `lastUpdate` carries no summary: the notes' summary comes from
control, `GET /v1/releases/:release/summary` (auth `session`, `rollout.releaseSummary` → `ReleaseSummary {release,
summary ≤ 500, publishedAt}`; `release_not_found` 404 when control has no record), so a box never stores release
notes.

## CT-139 Release records in control (UP-X02, UP-C3) (2026-09-28)

`ReleaseRecord {notes?: {summary ≤ 500, markdown ≤ 20 000}, apiLevel?, features?, migrations?: [{tag, class, readers,
writers, version}] ≤ 1000, twin?, env?: dev|prod, gates?: {build?, validate?, upgradeGates?, devSoak?: ReleaseGate {ok,
at, sha256, summary}}, builtFrom?: {appliance, whombat?, app?, contracts?}, knownIssues?: string ≤ 300 [] ≤ 20}` — not
signed (the tuple is). `operator.registerRelease` takes an optional `record` next to the tuple; `PUT
/operator/releases/:release/record` (`operator.setReleaseRecord`, `releases.write`) stores records as they arrive stage
by stage: members given replace, absent ones stay, `gates` merges gate by gate. `ReleaseRecord` is a tolerant object in
both the bodies and the answers (a newer pipeline's extra member is stripped by an older control rather than refusing
the stage). `RegisteredRelease` gains optional `record`, `versions {host, runtime, manager}`, `schemaWrites` and
`createdAt`.

## CT-140 Rollouts with safety (UP-E1, UP-E2, UP-E6) (2026-09-28)

`ROLLOUT_PRESETS` (`rollout.ts`): `default` = `internal` 100 % 3600 s, `pilot` 100 % 21 600 s, `canary` 100 % 43 200 s,
`general` 1000 bp 86 400 s, `general` 10 000 bp 0 s; `all-at-once` = one wave of the four cohorts, 10 000 bp, 0 s; every
wave `failureThresholdBp 0`, `minSample 1`. Cohort ids are the kind names control uses. `RolloutWaveInput` is the
create body's wave. `ROLLOUT_PAUSE_REASONS` documents `operator`, `failure_threshold`, `device_failed`,
`health_regression`, `quarantined` (the set stays open, `Ident`). `Rollout.pauseDetail` (optional, nullable):
`{device | null, reason, failureDetail | null, at}`. `GET /operator/rollouts/:rollout/devices`
(`operator.rolloutDevices`, `fleet.read`) → `{devices: RolloutDevice[] ≤ 10 000}` with `{device, org, cohort, wave,
state, attempt, failure, failureDetail, hold, managerVersion, updatedAt}`; `hold` is open, the known values
`manager_too_old` (UP-E6), `failed_before`, `not_older` (UP-X03), `emergency_stop`, `quarantined`.

## CT-141 Fleet, alerts and pending re-registrations (UP-B4, UP-G2, UP-E5) (2026-09-28)

`GET /operator/fleet` (`operator.fleet`, `fleet.read`) → `FleetSummary {generatedAt, devices {total, live, unseen24h},
releases [{release, devices, apiLevel | null, managerVersions ≤ 16}], rollouts (open), alerts {open, critical}}`.
`OperatorAlert {id, kind, severity, subject ≤ 120, detail ≤ 500, openedAt, lastSeenAt, resolvedAt, acknowledgedAt,
acknowledgedBy}` with `OPERATOR_ALERT_KINDS` (`rollout_paused`, `rollout_stopped`, `device_update_failed`,
`device_unseen`, `tuf_timestamp_stale`, `tuf_expiring`, `client_channel_expiring`, `backup_failing`): `GET
/operator/alerts?state=open|all` (`operator.alerts`, `fleet.read`, open by default), `POST /operator/alerts/:alert/ack`
(`operator.ackAlert`, `fleet.write`; idempotent; an acknowledged alert stays open until its condition clears).
`PendingRegistration {id, existingDevice, existingState, attempts, firstAt, lastAt}`: `GET /operator/registrations`
(`operator.registrations`, `fleet.read`) and `POST /operator/registrations/:id/retire-existing {reason}`
(`operator.retireExisting`, `fleet.write`) → the retired device as `operator.device` answers it. New reasons
`alert_not_found`, `registration_not_found`. Every endpoint is in `operatorApi`, so the panel's typed client has it.

## CT-142 Backup destinations beyond the REST server (UP-F1) (2026-09-28)

`BackupConfigureDestinationInput` gains optional `s3AccessKeyId`, `s3SecretAccessKey`, `s3Region`, `sftpUser` and
`sftpHostKey` (a known_hosts-style line to pin; absent: trust on first use). The repository stays credential-free
(still no `@`): `rest:https://…`, `s3:https://host/bucket/path`, `sftp:host:/path` or `sftp://host:port//path` (the user
separate; CT-146), and exactly
`disk:` for the disk labelled `WHOMBAT-BACKUP` (the backup service maps it). The output gains optional `kind`
(`BackupDestinationKind`: `rest | s3 | sftp | disk | local`) and `hostKeyFingerprint`. `backup.sshPublicKey` (owners, a
query, not a secret op: the key is public; made on the first call) answers `BackupSshPublicKey {publicKey (an
authorized_keys line, `ssh-ed25519 … whombat-backup@<applianceId>`), fingerprint (`SHA256:…`)}`; the runtime reads it
from the backup service at `GET /v1/ssh-public-key` (`BACKUP_PATHS.sshPublicKey`). `BackupRecoveryMaterial` gains the
optional `s3AccessKeyId`, `s3SecretAccessKey`, `s3Region`, `sftpUser`, `sftpPrivateKey` (≤ 8000) and `sftpHostKey`, so
the kit reaches the repository from another machine. The runtime passes the op's input unchanged as `PUT
/v1/destination`'s body; the backup service's own Go struct gains the same members. A client offers the new kinds only
to a runtime with the feature `backup.destinations` (CT-136): an older runtime refuses the unknown members (strict
input).

## CT-143 Contracts 0.22.0: robust updates (the appliance's robust-updates UP-A…UP-G) (2026-09-28)

One minor release for the robust-updates workstream (`docs/decisions/updates.md` in the appliance repository): CT-135
(version order, the exit-0 floors check), CT-136 (tolerant decoding, API level 22, runtime features, `welcome.runtime`,
the release manifest's level and features), CT-137 (update failure detail), CT-138 (waiting, last update, the owner's
release summary), CT-139 (release records), CT-140 (wave presets, pause detail, rollout devices), CT-141 (fleet,
alerts, re-registrations) and CT-142 (S3, SFTP and disk backup destinations). Everything is additive; no signed or
hashed document changes (tuple digests in `compat.json` are unchanged).

Order of adoption: device bodies and control request bodies are strict (CT-14), so control moves to 0.22 before a
manager built from 0.22 reports `runtimeVersion` or `failureDetail` and before the pipeline sends a release `record`
(a 0.21 control answers 400). Everything else tolerates skew: older runtimes strip the new facts members, older
clients strip `welcome.runtime`, 0.22 clients count a runtime without it as level 21 (inside their window) with
`LEGACY_FEATURES`, and offer the new backup destinations only to runtimes with `backup.destinations`. This is the
first minor that doesn't need runtime, web and Android to ship together. Every package is 0.22.0.

## CT-144 Contracts 0.22.1: control can offer a custody rollback (robust-updates security review, UP-B2, UP-X03) (2026-09-28)

Control's version-based `notOlder` (UP-X03) never assigns a release older than the one a device runs, and control
doesn't see the TUF-signed `allowDowngradeFrom`, so a custody rollback (UP-B2) could never reach a box. `ReleaseRecord`
gains the optional `allowDowngradeFrom: ReleaseId[] ≤ 16`, which the publisher copies from the release's TUF-signed
`custom.whombat.allowDowngradeFrom` (with `registerRelease {record}` or `setReleaseRecord`). Control uses it only to
*offer* the older release to devices currently on one of those ids; it is not an authorisation. The box still
verifies the TUF-signed list itself (the helper's and manager's `CheckForward`), so control alone can never downgrade a
device, and a record that lists more than the signed metadata does changes nothing on a box. `ReleaseRecord` is
TypeScript only (no Go, JSON Schema or vector change). A patch release; every package is 0.22.1.

## CT-145 Contracts 0.22.2: the recovery kit names the newest checkpoint (the appliance's backup security review I-2) (2026-09-28)

`BackupRecoveryMaterial` gains the optional `head: {seq, manifestSha256, at}` — the newest checkpoint the appliance
knows when the kit's material is read: its sequence number, the sha256 of its manifest (lowercase hex) and its time
(`Rfc3339`, which already takes up to nine fractional digits, as Go's `RFC3339Nano` writes them; a test pins it). A
restore from the kit alone can then tell a destination that withholds the newest checkpoints; restores work without it
(kits and backup services before 0.22.2). `BackupRecoveryMaterial` is TypeScript only (no Go, JSON Schema or vector
change: the backup service keeps its own struct). A patch release; every package is 0.22.2.

## CT-146 Contracts 0.22.3: restic's SFTP repository forms (the appliance's backup, CT-142) (2026-09-28)

`BackupConfigureDestinationInput`'s doc comment named a form restic doesn't have (`sftp:host:port:/path`). restic's
SFTP repositories are `sftp:host:/path` and, with a port, `sftp://host:port//path`; the user is always `sftpUser`, never
in the repository (still no `@`). A client composing the repository from host, port and path uses the second form for
a port other than 22. `session.json` gains a case for it. Doc and vector only, no shape change; 0.22.2 was already
released (release directories are immutable, CT-03), so this is a patch of its own. Every package is 0.22.3.

## CT-147 Contracts 0.22.4: retryable failures, waiting in device reports, stalled rollouts, retrying a device (robust-updates operations review) (2026-09-28)

All additive and optional.

- **`RETRYABLE_UPDATE_FAILURES`** (`@whombat/release`, Go `release.RetryableUpdateFailures`) with
  `isRetryableUpdateFailure(code)` (Go `IsRetryableUpdateFailure`): the manager's failure codes that mean “this box
  can’t right now; it retries by itself” and never a bad release — the failures in
  `manager/internal/update/engine.go` that count no attempt and carry their own retry time: `no_space`,
  `not_assigned`, `not_staged`, `boundary_lost`, `checkpoint_stale`, `checkpoint_required`, `activation_deferred`.
  Control shouldn't pause a rollout, open a `device_update_failed` alert or set `failed_before` for them. `compat.json`
  → `retryable` keeps the two lists equal.
- **Waiting in device reports:** `DeviceStatusReport.update.waiting` and `UpdateProgressReport.waiting`, optional
  `UpdateWaitingReport = z.strictObject({reason: UpdateWaitReason, since: EpochSeconds})` — codes and a time only (the
  report allowlist; the blockers stay on the box in `UpdateFacts.waiting`). Go `device.UpdateWaitingReport`. As with
  CT-137, control moves to 0.22.4 before a manager sends it (strict bodies).
- **Operator:** `OPERATOR_ALERT_KINDS` gains `rollout_stalled` (an active rollout that hasn't moved for longer than its
  window allows); `FleetSummary.alerts.mail` (optional: whether control mails alerts); `FleetSummary.devices
  .backupUnconfigured` (optional: claimed devices whose last report says no destination); `RolloutDevice.waiting`
  (optional `{reason, since}`). `POST /operator/devices/:device/retry` (`operator.retryDevice`, `fleet.write`, strict
  body `{release, reason}`) → `RolloutDevice`: clears the device's sticky `failed_before` hold for that release so its
  next poll may get it again, once the cause was dealt with on the box; refuses `device_not_found`,
  `release_not_found` (404) and the new `nothing_to_retry` (409). It only lifts control's hold: a manager that
  quarantined the release itself (same digest) still refuses the assignment, so a retry reaches boxes whose release
  failed without a local quarantine.

Every package is 0.22.4.

## CT-148 Contracts 0.23.0: rich messages, subscription usage, agent card copy (Whombat ui-improvements, workstream C) (2026-09-29)

One minor release for John's eight UI items of 2026-09-29 (`docs/implementation/ui-improvements/assignment.md` in the
Whombat repository): the Markdown parser's tables, task lists, heading levels and code previews (CT-149, CT-150), the
message text limit (CT-151), attachment previews and AVIF (CT-152), subscription usage (CT-153…CT-156), the session
API level and runtime features (CT-157) and agent card copy (CT-158). Every package is 0.23.0.

Order of adoption: everything is additive except the message text limit (CT-151): a client before 0.23 validates
`Message.text` at 8000 characters, so it fails to decode a page of messages that holds a longer one. Hosted web and the
Android app move to 0.23 no later than the runtimes that accept long messages; runtimes advertise `messages.long`.
The runner and the server of one runtime release ship together, so `SIGNIN_METHODS.usageProbe` (an enum member the
runner's poll parses strictly) needs no gate.

## CT-149 Markdown: GitHub tables, task lists, heading levels, nested quotes, code previews (2026-09-29)

`parseMessage` (`@whombat/core/text`, `markdown.ts`) stays pure, forgiving and chat-flavoured (a single newline is a
break; a list, a table, an SVG or an HTML page may start right under a line of text). Additions, all positional plain
data (the same text gives the same tree, so clients may key rendered blocks by index):

- **Headings** carry `level: 1…6` (`HeadingLevel`). `#channel` without a space stays text; seven hashes stay text.
- **Task items**: `- [ ] x` / `- [x] x` / `- [X] x`. `ListBlock.checked?: (boolean | null)[]`, one entry per item
  (null: an ordinary item), present only when at least one item is a task; the marker is not in the item's text.
  Clients show read-only checkboxes.
- **Tables**: a header row with a pipe, a delimiter row with the same number of cells (`---`, `:--` left, `:-:` center,
  `--:` right; outer pipes optional), then rows until a blank line, a line without a pipe, a fence, heading or quote.
  `TableBlock {type: 'table', align: TableAlign[], header: Inline[][], rows: Inline[][][]}`; every row has exactly
  the header's number of cells (missing cells empty, extra ones dropped, as GitHub does). `\|` is a pipe in a cell,
  and a pipe inside a code span does not split (more forgiving than GitHub). A table may interrupt a paragraph (chat).
- **Nested quotes** (`> >`, `>>`) already parsed recursively; now tested.
- **Fences** accept an info string after the language (```` ```ts title="a.ts" ```` → `lang: 'ts'`), as CommonMark.
- **`CodeBlock.preview?: 'svg' | 'html' | 'mermaid'`** (`CodePreview`), present only when a client may show more than
  code, decided by the exported `codePreview(lang, text)`: `svg` for a standalone SVG document in `svg` (and, as
  before, `xml`/`html`/`htm`/no language, then `lang` is `svg`); `html` for `html`/`htm`/`xhtml` holding a page or a
  fragment with at least one tag that is not just an SVG document, and for a fence without a language holding a page
  (then `lang` is `html`); `mermaid` for a non-empty `mermaid` fence up to `MERMAID_PREVIEW_MAX` (50 000, mermaid's
  own `maxTextSize`). `lang` keeps the case it was written in (`HTM`), except the `svg`/`html` normalisations above.
- **Raw HTML pages**: a paragraph from a line starting with `<!DOCTYPE html` or `<html` (after comments) to the first
  line ending in `</html>`, blank lines included, is `{type: 'code', lang: 'html', preview: 'html'}`. A `<!DOCTYPE
  html` page without `</html>` runs to the end of the message (browsers render truncated pages); an `<html` line
  without it stays text (“<html> is the root element”). At most `HTML_PREVIEW_MAX` characters.
- `plainMessageText`: an HTML page is `[page: <title>]` or `[page]`, a Mermaid diagram `[diagram]`, a table its rows
  with cells joined by ` | `, task items `☐` / `☑` after the bullet.

## CT-150 HTML helpers for previews (2026-09-29)

`@whombat/core/text` (`html.ts`): `isHtmlDocument(text)` (after a BOM, whitespace and comments: `<!DOCTYPE html` or
`<html`), `isHtmlPreviewable(text)` (a document, or a fragment with a tag, not just an SVG), `htmlTitle(html)` (the
`<title>` before `<body` or the first `<svg`, so an inline SVG's `<title>` never names the page; entities decoded,
whitespace collapsed, at most `HTML_TITLE_MAX` = 200 characters with `…`; null when absent or empty) and
`HTML_PREVIEW_MAX` = 512 KiB characters (attachments may be larger than a message). They only recognise and describe;
nothing sanitises: the security boundary is the client's sandboxed frame (`sandbox="allow-scripts"` without
`allow-same-origin`, its own CSP with `connect-src 'none'`, assignment item 8).

## CT-151 Message text: 48 000 characters within 48 KiB of JSON (2026-09-29)

`MESSAGE_MAX_LENGTH` was 8000, too short for an agent's HTML page (20–60 KB). It can't simply become 64 KiB: over a
managed appliance's session a message travels in one CONTROL message of at most 64 KiB (`SESSION_MAX_CONTROL_BYTES`)
— `messages.send`'s outcome and the `message.created`/`message.updated` events carry the whole text, and a larger one
fails to encode (the outcome becomes `too_large`, the event is dropped). So:

- `MESSAGE_MAX_LENGTH` = 48 000 (UTF-16 code units) and `MESSAGE_MAX_JSON_BYTES` = 48 KiB: the text as a JSON string
  (UTF-8, quotes and escapes counted; `messageTextJsonBytes(text)`) leaves 16 KiB for the envelope, ten attachments
  and reactions. `messageTextFits(text)` checks both. In practice an inline HTML page of about 40 KB fits.
- `MessageTextInput` (trimmed, both limits, message `MESSAGE_TOO_LONG` = “That message is too long.”) is the text of
  `SendMessageBody` and of the MCP `post_message` / `reply_in_thread` tools (whose description now says HTML and
  Mermaid preview and “post a larger page as an .html file with upload_file”). `post_card` keeps 8000 (the card carries
  the rest). `Message.text` (output) checks only the length.
- The runtime validates with its own copy of the rule (`apps/server/src/commands/messages.ts`,
  `domain/messages.ts` compare with `MESSAGE_MAX_LENGTH`): it must use `MessageTextInput` / `messageTextFits` so the
  byte limit applies too, and truncations that assumed 8000 (`github/mirror.ts`, `commands/prs.ts`) may stay.
- A larger page goes as an attachment (`upload_file`, up to 10 MB), previewed the same way (CT-152).
- Skew: see CT-148 (old clients fail on pages holding long messages); runtime feature `messages.long` (CT-157).

## CT-152 Attachment previews without a new kind; AVIF (2026-09-29)

`AttachmentKind` (`image | text | document | file`) is a closed enum that clients before 0.23 parse strictly inside
every `Message`; a new member would make them fail on any message carrying it. It stays as it is. How a client shows
an attachment follows from its sniffed `contentType`, `kind` and name: `attachmentPreview({name, contentType, kind})`
(`@whombat/core/text`, `media.ts`) → `'image' | 'svg' | 'html' | 'mermaid' | 'pdf' | 'audio' | 'video' | 'text' |
null` (null: a download chip). The extension decides only where the sniffed type can't (`''`,
`application/octet-stream`, and for `html`/`svg`/`mermaid` also `text/plain`, `text/xml`, `application/xml`): an
`.html` file the sniffer calls `text/plain` is an HTML page; a `text/plain` file named `a.png` is text.
`contentTypeForName(name)` / `MEDIA_TYPES_BY_EXTENSION`, `baseContentType`, `PREVIEW_IMAGE_TYPES` (png, jpeg, gif,
webp, avif), `PREVIEW_AUDIO_TYPES` (mpeg, mp4, aac, ogg, opus, wav, webm, flac), `PREVIEW_VIDEO_TYPES` (mp4, webm, ogg,
quicktime). `contentType` (≤ 120 characters) already represents every audio and video type. For the runtime: store
`text/html` for `.html`/`.htm` text uploads (and `image/avif`, `audio/*`, `video/*` from the bytes or the name) so
old clients' download names and new clients' previews agree; AVIF stays kind `file` (models don't take it as image
input) and still previews as an image. `isSafeImageSrc` accepts `data:image/avif` too.

## CT-153 Subscription usage snapshots (2026-09-29)

`@whombat/core/domain` (`usage.ts`), for Whombat assignment item 7 (names agreed with the runtime workstream R):

- `UsageProvider` = `claude | codex`; `UsageWindowKind` = `five_hour | seven_day | seven_day_opus | seven_day_sonnet
  | other` (clients drop unknown kinds through tolerant decoding); `UsageStatus` = `ok | warning | limited`.
- `UsageWindow {kind, label (1–80), usedPct (0–100 | null), resetsAt (Timestamp | null), status, windowMinutes?
  (int | null)}` — Codex reports windows by length (`usageWindowKindForMinutes`: 300 → `five_hour`, 10 080 →
  `seven_day`, else `other`), Claude by name. At most `USAGE_WINDOWS_MAX` = 8.
- `SubscriptionUsage {principalId, name, provider, kind: subscription | api_key, connected, plan (≤ 64 | null),
  windows, observedAt (null before the first probe), source: probe | turn | null, error (≤ 300 | null)}`: the latest
  snapshot of one person's sign-in for one provider, no history. An API key has no windows (“Pay as you go — see
  Spend”). Keyed by the person in the burrow, not the account: burrow screens show people.

## CT-154 Usage endpoints and event (2026-09-29)

- `usage.list` — `GET /burrows/:burrow/usage` → `{mine: SubscriptionUsage[] (≤ 4), everyone: SubscriptionUsage[] (≤
  1024) | null}`. Every member gets their own; owners (and admins of a self-hosted Whombat) also get everyone's in the
  burrow; `everyone` is null for members.
- `usage.refresh` — `POST /burrows/:burrow/usage/refresh` `{provider}` (strict) → `{usage}`: probes the caller's own
  sign-in now. At most once a minute per subscription (`USAGE_REFRESH_MIN_INTERVAL_MS`): sooner answers 429
  `rate_limited` with `details: UsageRefreshTooSoon {retryAfter}` (seconds); no sign-in for the provider is 404
  `not_found`. Both are `api` endpoints, so managed appliances serve them as session ops `usage.list` /
  `usage.refresh` (non-secret; `usage.refresh` is mutating).
- `usage.updated {usage: SubscriptionUsage}` realtime event, topic `me` only (`REALTIME_EVENT_TOPICS`): the
  subscription owner's and each burrow owner's and admin's `me:<principalId>`, never `burrow:` (members must not see
  each other's usage). Older clients skip the unknown event type.

## CT-155 The runner reads usage (2026-09-29)

- `SIGNIN_METHODS.usageProbe` (server → runner over `signin.poll` / `signin.answer`, like the sign-in steps): params
  `{owner: {kind: 'person', accountId}, provider}`, result `{ok: true, usage: ProbeUsage} | SignInFailure`.
  `ProbeUsage {provider, kind, plan (≤ 64 | null), windows (≤ 8), observedAt, error (≤ 300 | null)}`. The runner asks
  the unmodified CLI in the person's own credential home (Claude Code's stream-json `control_request` `get_usage` with
  `skip_behaviors: true`, no model turn; Codex app-server `account/rateLimits/read`), never its credential files
  (SUB-03). Only people's sign-ins (subscriptions are personal, SUB-04).
- `TurnRateLimits {provider, plan, windows, observedAt}`, optional `ProgressBody.rateLimits` and
  `CompleteBody.rateLimits`: what the provider reported during a turn (Claude `rate_limit_event.rate_limit_info`,
  Codex `account/rateLimits/updated`), normalised by the runner (`usagePct(value, 'fraction')` for Claude's 0–1
  `unifiedWindows`); the server stores it as the snapshot with `source: turn`. Older servers ignore it.

## CT-156 Usage levels, probing, alerts and copy (2026-09-29)

Pure helpers so the runtime, web and mobile agree:

- Levels: `USAGE_WARNING_PCT` 80, `USAGE_CRITICAL_PCT` 95, `USAGE_THRESHOLDS`; `usageLevel(pct)` → `ok | warning |
  critical | null`; `usageStatus(pct, limited)` → `UsageStatus` (≥ 100 % is `limited`); `windowLevel(w)`;
  `usagePct(value, 'fraction' | 'percent')` (clamped, one decimal); `USAGE_WINDOW_LABELS`; `sortUsageWindows`,
  `primaryUsageWindow` (the 5-hour window, else the fullest: the compact meter in Settings → General).
- Probing: `USAGE_PROBE_ACTIVE_MS` 15 min while used in the last `USAGE_ACTIVE_WITHIN_MS` 24 h, `USAGE_PROBE_IDLE_MS`
  1 h otherwise (`nextUsageProbeAt(observedAt, lastUsedAt, now)`); `USAGE_STALE_AFTER_MS` 20 min (`isUsageStale`):
  older snapshots show “as of 14:32”.
- Alerts: `usageAlertLevel(w)` → `80 | 95 | 'limited' | null`; `usageAlertKey(sub, w, level)` =
  `<principal>:<provider>:<window>:<resetsAt|none>:<level>` makes an alert once per window per level until the window
  resets (a new `resetsAt` is a new window); `dueUsageAlert(sub, w, wasSent)` → `{level, key, markSent}`, where
  `markSent` covers the lower levels too (70 % → 97 % says 95 % once, never 80 % afterwards). The runtime stores sent
  keys.
- Copy (`@whombat/core/text`, `usage.ts`; the reader's time zone, 24-hour clock like the rest of the product; a
  percentage is the number, a no-break space and `%`, `NBSP`): `formatUsagePct` (“85 %”, “<1 %”, “—”),
  `formatUsageSpan` / `formatResetsIn` (“resets in 2 h 10 min”, “resets in 45 min”, “resets in 3 d 4 h”, “resets
  now”), `formatResetTime` (“16:00”, “Thu 09:00”, “3 Oct”), `formatAsOf` (“as of 14:32”, “as of 28 Sep, 14:32”, “not
  read yet”), `formatUsageWindowLine` (“5-hour · 85 % · resets in 2 h 10 min”, “limit reached”), `usageSummaryText`,
  `USAGE_PAY_AS_YOU_GO` (“Pay as you go — see Spend”), `USAGE_PROVIDER_LABELS` (Claude, Codex) and
  `usageAlertText({level, provider, window, personName, forOwner, now, timeZone})`: “Your Claude subscription is at
  85 % of its 5-hour limit, resets at 16:00.”, “Jamie’s Claude subscription is at 96 % of its 7-day limit, resets Fri
  09:00.”, “Your Codex subscription hit its 5-hour limit, resets at 16:00. Turns on it wait until then.” The runtime's
  assistant posts it; `personName` is the owner's short name.

## CT-159 Contracts 0.24.0: a shared own sign-in; feature `signins.shared` (2026-09-30)

John, 2026-09-30 (Whombat SUB-57, SUB-58): an owner may share their own Claude or Codex sign-in with everyone, as an
override the app marks as against the providers' terms, and a feedback assessment runs on the sign-in of the owner who
set the integration up. `CredentialSource`'s `account` member gains `shared: true` (optional; absent = personal, as
before; `false` isn't a value, so one source has one spelling). The runtime lets only that account's own person set it
and runs everyone's requests on it; `DispatchCredential` is unchanged (its `source` carries the flag).

Skew: an older runtime's parser drops the flag, so the sign-in stays personal there (the safe side). The runtime

## CT-160 Contracts 0.25.0: Feedback's navigation trail and reporter sign-in (2026-09-30)

John, 2026-09-30 (Whombat `docs/implementation/feedback-reporters/assignment.md`, decisions FR-*): the widget sends the
visitor's last 10 page views on the site with a report, and a visitor may sign in with their email address and a
6-digit code, so their reports are marked “Email verified” and “Your reports” shows how each is going. Reporting
without signing in stays. These supersede, for these features only, the Feedback non-goals (no customer login, status
endpoint or customer email) and the frame's storage ban. 0.25.0 brings the shapes for every consumer: the runtime
(self-hosted routes, the managed drop and publisher), control (the managed routes and the device op), the manager
(forwarding) and the widget (loader, frame). CT-161…CT-165 say what each part adds. Every package is 0.25.0.

Deploy order stays **control before the embed widget before boxes**: control parses cards strictly, so a card whose
`config` has `trail`/`reporters` is refused by an older control (CT-161, CT-162).

## CT-161 The navigation trail (2026-09-30)

- `FeedbackTrailStep = strictObject({url, title, at})`: `url` the page URL sanitized like `page.url` (origin + path,
  1…`FEEDBACK_CONTEXT_LIMITS.url`), `title` ≤ `LIMITS.title` or null (default null), `at` the visitor's clock
  (`Timestamp`). `FEEDBACK_TRAIL_MAX = FEEDBACK_CONTEXT_LIMITS.trail = 10`: the limit also lives in the import-free
  `feedback/sanitize`, so the loader caps with the same number.
- `FeedbackContext.trail` (optional, ≤ 10, oldest first, the page sent from last). It lives in `context`, so the
  submission, the sealed drop, redaction, payload hashing, storage and the runner's `FeedbackDispatchContext` carry it
  without a new member. The runner and the server are one box release, so the runner's strict context is never older.
- **Answers lift it out.** `FeedbackContext` is strict, and clients parse report answers with it: a 0.24 web would
  refuse a whole `FeedbackReport` whose `context` held `trail`. So `FeedbackReport.submitted` gains
  `trail: FeedbackTrailStep[] ≤ 10` (default `[]`, older runtimes) and the runtime's read side moves
  `context.trail` there, leaving `submitted.context` without it. This departs from the assignment's “no new member” for
  the read projection only; storage is unchanged.
- `FeedbackIntegrationSettings.trail: FeedbackSwitch` (`'on' | 'off'`, default `'on'`), so stored settings without it
  parse. `FeedbackPublicConfig.trail?: boolean`: the frame sends `context.trail` only when it is true; absent means
  false, which is how a newer widget recognises an older runtime (and an older runtime never sees a trail).
- `WIDGET_ATTRIBUTES.trail = 'data-trail'`: `"off"` stops the loader recording and removes a stored trail; the snippet
  adds it when the integration's trail is off.
- Known skew, accepted: an older client that edits an integration sends settings without `trail`/`reporterSignIn`, and
  the defaults turn both back on. Both default on and the web offers the switches only with `feedback.reporters`
  (CT-165), so this needs an owner who turned one off in a new web and then saved in an old one.

## CT-162 Reporter sign-in: requests, answers, errors, limits (2026-09-30)

The same shapes on the runtime's `/embed/v1/sites/:site/reporter/…` (self-hosted, same-origin; `FEEDBACK_PUBLIC_PATHS`
`reporterCode`, `reporterSession`, `reporterReports`) and control's `/v1/feedback/sites/:site/reporter/…` (managed,
CT-164). All in `@whombat/core/domain`:

- `FeedbackReporterEmail`: trimmed, lower-cased (the parse does it, equal to `normalizeReporterEmail`), ≤ 254, the same
  `.email()` check as `FeedbackSubmission.reporter.email`, so an address that can sign in can also be sent.
- `FeedbackReporterCodeRequest {email, parent}` → 202 `FeedbackReporterOk {ok: true}` always (no hint whether a code
  was sent). `FeedbackReporterSessionRequest {email, code: /^[0-9]{6}$/, parent}` → `FeedbackReporterSession {token:
  /^fbrs_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/, email, expiresAt}`; DELETE with the bearer → 204. `FeedbackReporterReports {email,
  reports ≤ 200}` newest first, each `FeedbackReporterReport {reference, type, status, receivedAt, updatedAt, summary
  ≤ 140 | null}`. `FeedbackReporterStatus` = received, reviewing, needs_info, confirmed, in_progress, fixed, closed.
  All strict: the frame reads them without Zod, and a newer member would be a new shape. `FeedbackReporterToken` is
  the bearer's schema.
- `FeedbackPublicErrorCode` gains `code_refused` (400, “That code didn’t work. Check it or ask for a new one.”; one
  answer for every failed sign-in: wrong, expired, used, too many tries, unknown address) and `signed_out` (401, “Your
  sign-in has ended. Sign in again.”).
- `FeedbackIntegrationSettings.reporterSignIn: FeedbackSwitch` (default `'on'`); `FeedbackPublicConfig.reporters?:
  boolean` (absent = false; self-hosted it is false without mail).
- `FeedbackReport.submitted.reporter.verified: boolean`, default false on read (older runtimes' answers parse).
- Limits (in `feedback/reporters`, CT-163): `FEEDBACK_REPORTER_CODE_TTL_S` 600, `…_CODE_ATTEMPTS` 5 (the fifth wrong
  try ends the code), `…_CODES_PER_HOUR` 5 per site + email, `…_CODES_PER_NETWORK_PER_HOUR` 30, and, decided here,
  `…_SESSIONS_PER_NETWORK_PER_HOUR` 60 sign-in attempts per network (5 codes × 5 tries per address leave room for a
  few addresses behind one NAT, while guessing stays at 25 tries per address per hour against 10^6 codes),
  `…_RESEND_S` 30 (“Send a new code”), `…_SESSION_TTL_S` 30 days (not renewed by use: a sign-in lasts at most 30
  days), `…_REPORTS_MAX` 200, `…_SUMMARY_MAX` 140, `…_EMAIL_MAX` 254.

## CT-163 `@whombat/core/feedback/reporters`: the pure helpers (2026-09-30)

A new subpath (also in `@whombat/core/feedback` and the root), Zod-free like `feedback/drop` so the frame and loader
can bundle it: only `@noble/hashes` and type imports. `conformance/src/widget-safe.test.ts` now checks all three
widget subpaths (`sanitize`, `drop`, `reporters`) import nothing else at runtime, following relative files.

- `reporterStatusOf({status, assessmentState, assessmentOutcome})`: `resolved` → fixed, `closed` → closed,
  `in_progress` → in_progress, `triaged` → confirmed; `new`: assessment `running` → reviewing (checked first, so a
  re-assessment reads as being looked at), else a recorded outcome `needs_information`/`insufficient_evidence` →
  needs_info, `confirmed_bug`/`likely_bug`/`duplicate`/`feature_request` → confirmed, any other outcome → reviewing,
  no outcome → received; an unknown status → received. The owners' status wins over the assessment.
- `normalizeReporterEmail` (trim, `toLowerCase`) and `reporterEmailDigest(site, email)` = lower-case hex sha256 of
  `"whombat-feedback-reporter/1\n" + site + "\n" + normalized email` (vector in the tests).
- Decided here, so both stores agree: `reporterCodeMac(key, site, email, code)` = hex HMAC-SHA256 under the storer's
  secret of `"whombat-feedback-reporter-code/1\n" + site + "\n" + email + "\n" + code` (a keyed code, never the plain
  one; control derives its key from the discovery key, the runtime from its own secret), `reporterDigestEqual`
  (constant time), `newReporterCode` (6 uniform digits, rejection sampling), `newReporterToken` (`fbrs_` + 32 random
  bytes), `reporterTokenHash` (hex sha256, what is stored), `newReporterId` (`fbr_` + 16 bytes), `reporterTokenFrom
  (authorization)` (the `Bearer` token or null) and the patterns `FEEDBACK_REPORTER_CODE_PATTERN`, `…_TOKEN_PATTERN`,
  `…_ID_PATTERN`.
- `reporterSummaryOf(description)`: whitespace collapsed, ≤ 140 UTF-16 units with “…” when cut, never splitting a
  surrogate pair (the runtime's `summary`; the frame's local one).
- Copy: `REPORTER_STATUS_COPY` (bug: Received, Being looked at, Needs more information, Confirmed, In progress, Fixed,
  Closed; feature: Noted for confirmed, Done for fixed), `REPORTER_TYPE_COPY` (Problem, Idea) and
  `reporterCodeEmail({code, productLabel, parent})` → `{subject, text}`, the code email verbatim with the parent's host
  (and port), so the runtime's mailer and control's say the same.

## CT-164 Control and the device API for reporters (2026-09-30)

- `feedbackDropApi` gains `reporterCode` (`feedback.reporter.code`, POST, 202), `reporterSession`
  (`feedback.reporter.session`, POST), `reporterSignOut` (`feedback.reporter.signOut`, DELETE on the same path, 204)
  and `reporterReports` (`feedback.reporter.reports`, GET). Ids stay unique, so the DELETE has its own. All `auth:

  The drop POST takes an optional bearer: a valid session of the same site attests the drop, an invalid one is ignored.
  Control's reports answer has `summary: null` (it never holds report text; the frame shows its own).

  object like the rest of the pull answer; absent for anonymous drops and older controls.
- Device op `feedback.reporters.publish` (in `FEEDBACK_DEVICE_OPS`, so in `DEVICE_OPS`): body `{updates ≤ 100 of
  FeedbackReporterUpdate {site, reporterId, reference, type, status, receivedAt, updatedAt}, removals ≤ 100 of {site,
  reference}}` (strict, times epoch seconds as elsewhere in the device API; both lists may be empty) → `{ok: true}`.
  Control applies updates for the device's own sites only (others skipped silently), when `updatedAt` is not older
  than what it holds (equal overwrites, so a retry is harmless); removals delete (unknown ones ignored). A full
  request is well under `DEVICE_REQUEST_MAX_BYTES`, so it has no size exception. `FEEDBACK_REPORTERS_PUBLISH_MAX`
  (Go `FeedbackReportersPublishMax`).
- Local: `MANAGER_PATHS.feedbackReporters = '/v1/runtime/feedback/reporters'` (Go `ManagerPathFeedbackReporters`),
  `RuntimeFeedbackReportersRequest`/`Response` = the op's schemas; the same forwarding and error mapping as the three
  drop paths (older control → 501 `unsupported`; older manager → 404, treated like 501).
- Go regenerated: `FeedbackReportersPublishRequest`/`Response`, `FeedbackReporterUpdate`, `FeedbackReporterRemoval`,
  `FeedbackDropReporter`, the enums `FeedbackReportType` and `FeedbackReporterStatus` (re-exported from core so the
  names match), `DeviceOpNameFeedbackReportersPublish`. The digest stays TypeScript only; the manager just forwards.

`RUNTIME_FEATURES` gains `feedback.reporters` (`SINCE_0_25`): the web offers the trail and sign-in switches, and shows

## CT-166 Contracts 0.26.0: the essentials (Whombat essentials, stream C) (2026-09-30)

John, 2026-09-30 (Whombat `docs/implementation/essentials/assignment.md`, items 1–12 and 14): the contracts every other
stream (runtime R1–R3, web W1–W3, mobile M) builds on. CT-167…CT-184 say what each part adds and CT-184 lists every name
that differs from the assignment's proposal. Every package is 0.26.0; `SESSION_API_LEVEL` is 24 (CT-183).

Everything is additive: new fields are optional (older answers parse; older clients' tolerant objects strip them), and
new enum and union members (`ConversationKind` `direct`, `ConversationLink`/`LinkRef` `direct`, card `turn_failed`,
`NotificationKind` `direct`/`reply`, `DispatchTrigger` `approval_granted`/`retry`, `WorkAction` `retry_turn`, the push
kinds) are left out by older clients' tolerant decoding (CT-136) with the item that carries them. Two things are not
tolerant and need order: the runner parses `Dispatch.trigger` and `DispatchContext` strictly, so the runner and the server
of one runtime release ship together (they always do); and control is untouched (no device or local shape changed).

## CT-167 Failed turns: the `turn_failed` card, `dispatches.retry`, the classification (item 4) (2026-09-30)

- `TurnFailureCode` (`@whombat/core/domain`, `dispatch.ts`) = `signin | usage_limit | provider | sandbox | timeout | runner
  | workspace | internal`, as the assignment lists them. `TurnFailure {code, reason (1–200)}`, `TURN_FAILURE_REASON_MAX`
  200, `TURN_FAILURE_DETAIL_MAX` 2000.
- The runner classifies (both modes) and reports `CompleteBody.failure?: TurnFailureReport {code, resetsAt?: Timestamp |
  null}`; `error` stays the technical text. The server writes the sentence and classifies what the runner can't know
  (`runner` for a lost lease or no runner, `timeout`); an older runner sends no `failure` and the server says `internal`.
- Card `TurnFailedCard` `{kind: 'turn_failed', dispatchId, agentId, code, reason, retriedAt: Timestamp | null (default
  null), retryDispatchId: DispatchId | null (default null)}` in `MessageCard` and `StoredCard` (same shape stored; the
  server patches the two retry fields and sends `message.updated`), not `PostableCard` (server-made only), `CARD_KINDS`
  gains `turn_failed`. `canRetryTurn(card, agent, viewer)`: not retried yet, the viewer a person who may wake the agent
  (a personal agent: its owner only), the agent not retired.
- Endpoint `dispatches.retry` — `POST /burrows/:burrow/dispatches/:dispatchId/retry`, no body → `RetryDispatchResponse
  {dispatchId}` (status 200: get-or-create; a second press answers with the existing retry). New area `api.dispatches`,
  so a session op too. The new dispatch has trigger `retry` and `DispatchContext.retry: RetryContext {dispatchId, code,
  reason}` (the failed turn), so the agent knows it is trying again.
- `WorkAction` `retry_turn` (calls `dispatches.retry` with `refs.dispatchId`); `DispatchSummary.failure?: TurnFailure |
  null`; `WorkItem.failure?: WorkFailure {code, reason, detail (≤ 2000 | null), retriedAt, retryDispatchId}`. The
  technical detail goes in `WorkItem.failure.detail`, not `WorkItem.detail`: that one is 280 characters and older clients
  parse it strictly, so a longer value would break their whole Work view. `detail` is filled only for burrow owners and
  admins, redacted with `turnFailureDetail(raw)` (`redactSecrets`, control characters dropped, the last 2000 characters
  kept with a leading `…`, since errors say what broke at the end).

  14:32”.

`DispatchTrigger` gains `approval_granted`. The runtime queues it to the requesting agent in the approval's conversation
