## CT-190 Phone sign-in by QR code: a control handoff (2026-09-30)

John asked for a quick QR sign-in as the main way into the phone app. Signing a phone in takes two things: a cloud
session (today a magic link opened on the phone) and a trusted endpoint on the Whombat (today the phone shows a
pairing code that a trusted device types in). The QR code replaces both with one scan and one confirmation:

- `auth.createPhoneHandoff` (session): a one-time token (5 minutes, `PHONE_HANDOFF_TOKEN_TTL_S`) that the signed-in
  browser puts in the QR code, and a handoff id it watches (`auth.phoneHandoff`, only its own session, 15 minutes).
- `auth.redeemPhoneHandoff` (none): the phone's own cloud session on the same account, once, like `auth.verify`,
  plus the handoff id.
- `auth.reportPhoneHandoff` (session; only the session the token was redeemed for): the phone reports either the
  pairing request the Whombat gave it (`code` + `fingerprint` + `mac`) or that it needs nothing more (`signed_in`).

Control only relays. The report's `mac` is HMAC-SHA256 under a key the browser put in the QR code's fragment (never
sent to control), so control can't substitute another device's code; the browser still looks the code up on the
Whombat, compares the fingerprint and asks its person to confirm before `enroll.pair.approve`. No session operation
changes: pairing is the protocol's existing `enroll.pair.*`, so neither `SESSION_API_LEVEL` nor `RUNTIME_FEATURES`
moves, and this is a patch (0.26.1).

## CT-191 The Android APK is a control download (2026-09-30)

Until the app is in the stores, the hosted UI's “Mobile app” page links to a signed APK. Control serves it
(`downloads.android` metadata, the file under `/v1/downloads/android/<file>`): control already exists per environment
(DEV and PROD APKs differ in their control and UI origins), has configuration and runs on both hosts, while the
hosted UI's static root is rebuilt on every deploy. Public, no session: the file is the same for everyone.

John asked for Settings → “Repositories” with a way to create a new repository on the device (“Whombat_Website”),

## CT-193 The assessor's conclusion: reply, bug verdict, decision and the `assessment` card (contracts 0.28.0) (2026-09-30)

John, 2026-09-30, looking at Pepper's assessment of a feedback report: agents should sound like people. The assessor
answers with a short message in its own words; for a bug report it always says bug, not a bug or unsure; when it can't
settle what happens next it asks people with ready-made answers they click; the full assessment stays available, folded.
Owners' answers: a click acts for real, the assessor writes the labels freely, feature requests get the same treatment,
the verdict stays internal (the reporter's “Your reports” is unchanged).

- `submit_assessment` takes `FeedbackAssessmentSubmission`: every `FeedbackAssessment` field plus `reply` (1–700, the
  message people read), `bugVerdict` (`bug | not_a_bug | unsure | null`) and `decision` (`{question (1–300), options: 2–4
  × {label (1–60), action, recommended}} | null`). Rules on top of the assessment's own: `bug` needs observed evidence
  (as `confirmed_bug`); `bug` contradicts `feature_request` / `configuration_or_support`; `confirmed_bug` is `bug`;
  `likely_bug` isn't `not_a_bug`; at most one option recommended; labels distinct (case-insensitive). The runtime adds the
  one rule the schema can't know: a bug report needs a `bugVerdict`.
- `FeedbackDecisionAction` = `hand_off` (the existing development handoff: an approval the owners grant, FB-24; the
  label goes along as the asking person's note), `resolve`, `close`, `keep_open` (status `resolved`, `closed`,
  `triaged`: `FEEDBACK_DECISION_STATUS`). The assessor's words never choose an action: the option's fixed action does.
- The stored halves stay apart (`splitSubmission`): `FeedbackAssessment` is unchanged (it is a `strictObject` that older
  clients parse in `feedback.getReport`, so a new key there would break their report details) and the conclusion is a
  separate `FeedbackConclusion`. `FeedbackAssessmentStatus` gains `conclusion?` and `decided?`
  (`FeedbackDecisionChoice {option, label, action, decidedById, decidedAt}`), both optional and nullable (older
  runtimes, older assessments). `redactedConclusion` keeps the verdict and actions and removes the words (FB-F3-11).
- Card `AssessmentCard {kind: 'assessment', reportId, reference, type, status, assessment, bugVerdict, decision,
  decided, contentRemoved}`, stored as `{kind: 'assessment', reportId}` and resolved on read, in `MessageCard` /
  `StoredCard` / `CARD_KINDS`, not `PostableCard`. Helpers `assessmentCardLabel`, `assessmentHeadline`,
  `assessmentDetailRows`, `evidenceLine`, `FEEDBACK_BUG_VERDICT_LABELS`, `FEEDBACK_DECISION_ACTION_LABELS`,
  `FEEDBACK_REPRODUCTION_LABELS`.
- Endpoint `feedback.decide` `POST /burrows/:burrow/feedback/reports/:id/decision {option}` → `{report}`; `getReport`'s
  `can.decide?`. Feature `feedback.decisions`.
- The assessment types move to `domain/feedback-assessment.ts` (re-exported by `feedback.ts`, no name changes) so
  `cards.ts` can include the card without importing messages.
- `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 24 (as CT-159, CT-165, CT-192). The only union a session answer carries that grows is a
  server-made card kind, which older clients drop with CT-136's tolerant decoding while the message's text — the
  assessor's reply — still shows; everything else is optional or behind the feature name. A level 25 would send the
  level-22 runtimes to “needs an update” for nothing.

## CT-194 Retry safety is part of every operation's contract (contracts 0.29.0) (2026-09-30)

Until now a client decided what to do with a request whose answer it lost from the op's *name*: whombat-app's
`defaultIsDestructive` matched `DELETE` and a word list (`merge|deploy|decide|delete|remove|revoke|…`), and after
`status` answered `not_found` it resent everything else with the same id. So every mutation whose name didn't look
dangerous was treated as safe to resend — including ones that act outside the transaction their receipt is accepted
in — and every new op inherited that silently.

- **Two facts per op, on `OperationSpec`, from one table.** `destructive: boolean` (irreversible or high-impact: never
  sent again by a client on its own, a person decides) and `retry: OperationRetry` = `safe | receipt | never`:
  - `safe`: doesn't mutate — ask again. Exactly the non-mutating ops (a `secret` read such as `signins.consoleRead`
    included: reads have no receipt).
  - `receipt`: whatever the op does before its first commit-pipeline transaction is harmless to repeat, and that
    transaction marks the receipt `accepted` (MR-06). `not_found` then means it never committed — within the receipt
    retention and for a request never seen acknowledged (amendment below) — so the same request (same id, exact input)
    may be resent and the runtime runs it at most once.
  - `never`: not resent by itself. Rules: `secret` mutations (no input digest, no result, CT-44), ephemeral ops,
    export ops, and the `auth.*` ops sessions never carry (none has a receipt a retry could meet); every mutation on
    the enrollment channel (see below); and ops that act outside their receipt's transaction before committing.
  `OPERATION_SAFETY` (`session/operation-safety.ts`) is typed `Record<OperationName, OperationSafety>`, where
  `OperationName = ApiOpName | SessionOpName` and `SessionOpName` is the literal union of the session-native ops
  (`session()` keeps `op` literal). A missing or an extra entry fails typecheck, and `operation-safety.test.ts` checks
  the table covers exactly `API_OPERATIONS ∪ SESSION_OPERATIONS` plus the invariants: `safe` ⇔ not mutating; reads are
  never destructive; `receipt` ⇒ mutating, not ephemeral, not an export op, not secret (the runtime's receipt rule);
  secret/ephemeral/export/session-excluded mutations are `never`; the provider ops equal their `signins.*`
  equivalents; and every op the old heuristic called destructive still is.
- **How mutations were classified.** Each handler in the Whombat server was traced (routes, commands, services) for
  effects outside the receipt's transaction before its first commit. The runtime makes that window matter more than it
  looks: a session that closes cancels its requests that aren't accepted yet, and the cancel (like a passed deadline)
  rolls back the commit *after* the handler ran — exactly the lost-answer case. `never` beyond the rules:
  - `prs.merge`: merges on GitHub inside its `apply`, before the commit;
  - `repos.create`: creates the bare repository on disk (git) before the commit; a rerun is refused;
  - `signins.consoleStart`: starts `claude auth login` in a terminal and replaces the running one; no commit;
  - `enroll.claim`: consumes the claim's one-time PAKE state;
  - `enroll.claim` and `recovery.enroll`: the receipt is keyed `peer:<peerId>` while unenrolled and by the account once
    enrolled, so `status` can't find a committed one (the other enrollment-channel mutations are secret anyway);
  - `automations.webhook`: its answer can be a new webhook secret shown once, and it isn't a `secret` op (managed
    runtimes refuse it over a session).
  `receipt` although something happens before the commit, because it is harmless to repeat: content-addressed pack
  store writes (`packs.upload`, `packs.importLocal`, `packs.importBundled`, `skills.decide`, `agents.hire`,
  `onboarding.complete`), GitHub reads (`repos.add`, `repos.sync`, `github.connect`), read-only probes (`vault.check`,
  `connections.check`), in-memory flags and cancels (`host.recheckAgents`, `signins.loginCancel`,
  `providers.login.cancel`, `signins.consoleResize`, `signins.consoleCancel`), idempotent external calls (`clients.install`
  — the manager answers the running or installed client —, `licence.refresh`, sign-outs and removals). Work that only
  starts after the commit is `receipt` plainly: agent turns (`messages.send`), approved actions (`approvals.decide`),
  mail (`members.invite`), backups (`backup.runNow`), client installs (`onboarding.update`).
- **Destructive = at least the old heuristic** (every `DELETE`; `conversations.archive`, `prs.merge`,
  `approvals.decide`, `memory.decide`, `skills.decide`, `feedback.decide`, and the session ops revoking or removing),
  plus `agents.retire`, `feedback.redactReport`, `automations.cancelRun`, `automations.webhook` (it may replace the
  secret), `providers.logout` (as `signins.logout`), `recovery.kit.rotate`, `enroll.pair.approve` and
  `enroll.reenroll.confirm` (another device let in).
- **Clients.** `operationSafety(op)` (undefined for a name the build doesn't know) and `resendAfterNotFound(op)`:
  resend only a known, non-destructive `receipt` op. Unknown ops — a newer runtime's, any other name — are never
  resent. Clients prefer `status` and the stored outcome to resubmitting, always.
- **Advice, not authority.** The table is client-local: nothing is sent, it authorizes nothing and it makes nothing
  idempotent. The runtime's receipts (`(principal, op, requestId)` bound to `receiptDigest`) are what make a resend run
  at most once; the table only says where that covers everything an op does.
- **Versions.** No wire change, no feature name, `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 24: a new client with an older runtime and an
  older client with this one behave as before towards each other (an older client keeps its heuristic). Additive
  exports (`OPERATION_SAFETY`, `OPERATION_RETRIES`, `OperationRetry`, `OperationSafety`, `operationSafety`,
  `resendAfterNotFound`, `OperationName`, `SessionOpName`); `OperationSpec` gains two required fields, which only
  matters to code that builds specs itself (none does). Hence 0.29.0. Nothing reaches the generated Go or JSON Schema.
- **A new op** needs its entry to typecheck; the default a runtime-built spec falls back on (impossible past typecheck)
  is `safe` for a read and `never` for a mutation. When in doubt, `never`.

**Amendments after review (2026-09-30; doc-only, 0.29.0 is released unchanged):**

- **`not_found` is bounded.** A runtime sweeps finished receipts after `WHOMBAT_COMMAND_RECEIPT_HOURS` (7 days by
  default; `accepted` ones are kept). So `not_found` means “never committed” only within that retention and only for a
  request never acknowledged — no `accepted` frame, and no `status` answering `accepted` or `executing` (a runtime's
  `executing` may precede its commit; counting it is the safe side). After an acknowledgement it means the receipt
  expired: a client never resends then, as `nextCommandState` keeps `accepted` on `not_found`. `resendAfterNotFound`
  judges the op only; the acknowledgement is the client's to remember (whombat-app AP-574).
- **Six destructive `receipt` ops act before their commit; 0.29.1 makes them `never` (CT-195)**
  (`DESTRUCTIVE_NEVER`): `connections.remove` (revokes the Google grant first), `signins.logout` and `providers.logout`
  (the runner signs out and removes the credential home before the audit commit), `signins.orgRemove` and
  `providers.org.remove` (the same for an organization credential), `clients.remove` (the manager removes the client; no
  commit). For them `not_found` doesn't mean nothing happened, and repeating them later isn't harmless (a person may have
  reconnected, signed in or reinstalled meanwhile; a reconnected Google connection keeps its id). Nothing changes for
  clients meanwhile: they are destructive, so never resent by themselves, and a command tracker offers “Send again” only
  where `resendAfterNotFound` holds (AP-577). The non-destructive `receipt` ops that act harmlessly before their commit
  (`clients.install`, `licence.refresh`, `host.recheckAgents`, the sign-in cancels, `vault.check`, `connections.check`,
  the GitHub reads, content-addressed pack files) stay `receipt`: a client resends by itself only before a request's
  delivery deadline, and repeating them then is harmless.
- **Checklist for adding an op or changing its handler** (nothing checks the table against the runtime):
  1. give the op its `OPERATION_SAFETY` entry (typecheck insists) and read its handler down to the services it calls;
  2. anything observable before its first commit-pipeline transaction — HTTP (GitHub, Google, control, providers), a
     process, files or git on disk, a credential store, in-memory state, a direct `services.db` write — makes it `never`
     unless repeating it is harmless (a destructive op's, also later: people send those again);
  3. a secret in its input or result makes it a `secret` op (`SECRET_API_OPS` or the session spec), hence `never`;
  4. irreversible or high-impact makes it `destructive`;
  5. a runtime change that moves an effect before or out of an op's commit updates its entry in the same contracts
     release, and the runtime's review names the entry it relied on.

## CT-195 Contracts 0.29.1: retry-safety corrections, and `redacted` means “the result isn't kept” (2026-09-30)

A patch after CT-194's review. Under `docs/publishing.md` it is one: no session operation, output, frame or answer
union changes shape, nothing is exported that wasn't, and neither `SESSION_API_LEVEL` nor `RUNTIME_FEATURES` moves.

- **Six ops become `retry: never`** (they stay destructive), as CT-194's amendment said: `connections.remove`,
  `signins.logout`, `providers.logout`, `signins.orgRemove`, `providers.org.remove`, `clients.remove`. Their effect
  happens before their commit (or without one), so `not_found` doesn't mean nothing happened, and a repeat later isn't
  harmless. Client behaviour is the same as before (destructive ops are never resent by themselves); a command tracker
  that follows `resendAfterNotFound` no longer offers them as “not sent”. A test pins the six.
- **`automations.webhook` joins `SECRET_API_OPS`**: its answer may carry a new webhook secret in plain text, shown once.
  Managed runtimes refuse the op over a session (Whombat `dispatcher.ts` `EXCLUDED`), so this is defensive: a receipt
  of it would keep neither a digest of the input nor the answer, and a retry would get `unknown_outcome`. Nothing else
  keys on the list: the runtime reads `OperationSpec.secret` only for receipts, the app's session reads the op's
  `retry` (already `never`), and the conformance vectors' `secretOps` gain the name.
- **Frozen table.** `OPERATION_SAFETY` and every entry are `Object.freeze`d, so no consumer loosens one op (or, through a
  shared entry, dozens). The table is written `satisfies Record<OperationName, OperationSafety>`, which keeps a missing
  or an extra op a type error.
- **`outcome.redacted` is general**: the outcome is known, its result isn't kept. A `secret` op's never is (CT-44). A
  runtime also answers `completed` + `redacted` for a command committed by a process that died before storing its
  result — it answered `accepted` for ever, and clients polled — and for one whose handler failed after its commit while
  reading its result back — it answered `rejected`, though the writes had landed. Clients treat `completed` + `redacted`
  as done: fetch the current state, never resend (`OutcomeRedactedError` with state `completed` in whombat-app, which it
  has done since 0.5.1, so older clients need nothing). `redacted` never accompanies `rejected`. Only the doc comment of
  `Outcome.redacted` changes; no wire change.

## CT-196 `unknown_outcome` also means “it may have happened” (docs only, after 0.29.1) (2026-09-30)

The runtime fixes CS-01…CS-08 (Whombat) keep a receipt for a command that acted outside its commit (an outside effect
before the commit) and lost its answer, instead of letting it read `not_found`. The wire has no state for “may have
happened”, so the runtime answers `status` with `outcome{state: rejected, error: {code: unknown_outcome}}` and a
same-id retry with `error{unknown_outcome}`.

- `unknown_outcome` is no longer only a `secret` op's retry (CT-44): it is the appliance saying it has the request but
  can't give its outcome. With `rejected` in an `outcome` it means unknown, not rejected.
- Clients read it as an unknown outcome the appliance knows about: never resent by themselves (like an acknowledged
  request, whombat-app AP-574, AP-582), never shown as refused; a person checks the current state. A `secret` op's
  retry keeps its meaning (the answer isn't kept).
- Documented in `PROTOCOL_ERROR_CODES`' comment, `Outcome.error` and `docs/session-protocol.md`. No schema,
  version, `SESSION_API_LEVEL` or feature change: older clients read `rejected` with a code they map to a generic
  error, a wrong label but no resend.


## CT-197 Runs that don't get stuck: the runner's workspace report, Try again, a run that needs a person (contracts 0.30.0) (2026-10-01)

John, 2026-10-01, after Banjo's runs on FB-8QQQ-9R26 stopped twice — first without a checkout, then after committing,
asking for “Browse the web” to push while the runner had pushed already and its landing in the owner's clone had
failed unseen: “For future runs, how can we make Banjo (or any other agent) not get stuck at this?” — “Implement this
fully”. The runtime side is Whombat `docs/decisions/run-checkout.md` RC-08…RC-13.

- `CompleteBody.workspace?: WorkspaceReport {pushedCommits, problems: WorkspaceProblem[] ≤ 5}`, `WorkspaceProblem
  {step: checkout | push | land, message ≤ 500}`: what the runner did with a coding turn's checkout. The runner lands
  a direct checkout's commits before it completes, so a landing problem is in it. Older runners send none; older servers
  strip it.
- `Run.attention?: string | null` (≤ 280): why a live run needs a person — its agent stopped without finishing it,
  waiting on nobody, even after Whombat woke it once. Cleared when the run moves again.
- `runs.retry` `POST /burrows/:burrow/runs/:number/retry` → `{run}`: Try again on a failed run (it goes live again, its
  agent gets a new turn with the run's checkout). Retry safety `receipt`, like `runs.resume`.
- `DispatchContext.stalledRun?: boolean`: the turn Whombat woke because the agent's last turn on the run ended with the
  run still live.
- Audit event types `run.retried` (“Tried Banjo’s run #2 again”) and `run.stalled` (Code).
- Feature `runs.recovery` (`runs.retry`, `Run.attention`). Purely additive and gated by the feature, so
  `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays where it is (as CT-192).

## CT-198 `browser_preview`: an agent shows what it built (contracts 0.31.0) (2026-10-01)

John, 2026-10-01: “When Banjo finished a job (in this case change a color), I would like it to show a screenshot of the
new design.” Whombat's browser could only open internet pages; the agent's build sits in its checkout and its sandbox
can't serve it. The runtime side is Whombat `docs/decisions/browser.md` BT-48…BT-52.

- MCP tool `browser_preview {dir, path?, find?, attach?}` → `BrowserPreviewOutput` (the page shape, `attachmentId?`,
  `files`, `bytes`) with the screenshot as image content. `requiredKey: null`: it opens only the agent's own files,
  offline (the preview reaches no other address), so it needs no browser key; `readOnly: false` (it publishes the
  screenshot unless `attach: false`). In `BROWSER_TOOL_NAMES` (`BROWSER_PREVIEW_TOOL`), activity “Previewed the build”.
- `BROWSER_PREVIEW_ORIGIN` `https://preview.whombat.invalid` (served inside the host's browser only),
  `BROWSER_PREVIEW_MAX_FILES` 2000, `BROWSER_PREVIEW_MAX_BYTES` 50 MiB.
- Runner API: `ProgressResponse.previews?: PreviewRequest[] {id: pvw_…, dir}` — folders the server wants for a
  preview, on the turn's heartbeat — and `runner.submitPreview` `POST /dispatches/:dispatchId/previews/:previewId`
  `RunnerLease + {files?: PreviewFile[] {path, data base64}, error?}`. The runner reads the folder inside the turn's
  working directory (no `..`, no symlinks out). Older runners ignore `previews`: the tool then says the runner can't.

## CT-199 The Vault's SSH keys: kind `ssh`, its key and its servers (contracts 0.32.0) (2026-10-01)

John, 2026-10-01: “At Vault we should be able to add a private SSH key, so an agent gets the ability to SSH into a
server” and “A single SSH private key can give access to multiple servers”. The spec is Whombat
`docs/decisions/vault.md` VT-S01…VT-S15; this is its contract (stream 1 of `docs/implementation/vault-ssh/`).

- **Kind and template.** `VAULT_ENTRY_KINDS` `mcp|http|login|ssh|secret`, `VAULT_TEMPLATES`
  `mcp|token|basic|login|ssh|secret` (SSH key after Login, as the tiles read). `VAULT_TEMPLATE_DEFS.ssh` “SSH key” /
  “A private key your agents use to sign in to servers over SSH. They never see the key.”, auth `ssh_key`;
  `vaultTemplateOf('ssh', …)` → `ssh`.
- **`auth` `ssh_key`** `{keyType: ed25519|rsa|ecdsa, publicKey (OpenSSH line, no comment: VaultSshPublicKey),
  fingerprint ('SHA256:' + 43 base64: VaultSshFingerprint), origin: generated|imported}`. Written by the server only:
  `vaultEntryShapeProblems` refuses `auth` on an `ssh` create, any non-`ssh_key` auth on `ssh`, and `ssh_key` on any other
  kind. `url` and `secret` are refused on `ssh`; the private key is the sealed secret (`secret.set`). `vaultCredential`
  throws for `ssh_key` (it is never sent with a request).
- **Creating.** `CreateVaultEntryBody.sshKey?: VaultSshKeySource` = `{mode: 'generate'}` | `{mode: 'import',
  privateKey: VaultSshPrivateKeyText, passphrase?: VaultSshPassphrase}`, required for `ssh` (“Choose “Generate a new
  key” or “Use my own key”.”), refused on other kinds. `VaultSshPrivateKeyText` runs `inspectVaultSshPrivateKey`
  (≤ 16 000 characters), so field errors land on `sshKey.privateKey`.
- **Servers** (`VaultSshServer`, id `vss_…` = `VaultSshServerId`, `ID_PREFIXES.vaultSshServer`): `{id, name, host,
  port, username, hostKey: {algorithm, fingerprint, trustedAt} | null, seenHostKey: {algorithm, fingerprint, seenAt} |
  null, check: VaultSshServerCheck {status, outcome | null, summary, checkedAt}, createdAt, updatedAt}`. Two host-key
  fields, not one: `hostKey` is the pin every connection verifies, `seenHostKey` a key the last check saw that isn't
  trusted (unknown, or different from the pin) and what “Trust this server” confirms — so a changed key never
  overwrites the pin until the owner trusts it, and a transient MITM leaves the pin intact.
- **Views.** `VaultEntryDetail.servers` (default `[]`, by name), `VaultEntry.serverCount` (default 0),
  `VaultKeyView.servers: VaultKeyServers` (default null = All servers; an array, possibly empty once every listed server
  was removed), `VaultAgentKey.serverNames` (default null), `VaultUse.server` / `exitCode` (default null). All
  defaulted, so older answers parse; type-level, code that builds these objects adds the fields.
- **Check outcomes** gain `host_key_unconfirmed` and `host_key_changed` (`VAULT_CHECK_OUTCOMES`; `VaultCheckResult`
  can carry them). An `ssh` entry's own `check` is computed from its servers (`vaultSshEntryCheck`); `vault.check` on
  an `ssh` entry is `wrong_kind`.
- **Limits**: `VAULT_SSH_SERVERS_MAX` 20, `VAULT_SSH_SERVER_NAME_MAX` 40, `VAULT_SSH_HOST_MAX` 253,
  `VAULT_SSH_USERNAME_MAX` 32, `VAULT_SSH_DEFAULT_PORT` 22, `VAULT_SSH_PORTS_DEFAULT` [22],
  `VAULT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY_MAX` 16 000, `VAULT_SSH_PASSPHRASE_MAX` 1 024, `VAULT_SSH_RSA_MIN_BITS` 2048,
  `VAULT_SSH_COMMAND_MAX` 16 000, `VAULT_SSH_STDIN_MAX` / `VAULT_SSH_OUTPUT_MAX` 256 KiB, `VAULT_SSH_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_S`
  120, `VAULT_SSH_TIMEOUT_MAX_S` 900, `VAULT_SSH_FILE_MAX` 1 MiB, `VAULT_SSH_PATH_MAX` 4 096,
  `VAULT_SSH_WHAT_COMMAND_MAX` 160, `VAULT_SSH_CONNECT_DEADLINE_MS` 30 s, `VAULT_SSH_KEEPALIVE_MS` 15 s,
  `VAULT_SSH_IDLE_MS` 5 min, `VAULT_SSH_CHANNELS_MAX` 4.

## CT-200 SSH routes, session ops and the API level (contracts 0.32.0) (2026-10-01)

- Eight `api.vault.*` endpoints (each `wrong_kind` on a non-`ssh` entry): `generateSshKey` `POST …/vault/:entryId/
  ssh-key/generate` → `VaultEntryWriteResponse`; `replaceSshKey` `PUT …/ssh-key` `ReplaceVaultSshKeyBody {privateKey,
  passphrase?}` → `VaultEntryWriteResponse`; `addSshServer` `POST …/servers` (201) `AddVaultSshServerBody {name, host,
  port = 22, username}` → `VaultSshServerWriteResponse {entry, eventId, serverId}`; `updateSshServer` `PATCH
  …/servers/:serverId` `UpdateVaultSshServerBody` (any field, at least one) → `VaultSshServerWriteResponse`;
  `removeSshServer` `DELETE …/servers/:serverId` → `VaultEntryWriteResponse`; `checkSshServer` `POST
  …/servers/:serverId/check` → `VaultSshCheckResponse {entry, result: VaultSshCheckResult, eventId (null)}`;
  `trustSshHostKey` `POST …/servers/:serverId/trust` `TrustVaultSshHostKeyBody {fingerprint}` →
  `VaultSshCheckResponse` (trust signs in once right after, like a Check, so the owner sees “Signed in as deploy” at
  once); `setKeyServers` `PUT …/keys/:agent/servers` `SetVaultKeyServersBody {servers}` → `VaultEntryWriteResponse`.
- `GiveVaultKeyBody.servers?: VaultKeyServersChoice` (null = All servers, or 1–20 distinct ids): absent keeps an
  existing key's servers and gives a new key All servers. Both ways exist so “Give a key to…” with its Servers chooser
  is one call and a key row's chooser is another.
- Errors: `server_name_taken` (conflict), `host_key_mismatch` (conflict, `details.hostKey` = what the server shows
  now), `limit_reached` with `limit: 'servers'` (“An SSH key can have at most 20 servers. Remove one first.”),
  `address_not_allowed` with a `VaultSshDestinationProblemCode` in `details.problem`. Import problems found by parsing
  are `validation_failed` on `privateKey` / `passphrase` with `VAULT_SSH_KEY_PROBLEM_TEXT`.
- Events (the runtime signs; texts unchanged, VT-51): server add/change/remove and trust → `vault.entry.changed`;
  generate and replace → `vault.entry.secret_replaced`; `setKeyServers` and a `giveKey` that changes servers →
  `vault.key.changed`; Check signs nothing (VT-D08).
- **Session.** `vault.replaceSshKey` joins `SECRET_API_OPS` (VT-S03; the vectors' `secretOps` too); an import at
  create is `vault.create`, already secret. `vault.generateSshKey` is ordinary (only the public half returns) but
  `destructive` (the old key stops working everywhere: a person decides on a resend). Safety: `addSshServer`,
  `updateSshServer`, `checkSshServer`, `trustSshHostKey`, `setKeyServers` `receipt`; `removeSshServer` destructive
  `receipt`; `replaceSshKey` `never`.
- **Level and feature.** New ops and union members a session answer carries: `SESSION_API_LEVEL` 25 (Go
  `SessionAPILevel`). The window of a level-25 client is 23…26: runtimes at 23 and 24 (everything in the field) are
  served, level 22 now hears “This Whombat needs an update”. `RUNTIME_FEATURES` gains `vault.ssh` (`SINCE_0_32`); a
  client offers SSH keys only on runtimes that advertise it.

## CT-201 SSH's pure rules (contracts 0.32.0) (2026-10-01)

All in `@whombat/core/vault` (`vault/ssh.ts`), unit-tested:

- **Fields.** `VaultSshServerName` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$`, 1–40), `VaultSshUsername`
  (`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\$?$`, 1–32), `VaultSshHost` / `parseVaultSshHost` (a host name — ASCII labels, the last
  not a number, as `parseUrlAuthority` — or an IPv4/IPv6 literal, IPv6 with or without brackets, canonical lowercase
  RFC 5952; the server stores this form), `VaultSshPath` / `vaultSshPathProblem` (1–4 096, no C0, DEL or C1),
  `VaultSshFileMode` (`^0?[0-7]{3}$`: permission bits only — no setuid, setgid or sticky bit from an agent),
  `VaultSshCommand`; texts in `VAULT_SSH_FIELD_TEXT`.
- **Where a server may be** (VT-S06): `vaultSshDestinationProblem({host, port, resolved, networks, sshPorts?, at?})`
  → `{code: bad_host|unresolved|port_not_allowed|never|mixed|not_listed, message, suggestion?}`: every resolved address
  public → the port must be in `sshPorts` (default [22]; “Whombat reaches servers on the internet on port 22 only.”);
  any never-listable address → `never`; public and private at once → `mixed`; private → every address inside a
  listed network whose ports include the port, else `not_listed` with VT-13's sentence and suggestion. At `call`:
  `VAULT_SSH_ADDRESS_NOT_ALLOWED_ANY_MORE` “This server’s address isn’t allowed any more.”. `parseVaultSshPorts(env)`
  reads `WHOMBAT_VAULT_SSH_PORTS` (`22,2222`; empty → [22]; null when invalid).
- **Coverage** (VT-S07): `vaultKeyCoversServer(key, serverId)` (null/absent = all), `vaultKeyCoveredServers`.
  `decideVaultUse` gains optional `use: VaultUseKind` (`tool|request|sign_in|ssh {serverId, serverName}`) and
  `entryKind`; with both, after search and no-key: a use the entry's kind doesn't take → `blocked wrong_kind` (“That
  Vault entry can’t be used that way.”), an SSH use of an uncovered server → `blocked server_not_covered` (with
  `serverName`) **before** any pass or tier — a pass covers the key's servers, never more. `vaultUseMessage` writes
  “Your key to that Vault entry doesn’t cover the server “{name}”.” (`vaultServerNotCoveredText`). Without `use` the
  decision is unchanged. `VAULT_USE_ENTRY_KIND` maps use kinds to entry kinds.
- **Public keys.** `parseVaultSshPublicKey` (algorithm must match the blob's own name; comment dropped),
  `vaultSshFingerprint` / `vaultSshFingerprintOfBlob` (as `ssh-keygen -l`), `vaultSshAuthorizedKeysLine(publicKey,
  entryId)` = `restrict <publicKey> whombat-<vaultEntryKey(entryId)>` (`vaultSshKeyComment`),
  `vaultSshHostKeyLabel` (ED25519/ECDSA/RSA/DSA) and `vaultSshHostKeyFile`, `bytesToBase64` / `base64ToBytes` (no
  Buffer).
- **Pasted keys.** `inspectVaultSshPrivateKey(text)` → `{format: openssh|rsa|ec|pkcs8|pkcs8_encrypted, encrypted,
  algorithm, publicKey}` or a `VaultSshKeyProblemCode` with its sentence: `empty`, `too_long`, `not_a_key`,
  `public_key`, `putty`, `certificate`, `several_keys`, `fido`, `unsupported_type` (core finds these), and
  `rsa_too_short`, `passphrase_needed`, `wrong_passphrase`, `unreadable` (the server's parser finds these). An OpenSSH
  key's public half is readable even when encrypted, so the web can show the fingerprint and ask for the passphrase
  before saving.
- **Forms of a private key** (VT-S10): `vaultSshKeyForms({privateKeys, raw?, passphrase?})` — the whole text (LF,
  CRLF, JSON-escaped), the body joined, each base64 line of ≥ 24 characters that carries private bytes
  (`vaultSshPrivateKeyLines`), the raw key bytes in base64 (padded and not, ≥ 16 characters), the passphrase when it
  has ≥ 8 characters — longest first; `holdsVaultSshKey(text, forms)`. Lines wholly inside an OpenSSH key's header and
  public key are left out: line 1 is the same in every unencrypted ed25519 key, so counting it would withhold (and take
  the key back on) a server printing any other key. Short passphrases are left out for the same reason.
- **Uses.** `vaultSshUseWhat({tool: exec, server, command} | {tool: read|write, server, path})` → `ssh web-1 ·
  systemctl status nginx` (first 160 characters, control characters as spaces), `read web-1:/path`, `write
  web-1:/path` (≤ 300). RECENT USE: `vaultUseWhatText` drops the `ssh ` prefix, `vaultUseOutcomeText` reads an exit
  status as “exit 0”; `vaultUseRow` uses both (and accepts uses without the new fields).
- **Servers.** `vaultSshServerTarget` (`deploy@web1.example.com:22`, IPv6 in brackets), `vaultSshServerReady` (a
  trusted host key and nothing else seen), `vaultSshEntryCheck(servers)` (one server: its check; several: failing
  when any fails “1 of 3 servers failing”, reached “Signed in to all 3 servers” / “Signed in to 2 of 3 servers”, else
  unchecked; none: “No servers yet”), `vaultSshCheckSummary` (“Signed in as deploy”, “Host key not confirmed yet”,
  VT-S05's changed sentence, “The server refused the key.”, the Vault's failure texts, “It answered, but not as an SSH
  server.”), `vaultSshCheckStatus` (a host key waiting for its first trust is `unchecked`, not `failing`: nothing is
  wrong yet; a changed key is `failing`, as VT-S05 says).

## CT-202 What agents get: SSH tools, context and refusals (contracts 0.32.0) (2026-10-01)

- MCP tools in `VAULT_MCP_TOOLS` (so in `MCP_TOOLS` and `WHOMBAT_TOOL_NAMES`), `requiredKey: null`:
  `ssh_exec` `VaultSshExecInput {entry, server, command, stdin?, timeoutSeconds = 120 (1–900)}` →
  `VaultSshExecOutput` (`ok` + `VaultSshExecResult {exitCode, signal, stdout, stderr, stdoutCut, stderrCut, timedOut,
  ms}`, or `VaultToolRefusal`); `ssh_read_file` `{entry, server, path, offset?, maxBytes? ≤ 1 MiB}` → `ok` +
  `{content, encoding, size, cut}` (`readOnly: true`); `ssh_write_file` `{entry, server, path, content, encoding = text,
  mode?, append = false}` → `ok` + `{bytes}`. `entry` is `VaultEntryRef` (the id or the 8-letter key, VT-S08), `server`
  the server's name. `VAULT_SSH_TOOL_NAMES`; `isVaultToolName` / `isVaultActivityTool` include them, so activity reads
  “Used a private Vault entry” (VT-S11).
- `VAULT_FAILURES` gain `withheld` (VT-D22's sentence, for any kind), `no_server`, `host_key_unconfirmed`,
  `host_key_changed`, `rejected` (“The server refused the key.”) and `file_error`; SFTP errors are named by
  `VAULT_SSH_FILE_ERRORS` / `VAULT_SSH_FILE_ERROR_TEXT` (standard status codes only, never the server's words).
- `VaultContextEntry.servers?: VaultContextSshServer[] {name, target (user@host:port in the owner's own turn, else
  null), ready}` — the servers the key covers. `ready` is sent in every turn: it names nothing and saves a call that
  could only fail. `VaultDispatchContext.tools` lists the three SSH tools when an `ssh` entry is there.
- Prompt material (VT-S12): `vaultSshServerLine(server, ownersTurn)` (“web-1 — deploy@web1.example.com:22”, “web-1 —
  host key not confirmed yet”, or the name), `VAULT_SSH_NO_SERVERS_FOR_AGENTS`, `VAULT_SSH_AGENT_RULES` (the rules in
  order, for both providers). The tools' own descriptions repeat the essentials.

## CT-203 SSH copy (contracts 0.32.0) (2026-10-01)

`VAULT_SSH_COPY` holds the form and detail words: the spec's verbatim (“Key”, “Generate a new key”, “Use my own key”,
“Passphrase (if it has one)”, “PUBLIC KEY”, the `authorized_keys` hint, “Replace with my own key”, “SERVERS”, “Add
server”, “Check”, “Edit”, “Remove”, “Is this your server?”, “Trust this server”, the changed-key sentence, “Servers”,
“All servers”, Android's “SSH keys and servers are set up on the web, in Settings → Vault.”) and ours where the spec
has none (“Private key”, generate and passphrase hints, “Copy”/“Copied”, the replace warning, “No servers yet. Add the
servers this key signs in to.”, “Edit server”, field labels and the name hint, the remove-server confirmation, the
host-change note). `vaultSshTrustCopy(hostKey)` returns the trust card in parts (`question`, `fingerprint` “SHA256:…
(ED25519).”, `compare`, `command` — set as code —, `after`) and as one `text`. `VAULT_SSH_KEY_TYPE_LABELS`,
`vaultKeyServersText` (“All servers”, “web-1, nas”, “No servers”), `vaultSshServerCheckLine`, and `vaultEntryMeta`
for `ssh` (“SSH key · ED25519 · 3 servers · 2 agents”).

## CT-204 Fixtures for SSH keys (contracts 0.32.0) (2026-10-01)

`vaultSshDeployKey` (“Deploy key”, opt-in like `vaultShopLogin`: not in `VAULT_ENTRIES`, so the seeded Vault page is
unchanged): web-1 trusted and signed in, staging waiting for trust, Dusty's key on All servers, Pippa's on staging
only at Asks, one RECENT USE “ssh web-1 · systemctl status nginx” exit 0. `FIXTURE_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`,

entries in the world, and the fixture fetch serves all eight new endpoints: Generate gives the fixture key, an import
of an OpenSSH key its own public half, every reachable server shows the fixture host key (`*.invalid` hosts are
unreachable), trust compares fingerprints.

## CT-205 Names chosen for SSH keys, and where they differ from the spec (2026-10-01)

Every new name, so the runtime and app streams can look them up: ids `VaultSshServerId` (`vss_`); schemas
`VaultSshKeyType`, `VaultSshKeyOrigin`, `VaultSshPublicKey`, `VaultSshFingerprint`, `VaultSshKeyAuth` (type),
`VaultKeyServers`, `VaultKeyServersChoice`, `VaultSshHostKey`, `VaultSshServerCheck`, `VaultSshServer`,
`VaultSshCheckResult`, `VaultSshKeySource`, `VaultSshPrivateKeyText`, `VaultSshPassphrase`, `VaultSshServerName`,
`VaultSshUsername`, `VaultSshHost`, `VaultSshPath`, `VaultSshFileMode`, `VaultSshCommand`, `VaultContextSshServer`,
`VaultEntryRef`; bodies `ReplaceVaultSshKeyBody`, `AddVaultSshServerBody`, `UpdateVaultSshServerBody`,
`TrustVaultSshHostKeyBody`, `SetVaultKeyServersBody`; responses `VaultSshServerWriteResponse`, `VaultSshCheckResponse`;
tools `VaultSshExecInput/Result/Output`, `VaultSshReadFileInput/Result/Output`, `VaultSshWriteFileInput/Result/Output`.

Where the spec's words became something else:

- “host_key_algorithm, host_key_fingerprint, host_key_trusted_at” (VT-S04's columns) are two view fields, `hostKey`
  (trusted) and `seenHostKey` (waiting), not one key with a nullable `trustedAt` (CT-199).
- “key servers” is both `vault.setKeyServers` and `GiveVaultKeyBody.servers`; the profile pane's `VaultAgentKey`
  carries `serverNames`, not ids.
- “replace key” / “generate new key” are `vault.replaceSshKey` / `vault.generateSshKey`; the create body's key is
  `sshKey` (not `secret`).
- `decideVaultUse` “gets use kind `ssh`” as the optional `use` + `entryKind` inputs (no input means the old decision);
  new blocked reasons `wrong_kind` and `server_not_covered`.
- `VaultUse.server` / `exitCode` as specified; `exitCode` is 0–255.
- A server waiting for its first trust reads `unchecked` (grey), not `failing`.
- `VaultEntryDetail.servers` is defaulted `[]` for every kind rather than optional.
- Check of a whole `ssh` entry: none (`vault.check` is `wrong_kind`); the card's dot comes from `vaultSshEntryCheck`.

## CT-206 Contracts 0.32.0: the Vault's SSH keys (2026-10-01)

One minor release of CT-199…CT-205. Closed unions grow (`VAULT_ENTRY_KINDS`, `VAULT_TEMPLATES`, `VaultAuth`,
`VAULT_CHECK_OUTCOMES`, `VAULT_FAILURES`, `VAULT_ERROR_CODES`, `VaultLimit`, the `VaultUseDecision` reasons); clients
decode with `decodeTolerant` (CT-136), and a client offers SSH keys only where the runtime advertises `vault.ssh`.
`SESSION_API_LEVEL` 25. Go changes only the generated `SessionAPILevel`; `vectors/session.json` lists the new secret op.
No other Go, JSON Schema or vector change (the Vault has no Go bindings, as CT-105). Every package is 0.32.0.

## CT-207 Mentions in any letter case (contracts 0.33.0) (2026-10-01)

John, 2026-10-01, after `@banjo are you able to connect to root@203.0.113.44 …` woke nobody: “if I can make this
mistake any user can”; lowercase must wake the agent, “or even better auto-correct it in the chat”. The spec is
Whombat `docs/decisions/messaging.md` MS-C01…MS-C03 (stream 1 of `docs/implementation/agent-guidance/`). All in
`@whombat/core/text` (`text/mentions.ts`), pure, unit-tested (`mentions-case.test.ts`).

- **`mentionCorrections(text, targets)`** → `MentionCorrection[] {start, end, from, to}`: every `@word` that names a
  target in another letter case (`@banjo`, `@BANJO`, `@bAnJo` → `@Banjo`), in order. `to` always has `from`'s length.
- **`canonicalizeMentions(text, targets): string`** (MS-C02) applies them; everything else stays byte-identical, and a
  second pass changes nothing. **`resolveMentions`** now resolves on `canonicalizeMentions(text, principals)`, with
  the same order as before (agents, people, personal agents, PA-04).
- **`autocorrectMentionAt(text, caret, targets)`** → `{text, caret} | null` (MS-C03), one rule for web and Android:
  the character just before `caret` ended a correctable `@word` → that word is replaced in place, caret kept. After
  `.` or `-` the word isn't decided yet (`@banjo.example`, `@banjo-ci`), so it is corrected one character later when what
  follows shows it is a mention (`@banjo. `). A code span still open on the caret's line (an unmatched backtick before
  the `@`) corrects nothing.
- **`mentionNameOf(target)`**: the word a target is mentioned by (agent name; person short name, else first name),
  shared by resolution and canonicalisation.
- **The canonical form keeps today's behaviour exactly.** `MENTION_PATTERN`, `segmentMentions` and `mentionNames` are
  unchanged: `x/@Banjo`, `john@Banjo.example`, `` `@Banjo` `` and `@BanjoBot` still mention Banjo as before. Only
  non-canonical forms follow the new boundaries.
- **Boundaries for a non-canonical form** (MS-C01, made stricter where the spec left room): before the `@` the start
  of the text or a character that isn't a letter, mark, digit, `_`, `.`, `@`, `/` or `-`; the word is all letters
  and marks (`@banjoé` is one word naming nobody); after it no letter, mark, digit, `_`, `@` or `/` (`@banjo2`,
  `@banjo_bot`, `@banjo@host`, `@whombat/core` — an npm scope must never become `@Whombat/core`), and no `.` or
  `-` + a letter, mark or digit (`@banjo.example`, `@banjo-ci`). The spec says “ends at a non-letter”; a handle-like
  continuation waking an agent is worse than a missed correction, which the person still sees (it stays plain text).
- **Only canonical-shaped names are targets.** A target whose mention name isn't `[A-Z][a-z]+` (`JP`, `R2d2`, `anne`,
  `Code Reviewer`) can't be mentioned canonically either (`MENTION_PATTERN`), so rewriting to it would mention
  nobody: it is skipped. Hence two targets that compare equal ignoring case have the same canonical text, and the
  ambiguity between an agent, a person and a personal agent is left to `resolveMentions`' order.
- **ASCII comparison, no Unicode case folding.** The word must be ASCII letters to match (`@Kate`, KELVIN SIGN,
  lowercases to “kate” but stays text; Turkish `İ`/`ı` don't match `i`).
- **Code.** Fenced blocks as `parseBroadcast` finds them (an unterminated fence runs to the end); inline code spans as
  the Markdown renderer reads them (a backtick run up to the next same run on that line, backticks inside included).
  `parseBroadcast` keeps its own, older code stripping (unchanged behaviour).
- **`@channel` / `@here`** (lowercase, CT-176) are never corrected, even with an agent called Channel or Here; other
  casings (`@HERE`) follow the normal rule.

## CT-208 Agents without a key are guided to the Vault (contracts 0.33.0) (2026-10-01)

The spec is Whombat `docs/decisions/vault.md` VT-G01…VT-G05. Contract and copy only; the runtime fills and prints them.

- **`VaultDispatchContext.unheld: VaultUnheldEntry[]`**, `.default([])` so older servers' payloads parse (the parsed
  type has it always). `VaultUnheldEntry {id, name, description, kind (http|mcp|login|ssh, never secret),
  ownerFirstName, site?: string | null, servers?: VaultContextSshServer[]}` — the requester's own entries the agent
  holds no key to, in the owner's own turn only. `servers` reuses the held entries' server shape `{name, target,
  ready}` (all of the entry's servers; targets allowed, it is the owner's turn). `ownerFirstName` is added to the spec's
  shape so the prompt can say “ask John” without looking the requester up elsewhere.
- **`VAULT_UNHELD_MAX` 20** (in `@whombat/core/vault`) is the server's cap; the schema doesn't enforce it, so a later
  server sending more never makes an older runner refuse the whole context.
- **Copy** (`vault/copy.ts`): `VAULT_ACCESS_RULES` (the two VT-G01 lines, verbatim), `VAULT_SSH_SETUP_INTRO`
  (“How someone sets up SSH access for you (tell them only the steps still missing):”), `VAULT_SSH_SETUP_STEPS` (the
  five steps without numbers, `{agent}` placeholder) and `vaultSshSetupSteps(agentName)` (numbered, filled in),
  `VAULT_UNHELD_NOTE` (“you hold no key to it”, the block tag) and `vaultUnheldAskLine({ownerFirstName, entryName,
  agentName})` (“To use it, ask John to give you a key: Settings → Vault → “Server Access Key” → Give a key to… →
  Banjo.” — the caller passes the entry name already defused, BP-07).
- **VT-G04.** `VAULT_SSH_AGENT_RULES` gains a last rule: “When someone names a host that isn’t one of the key’s
  servers, don’t guess: tell them to add it as a server (step 2 of the SSH setup), or which listed server it is.”
  `vaultNoServerText(serverNames)` is the `no_server` answer naming the servers the key covers: “That Vault entry has
  no server by that name. Its servers: web-1, nas.”, or “… It has no servers your key covers yet.” Names only, in
  every turn (server names are `[a-z0-9._-]`, safe to print; targets are already in the owner's prompt).
  `VAULT_FAILURE_TEXT.no_server` is unchanged.
- No tool, decision or feature changes: unheld entries are never usable (`decideVaultUse` untouched).

`SESSION_API_LEVEL` counts session operations, outputs, frames and unions a session answer carries (CT-136,

never bumped the level (`stalledRun` CT-197, `VaultContextEntry.servers` CT-202). Mentions need no feature either:
clients canonicalise before sending (MS-C03), so an older runtime still receives `@Banjo`; a newer runtime
canonicalises what older clients send. No Go, JSON Schema or vector change (`pnpm gen:check` is clean).

## CT-210 Contracts 0.33.0: mentions in any case, agents guided to the Vault (2026-10-01)

One minor release of CT-207…CT-209. New exports only, plus `resolveMentions` resolving any letter case and
`VaultDispatchContext.unheld` (defaulted; code that builds a `VaultDispatchContext` adds `unheld`). Every package is
0.33.0.

## CT-211 Merge into main and the deploy keys are agents' keys; Push to main stays people only (contracts 0.34.0) (2026-10-01)

John, 2026-10-01, after he couldn't give Banjo (Developer) “Deploy” or “Merge into main” in Configure: “I would like to
be able to assign both merge and deploy to an agent when I want to. For both I would like to introduce 3 states:
disable / enable / ask.” This supersedes the mock's “Merge into main · people only” and “Deploy · always asks a
person” (it is John's call). The spec is Whombat `docs/decisions/runs-approvals.md` MDS-01…MDS-07
(`docs/implementation/merge-deploy-keys/assignment.md`).

- **Caps lifted (MDS-01).** `merge.main`, `deploy`, `deploy.staging`, `deploy.production` have `agentMaxTier: 'can'`.
  Descriptions lose their caps: Merge into main “Merge pull requests into the default branch.”, Deploy “Deploy to any
  environment.”, Deploy to staging “Deploy a commit to the staging environment.”, Deploy to production “Deploy a commit
  to production.” No other cap changes: `agents.manage`, `approvals.decide`, `members.invite`, `burrow.manage` stay
  people only; `mail.send`, `calendar.invite`, `files.share`, `files.delete` still always ask. So `ALWAYS_ASKS_KEYS` is
  those four, `lockedNote` of the four lifted keys is null, and `clampTier` / `clampGrants` / `validateGrants` let
  them through at `can`. The engine is unchanged: `can` allows, `ask` asks (an approval card), `cannot` or no key
  denies; the most specific level with a grant still decides (a stale `merge.main: cannot` under `merge: can` still
  denies a merge into main — CT-212's rows align it).
- **New key `branch.main.push` “Push to main”** (group `code`, no parent, `agentMaxTier: 'never'`, “Push commits
  straight to the default branch. People only: agents merge through pull requests.”). `branchWriteKey(defaultBranch)`
  returns it instead of `merge.main`. Until now the same key gated merging into main and *writing* main (a run started
  on main, the git credential for a push to main, the automation workspace, the sandbox's write access): lifting the cap
  on `merge.main` alone would have let an agent with Merge On push straight to main, which MDS-06 rules out (merging is
  only Whombat's `merge_pr` / `merge_pull_request`, never `git push` to main). A new id rather than a runtime-only rule
  keeps the one engine check in every place that already asks `branchWriteKey`, and its Blocked events name the right
  key (“KEY IT NEEDED · Push to main”). `KeyId` grows: a union in session answers (grants, `keyNeeded`), decoded
  tolerantly by clients (CT-136).
- **Copy.** The `merge_pull_request` tool: “Merge a pull request, into main too. Your Merge key decides: held, it
  merges; held at ask, a person approves it on a card first (pending_approval); not held, it is blocked and you can ask
  for the key. Never push to main or merge with git or gh yourself.” Engine reason comments name the capped personal
  keys instead of deploys. `HANDOVER_KEYS` gains `merge.main` and `merge` after `pr.open` (a delegator sees who can
  merge). `MERGE_NOTE` (“Merging is for people. Agents in this burrow don’t hold a merge key.”, the branch pane's mock
  note under the people's Merge into main button) is left as it is; the app decides whether to show it (it is only true
  while no agent holds Merge).

## CT-212 Merge and Deploy rows in three states (contracts 0.34.0) (2026-10-01)

The hire modal and Configure (MDS-02). All in `@whombat/core/keys` (`keys/grants.ts`, `keys/configure.ts`), pure,
unit-tested (`keys.test.ts`, `configure.test.ts`).

- **The rows.** `KEY_TIER_ROWS = ['merge', 'deploy']`, `KeyTierRow`, `isKeyTierRow(keyId)`. The Merge row's key is the
  umbrella `merge` (label “Merge”, as the catalog), not `merge.main`: the row decides every merge, into main too, so its
  Keys events read “Gave Banjo a new key: Merge” (MDS-07). It replaces the mock's “Merge into main · people only” row in
  `HIRE_KEY_OPTIONS` (where the Merge/Deploy rows were, last). `KEY_TIER_CHOICES` `['cannot', 'ask', 'can']` with
  `KEY_TIER_LABELS` Off · Ask · On is the control's order and copy; `DEPLOY_NO_WORKFLOW_HINT` “No deploy workflow is set
  up on this Whombat yet.” is MDS-05's hint, shared by web and Android.
- **`HireKeyOption.defaultTier?: Tier`**, set on the three-state rows only: the row shows Off · Ask · On and opens at
  this tier; `defaultOn` is `defaultTier === 'can'`, `locked` and `lockedTier` null. An optional field, so older row
  literals (the app's `PROPOSE_SKILLS_OPTION`) still type.
- **Defaults per role.** `hireKeyOptions(role)` sets `defaultTier = keyRowTier(roleDefaultGrants(role), row)`: Off for
  every role, except the Operator's Deploy, Ask (its `deploy.staging` and `deploy.production` ask). No “not for this
  role” lock on these rows: a Lead, Tester or Writer opens at Off and can be set to Ask or On. Extra role rows still
  come before them; they stay last. `ROLE_LOCKED_NOTE` and the capped-row branch stay for capped rows to come (none of
  the fixed rows is capped now).
- **Read: `keyRowTier(grants, row): Tier`** — what the row shows: the tier that decides a merge into main
  (`KEY_TIER_ROW_READS.merge = ['merge.main']`) or a deploy to staging and to production (`deploy: ['deploy.staging',
  'deploy.production']`, the most restrictive when they differ), each walked as the engine walks the umbrella chain
  (most specific level with a grant, direct before bundle, strictest at one level, clamped), scopes not looked at, no
  grant → `cannot`. Nothing more is shown when narrower grants differ (MDS-02: keep it simple). The bare `deploy` is
  left out of the read so an Operator, holding the two environments at ask and no umbrella, reads Ask.
- **Write: `withKeyRowTier(grants: GrantInput[], row, tier): GrantInput[]`** — the umbrella at `tier` and every
  narrower key of the row the agent holds (`KEY_TIER_ROW_KEYS`: `merge.main`; `deploy.staging`, `deploy.production`)
  aligned to `tier`, all without a scope; narrower keys not held stay absent. Aligning instead of clearing keeps the Keys
  events honest: turning Merge on for a Developer reads “Gave Banjo a new key: Merge” and “Gave Banjo a new key: Merge
  into main”, where clearing would have read “Took Banjo’s “Merge into main” key away”. Off writes `cannot` (an
  explicit “× no key” row, as the role defaults list them), never a removal. A scope on a row grant is dropped: the row
  is the whole truth (a deploy scoped to environments is a `set keys` matter, and an edit of the row replaces it).
- **Hire: `HireBody.keyTiers?: KeyRowTiers`** (`{merge?: Tier, deploy?: Tier}`) and **`hireGrants(agentId, selected,
  channelIds, role?, tiers = {})`**: each row is always granted once, as its umbrella key, at `tiers[row]`; else `can`
  when `selected` lists the row (a client still drawing it as a switch); else the role's default; else (no role) Off.
  `selected` never grants `merge.main`, `deploy.staging` or `deploy.production`: the row decides them. So a hired
  Developer now holds `merge: cannot` and `deploy: cannot` (before: `merge.main: cannot`, `deploy: ask` — the old
  locked Deploy row asked for every hire); an Operator `deploy: ask`, as before. Onboarding and the seed keep
  `ROLE_DEFAULT_KEYS` unchanged (the mock's AG0 keys: a Developer's “× Merge into main”).
- **Configure.** `configureKeyTiers(grants, options)` → `KeyRowTiers` for the rows shown; `ConfigureEdit` gains
  `baseTiers?` / `tiers?`; `configureGrants` applies a row whose tier changed with `withKeyRowTier`, and leaves it alone
  otherwise (a save at the tiers it opened with sends null). Without `tiers` a row's `keys` switch is read as On/Off
  (`configureKeyState` sets it to `keyRowTier === 'can'`), so a client that hasn't learned the rows yet still saves
  something sensible.

## CT-213 Key requests: Merge into main may be asked for; Merge and Deploy are given at ask (contracts 0.34.0) (2026-10-01)

MDS-04, amending Whombat KR-04 for these keys. `keys/requests.ts`, unit-tested in `approvals/key-requests.test.ts`.

- `keyRequestProblem` no longer refuses `merge.main` (it isn't people only); `branch.main.push` and the burrow keys
  still are (“… is for people. Agents never hold this key.”).
- `requestedTier` is `ask` for every key of a three-state row (`merge`, `merge.main`, `deploy`, `deploy.staging`,
  `deploy.production`): the person switches the row to On in Configure if they want. The card's copy follows from it
  (“…, still asking a person each time”; “Given. Tinker holds “Deploy to staging” and asks a person each time it uses
  it.”).
- A key held at ask is held as far as a request gives it: “Tinker already holds “Deploy to staging” and asks a person
  each time. A person can switch it to On in Configure.” (held at can: “Tinker already holds …”).
- `grantsWithRequestedKey` for a row key sets the whole row to ask (`withKeyRowTier`), so a request for “Deploy to
  staging” leaves a Deploy row that reads Ask instead of a production deploy still blocked by `deploy: cannot`; and a
  Developer's request for Merge into main gives `merge: ask` with its `merge.main` aligned. Unless a key of the row is
  already held at can: then only the asked key's own grant becomes ask, so an approval never lowers anything.

## CT-214 Contracts 0.34.0: Merge and Deploy in three states (2026-10-01)

One minor release of CT-211…CT-213. `KeyId` grows (`branch.main.push`), `HireBody.keyTiers` is optional,
`HireKeyOption.defaultTier` optional, `ConfigureEdit.baseTiers` / `tiers` optional, `hireGrants` gains an optional
fifth parameter; the behaviour of `branchWriteKey`, `requestedTier`, `grantsWithRequestedKey`, `keyRequestProblem`,
`hireKeyOptions`, `hireGrants`, `configureKeyState`, `configureGrants` and the catalog's caps changes as above. New
exports: `KEY_TIER_ROWS`, `KeyTierRow`, `isKeyTierRow`, `KEY_TIER_ROW_KEYS`, `KEY_TIER_ROW_READS`, `KEY_TIER_CHOICES`,
`KEY_TIER_LABELS`, `DEPLOY_NO_WORKFLOW_HINT`, `keyTierRowOf`, `KeyRowTiers` (schema and type), `keyRowTier`,
`withKeyRowTier`, `configureKeyTiers`.

- **Feature `keys.merge_deploy`** (`RUNTIME_FEATURES`, `SINCE_0_34`): a client shows the three-state rows only on a
  runtime that advertises it. An older runtime would deny Merge into main and clamp deploys to ask whatever the row
  says, and ignore `keyTiers`.
- **`SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 25** (as CT-159, CT-165, CT-192, CT-193): no session op, output shape or frame changes;
  the one union that grows is `KeyId`, which older clients drop with tolerant decoding (a grant row or a `keyNeeded`
  they don't know), and the rest is optional or behind the feature name. No Go, JSON Schema or vector change
  (`pnpm gen` is clean). Every package is 0.34.0.

## CT-215 Contracts 0.34.1: `HostInfo.deployWorkflow` for the Deploy row's hint (2026-10-01)

A patch over 0.34.0 for MDS-05: the app needs to know whether deploys work on this Whombat to show
`DEPLOY_NO_WORKFLOW_HINT` under the Deploy row. **`HostInfo.deployWorkflow?: boolean`** (`host.info`): true when a
deploy workflow is set up (the runtime's `DeployExecutor` is configured, `GITHUB_DEPLOY_WORKFLOW` today), false when a
deploy would answer “Whombat can’t deploy here…” (`approvals/unavailable.ts`). Absent from older servers: unknown, and
clients show no hint. A flat boolean rather than a `deploys: {workflow}` object: one fact, beside `browser`, and a
later status can be its own field. Optional, so no feature name and no `SESSION_API_LEVEL` change (as CT-159); the
fixtures' `FIXTURE_HOST` leaves it out (the mock shows no hint). No Go, JSON Schema or vector change. Every package
is 0.34.1.

## CT-216 Clearing a channel: `conversations.clear` (contracts 0.35.0) (2026-10-02)

John, 2026-10-02: “When I right click on a channel I want to be able to remove all messages in that channel so the
channel is empty again.” The runtime side is Whombat `docs/decisions/channel-clear.md` (CC-01…), the web's whombat-app
`docs/decisions/channel-clear.md`.

- `conversations.clear` `POST /burrows/:burrow/conversations/:conversationId/clear` → `ClearConversationResponse
  {removed, kept}`: every message of the channel goes, replies, files and reactions included, in one commit. `removed`
  counts what went, `kept` the messages that stay because their thread still holds work in progress — the same idea as
  a single delete's “holds work in progress” (CT-173), narrowed to work that is actually unfinished: a run not yet
  finished, an approval waiting for its decision, a report being worked on, a plan with steps to go, a skill proposal
  waiting, a guide, an open handoff, an
  agent's turn queued or running there. Finished work's cards go: the run, the approval and the report themselves stay
  in Work, Approvals and Feedback.
- `canClearConversation(conversation, viewer)`: burrow owners, channels only (`kind: 'channel'`; not DMs, direct
  conversations or branch rooms). Owners because removing other people's words is moderation (as `canDeleteMessage`).
- Audit event type `channel.cleared` (Messages), ids and counts only; clients see one `message.deleted` per removed
  message on the conversation topic, as for single deletes, so no new realtime frame.
- Retry safety `destructive` + receipt, like `conversations.archive`.
- Feature `channels.clear` (`SINCE_0_35`): a client offers “Clear all messages” only on a runtime that advertises it.
  Purely additive and gated by the feature, so `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 25 (as CT-192, CT-197). No Go, JSON Schema or
  vector change (`pnpm gen` is clean). Every package is 0.35.0.

## CT-217 The `run_command` approval: a command a person allows once, for the task, or always (contracts 0.36.0) (2026-10-02)

John, 2026-10-02: “Give each agent a real computer and let it do what it's asked. Keep a person in the loop only for
consequential actions, and keep the walls that protect the team.” The spec is Whombat `docs/decisions/agent-computer.md`
(AC-00…AC-52; stream 1 of `docs/implementation/agent-computer/assignment.md`). An agent's computer is an unprivileged
container inside the appliance (AC-00, AC-01).

  null (≤ 253), reason: string | null (≤ 500)}}`, in `ApprovalAction` and in `SERVER_ONLY_ACTION_TYPES` (`['vault_use',
  'run_command']`): the server creates it when the runner's guard finds a command whose key is held at ask (AC-41); an
  agent can never ask for or perform one. `Approval.keyId` is the category's key.
- **Categories** (`computer/commands.ts`): `COMMAND_CATEGORIES` `deploy`, `deploy_production`, `merge`, `push_main`,
  `destructive`, `message_external`; `commandCategoryKey` / `COMMAND_CATEGORY_KEYS` → `deploy`, `deploy.production`,
  `merge.main`, `branch.main.push`, `commands.destructive`, `messages.external`; `COMMAND_CATEGORY_RANK` (most severe
  first: deploy to production > push to main > merge > deploy > destructive > outside message), `moreSevereCategory`;
  `COMMAND_MAX` 8000, `COMMAND_TARGET_MAX` 253, `COMMAND_REASON_MAX` 500.
- **Scope** (`COMMAND_SCOPES`, `CommandScope`: `once`, `task`, `agent`, AC-42). `approvals.decide`'s body is now the named
  `DecideApprovalBody` with optional `scope`: valid only with `approve` of a `run_command` (the server answers
  `validation_failed` otherwise); absent means `once`, so a client that doesn't know scopes allows once — the union grows
  as tolerated in CT-214. `Approval.scope` (nullable, optional) is the scope chosen; null while pending, after a decline
  and on every other action.
- **Keys and texts** (`keys/actions.ts`): `actionKey` → `commandCategoryKey`; `actionScope` names the branch of a push to
  main (`{branch}`), else `{}`; `describeAction` never quotes the command (it is signed, and may hold a value the agent
  shouldn't have put there): `runCommandPhrase` — “run a command on the production server web-1”, “run a deploy
  command”, “run a command that pushes to main”, “run a destructive command on staging”, “run a command that merges a pull
  request in o/r”, “run a command that sends a message to hooks.slack.com”.
- **Card** (`approvals/copy.ts`, `display.ts`): title `cap(describeAction)` (“Run a command on the production server
  web-1”), target “web-1 · Deploy to production” (target · the key's label), WHAT HAPPENS 01 “Run “<command on one line>”
  on Banjo’s computer”. `ApprovalView.content` = `{label: 'COMMAND', text: command}` (upper case like the mail body's
  `MESSAGE`: the web's section label upper-cases, Android's doesn't). New **`ApprovalView.scopeChoices`**: `[{scope,
  label}]` “Allow once”, “Allow for this task”, “Always allow for {Agent}” for a `run_command`, null for every other
  action; `cta`/`mobileCta` “Allow once”, `declineCta` “Don’t allow” (`COMMAND_DECLINE_CTA`). Verbs “run the command”
  (labels “APPROVED · RUNNING THE COMMAND”, “RAN”); executing and executed messages and the approve toast say how long
  the yes lasts (“Allowed once. Banjo runs the command in its turn.”, “Allowed for this task. …”, “Always allowed for
  Banjo. …”). No Undo: `undoBlock` answers `already_executed` as for `vault_use` (the command runs, or is refused, the
  moment a person answers).
- **What the agent reads** (`computer/copy.ts`): `commandBlockedText(category, agent)` for Off (exit 126, names the key
  and points at `request_approval` with `grant_key`), `commandWaitingText(category)`, `commandDeclinedText(person)` “Mara
  said no; the command didn’t run.” (exit 126), `commandTimedOutText(minutes)` (exit 125; the card stays and a later yes
  wakes the agent), `commandAllowedText(scope, person)`; `COMMAND_EXIT_CODES` `{refused: 126, timedOut: 125}`,

## CT-218 The guard: `classifyCommand` (contracts 0.36.0) (2026-10-02)

AC-40. `classifyCommand(command, {productionServers: {name, host, addresses?}[], defaultBranches?})` →
`{category, target, summary} | null` in `@whombat/core/computer` (`computer/classify.ts`), pure and synchronous, never
throws; about 230 cases in `classify.test.ts`. The runner runs it on every command of a computer turn; the server may run it
again on what the runner sent.

- **Reading the shell.** A small tokenizer: single and double quotes, `$'…'`, backslash escapes and line continuations,
  comments, redirections (their targets dropped, `2>&1`), here-documents and here-strings (kept as the command's stdin).
  Simple commands split at `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, `&`, newlines and parentheses; `$(…)` and backticks are commands of
  their own (`$((…))` is arithmetic, not); shell keywords (`if`, `then`, `do`, `{`, …) are skipped and `for`/`case`
  headers ignored. Each simple command is looked through: assignments (`VAR=…`, and `export VAR=…` for later commands),
  `sudo`/`doas` and their options, `env` (with `-i`, `-u`, `-C`, `-S`), `nohup`, `exec`, `command` (`command -v` is a
  lookup), `time`, `timeout [opts] N`, `nice`, `ionice`, `stdbuf`, `xargs`, `watch`, package runners (`npx`, `pnpx`,
  `bunx`, `pnpm|yarn|npm|bun exec|dlx|x`, versions stripped: `wrangler@3`), shells (`bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh|fish -c '…'`,
  `-lc`, and `-s` or a here-document as the script), and `ssh`, whose remote command (words joined, as ssh does) or
  here-document runs on that host. Nesting is followed to `CLASSIFY_MAX_DEPTH` 4 levels (the spec's “one level of
  `bash -c`” is a minimum).
- **ssh** parses the OpenSSH options that take a value (`BbcDEeFIiJLlmOoPpQRSWw`, attached or separate), also right after
  the destination; `[user@]host`, `ssh://user@host:port`; jump hosts (`-J`, `-o ProxyJump=`) and `-o HostName=` count as
  reached. `ssh -G` / `-V` connect nowhere: nothing. **scp/rsync/sftp**: operands `[user@]host:path`, `[v6]:path`,
  `host::module`, `rsync://`/`scp://`/`sftp://` URLs; sftp's first operand. A production server matches by name (the
  `ssh_config` alias), host or any of its addresses, case-insensitive, `user@`, brackets and a trailing dot ignored.
- **Categories.** ssh/scp/rsync/sftp to a production server → `deploy_production` (target the server's name).
  `docker -H …`/`--host=…`/`DOCKER_HOST=…` naming anything but a local socket (`unix://`, `npipe://`, `fd://`; the spec
  says `ssh://`, `tcp://` is another machine too) → `destructive` (target the host), `deploy_production` when it is a
  production server. Deploy tools → `deploy`, `deploy_production` when an argument names a production server: `fly|flyctl
  deploy`, `wrangler deploy|publish`, `wrangler pages|versions deploy|publish`, `vercel --prod|--production|--target
  production`, `netlify deploy --prod|-p|--prod-if-unlocked`, `kubectl apply|create|replace|patch|delete|rollout|scale`
  (not `rollout status|history`, which only read), `helm install|upgrade|rollback|uninstall|delete`, `terraform|tofu|
  terragrunt apply|destroy`, `pulumi up|update|destroy`, `docker|podman push`, `docker image push`, `npm|pnpm|yarn|bun
  publish`, `yarn npm publish`. `gh pr merge` and `gh api -X PUT …/pulls/N/merge` → `merge` (target the repository when
  named). `git push` whose refspec's destination is a default branch (`main`, `HEAD:main`, `+main`, `refs/heads/main`,
  `:main`, `--delete … main`, with or without `--force`) or with `--all`/`--mirror` → `push_main` (target the branch); a
  bare `git push`, `git push origin` or `HEAD` names no branch and is nothing (the branch isn't in the words).
  Destructive on another machine — inside an ssh remote command, any host: `rm` with recursive and force (`-rf`, `-fr`,
  `-Rf`, `-r -f`, `--recursive --force`), `DROP TABLE|DATABASE|SCHEMA` and `TRUNCATE` anywhere in the remote text,
  `docker compose down`, `docker-compose down`, `systemctl stop|disable|mask`, `mkfs*`, `dd of=/dev/…`; also (an addition)
  `psql|mysql|mariadb` with `DROP`/`TRUNCATE` against a host that isn't local (`-h`, a URL) → `destructive`, or
  `deploy_production` on a production server. Outside messages: `sendmail`, `swaks`, `msmtp`, `ssmtp` always; `mail`,
  `mailx`, `s-nail`, `mutt` with an address; `curl|wget|http|https|xh|xhs|httpie` with a URL of `hooks.slack.com`,
  `discord.com`/`discordapp.com` `/api/webhooks…`, `api.telegram.org/bot…/send…`, `outlook.office.com/webhook…`,
  `*.webhook.office.com` → `message_external` (target the host or the address).
- **Not asked**: destructive commands on the agent's own computer (`rm -rf node_modules`, `sudo rm -rf /`, `docker
  compose down`, `psql -h localhost …`), quoted text (`echo "fly deploy"`, `grep 'git push origin main' file`), comments,
  previews and reads (`vercel`, `terraform plan`, `kubectl get`), `ssh staging ls`.
- **Severity**: when several parts match, the most severe category wins, with its first match (`COMMAND_CATEGORY_RANK`).
- **Summaries** (the card's and the runner's line): “SSH to the production server web-1”, “Copy files to or from the
  production server web-1”, “Run Docker on the production server web-1”, “Deploy with fly to the production server
  web-1”, “Change a database on the production server db-prod”, “Deploy with fly”, “Publish a package with npm”, “Push an
  image with docker”, “Push to main”, “Push every branch, main included”, “Merge pull request #12”, “Merge a pull request
  in o/r”, “Run a destructive command on staging”, “Run Docker on staging”, “Send a message through hooks.slack.com”,
  “Send an email with sendmail”.
- **`normaliseCommand`**: runs of whitespace become one space, ends trimmed; quoting kept as written (allowances compare
  it, AC-42).
- `DEFAULT_BRANCHES` `['main', 'master']`, `ClassifyContext`, `ClassifyProductionServer`, `CommandClassification`.

## CT-220 The runner's computer API and `DispatchContext.computer` (contracts 0.36.0) (2026-10-02)

AC-02, AC-11, AC-30…AC-32, AC-40…AC-42. `contracts/runner.ts`.

- **`DispatchContext.computer?: DispatchComputerContext | null`** `{productionServers: ComputerProductionServer[]
  {entryId, name, host, port, addresses}, homeNetworks: string[] (CIDRs)}`: the turn's shell runs on the agent's
  computer. Production servers of every entry in the burrow (the wall closes them all, whoever's turn), addresses
  resolved when the turn starts; `entryId` added to the spec's shape so the runner can say which Vault entry opened.
  Null or absent: no computer. Optional, so no `SESSION_API_LEVEL` meaning (runner contract, CT-209).
- **`runner.authorizeCommand`** POST `/internal/runner/commands/authorize`, `AuthorizeCommandBody {dispatchId, attempt,
  runnerId, command, category, target, reason?}` → `AuthorizeCommandReply {outcome: run | blocked | pending,
  approvalId | null, message, open: ComputerOpening[] {host, port | null}}`. The lease is in the body (the path names no
  dispatch); 409 when the runner lost the dispatch.
- **`runner.authorizeWait`** GET `/commands/authorize/:approvalId?dispatchId&attempt&runnerId&waitMs` (long poll,
  `AuthorizeWaitQuery`, `waitMs` ≤ 30 s, default 25 s) → `AuthorizeWaitReply {outcome: run | declined | pending, scope |
  null, message, open}`.
- **`runner.computerKeys`** GET `/dispatches/:dispatchId/computer-keys?runnerId&attempt` → `ComputerKeys {files: {path:
  ComputerKeyPath, mode ('600'/'0600'), base64}[], env: {name, value}[], needles: string[], entries: {entryId, name,
  ownerName}[]}`. `ComputerKeyPath`: relative, ≤ 4 plain segments of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, never `.`/`..`. GET as the
  assignment said, with the lease in the query; it holds secrets, so the server answers it once per attempt.
- **`runner.computerReport`** POST `/dispatches/:dispatchId/computer-report`, `ComputerReportBody {dispatchId, attempt,
  runnerId, sweep: {files (≤ 200 absolute paths), replaced}}` → `OkResponse`; the owners are told, `vault.swept` signed.
  `dispatchId` is in the body too, as the assignment's shape; it must equal the path's.

  screens (Banjo's “× Merge into main”, “× Deploy”) stay as drawn. Changing `ROLE_DEFAULT_KEYS` alone would have changed

## CT-240 Contracts 0.39.1: a retired agent can't hold a Vault key (2026-10-02)

John found retired agents in a Vault entry's “Give a key to…” list. `vaultKeyHolderProblem` is the one rule for the
server's list, the server's `vault.giveKey` check and the clients' re-check, and it didn't know about retirement (EP-04:
a retired agent keeps no keys). Its input's `agent` takes an optional `retiredAt` (ISO string or `Date`, so the server
passes its row and the clients a `Principal`), and a new code `retired`, “That agent is retired, so it can’t hold a key.”,
checked right after `system`. On the wire this is only a new value of `VaultErrorDetails.reason`, which is a plain string:
every 0.39.0 payload parses, no session API level change. `mentionTargetsFor` and `agentWorksFor` keep retired agents on
purpose (they resolve names in history); pickers filter with `isActivePrincipal`. Every package is 0.39.1.

## CT-241 The file view: `prs.file` (contracts 0.40.0) (2026-10-02)

John, 2026-10-02: clicking a file in a branch room's Files changed should open the file in a full, view-only editor that
shows the changes with the `+ −` colours. A PR carried only each file's counts, so this adds the file itself. The
runtime side is Whombat `docs/decisions/pr-file-view.md`, the web's whombat-app `docs/decisions/pr-file-view.md`.

- `prs.file` `GET /burrows/:burrow/prs/:number/file?repo=&path=` → `PrFileView {path, status: added|modified|deleted,
  shown: text|binary|too_large, add, del, lines, baseSha, headSha}`. `lines` is the whole head version with the base's
  removed lines in place, each `PrFileLine {kind: context|add|del (DiffLineKind), old, new, text}` numbered in its
  version(s). A whole file rather than hunks: the view is an editor, not a patch. 404 when the PR doesn't change `path`.
  The base is the merge base of the PR's base branch and its head, so the lines match Files changed's counts.
- One rule for the lines, pure in core: `fileViewLines(base, head)` — Myers' line diff after the common start and end,
  removals before additions within each change (as a unified diff shows them), lines cut at `PR_FILE_LINE_MAX` (2000)
  with `…`; past 2000 edits the middle is shown as removed then added (bounded memory). `splitFileLines` (`\n`/`\r\n`,
  no phantom last line), `looksBinary` (a NUL in the first 8 KiB, git's rule). Limits: `PR_FILE_MAX_BYTES` 1 MiB per
  version and `PR_FILE_MAX_LINES` 20 000 lines, else `too_large`; `PR_FILE_SHOWN_TEXT` says why there are no lines.
- Retry safety `safe` (READ). A view above 64 KiB is read through an export stream like every read (G-03), so no new
  limit for the session.
- Feature `prs.file` (`SINCE_0_40`): a client makes file rows openable only on runtimes that have it. Additive and
  gated, so `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 29 (as CT-216). The fixture world answers it for PR #482 with made-up versions
  (`prFileVersions`) that give each file exactly its `+add −del`. Every package is 0.40.0.
