## CT-243 `gh` through Whombat: `runner.ghAuthorize` and `DispatchContext.gh` (contracts 0.41.0) (2026-10-03)

John, 2026-10-03: once GitHub is signed in under Settings → Repositories, Banjo should use it directly. Agreed on the
condition that the token never enters the agent's environment: the agent's shell gets a stand-in `gh` that hands each
command to Whombat, which decides it by the agent's keys and the burrow's switched-on repositories (Whombat
`docs/decisions/agent-gh.md` AGH-01…). The wire parts:

- `DispatchContext.gh` (`GhDispatchContext {repos, defaultRepo}`, nullable, optional): the turn's `gh` goes through
  Whombat, for these switched-on GitHub repositories; `defaultRepo` for commands that name none. Null or absent: it
  doesn't (older servers too).
- `runner.ghAuthorize` `POST /internal/runner/dispatches/:dispatchId/gh` (runner token, `RunnerLease`):
  `GhAuthorizeBody {args, files[{path, base64}], stdin}` (bounded by `GH_ARGS_MAX` 200, `GH_ARG_MAX`, `GH_FILES_MAX` 8;
  `GH_INPUT_MAX_BYTES` 1 MiB is the stand-in's and the runner's limit) → `GhAuthorizeReply`: `run {args, repo, token,
  expiresAt}` (the runner runs the real gh with exactly these words) or `done {exitCode, stdout, stderr}` (Whombat
  answered: its own commands, a refusal, a card).
- `ClassifyContext.ghThroughWhombat`: a computer turn's guard leaves `gh` to Whombat, so a `gh pr merge` is decided
  once (by “Merge into main” in Whombat), not asked twice.
- Copy: `pr.comment`'s description now covers issues (“Leave comments on pull requests and issues, and open, edit and
  close issues.”; the label stays the mock's); `merge_pull_request`'s description says `gh pr merge` is the same merge
  where gh goes through Whombat.

Additive (optional fields, a new runner endpoint the runtime's own runner calls): no session API level change, no
feature flag — clients don't see it. Every package is 0.41.0.

## CT-244 `ssh_upload`: copy a folder of the working directory to a Vault server (contracts 0.42.0) (2026-10-03)

John, 2026-10-03, after Banjo merged the website's PR but couldn't publish it: “It has full root access to the server
via the vault keys … I would like Banjo to … figure out itself how to publish it.” Without a computer (the dev stack's
agents have none, Whombat AC-23) an agent could run commands and write files whose content it typed itself, but had no
way to move a build onto a server. The wire parts:

- MCP tool `ssh_upload` (`VaultSshUploadInput {entry, server, from, to}` → `VaultSshUploadOutput`: `ok {files, bytes}`
  or `VaultToolRefusal`): `from` is a folder of the turn's working directory, read by the runner exactly as for
  `browser_preview` (CT-198: inside the working directory, no symlinks, no `.git`, at most
  `BROWSER_PREVIEW_MAX_FILES` / `_BYTES`); `to` a folder on the server, made if missing, files with the same names
  replaced. `requiredKey: null`, decided like `ssh_write_file` (use kind `ssh`). In `VAULT_SSH_TOOL_NAMES`, so it is
  listed and allowed wherever the other SSH tools are.
- `vaultSshUseWhat` gains `{tool: 'upload', server, path, from}` → “upload dist → web-1:/var/www/site/releases/r2”.
- Copy: `VAULT_SSH_AGENT_RULES` adds how to publish with it (build, upload into a new folder, switch with ssh_exec);
  `VAULT_ACCESS_RULES`' first line names `ssh_upload` among the ways SSH goes.

Additive (a new tool an agent only sees from a runtime that lists it): no session API level change, no feature flag.
Every package is 0.42.0.

## CT-245 A Vault yes for the task; access rules that look for another way first (contracts 0.43.0) (2026-10-03)

John, 2026-10-03, after a day of one-turn Vault cards and an agent that stopped at the first refusal: re-think it the
way Hermes Agent works (Whombat `docs/decisions/goal-first.md`). The wire parts:

- `approvals.decide`'s `scope` is valid for a `vault_use` too (GF-05): `once` (this turn, as before) or `task` (the
  rest of the run, or of the thread without a run); `agent` stays a `run_command`'s only. `ApprovalView.scopeChoices`
  for a `vault_use`: “Allow for one turn”, “Allow for this task” (`VAULT_SCOPE_LABELS`); its messages and toasts say

Additive (an optional field's new value a server accepts; a client that doesn't know it still allows once): no session
API level change. Every package is 0.43.0.

## CT-246 Keys by risk: six rows, everything else on (contracts 0.44.0) (2026-10-03)

John, 2026-10-03: “make the agents really capable … I think that we have too many restrictions”. The spec is Whombat
`docs/decisions/resourceful-agents.md` (RA-01…RA-62; this is stream C of
`docs/implementation/resourceful-agents/assignment.md`). The keys part (RA-01, RA-02, RA-04), in `@whombat/core/keys`:

- **Six risk rows (RA-01).** `KEY_TIER_ROWS` is `['deploy', 'merge', 'branch.main.push', 'commands.destructive',
  'messages.external', 'refunds.issue']` (RA-01's order; until 0.43 Merge, Deploy, Push to main). A row is still named
  by its first key (CT-222), so every row helper keeps working; what people read is `keyTierRowLabel(row)` from
  `KEY_RISK_ROWS` (`KeyRiskRow {row, label, description, keys, verb}`): Deploy, Merge into main, Push to main,
  Destructive commands on other machines, Message people outside the burrow, Money. `KEY_TIER_ROW_KEYS`: Deploy →
  `deploy`, `deploy.staging`, `deploy.production`; Merge → `merge`, `merge.main`; Money → `refunds.issue`,
  `billing.write`; the others one key each. `KEY_TIER_ROW_READS` reads the same keys (Deploy without the bare
  umbrella, as before). `RISK_ROW_KEYS` lists all ten. `KeyRowTiers` grows by three optional rows.
- **Money writes both keys.** `billing.write` isn't under `refunds.issue` in the catalog, so `withKeyRowTier` now writes
  every key of a row that no other key of the row covers (`coveredInRow`), not only the umbrella: setting Money always
  writes `refunds.issue` and `billing.write`; Deploy and Merge still write their narrower keys only when held.
- **Everything else is on (RA-02).** `ALWAYS_ON_KEYS`: every key with `agentMaxTier` `can` that is neither personal nor
  in a risk row, except `ALWAYS_ON_EXCEPTIONS` (`pr.approve`, reviews stay a person's thing; `packs.tool.write`, asks),
  one id per permission — other wordings (`repos.read_all`, `branch.feature.write`, `code.change`) and the bundle
  `tests_ci.run` (it brings in `tests.run` and `ci.run`, both listed) are left out. 25 keys, catalog order.
  `isAlwaysOnKey` (wordings count). Every team role's `ROLE_DEFAULT_KEYS` is the same set: can `ALWAYS_ON_KEYS`, ask
  `RISK_ROW_KEYS` and `packs.tool.write`, cannot none. `SEED_ROLE_KEYS` (the mock world) is unchanged; its Associate
  and Assistant entries are frozen as they were.
- **The Assistant (RA-04).** `PERSONAL_AGENT_EXTRA_KEYS` (`messages.search`, `memory.propose`, `skills.propose`,
  `workspace.scratch`, `web.browse`, `browser.use`, `tasks.create`) is what `personalAgentMayHold` allows besides the
  personal keys; `PERSONAL_DEFAULT_GRANTS` holds them all at can (so a new assistant gets them through
  `personalDefaultGrants`, no runtime change), `ASSISTANT_ALWAYS_ON_KEYS` is the same list, and `PERSONAL_KEY_OPTIONS`
  (the assistant's Configure) lists them before the personal keys.
- **Hire.** `hireKeyOptions(role)` and `HIRE_KEY_OPTIONS` are the six rows, Off · Ask · On, at Ask for every team role
  (legacy roles too), never locked. `hireGrants` grants `ALWAYS_ON_KEYS` at can (`channels.read` scoped to the agent's
  channels when given), every key of each row at its tier (`tiers[row]`, else can when `selected` lists the row, else the
  role's default, else Ask), `packs.tool.write` at ask (can when selected) and other selected keys at can; `selected`
  can't switch an always-on key off. `ROLE_LOCKED_NOTE` is deprecated.
- **Configure.** The six rows first; under All keys `ALL_KEY_OPTIONS`: `ALWAYS_ON_KEYS` as switches (on), `pr.approve`
  (a switch, off) and `packs.tool.write` as a three-state option of its own key (`defaultTier: 'ask'`). The configure
  helpers take any option with `defaultTier` as three-state (`isThreeStateOption`): a row by `keyRowTier` /
  `withKeyRowTier`, a single key by `keyHeldTier` (the former private `heldLevelTier`, exported) and its own grant.
  `ConfigureEdit.tiers`/`baseTiers` and `configureKeyTiers` use `KeyTiers` (`Partial<Record<KeyId, Tier>>`; a
  `KeyRowTiers` fits in it).
- **Requests.** `requestedTier` is ask for every key of the six rows (MDS-04 widened): a request for an outside message
  or billing data is given at ask, Money's request sets the whole row to ask.

## CT-247 `alwaysOnUpgrade`: existing agents get the always-on keys (contracts 0.44.0) (2026-10-03)

RA-03, for Whombat's migration 0066. `alwaysOnUpgrade(grants, personSwitchedOff, {personal?})` → `{grants, added,
raised}`, pure: every always-on key (`ASSISTANT_ALWAYS_ON_KEYS` for a personal agent) held at `cannot` becomes `can`
(the grant's own wording and scope kept), and every one with no grant of its own is added at `can` — unless it is in
`personSwitchedOff` (the server's list of keys a person last changed to cannot or away after the hire; wordings count).
A key isn't added while a person switched off a key above it (`code.write` above the branch keys) or a bundle that
brings it in (`browser.use` → `web.browse`), nor while an umbrella or a bundle it holds already gives it at can. Keys
held at `ask` stay ask (RA-03 names only no-grant and cannot), risk rows and every other key keep their tier.
Idempotent. `alwaysOnUpgradeText(agent)` “Whombat gave Banjo the keys every agent has now” for the one Keys event
(`keys.upgraded`).

## CT-249 “Always allow” on a risk-row card (contracts 0.44.0) (2026-10-03)

RA-06. `alwaysAllowRow(action)` (`keys/actions.ts`): the row of the key a typed action of `ALWAYS_ALLOW_ACTION_TYPES`
needs — `deploy`, `merge_pr`, `push_shared_branch` (to the default branch only), `message_external`, `refund` — else
null (never `custom`, `grant_key`, personal actions, `vault_use`, `run_command`). `approvals.decide` takes `scope:

## CT-250 A person's profile and an agent's notes (contracts 0.44.0) (2026-10-03)

RA-20…RA-23, RA-26 (`domain/memory.ts`, `contracts/memory.ts`).

- **Entries.** `ProfileEntry {id (pfe_), text ≤ 300, kind 'stated'|'inferred', writtenBy, createdAt, updatedAt}`,
  `NoteEntry {id (nte_), text ≤ 500, writtenBy, createdAt, updatedAt}`; `PROFILE_BUDGET` 2000, `NOTES_BUDGET` 4000,
  `MEMORY_LIMITS`, `MEMORY_OPERATIONS_MAX` 10. A profile belongs to a person of a burrow (a principal).
- **`applyMemoryOps(entries, ops, {budget, entryMax, writtenBy, now, newId, defaultKind?})`**, pure and atomic: add,
  replace, remove in order on a copy; `match` is a piece of exactly one entry's text, case and spacing aside, an entry
  whose whole text is `match` winning over ones that only contain it; texts normalised (`normalizeMemoryText`: one
  line); an add of a text the store holds is a no-op; a replace keeps the entry's kind unless one is given; every new
  text checked against `entryMax` (`too_long`) and `scanMemoryText` (`scan_refused`); the budget checked on the result
  only (`memory_full` returns the store unchanged). Errors `no_match`, `ambiguous_match` carry the operation's index.
- **`scanMemoryText`**: `literalSecretKind` (tokens, private keys, passwords in URLs, random-looking keys: “Secrets
  belong in the Vault, never in memory.”) and the pack scanner's dangerous findings read as prose (injection, hidden
  characters, imitated delimiters).
- **The `memory` tool** (no key): `{target: 'profile'|'notes', operations: 1–10}` → `ok {target, entries [{text, kind
  | null}], usedChars, budgetChars}`, `memory_full` (same, plus the message), `no_match | ambiguous_match | too_long |
  scan_refused {message, operation}`, `unavailable {message}`. Its description carries RA-22 and RA-23 (what goes
  where, declarative facts, never a person's private details in notes). `propose_instruction` stays defined;
  `UNLISTED_MCP_TOOL_NAMES` (`['propose_instruction']`) is what servers from 0.44 don't list.
- **Dispatch.** `DispatchContext.profile` (`{person: {id, name}, entries} | null`: null when the turn isn't for a person
  or learning is off) and `DispatchContext.notes` (`{entries} | null`), optional.
- **REST** (area `memory`): `memory.profile` GET `/burrows/:burrow/profile`, `memory.addProfileEntry` POST
  `…/profile/entries` (`stated` by default), `memory.updateProfileEntry` PATCH `…/profile/entries/:entryId`,
  `memory.removeProfileEntry` DELETE, `memory.setLearning` PUT `…/profile/learning` — all answer
  `PersonProfileResponse {learning, entries, usedChars, budgetChars, eventId}`; `memory.notes` GET
  `/burrows/:burrow/agents/:agent/notes`, `memory.updateNote` PATCH `…/notes/:noteId`, `memory.removeNote` DELETE —
  `AgentNotesResponse {entries, usedChars, budgetChars, canEdit, eventId}`. Refusals are `validation_failed` with
  `details.reason` (an `applyMemoryOps` error).
- **Copy**: `PROFILE_COPY` (“What your agents know about you”, “Let agents learn about me”, You said / Inferred, …),
  `NOTES_COPY` / `notesCopy(agent)`, `memoryUsageText` (“1,240 of 2,000 characters”), `profileEntryKindLabel`.
- **Search (RA-26)**: `search` takes `mine?: boolean` (the agent's own earlier messages and runs); its description says
  words match as written and by English stems.

## CT-251 Agents schedule their own turns (contracts 0.44.0) (2026-10-03)

RA-30 (`domain/schedules.ts`, `contracts/mcp-schedules.ts`, `contracts/schedules.ts`).

- **`ScheduleWhen`**: `{kind: 'at', at}` (an instant with its offset), `{kind: 'every', minutes ≥ 5}`, `{kind: 'cron',
  expr, zone}`. `AgentSchedule {id (sch_), agentId, conversationId, threadRootId, forAccountId, prompt ≤ 2000, when,
  status active|paused|ended, endedReason (done, cancelled, expired, person_left, agent_retired), nextAt, endsAt, runs,
  lastRunAt, createdAt}`; `AgentScheduleView` adds `forName`, `canChange`, and `prompt` null for a viewer who can't
  read the room.
- **Pure rules**: `nextScheduleRun(when, after, {anchor?})` (a one-off once; `every` from its anchor; cron in its own
  zone with the automations' DST rules: a skipped time shifted, a repeated one once), `scheduleEndsAt` (90 days for a
  repeating one), `scheduleWhenProblem` (a past or > 1 year one-off, a bad cron or zone, one that never runs or runs
  more often than every 5 minutes), `scheduleLimitProblem` (20 active), `describeScheduleWhen` (“Once, Sun 4 Oct at
  09:00”, “Every 30 minutes”, “Weekdays at 08:30 · Europe/Amsterdam”), `schedulePromptLine`, `scheduleActions`.
- **The `schedule` tool** (no key): `{action: create|list|cancel, when?, prompt?, scheduleId?}` (refined per action) →
  `ok {schedule | null, schedules, others}`, `invalid {problems}`, `unavailable {message}`. `list` shows the schedules in
  this conversation and those for the person this turn is for; the rest are only counted, so one person's reminders
  never reach another's turn.
- **The card**: `ScheduleCard {kind: 'schedule', scheduleId, schedule: AgentScheduleView | null}` (server-made,
  resolved per viewer; stored by reference; never postable), `scheduleCardTitle` “Dusty scheduled: …”,
  `scheduleCardText`. Cancel is `schedules.remove`.
- **REST** (area `schedules`): `schedules.list` GET `/burrows/:burrow/agents/:agent/schedules`, `schedules.pause` /
  `schedules.resume` POST `…/:scheduleId/pause|resume` (resume also renews an `expired` one for 90 days),
  `schedules.remove` DELETE — the person a schedule is for and people who hold `agents.manage`.
- **Dispatch**: trigger `schedule` (it existed, unused) with `DispatchContext.schedule {id, prompt, when, runs, nextAt?}`.

## CT-253 The computer: the LAN, published ports, keep-awake (contracts 0.44.0) (2026-10-03)

RA-41…RA-44.

- **LAN.** `Burrow.agentsReachLan?` (absent = on), `agentsReachLanOn(burrow)`, `AGENTS_REACH_LAN_COPY`, and its own
  setter `burrows.setAgentsReachLan` PUT `/burrows/:burrow/agents-reach-lan` `{agentsReachLan}` → `{burrow, eventId}`
  (owners, `burrow.manage`; signs `burrow.agents_lan_changed`, Keys) rather than `burrows.update`: opening the network
  is a security change with its own event. `DispatchComputerContext.lan?: boolean` (absent: false).
- **Ports and keep-awake.** `PublishedPort {port, hostPort, name | null, url | null}`, `AgentComputer.published`
  (default `[]`, at most `COMPUTER_PUBLISHED_MAX` 5) and `keepAwakeUntil` (default null); `COMPUTER_PUBLISH_PORTS`
  20000–20099, `KEEP_AWAKE_MAX_DAYS` 7, `PUBLISHED_PORT_NAME_PATTERN`. Ops `computers.unpublish` POST
  `…/computer/unpublish` `{port}` and `computers.sleep` POST `…/computer/sleep` (people who hold `agents.manage`; sign
  `agent.computer` with `unpublish` / `sleep`). Copy `COMPUTER_PORTS_COPY`, `publishedPortLine`,
  `computerKeepAwakeLine`.
- **Memory by hardware (RA-45).** `computerMemoryMiB(applianceMemoryMiB)`: min(`COMPUTER_DEFAULTS.memoryMiB` 4096, a
  quarter of the appliance's memory), what computerd uses when `WHOMBAT_COMPUTERS_MEMORY_MB` isn't set, so computerd
  and the appliance's setting follow one rule.

## CT-254 Learned skills grow; skills from a link (contracts 0.44.0) (2026-10-03)

RA-25, RA-54.

- `OWN_PACK_SKILLS_MAX` 100 (the manifest's `skills` limit too), `SKILL_FILES_MAX` 16, `SKILL_FILES_MAX_BYTES` 256 KB,
  `OWN_PACK_LIMITS` (`PACK_LIMITS` with 2000 files and 32 MB, for the own pack's next version). A skill's files sit next
  to `SKILL.md` or in `SKILL_FILE_DIRS` (`references/`, `templates/`, `scripts/`): `skillFileDirProblem`, enforced by
  `SkillFilePath` (RA-25 lists the three folders; files next to `SKILL.md` stay allowed as before, so Anthropic-style
  skills with `forms.md` beside the body import whole).
- `propose_skill` takes `source` (`SkillSource`, https); `SkillProposalSummary.source?` (nullable, optional: builders
  and older servers leave it out). The description adds fixing a skill that was wrong (RA-16), the folders, `source`
  and RA-21's rule (never a person's private details).
- **From a link**: `skills.previewLink` POST `/burrows/:burrow/agents/:agent/skill-links/preview` `{url}` →
  `SkillLinkPreview {previewId (slp_), url, name, description, files [{path, bytes}], verdict, findings, problems,
  canAdd, expiresAt}`; `skills.addLink` POST `…/skill-links` `{previewId}` → `{proposal, eventId}` (201, signs
  `skill.learned`). The agent is in the path, as every agent op. Pure helpers: `skillLinkRawUrl` (GitHub blob/tree
  pages → raw `SKILL.md`; core has no URL class, so by hand) and `skillLinkFiles(body)` (the files a body links or names
  in inline code that a skill may carry, once each, at most 16). `SKILL_LINK_COPY`.

## CT-256 Session API level 30, features, operation safety, audit types, fixtures (contracts 0.44.0) (2026-10-03)

- **`SESSION_API_LEVEL` 30** (window 28…31): new session ops (`memory.*` profile and notes, `schedules.*`,
  `computers.unpublish`, `computers.sleep`, `burrows.setAgentsReachLan`, `skills.previewLink`, `skills.addLink`) and grown
  unions a session answer carries (`MessageCard` `schedule`, `DispatchTrigger`, `KeyRowTiers`). Go's `SessionAPILevel`
  follows; `pnpm gen` changes nothing else.
- **Features** (`SINCE_0_44`): `agents.memory` (profile, notes, the memory tool, reflection, skills from a link),
  `agents.schedules` (schedules and notify), `agents.risk_rows` (the six rows, always-on keys, “Always allow”, the LAN
  switch, ports and keep-awake).
- **Operation safety**: reads `READ`; `memory.addProfileEntry`, `updateProfileEntry`, `setLearning`, `updateNote`,
  `schedules.pause`, `resume`, `computers.sleep`, `burrows.setAgentsReachLan`, `skills.previewLink` (it only fetches and
  stores a new preview), `skills.addLink` (content-addressed like `skills.decide`) `RECEIPT`; `memory.removeProfileEntry`,
  `memory.removeNote`, `schedules.remove`, `computers.unpublish` `DESTRUCTIVE`.
- **Audit event types**: `keys.upgraded`, `burrow.agents_lan_changed`, `notes.changed` (Keys); `profile.changed` (System,
  hidden: private), `schedule.created|paused|resumed|ended` (System). Ids `pfe`, `nte`, `sch`, `slp`.
- **Fixtures**: the mock world keeps its keys (`SEED_ROLE_KEYS`); the fixture fetch serves an empty profile, empty
  notes and no schedules (`memory.profile`, `memory.notes`, `schedules.list`); its hire follows `hireGrants`.

## CT-257 Names and details that differ from the assignment (2026-10-03)

- Risk rows are named by their first key (`refunds.issue` is Money), labels from `keyTierRowLabel` (CT-246).
- `alwaysOnUpgrade` takes a third optional `{personal}` for the Assistant (RA-04's “existing ones through 0066”) and
  returns `{grants, added, raised}` (CT-247).
- The `once` choice of a risk-row card is labelled with the card's `cta`, not “Approve” (the mock's “Approve and deploy” /
  “Approve in advance” stay), and `canChangeAgentKeys` / `toasts.always` are additions (CT-249).
- `nextScheduleRun(when, after, {anchor})`: a cron's zone is in its `when`, so the third argument is the `every` anchor,

## CT-259 Contracts 0.44.1: usage as billed, the context size, a stable-prompt hash (2026-10-03)

John, 2026-10-03, on a 75 000-token Pippa turn: “I want prompts to be efficient.” Whombat `docs/decisions/prompt-efficiency.md`
PE-01…PE-10 (rows PE-DC01…). A patch over 0.44.0: optional fields and pure helpers only, so every 0.44.0 payload parses
both ways, no feature name and no `SESSION_API_LEVEL` change (as CT-215).

- **Usage (PE-04).** `SpendUsage` (which `CompleteBody.usage` now is, same fields as before) takes `UsageCacheFields`:
  `cacheReadTokens` and `cacheWriteTokens` (parts of `inputTokens`, which stays the total of every input token, cached or
  not) and `largestCallInputTokens` (the largest model call's input: the context the provider session reached). The
  same optional fields ride on `MemoryContext.usage` (the checkpoint nudge), `MemorySession.lastUsage` and
  `AgentContextResponse.lastTurn.usage` (cached vs uncached in the usage view), and `SpendTotals` takes
  `cacheReadTokens`/`cacheWriteTokens`, present once a turn in the window reported a split, so totals from older
  runners compare equal to 0.44.0's. No cross-field refinement (reads ≤ input): a runner's slip must not lose a turn's
  completion; the helpers clamp instead.
- **`billedTokens(usage)`** — uncached input + cache writes + output in full, cache reads at `CACHE_READ_WEIGHT` (0.1),
  rounded; without a split, input + output. `spendTokens(totals)` is now `billedTokens(totals)`, so spend lines and the
  overview's ordering count as billed, and handoff budgets (`HandoffContext.used.tokens`, `SpendHandoffs`,
  `SpendPlanRow`) are documented as billed. Cache writes count 1×, not the 1.25× Claude bills for five-minute writes:
  a budget is a guard, not an invoice, and Codex has no write price.
- **`usageContextTokens(usage)`** — `largestCallInputTokens`, else `inputTokens` (older runners: the turn's sum, an
  overestimate). Session rotation and the checkpoint nudge use it.
- **The stable-prompt hash (PE-03).** `PromptHash` (8–128 of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`; `stablePromptHash(prompt)` = sha-256
  hex of the UTF-8 bytes) travels with the provider session id: `ProgressBody.promptHash` (the beat that reports
  `providerSessionId`) and `CompleteBody.promptHash` from the runner, `DispatchContext.resumePromptHash` (nullable,
  optional) from the server when it hands `dispatch.providerSessionId` back. The server can't know the prompt before
  the runner renders it, so the runner decides: it resumes only on an exact match. On a mismatch it starts a fresh
  session with the context it got — unless the window holds only what is new since that session's last turn
  (`memory.session.resumed`), too little to start over with; then it runs nothing and completes `failed` with
  **`SESSION_PROMPT_CHANGED`** (`session_prompt_changed`, like `RUNNER_SHUTDOWN` a plain error string an older server
  treats as a failure). A newer server retires the session and queues the turn again at once, uncounted, for a fresh
  session with the whole window. Null `resumePromptHash` (a session an older runner recorded) never matches; absent
  (older server) means resume as before.

Every package is 0.44.1.

## CT-260 Contracts 0.44.2: earlier runs carry over, a run on a pull request uses its branch (2026-10-04)

John, 2026-10-04, after Banjo's deploy run re-read what his fix run had read two minutes earlier, on a new branch:
“Implement the improvements.” Whombat `docs/decisions/agent-efficiency.md` AE-05, AE-06 (rows AE-DR…). A patch over
0.44.1: optional fields only, so every 0.44.1 payload parses both ways, no feature name and no `SESSION_API_LEVEL`
change (as CT-259).

- **`DispatchContext.earlierRuns` (AE-06).** With `run`: the burrow's earlier runs on the run's pull request, else on its
  repository and branch — those the turn's audience may read — newest first, the run itself not among them. Each
  `EarlierRun` is `number`, `title`, `status`, `summary` (the line it finished with, null when it didn't) and `log`, its
  last lines, oldest first. Bounded: `EARLIER_RUNS_MAX` 3 runs, `EARLIER_RUN_LOG_LINES_MAX` 12 lines, each at most
  `EARLIER_RUN_LOG_LINE_MAX` 300 characters (the server cuts a longer one; the contract refuses it). The runner shows them
  in the turn's message, never the stable system prompt (PE-02): build on what they found, don't redo their checks
  unless something changed. Their words are agents' own: data in a delimited block, not instructions. Absent or empty:
  none (older servers).
- **`start_run` and a pull request (AE-05).** `prNumber` says that an open pull request's branch is the run's, whatever
  `branch` says (the server asks the branch key for that branch); the `ok` outcome may carry `branch`, the branch the
  run works on. Absent from older servers.

Every package is 0.44.2.

## CT-263 Contracts 0.46.0: a reply that names nobody finds its agent (2026-10-05)

John, 2026-10-05: in a thread with only Banjo he still had to write `@Banjo`; in a channel with several people a
reply meant for the agent should reach it without the mention. Whombat `docs/decisions/reply-to.md` (RT-01…).

- **`replyAddressee(input)`** (`@whombat/core/text`, `addressee.ts`): the agent a person's message is for when it
  names nobody, or null. A mention or a broadcast names someone: null. In a thread: the agent whose message is the
  last before yours (your own skipped); when you are the only person who wrote in the thread, the agent that last
  wrote there or that you named there. At the top level: the same when you are the only person in the conversation;
  otherwise only the agent whose message is the last before yours, when it answered you (it names you, or the person
  message before it is yours) and it is at most `REPLY_WINDOW_MINUTES` (10) old. One rule for the server and the
  composers.
- **`SendMessageBody.to`** (optional, nullable `PrincipalId`): the composer's “To Banjo” chip. An id wakes that agent
  as a mention would; null wakes nobody beyond what the text names (the chip was removed); absent, the runtime applies
  `replyAddressee` itself, so older clients get the rule too.
- **Feature `messages.reply_to`**: a client shows the chip only on runtimes that have it. An older runtime ignores
  `to` (Zod strips it) and wakes only on mentions, as before.
- **No `SESSION_API_LEVEL` change** (stays 31): the operation gains an optional input field that the feature name
  covers, and its output is unchanged. A bump would have put level-28 runtimes outside the window of new clients for
  nothing.

Every package is 0.46.0.

## CT-265 Contracts 0.47.0: a person's photo (2026-10-05)

John, 2026-10-05: “Add the ability to change a person's avatar.” Until now a person was always their initials on a tone.
Whombat `docs/decisions/person-avatars.md` (PVA-01…), whombat-app `docs/decisions/person-avatars.md`.

- **`Person.avatarUrl`** (optional, nullable): the URL of their photo, an attachment URL (`attachmentUrl`), so web and
  Android load it exactly like an image attachment, over HTTP or through the session's resource streams, with no new
  transfer. Absent or null: the initials on `tone`, as before; clients show the initials while the photo loads or when
  it fails.
- **`me.setAvatar`** `PUT /me/avatar` `{image: base64 | null}` → `ProfileResponse`: account-wide like
  `me.updateProfile` (the account and the person in each burrow, a signed `member.updated` in each). The photo travels
  as base64 inside the request rather than through `uploads.create`: an upload is reserved for a conversation and a
  photo belongs to none, and a cropped photo is small. `AVATAR_MAX_BYTES` 32 KiB decoded keeps the request inside one
  64 KiB session control message; clients crop and scale to an `AVATAR_PIXELS` (256) square first. JPEG, PNG or WebP
  (`AVATAR_TYPES`, sniffed by the runtime; never SVG), each side `AVATAR_MIN_PIXELS`…`AVATAR_MAX_PIXELS`. Retry safety
  `RECEIPT`.
- **Feature `people.avatars`** (`SINCE_0_47`): “Change photo” only on runtimes that have it. Additive and gated, so
  `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 31 (as CT-216, CT-241). An older runtime has no `avatarUrl` (initials as before).

Every package is 0.47.0.

## CT-266 The connections catalog in `@whombat/core` (contracts 0.48.0) (2026-10-05)

John, 2026-10-05: “For Whombat Connections I would like to extend the connections a lot, for example Home Assistant,
Dropbox, Notion, Todoist, Nextcloud, Moneybird, etc.” Whombat `docs/decisions/connections-catalog.md` (CX-01…CX-75).

- **`domain/connections-catalog.ts`** (exported from `@whombat/core/domain` and the root): pure data and helpers.
  `CATALOG` (validated `CatalogEntry` objects, overview order), `CATALOG_IDS` / `CatalogId` (the 19 v1 entries: builtins
  `github`, `google`, `microsoft`, `feedback`; `homeassistant`, `notion`, `todoist`, `nextcloud`, `dropbox`, `moneybird`,
  `paperless`, `immich`, `proxmox`, `hetzner`, `mollie`, `gitlab`, `forgejo`, `custom_mcp`, `custom_api`), `CatalogIdText`
  (an open slug: payloads carry it, so a newer runtime's entries parse), `CATALOG_CONNECTABLE`.
- **Entry shape**: `id`, `name`, `category` (`CATALOG_CATEGORIES`, labels), one-line `description`, `scopes` /
  `defaultScope`, `signIn` (`CatalogSignIn`: `token` with `TokenAuth` bearer · header{name, template over `{secret}` and
  fields} · basic{usernameField} · query{name}; `nextcloud_login`; `ha_oauth`; `mcp_oauth` with an optional fixed
  `mcpUrl`; `app_oauth` with authorize/token/revoke URLs, scopes, extra parameters, `clientSecretOptional` and the console
  link; `none` for a Custom MCP server), `fields` (`CatalogField`: url | text | select, required, default, validation
  pattern, `fromService`, `methods`, `guide`), `transport` (`ConnectionTransport`; a sign-in may override it: Notion's token
  is `rest`), `baseUrl` template, `mcpPath`, `mcpMissingHint`, `check` (`CatalogCheck`: request | mcp | reach), typed
  `tools` (`ConnectionToolDef`), `request` (`RequestSpec`: prefixes as templates, methods, read methods, read paths, fixed
  headers, extra agent headers, other bases, `alongsideMcp`), `guide` (≤ `CONNECTION_GUIDE_MAX` 1 500), `sensitive`
  (`SensitiveRule` as data: tool globs, methods, path pattern, argument-value pattern, reason), `docsUrl`, `tokenUrl`
  (template), `handle`.
- **Neutral tools (CX-34)**: `FILES_TOOLS` (`files_list|search|read|write|move|delete`, delete marked sensitive) on
  Dropbox and Nextcloud, `TASKS_TOOLS` (`tasks_list|add|update|complete`, `projects_list`) on Todoist; `REQUEST_TOOL_NAME`
  `request` on every entry with a `request` spec.
- **Helpers**: `catalogEntry`, `catalogSignIn`, `fieldsFor`, `connectionTransport`, `hasRequestTool`, `templateFields`,
  `fillTemplate`, `resolveBaseUrl`, `resolveMcpUrl`, `resolveRequestPrefixes`, `resolveCheckPath`, `resolveTokenUrl`,
  `connectionHost`, `defaultConnectionLabel`, `handleFor(catalogId, taken, label?)` (a Custom entry's handle from its
  label), `fieldProblem`, `fieldsProblems`, `connectionGuide`, `tokenCredential`, `tokenAuthProblem`, `isReadRequest`,
  `requestAllowed`, `callAccess`, `connectionCallKey`, `sensitiveReason`, `isSensitiveCall`, `isSensitiveRequest`,
  `toolAlwaysAsks`, `requestCallTier` (a read through `request` is Allowed unless the tool is Off; the tool's tier covers
  writes), `effectiveTier(keyTier, toolTier, sensitive)`, `toolOffText`, `connectionPromptLine`, `defaultToolTier`.
  Limits `CONNECTIONS_SHARED_MAX` 30, `CONNECTIONS_PERSONAL_MAX` 20, `CONNECTION_TOOLS_MAX` 128, `CONNECTION_SECRET_MAX`
  8 000, `CONNECTION_OUTPUT_MAX` 64 KiB, `CONNECTION_CALL_DEADLINE_MS` 30 s, `NEXTCLOUD_POLL_MS`, `NEXTCLOUD_LOGIN_MAX_MS`.
- Every `DELETE` asks (built into `sensitiveReason`), as does a typed tool marked sensitive and an MCP tool whose server
  marks it destructive (`hints.destructive`). Home Assistant's rules match the domains `lock`, `alarm_control_panel`,
  `cover`, `valve`, `siren`, `garage` (and entity ids in them) anywhere in the arguments, the words lock/unlock/alarm/
  garage/gate in a `Hass*` tool's arguments, and `POST /api/services/<those domains>/…`.

## CT-268 Where providers' docs differ from the spec (2026-10-05)

Checked against each provider's current documentation on 2026-10-05 (CX-50…CX-62 “the build follows the doc”):

- **Notion**: `Notion-Version` is `2026-03-11` (`NOTION_VERSION`), not an older pin; since 2025-09-03 a database holds
  data sources and is queried with `POST /v1/data_sources/{id}/query` (read path, as is the older
  `/v1/databases/{id}/query` and `/v1/search`). The token is a personal access token or an internal connection
  (`tokenUrl` `https://www.notion.so/developers/tokens`). The hosted MCP server is OAuth only.
- **Todoist**: REST v2 is shut down (410); the unified API v1 at `/api/v1/` (lists `{results, next_cursor}`, filters at
  `/api/v1/tasks/filter`). Check `GET /api/v1/user`.
- **Home Assistant**: the MCP Server integration is stateless Streamable HTTP at `/api/mcp` (the old SSE path is gone);
  the REST check is `GET /api/` (the trailing slash matters).
- **Nextcloud**: a Login Flow v2 token lives 20 minutes; Whombat polls at most 10 (`NEXTCLOUD_LOGIN_MAX_MS`, CX-11).
- **Dropbox**: `users/get_current_account` needs the body `null` with a JSON content type (the check sends it); docs at
  docs.dropboxapi.com.
- **Immich**: keys can be scoped, so the check is `GET /api/api-keys/me` (needs no permission), not `/api/users/me`.
- **Mollie**: keys are made under Developers → API access tokens; balances and settlements need an organization token.
- **Moneybird**: the administration is chosen once the token works without a second secret round-trip: the server picks
  the only one or refuses `connections.create` with `field_choice_needed` and the choices (`ConnectionErrorDetails.options`).
- **MCP authorization** (revision 2026-07-28): dynamic client registration is deprecated in favour of Client ID Metadata
  Documents (HA, Notion, Moneybird and Mollie advertise them), and clients check RFC 9207's `iss`. So `mcp_oauth` uses a
  Client ID Metadata Document on this Whombat when the server supports it and registers dynamically otherwise
  (`connection_clients`, CX-19), and `connections.finishOAuth` takes `iss` (`issuer_mismatch`).
- **GitLab** recommends `PRIVATE-TOKEN`; `Authorization: Bearer` works and is what the catalog sends.
- Not in v1: official hosted MCP servers exist for Todoist, Dropbox, Moneybird, Mollie and GitLab (OAuth); entries may
  offer `mcp_oauth` later.

## CT-269 REST endpoints and refusals (2026-10-05)

`contracts/connections.ts`, merged into `api.connections` (`connectionCatalogEndpoints`) and `api.connectors`
(`connectorAppEndpoints`):

- `connections.catalog` `GET /connections/catalog` → `ConnectionsCatalogStatus`.
- `connections.list` `GET /burrows/:burrow/connections` → `ConnectionsListResponse` (shared + the caller's personal ones,
  `canManageShared`, counts).
- `connections.create` `POST /burrows/:burrow/connections` (`CreateConnectionBody`: catalogId, scope, label?, fields,
  signIn `token|none`, method index, own `auth` for Custom entries, secret) → `ConnectionWriteResponse`, 201.
- `connections.update` `PATCH …/:connectionId` (label, fields), `connections.setSecret` `PUT …/:connectionId/secret`,
  `connections.recheck` `POST …/:connectionId/check` → `ConnectionCheckResponse`, `connections.disconnect`
  `DELETE …/:connectionId`, `connections.tools` `GET …/:connectionId/tools` → `ConnectionToolsResponse` (tools, guide,
  truncated), `connections.setTool` `PATCH …/:connectionId/tools/:tool` (`{tier}`).
- `connections.startOAuth` `POST /burrows/:burrow/connections/oauth/start` (catalogId, method `ha_oauth|mcp_oauth|app_oauth`,
  scope, label, fields, connectionId to reconnect, returnTo) → `{authorizeUrl}`; `connections.finishOAuth`
  `POST /connections/oauth/finish` (`{code, state, error, iss}`) → `{returnPath, connectionId}`;
  `ConnectionConnectError` codes for `connect_error=`.
- `connections.startNextcloud` `POST /burrows/:burrow/connections/nextcloud/start` → `{loginUrl, flowId (oas_), pollEveryMs,
  expiresAt}`; `connections.pollNextcloud` `POST /connections/nextcloud/:flowId/poll` → pending | connected | expired |
  failed.
- `connections.probe` `POST /connections/probe` (catalogId, fields; never a secret) → `{needs: open|oauth|token|unreachable,
  issuer, serverName, message}`.
- `connections.allowNetwork` `POST /connections/networks` (`{cidr, port, note?}`) → `VaultNetworksResponse`: “Add this
  network” adds the network or the port to a listed one (the Vault's `vaultNetworks.add` refuses a listed network, so a
  quick add needs its own op; one list for both, VT-12).
- `connectors.setApp` `PUT /connectors/apps/:catalogId` (`SetConnectorAppBody`: clientId?, clientSecret? | null) and
  `connectors.removeApp` `DELETE …` → `ConnectionsCatalogStatus`.
- Refusals `CONNECTION_ERROR_CODES` (`destination_refused` with `{problem, cidr, port, canAdd}`, `limit_reached`,
  `managers_only`, `not_supported`, `app_not_configured`, `check_failed`, `field_choice_needed`, `app_in_config`,
  `admins_only`, `login_expired`, `unknown_tool`), `CONNECTION_ERROR_STATUS`, `CONNECTION_ERROR_MESSAGES`,
  `ConnectionErrorDetails`, `destinationRefusedText(cidr, port, canAdd)` (CX-41's sentence).
- Names: the existing `connections.check` and `connections.remove` (Google, Microsoft at `/me/connections/…`) keep their
  names, so the catalog's are `recheck` and `disconnect`.

## CT-270 Keys: “Connected services” (2026-10-05)

- Group `connections` (“Connected services”), keys `connections.read` (“Read connected services”, agentMaxTier `can`) and
  `connections.write` (“Change things in connected services”, agentMaxTier `can`).
- Team agents: `connections.read` is always on (in `ALWAYS_ON_KEYS` by the existing rule); `connections.write` joins
  `ALWAYS_ON_EXCEPTIONS`, `ROLE_DEFAULT_KEYS` asks, `hireGrants` gives it at ask (`can` when `selected` lists it), and
  Configure's All keys shows it in three states like `packs.tool.write`.
- The Assistant may hold both (`PERSONAL_AGENT_EXTRA_KEYS`); `PERSONAL_DEFAULT_GRANTS` reads at `can`, writes at `ask`;
  `ASSISTANT_ALWAYS_ON_KEYS` leaves `connections.write` out.
- **`ASK_BY_DEFAULT_KEYS`** (`['connections.write']`): `alwaysOnUpgrade` adds them at `ask` for an existing agent that
  holds no grant and that no person switched off, so existing team agents and Assistants get the defaults (CX-20) on the
  server's next upgrade pass. The server needs to queue its agents again (`keys_upgrades`) for that pass to run.

- `MCP_TOOLS.connection_tools` (`{connection}` → ok {connection, guide, tools} | refusal) and `connection_call`
  (`{connection, tool, arguments}` → ok {content, structured?, isError, truncated, httpStatus?} | refusal), both

## CT-272 Session ops, secret ops, safety, feature, API level 32 (2026-10-05)

- Session ops come from the endpoints (`connections.*`, `connectors.setApp|removeApp`). `SECRET_API_OPS` gains
  `connections.create`, `connections.setSecret` (CX-16), `connections.finishOAuth` (a code) and `connectors.setApp` (a
  client secret), following `finishGoogle` and `setGoogleApp`.
- Operation safety: reads `READ`; `update`, `recheck`, `setTool`, `startOAuth`, `probe`, `allowNetwork` `RECEIPT`; the
  secret ops, `startNextcloud` and `pollNextcloud` (a one-time app password) `NEVER`; `disconnect` `DESTRUCTIVE_NEVER`
  (revokes tokens outside its receipt); `connectors.removeApp` `DESTRUCTIVE`.
- Feature `connections.catalog` (`SINCE_0_48`).
- **`SESSION_API_LEVEL` 32** (window 30…33): new session ops and grown unions a session answer carries (`KeyId`,
  `KeyGroup`, `ApprovalAction`), the CT-225 precedent. Go's `SessionAPILevel` follows; `pnpm gen` changes the session
  vectors' secret ops and nothing else.

## CT-273 Contracts 0.48.0: the connections catalog (2026-10-05)

One minor release of CT-266…CT-272. Closed unions grow (`KeyId`, `KeyGroup`, `ApprovalAction`, `EVENT_TYPES`); clients
decode with `decodeTolerant` (CT-136) and show the catalog only where the runtime advertises `connections.catalog`.
Type-level for builders: switches over `ApprovalAction['type']` gain `connection_call`; `Api['connections']` and
`Api['connectors']` are intersections. Behaviour changes: `ALWAYS_ON_KEYS` (+`connections.read`), `ALWAYS_ON_EXCEPTIONS`,
`ROLE_DEFAULT_KEYS`, `hireGrants`, `ALL_KEY_OPTIONS`, `PERSONAL_DEFAULT_GRANTS`, `PERSONAL_KEY_OPTIONS`,

is 0.48.0.

## CT-274 Files: a shared file space per conversation (contracts 0.49.0) (2026-10-05)

John, 2026-10-05, after Pippa couldn't open a 136 MB SketchUp file he had attached in #private: “why not create a shared
Files space where people in the same channel can see the files”, “Files in the sidebar, but only when there are actually
files saved”. Whombat `docs/decisions/files-space.md` (FS-01…FS-13), whombat-app AP-772…, appliance IN-206.

`contracts/files.ts`, `api.files` (`filesEndpoints`):

- **Folders (FS-03)**: `FilesFolder` is `''` (the top) or `A/B`, at most `FILES_FOLDER_DEPTH_MAX` (4) segments of 1…
  `FILES_FOLDER_SEGMENT_MAX` (64) characters, already normalized. `normalizeFilesFolder(raw)` gives the folder a person
  typed or null: blank segments dropped (so `/Drawings/` and `a//b` are fine), each segment by `safeDisplayName`'s rules
  (NFC, whitespace collapsed, control/bidi/zero-width characters dropped — `unsafeNameChar`, now exported — and no
  leading dots or spaces), null for `.`, `..`, a `\`, an empty or too long segment, or more than four. It is idempotent
  and the schema accepts exactly its fixed points, so clients normalize before sending and the runtime can trust the
  value. Case is kept; `filesFolderKey` / `sameFilesFolder` compare case-insensitively. Leading dots and spaces are
  stripped together (`. .x` → `x`), so normalizing twice never changes a folder (`safeDisplayName` keeps its own rule).
- **`FileEntry`** `{attachment: Attachment, conversationId, folder, uploadedById, addedAt, messageId | null,
  threadRootId | null, canRename, canMove, canRemove}`: `messageId` null for a file saved straight into Files; the
  `can*` flags are FS-05 for the viewer. **`FilesSummaryEntry`** `{conversationId, count, bytes, lastAddedAt}`.
- **Endpoints** (session ops too, from `api.files`):
  - `files.summary` `GET /burrows/:burrow/files` → `{conversations: FilesSummaryEntry[]}`, newest activity first.
  - `files.list` `GET /burrows/:burrow/conversations/:conversationId/files?cursor=&limit=` (limit ≤ `FILES_LIST_MAX`
    200, default `FILES_LIST_DEFAULT` 100) → `{files: FileEntry[], nextCursor: Cursor | null}`, newest first, all
    folders.
  - `files.save` `POST /burrows/:burrow/files` `{attachmentId, folder = ''}` → `{file}`.
  - `files.update` `PATCH /burrows/:burrow/files/:attachmentId` `{name?, folder?}` (at least one) → `{file}`.
  - `files.remove` `DELETE /burrows/:burrow/files/:attachmentId` → `{ok: true}`.
  The spec's `{attachmentId, …}` inputs are split the REST way: the id of an existing file is a path parameter (as
  `uploads.discard`); `files.save` carries it in the body because it doesn't address a file in Files yet. Errors are the
  usual codes: another conversation or file is `not_found`, a rename or move FS-05 doesn't allow `forbidden`.

## CT-275 The `files.changed` event, audit types, safety, feature; no API level change (2026-10-05)

- **`files.changed {conversationId}`**, topic `me` only (`REALTIME_EVENT_TOPICS`): sent to each member of the
  conversation now, never on `burrow` (a private channel's or DM's files are its members'). It carries no file data;
  clients refetch `files.summary` and the open `files.list`. Older clients skip the unknown type.
- Audit types `file.saved`, `file.updated` (rename or move), `file.removed` (Messages), ids only — never names or
  folders. Message files come and go with `message.posted` / `message.deleted` as before.
- Operation safety: `files.summary`, `files.list` `READ`; `files.save`, `files.update` `RECEIPT` (saving or moving the
  same file again ends where it is); `files.remove` `DESTRUCTIVE` (as `uploads.discard`). No secret ops.
- Feature **`files.space`** (`SINCE_0_49`): clients show Files only on runtimes that advertise it.
- **No `SESSION_API_LEVEL` change** (stays 32), the CT-216/CT-241/CT-265 precedent: new operations gated by a feature
  name, an event older clients skip, an open audit type string, and no change to an existing operation's output or to a
  union an existing answer carries. A bump would have put level-30 runtimes outside new clients' window for nothing.
  `pnpm gen` is clean.

## CT-276 The runner sees the conversation's Files (2026-10-05)

  Only the dispatch's own conversation, never another, even where the agent is a member (FS-08).

  `FILES_HOME_LINK` `files` (`~/files` on a computer, `files/` in a scratch folder).

- `MCP_TOOLS.list_files` `{folder?: FilesFolder}` (that folder and the ones in it; all when absent) → ok `{files:
  [{attachmentId, name, folder, size, contentType, kind, uploadedBy (a name), addedAt}] (≤ 200), truncated}`; the turn's

## CT-280 Passkeys that open a Whombat: identifiers and challenges (contracts 0.50.0) (2026-10-05)

John, 2026-10-05: signing in on a new device should be one touch (“I want to instantly open my environment”), while
control still can never let a device into a Whombat (MA-03). Whombat `docs/decisions/passkeys.md` (PK-01…PK-11),
control CL-117…, whombat-app AP-785…, appliance IN-208.

`@whombat/protocol/session` (`session/passkeys.ts`), pure (`@noble/hashes` through core's `sha256Bytes`, `@scure/base`):

- **`PasskeyNonce`**: 32 random bytes, lowercase hex (64 characters), for control's sign-in nonce and both registration
  nonces. PK-03 says 32 bytes; the existing `NonceHex` (protocol and control) is 16 bytes, so the passkey nonces get
  their own schema rather than widening one that other signatures use.
- **User handle (PK-01)**: `PASSKEY_USER_HANDLE_PREFIX` `wb1:`; `passkeyUserHandle(appliance)` → UTF-8 of `wb1:` +
  PeerId (56 bytes, throws on a malformed PeerId), `passkeyUserHandleBase64url`, `parsePasskeyUserHandle(base64url |
  bytes)` → the PeerId or null (bad base64url or UTF-8, another prefix, a malformed PeerId — an account-level passkey of
  CL-11 names no Whombat).
- **Challenges (PK-03)**: `passkeyEnrollChallenge({nonce, endpoint})` = `SHA-256(utf8(canonicalJson({purpose:
  'whombat-passkey-enroll/1', nonce, endpoint})))`, `passkeyRegisterChallenge({controlNonce, applianceNonce,
  appliance})` = the same over `{purpose: 'whombat-passkey-register/1', controlNonce, applianceNonce, appliance}`, and
  `…Base64url` variants (the WebAuthn `challenge`). Both parse their input and throw on anything malformed.
  `PASSKEY_ENROLL_PURPOSE`, `PASSKEY_REGISTER_PURPOSE`.
- **`PASSKEY_ANDROID_ORIGINS`** `['android:apk-key-hash:hcREl8X1DtHfXqk1yeVFTAZ7nhsYeSGr8uoly49gZtM']` (PK-02).
- Limits: `PASSKEY_REGISTER_BEGIN_TTL_S` 300, `PASSKEYS_PER_ACCOUNT_MAX` 20, `PASSKEY_ENROLL_FAILURES_PER_HOUR` 10.
- Vectors: `session.json` → `passkeys {userHandles, enroll, register}` (inputs and base64url results); the unit test pins
  the same values computed independently (Python `hashlib` over sorted compact JSON). TypeScript only, as the session.

## CT-281 Passkey session ops (2026-10-05)

- WebAuthn JSON as `@simplewebauthn` (and `PublicKeyCredential.toJSON()`, Android Credential Manager) gives it:
  `WebAuthnAuthenticationResponse` `{id, rawId, type: 'public-key', response {clientDataJSON, authenticatorData,
  signature, userHandle?}, clientExtensionResults, authenticatorAttachment?}` and `WebAuthnRegistrationResponse`
  `{…, response {clientDataJSON, attestationObject, authenticatorData?, transports?, publicKeyAlgorithm?, publicKey?}}`,
  base64url members with size bounds. These objects **strip** unknown members (a newer browser's additions must not
  break a sign-in; the verifier uses only what it knows); the op inputs around them stay strict.
- **`enroll.passkey`** (channel `enroll`, mutating) `{nonce: PasskeyNonce, response: WebAuthnAuthenticationResponse,
  endpoint: NewEndpoint}` → `EnrolledOutput`. The Whombat verifies everything itself (PK-05); a missing `userHandle`
  is `passkey_invalid`, not a schema error, so the schema matches the WebAuthn type.
- **`passkey.register.begin`** (app, ephemeral like `enroll.claim.begin`) `{}` → `{applianceNonce, rpId, user {id,
  name?, displayName?}, excludeCredentialIds}` (PK-06; `user.id` = `passkeyUserHandleBase64url(appliance)`).
- **`passkey.register`** (app, mutating) `{controlNonce, response: WebAuthnRegistrationResponse, name: 1…64}` →
  `PasskeySummary`.
- **`passkeys.list`** (app, query) `{}` → `{passkeys: PasskeySummary[] (≤ 1000), policy: {deviceBoundOnly}}`.
  `PasskeySummary` `{id (credential id, base64url), name, accountId, personName, createdAt, lastUsedAt | null, synced,
  current}`: `personName` always (the client needs no second lookup for an owner's view), `synced` = the BE flag at
  registration (the passkey can sync; what PK-07 refuses), `current` = this session's endpoint was enrolled with it.
- **`passkey.remove`** `{id}` → `{ok}`; **`passkeys.policy`** `{deviceBoundOnly}` → `{ok}` (owners; `not_owner`).
- None is a secret op (an assertion is bound to one endpoint key and one nonce, as `recovery.enroll`'s signature).
- Operation safety: `enroll.passkey` `NEVER` (its receipt moves to the passkey's account, as `recovery.enroll`),
  `passkey.register.begin` `NEVER` (ephemeral), `passkey.register` `NEVER` (consumes the begin's nonce, which a
  dropped session loses anyway), `passkeys.list` `READ`, `passkey.remove` `DESTRUCTIVE`, `passkeys.policy` `RECEIPT`.

## CT-282 Passkey error codes and audit events (2026-10-05)

- `APP_ERROR_CODES`: `passkey_invalid` (`forbidden`; every failed check, PK-05's no-oracle rule, also no live begin),
  `passkey_not_allowed` (`not_allowed`, PK-07), `passkey_limit` (`conflict`, 20 per account; PK-06 sets the limit,
  so it needs a code). Control already had `passkey_invalid` in `CONTROL_REASONS`; it enforces no policy, so nothing new
  there.
- `APPLIANCE_EVENT_TYPES` + `passkey.registered`, `passkey.removed` (`PasskeyAuditPayload {credentialId, accountId,
  byAccountId | null, synced}`), `passkeys.policy_changed` (`PasskeysPolicyAuditPayload`); a device a passkey enrolled
  is `endpoint.enrolled` with `PasskeyEnrolledAuditDetail {via: 'passkey', credentialId, endpointId}`.

## CT-283 Control: Whombat passkeys at sign-in and registration (2026-10-05)

`@whombat/control-contracts` `auth.ts`:

- `auth.passkeyAuthenticateOptions` body `PasskeyAuthenticateOptionsBody` `{endpoint?: PeerIdString}`; response
  `PasskeyAuthenticateOptions` `{challengeId, nonce?: PasskeyNonce, options}`. With `endpoint`, control returns a
  `nonce` and `options.challenge` = `passkeyEnrollChallengeBase64url({nonce, endpoint})`; the client recomputes it.
  Still `auth: 'none'` (as `authenticateVerify`). An empty body works as before.
- `auth.passkeyRegisterOptions` body `PasskeyRegisterOptionsBody` `{appliance?, applianceNonce?}` (both or neither,
  refined); response `PasskeyRegisterOptions` `{controlNonce?, options}`: with a Whombat, `user` per PK-01 and
  `challenge` = `passkeyRegisterChallengeBase64url({controlNonce, applianceNonce, appliance})`. **Breaking for this
  endpoint**: the options used to be the whole response, now they are in `options`. No client calls it yet (CL-11's
  passkeys were never offered in a UI), so control and clients move together in 0.50.
- `Passkey.appliance: PeerIdString | null`: the Whombat a passkey opens, null for an account-level passkey.

## CT-284 Feature `passkeys`, `SESSION_API_LEVEL` 33 (2026-10-05)

- Feature **`passkeys`** (`SINCE_0_50`): clients offer “Add a passkey”, the Passkeys section and `enroll.passkey` only on
  runtimes that advertise it; elsewhere a passkey sign-in stops at the cloud session and goes on to “Set up this
  device”.
- **`SESSION_API_LEVEL` 33** (window 31…34), as the orchestrator's brief for this release asked. By CT-275's precedent
  (new ops behind a feature, an open audit type) it could have stayed 32. The cost: new clients no longer serve level-30
  runtimes (contracts 0.44); 0.45 (31) and later stay inside the window. Go's `SessionAPILevel` follows (`pnpm gen`).

One minor release of CT-280…CT-284. Additive on the session (new ops, codes, audit types, feature); the closed
`APPLIANCE_EVENT_TYPES` enum grows. Breaking for one control endpoint nobody calls yet:

## CT-286 Push previews (2026-10-06)

John, 2026-10-06: “we should embrace privacy, but this is ridiculous if we even encrypt notification messages”. A
managed Whombat's notifications now say who wrote and how the message starts; the content-free rule of MA-03/MA-10 and
CL-14 is narrowed to: a preview of at most two short lines, plain text, passed through control and never stored there.

- `device.PushRequest` (and `local.RuntimePushRequest`, the same schema) gains optional **`preview {title, body}`**
  (`PushPreview`, strict): one line each, any script, no control, format or surrogate code points and no separator but
  U+0020; title 1–80 and body 0–160 code points. The length is in the patterns `PUSH_PREVIEW_TITLE_RE` /
  `PUSH_PREVIEW_BODY_RE` (`u` flag), admitted by name into the cross-language subset like `ConsoleDisplayText`
  (CT-116), with the same general categories. Absent = the phone's generic text for `kind`.
- **`clear`** (optional boolean): remove the notification with this request's `collapseKey` from the phone instead of
  showing one (an approval decided elsewhere). Ignored without a `collapseKey`.
- `collapseKey` also groups on the phone now: notifications with the same key replace each other (one per conversation
  thread or approval). The FCM data control sends is the app's business (control CL-*), not this schema.
- `Preferences.notifications.previews` (boolean, default true): “Show message text in notifications”; off = the generic
  text. Feature **`notifications.previews`** (`SINCE_0_51`); clients show the switch only on runtimes that have it.
  `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 33 (an additive field with a default, CT-275's precedent).
- Go: `device.PushSendRequest.Preview` / `.Clear` (`pnpm gen`); `go/local/push_preview_test.go` checks the manager's
  validation with Unicode, newlines and invisible characters.

## CT-287 Contracts 0.51.0: push previews (2026-10-06)

One minor release of CT-286. Additive everywhere: a manager or control on 0.50 refuses a request that carries
`preview` or `clear` (strict schemas), so a runtime sends them only to a manager on 0.51 (the candidate moves them
together). Every package is 0.51.0.


## CT-288 Feedback from a connected system: The tracker (2026-10-06)

John, 2026-10-06: A customer's tracker keeps its own Feedback button, My reports and email updates; Whombat should
read those reports, let Banjo assess and fix them, and write back (Whombat `docs/decisions/archive/feedback-sources.md`). All
additive, behind feature **`feedback.sources`** (`SINCE_0_52`); `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 33 (new ops behind a
feature, new fields optional or defaulted: CT-275's precedent).

- `FeedbackIntegrationSettings.source` (`FeedbackSource {kind: 'widget' | 'tracker', url: FeedbackOrigin | null}`,
  default `{kind: 'widget', url: null}`): where reports come from. A `tracker` source needs its https address; the
  server sets `allowedOrigins` to exactly it. `FeedbackExternalSystem` = the kinds that aren't the widget.
- `FeedbackReport.external` (`FeedbackExternalReport`, default null): the system's side (id, number, title,
  organization, environment, status and priority in its own words, release, its conversation, diagnostics as text up
  to `FEEDBACK_EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE_MAX`, `syncedAt`) and `writeBack {state: synced | pending | failed, error, at}`.
- `FeedbackIntegrationHealth.source` (`FeedbackSourceHealth`, default null): token set, last check, last success,
  `problem {code: token_missing | unreachable | refused | invalid_answer, message}`, imports of 7 days, write-backs
  pending and failed. Kept out of `warnings` so older clients (a closed enum) never meet a new code.
- `FeedbackDispatchContext.external` / `FeedbackHandoffContext.external` (`FeedbackDispatchExternal`, optional): what
  the assessor and the developer get from the system (number, title, organization, environment, evidence, messages).
- Ops: **`feedback.setSourceToken`** `{token}` (owners; secret: `SECRET_API_OPS`, safety `never`) and
  **`feedback.replyToReporter`** `{message ≤ FEEDBACK_REPLY_MAX}` (destructive: it emails a customer).
  `getReport.can.reply` (optional). Snippets of a connected system's integration are empty strings.

John asked Banjo to merge a pull request in a Morphe patches repository whose releases need the branch's history kept;

## CT-295 Stop an agent's turn: `dispatches.cancel` (contracts 0.55.0) (2026-10-07)

Whombat `docs/implementation/improvement-review/assignment.md` §3 item 1 (John, 2026-10-07: new feature 4). Feature
**`dispatches.cancel`**.

- **`dispatches.cancel`** — `POST /burrows/:burrow/dispatches/:dispatchId/cancel`, no body → `CancelDispatchResponse
  {dispatch: DispatchSummary}` (the turn as it is now: `cancelled`, or how it had already ended — a second press only
  answers). Who: the person the turn is for, people who may wake that agent there (the retry rule), burrow owners;
  never agents. A run's turn answers 409 with `TURN_STOP_RUN_REFUSAL` “Pause the run instead.”. The runner stops at its
  next beat through the existing `ProgressResponse {cancel: true, reason: 'cancelled'}`: no runner-protocol change.
- **`typing.dispatchId`** (`DispatchId.nullable().optional()`): the turn that thinks, what Stop on the thinking line
  cancels. Older clients strip it.
- **`WorkAction` `stop_turn`** on QUEUED and RUNNING turn items; older clients drop the action (CT-136).
- **`canStopTurn(turn, agent, viewer)`** (`domain/work.ts`) and **`isTurnLive(state)`**: live (queued, claimed,
  running), not a run's turn (`runId` null), the viewer a person who may wake the agent (personal agent: its owner, as
  `canRetryTurn`) or a burrow owner (`viewer.role === 'owner'`). Clients don't know whom a turn is for, so they show Stop
  by this rule; the server decides again and also lets that person stop it.
- Copy (`text/turns.ts`): `TURN_STOP_LABEL` “Stop”, `turnStoppedText(name)` “Stopped by Mara” (the `DispatchSummary.reason`
  of a stopped turn), `TURN_STOP_RUN_REFUSAL`.
- Audit type **`dispatch.cancelled`** (`System`, hidden: `text: null`, `{dispatchId, agentId}`).
- Operation safety: **`receipt`, not destructive**. Sending the same stop again can't stop anything else; it only
  answers how the turn ended.

## CT-296 Deployments: the record, the board, `record_deploy` (contracts 0.55.0) (2026-10-07)

§3 item 2 (new feature 5). Feature **`deployments`**.

- **`DeploymentId`** prefix `dpl` (`ID_PREFIXES.deployment`).
- **`Deployment`** (`domain/deployment.ts`) `{id, environment (1–60), service (1–80), status: succeeded | failed, how:
  github_actions | ssh | computer | other, repo, ref, sha, url, summary (≤ 500), byId, runId, conversationId, messageId,
  previousId, createdAt}`. The optional facts are `.nullable().default(null)`: always present in output, absent input
  reads as null. Names refuse control characters, are trimmed (`normalizeDeployName` collapses whitespace) and grouped
  case-insensitively (`deployGroupKey`); the newest record's spelling is shown. `sha` is 7–64 hex (agents often know
  the short one), `url` http(s) only, `ref` ≤ 255. Never edited: a redeploy is a new record; `previousId` is the
  deploy of the same service and environment that **succeeded** before it (what a rollback goes back to).
- **`deployments.list`** — `GET /burrows/:burrow/deployments` `?environment&service&before&limit` (default 50, ≤ 200)
  → `DeploymentsPage {deployments (newest first), before: Cursor | null}` (the approvals list's cursor style).
- **`deployments.environments`** — `GET /burrows/:burrow/deployments/environments` → `DeployEnvironmentsResponse
  {environments: [{environment, lastAt, services: [{service, current, failed, previous}]}]}`: `current` the newest
  succeeded deploy, `failed` the newest attempt when it failed (so newer than `current`), `previous` the succeeded one
  before `current`. Environments most recently deployed first (≤ 50), services by name (≤ 200).
  **`deployEnvironmentsFrom(deployments)`** is the pure reference (fixtures use it; the runtime may build the board
  with it from each service's last rows).
- Visibility: every member reads deployments and summaries (the board is burrow-wide; the tool's description says
  so); `conversationId` and `messageId` only for members of that conversation, null for everyone else.
- Realtime **`deployment.recorded {deployment}`** on `burrow`, personalized per viewer for those two ids.
- MCP **`record_deploy`** (`contracts/mcp-deploy.ts`): input `{environment, service, status, how, summary, sha?, ref?,
  url?, repo?, runId?}` (`runId` absent: the run the turn works on, if any); output `commitOutcome({deploymentId,
  previousId, messageId})`. No key (recording isn't deploying), not read-only, in `WHOMBAT_TOOL_NAMES`, **not** in
  `MCP_POSTING_TOOLS` (like `schedule`: the agent still reports in its own words, and the thinking line stays).
  Description: “Call it after every deploy you do, whether it succeeded or failed: it records the deploy on the burrow’s
  Deploys board and posts a deploy card here. The summary is visible to everyone in the burrow, so keep secrets out of
  it.” Activity verbs “Recording a deploy” / “Recorded a deploy”.
- Audit type **`deploy.recorded`** (`Code`): payload ids, names, status, how and sha; never the summary or the URL.
- `WorkLink {type: 'work', section: 'deploys'}` (`DEPLOYS_SECTION`) paths to `/:burrow/work/deploys` (WE-17); other
  sections keep `?section=`.
- Fixtures: five deploys (`DEPLOYMENTS`: production api ×3 with the newest failed, staging api, production web over SSH)
  served by `createFixtureFetch()`.

## CT-297 The `deploy` card (contracts 0.55.0) (2026-10-07)

`DeployCard {kind: 'deploy', deploymentId, environment, service, status, sha: | null (default null), url: | null
(default null), runId?: RunId | null}` in `MessageCard`, `StoredCard` (same shape) and `CARD_KINDS`; never
`PostableCard` (server-made by `record_deploy` and the deploy executor, so it can't be forged). `runId` as CT-261's
`skill`/`schedule` cards: a chat shows it inside that run's line. It is a settled, one-line card: `deployLine(card)` →
“Deployed api to production · 3f9c2a” / “Deploy of api to production failed · 3f9c2a” (the existing 6-character
`shortSha`), `deployCardText(card)` → `[deploy: api to production, succeeded]` for inboxes, search and agents' windows;
`DEPLOYMENT_STATUS_PILLS` `DEPLOYED`/`FAILED`, `DEPLOYMENT_HOW_LABELS`. Clients in the field get the card nulled by
tolerant decoding and show their “This needs a newer version of the app.” pill (AP-255), as with `turn_failed`,
`schedule` and `assessment`.

## CT-298 Thumbnails (contracts 0.55.0) (2026-10-07)

§3 item 4. Feature **`attachments.thumbnails`**. `Attachment.thumbnailUrl` (`string | null`, optional),
`thumbnailWidth`/`thumbnailHeight` (optional, nullable). `THUMBNAIL_MAX_EDGE` 720 (a 360-point tile at 2×). The route
is a raw byte transfer like the download: `ATTACHMENT_TRANSFER.thumbnail` `GET /api/v1/burrows/:burrow/attachments/:attachmentId/thumbnail`
(`attachmentThumbnailUrl(burrow, id)`), authorized exactly like the file, 404 without one, immutable caching. Over a
session no change: the thumbnail is the attachment download's existing `variant: 'preview'`
(`variant_unavailable` without one). Clients fall back to `url`.

## CT-299 Thread paging (contracts 0.55.0) (2026-10-07)

§3 item 3. Feature **`messages.thread_paging`**. `messages.thread` gains `query: ThreadQuery {before?: MessageId,
limit?: 1…THREAD_PAGE_MAX (200)}` and `ThreadView.more: {before: MessageId} | null` (optional: older servers omit it and
send every reply). No `limit`: every reply (older clients, unchanged). With `limit`: the newest `limit` replies before
`before` (a reply id; an unknown one pages from the newest), oldest first, `more.before` = that page's oldest reply while
earlier ones exist. `pageThreadReplies(replies, query)` is the pure reference; the fixtures page with it.

## CT-300 Read state across devices: `notification.read` (contracts 0.55.0) (2026-10-07)

§3 item 5. Feature **`notifications.read_events`**. Realtime `notification.read {ids: NotificationId[] (≤
NOTIFICATION_READ_IDS_MAX 200) | null, before?: Timestamp, unread?: Count}` on `me`. `ids` null: every notification up
to `before` (`markRead {all: true}`); more than 200 ids go in several events. `unread` (added): the viewer's unread count
after it, so badges update without a refetch. Every mark-read path publishes it. Older clients skip the event type
(counted, no false gap, AP-255).

## CT-301 Names and details that differ from the assignment (2026-10-07)

- Feature names are lowercase (`FeatureName` is `^[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]*$`, and the conformance test checks every name):
  `messages.thread_paging` (assignment `messages.threadPaging`), `notifications.read_events` (`readEvents`),
  `work.needs_you_count` (`needsYouCount`).
- `canvases.content` answers `canvas` too (`{canvas, markdown, updatedAt}`): the phone's screen needs the title and
  the link carries only the slug, so one request is enough.
- `notification.read` carries `unread`.
- A follow-up handed to the running turn is `TurnInjection {dispatchId, messageId, message: Message, attachments}`
  rather than loose text fields: the runner renders it with the window's message renderer (author, mentions, files).
- `ProgressBody.forked` (added): the runtime records whether a `forkFrom` took (TE-03's measurement).
- `COMPUTER_WAIT_TOOL` `whombat.computer_wait` (added): the runner's “Waiting for the computer” activity row (TE-04),
  like CT-264's setup row.
- `record_deploy` answers `messageId` (the card) and `previousId`; the `deploy` card has `runId` (CT-261's rule).
- The deployment's optional facts are nullable with a null default rather than optional (one shape for every reader).

## CT-302 The needs-you count: `work.needsYou` (contracts 0.55.0) (2026-10-07)

§3 item 6. Feature **`work.needs_you_count`**. `GET /burrows/:burrow/needs-you` → `NeedsYouResponse {count}`: the number
`conversations.bootstrap` carries in `sidebar.counts.needsYou`, without the rest of bootstrap (WE-07: decisions and
needs-you changes refetch this, not bootstrap). Read; a session op too.

## CT-303 A canvas as Markdown: `canvases.content` (contracts 0.55.0) (2026-10-07)

§3 item 7. Feature **`canvases.content`**. `GET /burrows/:burrow/canvases/:slug/content` → `CanvasContentResponse
{canvas, markdown, updatedAt}`: the same text `canvas_read` gives agents, for the phone's read-only canvas screen
(MQ-05). Read; a session op too. Fixtures serve `CANVAS_MARKDOWN`.

## CT-304 Runner protocol: the computer, a warm fork, the known head (contracts 0.55.0) (2026-10-07)

§3 item 8 (TE-03, TE-04, TE-10). Runner and server of one runtime ship together; every field is optional all the same.

- `ProgressBody.computerBegun?: boolean`: the turn has started using the agent's computer (sent once, with the beat after
  its first command there); AC-20's claim exclusion counts only such turns. `COMPUTER_WAIT_TOOL` is the row of a turn
  whose first command waits for the computer (“Waiting for the computer”, “Got the computer”, “Couldn’t get the
  computer”).
- `DispatchContext.forkFrom?: ForkFromSession {providerSessionId, promptHash} | null`: without
  `dispatch.providerSessionId`, a warm session of the same agent to fork; the runner forks (Claude `--resume <id>
  --fork-session`; Codex if its app-server forks) only when its stable prompt hashes to `promptHash`, else starts fresh.
  `ProgressBody.forked?: boolean` says it took.
- `DispatchContext.workspace.headSha?: GitSha | null`: the branch head the server knows; a clone that has it skips
  `git fetch`. `GitSha` (full 40/64 hex) moved above `DispatchContext` in `runner.ts`.

## CT-305 Steering follow-ups into a running turn (contracts 0.55.0) (2026-10-07)

§3 item 8 (Whombat SX). `ProgressResponse.inject?: TurnInjection[]` (≤ `TURN_INJECT_MAX` 8, oldest first, repeated on
every beat until delivered or the turn ends) with `TurnInjection {dispatchId, messageId, message: Message, attachments:
AttachmentRef[] (default [])}`; `ProgressBody.injected?: DispatchId[]` (≤ 8) the ones the runner delivered to the
provider. The server merges a delivered one: the queued dispatch becomes `cancelled` with `TURN_MERGED_REASON`
“Answered in the running turn” and a server-only link to the turn that took it. One the runner never confirms runs as
its own turn. A runner that can't steer its provider ignores `inject`.

## CT-306 Skills hash-first (contracts 0.55.0) (2026-10-07)

§3 item 8 (TE-09). `runner.packSkills`'s body gains `knownHashes?: Sha256Hex[]` (≤ `PACK_SKILL_KNOWN_HASHES_MAX` 200);
each `PackSkillFiles` gains `hash?` (`packSkillHash(files)`: sha-256 hex over the files sorted by path, each `path` NUL
`data` NUL) and `cached?: boolean` (`files` empty: use the copy kept under `hash`). Older runners send no hashes and get
every file; older servers send no hash.

## CT-307 Session API level 34, features, operation safety (contracts 0.55.0) (2026-10-07)

`SESSION_API_LEVEL` **34** (Go `protocol.SessionAPILevel`): new session ops (`dispatches.cancel`, `deployments.list`,
`deployments.environments`, `work.needsYou`, `canvases.content`), an op's new input and output (`messages.thread`), and
grown unions a session answer carries (card `deploy`, `WorkAction` `stop_turn`, two event types). The window: a level-34
client serves runtimes 32…35, so boxes at 33 (0.50…0.54) keep working with the new apps, and the apps in the field (33)
serve a level-34 runtime. Whombat's skew pin (`vendor/whombat-contracts/previous`, MD-16) doesn't move: no release moved
it since 0.20.3, and every 0.55 change is additive to what a field client decodes.

`SINCE_0_55`: `dispatches.cancel`, `deployments`, `messages.thread_paging`, `attachments.thumbnails`,
`notifications.read_events`, `work.needs_you_count`, `canvases.content` (no runtime feature for the runner-only items).
`RUNTIME_FEATURES` stays under the welcome's 128. Operation safety: the four reads `safe`, `dispatches.cancel`
`receipt` (CT-295).

## CT-308 Contracts 0.55.0: the improvement review (2026-10-07)

One minor release of CT-295…CT-307. Every package is 0.55.0.

## CT-309 The local network open by default (contracts 0.56.0) (2026-10-08)

destination rules take `lan?: boolean`: `vaultDestinationProblem`, `browserDestinationProblem` and
`vaultSshDestinationProblem` let every `private` address through on any port when it is true (after the `never` and

burrow has `agentsReachLan` on). `agentsReachLan`'s meaning grows from the appliance's own networks to every private
address, for the computers and for Whombat's own calls; `AGENTS_REACH_LAN_COPY` says “Agents may reach your local
network”; `VAULT_COPY.homeNetworkIntro`/`noNetworks` say the list matters when that is off. No wire change. Every
package is 0.56.0.
