## CT-311 Ask only for what is risky: deleting, locks, alarms, gates and doors (contracts 0.58.0) (2026-10-08)

John, with Home Assistant's 127 tools on his box, 102 marked “Always asks”: “I want the default to be Allowed as much
as possible (not only for Home Assistant, for all connections), unless they pose a security issue (locks, deletion,
etc)”. An MCP server's `destructiveHint` no longer makes a call ask (`sensitiveReason`'s `hints.destructive` is
ignored, deprecated): Home Assistant sets it on nearly every action. Instead, for every connection, a tool named for
deleting asks (`deletesByName`: delete, remove, destroy, erase, purge, wipe, trash as a word, camel case split). A call
the caller knows only reads (`hints.access: 'read'`) skips the rules on arguments. `SensitiveRule` gains `name` (a
regular expression over the tool's name). Home Assistant: an action naming a lock, alarm, gate or door (English and
Dutch words, `HA_SENSITIVE_WORDS`) or a domain of `lock`, `alarm_control_panel`, `valve`, `siren` asks for any tool
(prefixed names like `assist__intent__HassTurnOff` included); `cover` left the domain list (blinds; a garage door or
gate says so in its name); scripts named that way and raw KNX bus writes (`group_value_write`) always ask. Its
`mcpReadyNote` is gone: the guide tells agents what Assist exposes. Every package is 0.58.0.

## CT-312 Save to Files: an agent's file reaches Files only when a person saves it (contracts 0.59.0) (2026-10-08)

John, 2026-10-08: “When an agent creates an images or any other file, it shouldn't automatically store this in /files
unless we click on "Save to Files" and we should also create a "Download" button.” On his box agents had posted 16
files and put 11 into Files themselves (`upload_file` with `saveToFiles`, 8 of them on no message at all), and every
file on a message counted as in Files (FS-01). Whombat files-space.md FS-14…FS-19 has the rules.

`Attachment.inFiles` (optional boolean): whether a message's file is in its conversation's Files now — a file a person
sent is, an agent's only once someone saved it, neither once removed from Files. Set by the runtime on messages' files
only; absent from older runtimes, and clients then show no Save to Files. `files.save` also takes a file on a live
message of a conversation the caller is in (people only, “Save to Files”): an agent's file comes into Files, a file
removed from Files comes back, one already there is answered as it is. Saving or removing a message's file also sends
that message's `message.updated`. `upload_file` loses `saveToFiles` and `folder` (a caller that still sends them has
them dropped by the schema) and its description says to attach the file and that people save it; `list_files` says it
lists what was shared, posted or saved. Feature `files.save_from_messages`. `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 34: the field is
optional, `files.save`'s body and answer keep their shape, and clients gate on the feature (as 0.49's Files did); a bump
would only narrow the client window. Every package is 0.59.0.

## CT-313 Nine more connections for the homelab and infrastructure (contracts 0.60.0) (2026-10-08)

John, 2026-10-08, asked for more connections (Proxmox, UniFi Network, UniFi Protect, Cloudflare, Tailscale) and said
yes to the first group of the list he was given: services that sign in with a pasted token, so each is a catalog entry
with a guide and its “always asks” rules, and no new code (Whombat connections-catalog.md CX-D33). New entries, each
checked against the vendor's current docs on 2026-10-08: **Proxmox Backup Server** (`proxmox_backup`, handle `pbs`),
**UniFi Network** (`unifi_network`, `unifi`; the console's Integration API, `X-API-KEY`), **UniFi Protect**
(`unifi_protect`, `protect`, category Home), **OPNsense** (`opnsense`; basic auth with the API key as a field and the
secret as the token), **Tailscale** (`tailscale`; `Accept: application/json` always sent so the policy file comes back
as JSON), **Cloudflare** (`cloudflare`; checked with `GET /client/v4/accounts`, the one read both user and account
tokens pass), **Portainer** (`portainer`), **Unraid** (`unraid`; GraphQL, every call a write so mutations are never
skipped as reads) and **Grafana** (`grafana`; `POST /api/ds/query` reads). Following CT-311 they ask only for deleting,
doors and keys (firewall, NAT, VPN, policy files, Zero Trust Access, tunnels, API keys and tokens, users and roles),
alarms, and powering off or restarting what everything else runs on; everyday changes (DNS records, guest access,
dashboards, containers) are Allowed. The overview groups them under Infrastructure, Protect under Home.

A shared `certificateField(where)` builds the certificate fingerprint field (Proxmox VE's now too): its help says that
left empty, Whombat shows the fingerprint it finds. `ConnectionErrorDetails.certificateSha256` (optional, `AB:CD:…`)
carries it on `check_failed`: a home-network server whose certificate couldn't be verified, or wasn't the pinned one,
for an entry with that field. A request check gains `okJsonPath` (with `jsonPathValue`): the answer must also hold a
value there, or the token was refused, because Unraid's GraphQL answers a wrong key 200 with `errors`; Unraid checks
`data.me.name`. `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays: the detail is optional and older clients ignore it, and
`CatalogIdText` already lets older clients skip ids they don't know. Every package is 0.60.0.

## CT-314 Setting up connections: sign in once, Look only, found on your network (contracts 0.61.0) (2026-10-08)

John, 2026-10-08, on the Proxmox connect form: “instead of guiding the user to "Documentation" and "figure it out
yourself", I'd rather guide the user more”; then: one-time password is okay, a network scan is okay, no assistant for
now, and “if we can do this for the other services also, that would be huge … Otherwise, find solutions per connection
to simplify the configuration.” Whombat `docs/decisions/connections-setup.md` (CS-*) has the rules and the per-service
sequences.

- **Sign in once** is a sign-in kind, `password`: the account field (`account`: label, placeholder, help, `fixed` for
  Unraid's `root`), when a second factor comes in (`secondFactor`: `asked` — the server answers `second_factor_needed`
  and the form sends the same again with `login.code`; `optional` — the code field is offered from the start because
  the service can't tell a missing code from a wrong password; `never`), what Whombat makes (`creates`), which token
  sign-in the made key is stored as (`tokenMethod`) and whether the service itself limits the key to the level
  (`serviceLimits`). `connections.create` takes `signIn: 'password'` with `login {account, password, code?}` (still a
  secret op: the password travels as a token does and is never stored). Fields only the key fills (Proxmox's token ID,
  OPNsense's API key) carry `methods: ['token']`. Thirteen entries offer it first: Home Assistant, Nextcloud,
  Paperless-ngx, Immich, Proxmox VE, Proxmox Backup Server, UniFi Network, UniFi Protect, OPNsense, Portainer, Unraid,
  Grafana, Forgejo / Gitea.
- **Look only / Manage** (`ConnectionAccessLevel`, `access` on create and update, `ConnectionView.access`,
  `DispatchConnection.access`): sign in once asks the service for a key at that level where it can; Whombat itself
  refuses every write on a connection that looks only (`accessTier`, `lookOnlyText`), so the level holds also where the
  service can't limit a key (UniFi, Portainer, Home Assistant). Each entry says what the levels mean (`access`,
  `accessText`); the prompt line says “look only”.
- **`client_credentials`** (Tailscale's OAuth client): the secret is exchanged at `tokenUrl` for an hour's bearer token,
  with `scopes` per level (`all:read` / `all`); it never expires, unlike an API access token (≤ 90 days).
- **Making a token by hand, guided**: a `token` (and `client_credentials`) sign-in has `steps` (numbered, with values to
  copy), `paste` (patterns that read a pasted dialog or a dropped file into the fields: Proxmox's Token ID and Secret,
  OPNsense's `key=`/`secret=` file; `pasteValues`), and `links` per level where the service fills its form from the
  link (Cloudflare's permission groups, GitLab's scopes, Unraid's key authorization, Grafana's new service account).
- **Found on your network**: `CatalogEntry.discovery` (ports with their scheme, one or two unauthenticated probes that
  must match: status, a header, the body; where the version is; `probeMatches`, `probeVersion`, `jsonPathValues` with
  `*`, `discoveredUrl`). `connections.identify` says what is at an address before anything else is sent (the address
  to use, the entry and version, the certificate); `connections.discover` scans (managers; the box's own networks,
  its connections' networks, the home network list and the networks given) and answers its progress and what it found.
- Errors: `second_factor_needed`, `sign_in_refused` (`details.reason`: `password`, `code`, `rights`, `locked`,
  `single_sign_on`, `unsupported`, `second_factor` with `details.method`, Nextcloud's login flow).
- `SESSION_API_LEVEL` **35** (new session ops `connections.identify`, `connections.discover`; `connections.create`'s new
  input): the window moves to 33…36; features `connections.sign_in_once`, `connections.discover`; both new ops
  `receipt`. Every package is 0.61.0.

## CT-315 Every agent has its own area: pass it on, and connections looked after (contracts 0.62.0) (2026-10-08)

John, 2026-10-08, after Pippa (Associate) answered “What is currently running on PVE-01?” herself while Dusty (Operator)
looks after the homelab: “I'd like each agent to have their own responsibilities just like in real life. So the agents
should delegate the work to each other when it's not in their domain. I think for quick questions also.” Whombat
`docs/decisions/agent-responsibilities.md` (OW-01…OW-12) has the rules.

- **`pass_on`** (MCP tool, key `tasks.create`, a posting tool): `PassOnBody {to, about?, note?}` hands the person's
  message that woke the turn to the teammate whose area it is; answers `{status: 'ok', messageId, dispatchId, where,
  conversationId}` or `{status: 'refused', code, reason}` (`PassRefusalCode`: `not_from_person`, `passed_already`,
  `self`, `not_team_agent`, `not_ready`, `capped`, `licence`; `passRefusalText`). `PassWhere`: `here` (the message's
  thread, the teammate is in that conversation) or `dm` (the person's DM with the teammate). Activity label “Passing it
  on” / “Passed it on”.
- **Trigger `passed`** and `DispatchContext.passed` (`PassedContext`: who passed whose message, `about`, `note`, `where`,
  `fromConversation`, `messageId`).
- **Words**: `passLineText` (“@Dusty looks after PVE-01, so I’ve passed this on.”, “… Dusty will answer you in your DM
  with Dusty.”), `passForwardText` (“John asked me in our DM:” + the quote, `passQuote`, cut at `PASS_QUOTE_MAX` 1 500),
  `passPlace`.
- **Connections looked after**: `ConnectionView.lookedAfterBy {id, name} | null` (`ConnectionCaretaker`, default null
  for older runtimes), `UpdateConnectionBody.lookedAfterById` (nullable), `DispatchConnection.lookedAfterById` /
  `lookedAfterName`, `CATALOG_CATEGORY_CARETAKER_ROLE` + `caretakerRoleFor` (home and infrastructure → operator,
  developer → developer, business, productivity and files → associate, accounts and custom → nobody).
- **`ROLE_GUIDANCE`** (OW-03): the Associate's “a small fix or a script you do yourself” becomes “Code is a Software
  Developer’s and servers are an Operator’s: pass them on when there is one.”; the Lead's second line “Pass questions on
  with pass_on and hand out work with delegate, so you can track it; you plan, follow up and report, and build nothing
  yourself.”
- `SESSION_API_LEVEL` **36** (`ConnectionView`'s new field, `connections.update`'s input, the trigger union): the window
  moves to 34…37; features `agents.pass_on`, `connections.looked_after`. Every package is 0.62.0.

## CT-316 Found on your network: connected ones left out, hide a found service (contracts 0.63.0) (2026-10-08)

John, 2026-10-08, on his box's Found on your network (four connected services listed again among the new ones):
“Devices that are already connected shouldn't be discovered again, furthermore I would like to have the ability to hide
a discovered device.” Whombat `docs/decisions/connections-setup.md` CS-52 and CS-53 have the rules.

- **`DiscoveredService.hidden`** (default false, so an older runtime's answer reads as nothing hidden): a manager of the
  burrow hid it. `connectionIds` now names the caller's connections of the same entry on that host (any port), or a
  Custom API on that host and port, so a UniFi console's Protect isn't “connected” through its Network connection.
  The app leaves connected services out of the list (CS-52); the answer still carries them, for the counts.
- **`connections.hideFound`** (`POST /burrows/:burrow/connections/discover/hidden`, `HideFoundServiceBody {catalogId,
  url, hidden = true}`): hides the entry at the url's host and port, or shows it again, for the whole burrow, kept
  across scans and restarts; answers `ConnectionDiscovery` without starting a scan. Managers (`managers_only`); session
  op `receipt` (the same state each time).
- `SESSION_API_LEVEL` **37** (a new session op and `DiscoveredService`'s new field): the window moves to 35…38; feature
  `connections.hide_found`. Every package is 0.63.0.

## CT-317 A site that turns the browser away: `blocked` (contracts 0.64.0) (2026-10-08)

John, 2026-10-08, on his box's Bol.com login (Test sign-in: “It didn’t answer within 30 seconds.”): the sign-in page
sends the browser on to a page that answers 403 (“IP address is blocked … possible abuse”) and, to a headless browser,
holds that page back for minutes. Nothing was wrong with the login; the words blamed the wrong thing. Whombat
`docs/decisions/browser.md` BT-53…BT-57 have the runtime's rules.

- **`VAULT_SIGN_IN_OUTCOMES` and `VAULT_CHECK_OUTCOMES` gain `blocked`**: the site's page answered 403 or 429 and still
  did a few seconds later (a bot check), before a sign-in form showed or after submitting. `vaultSignInCheck('blocked')`
  records `{outcome: 'blocked', status: 'failing'}`; `vaultSignInSummary('blocked', {httpStatus?})` and
  `vaultCheckSummary('blocked', {kind, httpStatus?})` say “The site blocked the Whombat’s browser (403).” (no status:
  without the brackets). `vaultSignInSummary` takes an optional `httpStatus`; a `login` check passes its
  `httpStatus` on.
- **`BROWSER_REFUSAL_CODES` gains `blocked`** (`failed`: it tried, the site refused), with `browserBlockedText(status?)`:
  “The site blocked the Whombat’s browser (it answered 403): it turns automated browsers away. Trying again won’t help;
  ask the person to do this step themselves.” — so an agent stops instead of retrying, which a bot check punishes.
- `SESSION_API_LEVEL` **38** (a union a session answer carries grew): the window moves to 36…39. No feature name: an
  older runtime never answers `blocked`, and an older client decodes a `blocked` check outcome to null and still shows
  the stored summary (CT-136). Every package is 0.64.0.
