## CT-319 Contracts 0.64.2: a server's name may hold capitals (2026-10-09)

John, 2026-10-09: “Add server” refused `PVE-01` — “it's a name, not a hostname or username”. A patch over 0.64.1, as
CT-318: a rule loosened, no schema shape, field, feature name or `SESSION_API_LEVEL` change. An older server refuses a
name with capitals with the field's words, as before.

- **`VAULT_SSH_SERVER_NAME_PATTERN`** is `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$` (was lowercase only, VT-S04); still 1–40, no
  spaces: agents type the name in tool calls and as an `ssh` alias on their computers (`ssh PVE-01`).
- **`VAULT_SSH_FIELD_TEXT.name`**: “Use 1–40 letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, starting with a letter or
  digit.”
- Names stay unique per entry **ignoring case** (the server's rule, Whombat `docs/decisions/vault.md` VT-D61): the
  tools find a server by its name in any case, and on agents' computers `PVE-01` also answers to `ssh pve-01`.

Every package is 0.64.2.

## CT-320 Contracts 0.65.0: Ask an agent, and suggestions from an agent's area (2026-10-09)

John, 2026-10-09: in #general he always has to name the agent a question is for. After comparing local word rules,
hosted decision models (TypeSafe's Jev, OpenAI's Decisions API), a mini-turn on the existing sign-ins and a receptionist
agent, he chose the local option: data stays on the Whombat. Plus a way to send a message to an agent afterwards, from
the message's toolbar with a wombat icon. Whombat `docs/decisions/ask-agent.md` (SA-01…), whombat-app
`docs/decisions/ask-agent.md`.

- **`suggestAgent(input)`** (`@whombat/core/text`, `suggest.ts`): the agent a person's request is for by its words,
  or null. The words are each agent's area: the shared connections it looks after (label, the service's name and
  `CATALOG_ROUTING_WORDS`), its role's `ROLE_ROUTING_WORDS` and its own name. Strong word 3, a looked-after service's
  everyday word 2, a role word 1, each distinct word once; the best needs `SUGGEST_MIN_SCORE` (2) and `SUGGEST_MARGIN`
  (2) over the next. Only for a request (**`looksLikeRequest`**: a question, an imperative or question word first, or an
  ask such as “can you”, “please”, “kun je”, “graag”; English and Dutch), never when the text names someone or
  broadcasts. Clients ask it only when `replyAddressee` finds nobody; the composer's chip shows it.
- **`SendMessageBody.suggested`** (optional, nullable `PrincipalId`): the agent the chip offered before the person
  changed anything (reply rule or area); `to` says what was sent. The runtime keeps the pair for a review of the
  suggestions and tells the agent why it was woken.
- **`messages.ask`** `POST /burrows/:burrow/messages/:messageId/ask` `AskAgentBody {agentId, suggested?}` →
  `{message}`: “Ask” on a person's message in a channel or branch room (**`canAskAboutMessage`**). The asker's own
  message wakes the agent on it; someone else's gets the asker's line in its thread (**`askLineText`**: “This one is
  for @Dusty.”, with a quote of the message when it isn't the thread's root), and the agent answers its author. The
  same agent again changes nothing. Retry safety `RECEIPT`.
- **`Message.asks`** (optional `MessageAsk[]`, `{agentId, byId, at}`, at most `MESSAGE_ASKS_MAX`): who was asked.
- **`DispatchContext.addressed`** (optional **`AddressedContext`**): how a `mention` turn's message reached an agent
  it doesn't name: `reply` (RT-01…RT-05), `suggested` (`about`), or `ask` (`message`, `byId`, `byName`).
- **Feature `messages.ask_agent`** (0.65): clients show Ask and area suggestions only on runtimes that have it. An
  older runtime strips `suggested` and has no `messages.ask`.
- **No `SESSION_API_LEVEL` change** (as CT-263, CT-265): an optional input field, an additive output field and a new
  operation, all behind the feature name.

Every package is 0.65.0.

## CT-321 Contracts 0.65.1: a channel's only person doesn't carry the last-named agent over (2026-10-09)

John, 2026-10-09, on his box: “I am considering adding a 3rd Proxmox server” in #general woke Dusty. He is the only
person in that #general (with three agents), so RT-01's only-person rule made every top-level message that names nobody
the agent he last named there — Dusty, hours earlier, since agents answer a channel's top-level messages in threads
(Whombat channel-threads.md CH-01) and the top level holds only his own messages. The suggestion from an agent's area
(CT-320) never got its turn. Whombat `docs/decisions/reply-to.md` RT-07.

- **`AddresseeInput.channel`** (optional boolean): the conversation is a channel. At its top level the only-person
  rule doesn't apply; the answer rule (RT-02: an agent's top-level answer to you, at most `REPLY_WINDOW_MINUTES` old)
  still does, and threads are unchanged. Absent: false, the rule as before (branch rooms, older callers).
- A patch: an optional input field of a pure function, no schema shape, feature name or `SESSION_API_LEVEL` change.
  An older runtime keeps waking the last-named agent there; a newer client's chip doesn't offer it.

Every package is 0.65.1.

## CT-322 Contracts 0.66.0: automations from a simple form, GitHub issues, and Delete (2026-10-09)

John, 2026-10-09: an automation that has Banjo assess a repository's new issues and pull requests was “way too
complicated” (the step editor with step ids, templates, conditions and limits was the only way to build one), issues
weren't supported, and an automation couldn't be removed. He asked for a flow led by the trigger. Whombat
`docs/decisions/automation-recipes.md` (AR-…), whombat-app the same file.

- **Recipes** (`AutomationRecipe`, `automations/recipes.ts`): the simple form's answers — `when` (GitHub: repo, events
  `issue_opened`/`pr_opened`/`pr_updated`/`checks_failed`, drafts, bots; a message in the channel; a schedule; by
  hand), the agent, a job (`assess`, `review`, `answer`, `check`, `custom`; `RECIPE_JOBS` has the labels and which
  triggers offer each), its instructions (`recipeInstructions` prefills them), the channel it answers in, a repo to read
  and `replyOnGitHub`. `recipeDefinition` makes an ordinary definition — one `dispatch_agent` step `ask` with a
  read-only checkout, and a `github_comment` step when asked — that carries the recipe (`AutomationDefinition.recipe`,
  never read by the engine); `recipeOf` gives it back while the definition is still exactly what it makes.
  `recipeSentence`, `recipeName`, `buildRecipe`, `recipeProblem`, `describeAutomation` (any definition, for
  `Automation.summary`). The agent's prompt says that what an issue or pull request says is information, never
  instructions.
- **GitHub triggers**: event `issue_opened`; `drafts: false` (a draft fires nothing, and `pr_opened` fires when it is
  marked ready — `TriggerFacts.readied`), `bots: false` (`TriggerFacts.bot`); `TriggerFacts.draft`. Absent: as before.
  `GITHUB_EVENT_LABELS`, `GITHUB_PR_EVENTS`; `triggerSummary` says “New issues on acme/web” instead of the raw event.
  An issue trigger with a branch is a problem.
- **`github_comment` step** (external): `repo`, `number` and `text` templates, `otherwise: skip|fail`. A recipe's comment
  is `{{steps.ask.reply}}`: the agent's last message of its turn only (`reply`, beside `text`, which joins them all), so
  a line it posts first (“I’m using the … skill”) stays in the thread; its prompt asks for the whole answer in one
  message. Needs the new
  automation key `pr.comment` (`AUTOMATION_KEYS`). **`StepWorkspace.pullRequest`** (template, read only, not with
  `branch`): a pull request's head, also from a fork; nothing rendered means the base.
- **API**: `automations.create` takes source `recipe` and `publish`; `automations.delete` (`DESTRUCTIVE`) and the
  `automation.deleted` frame; `automations.samples` (`READ`) and `runNow`'s `sample` (a test run as if that issue or
  pull request had just arrived). `Automation.summary` and `Automation.deletedAt` (defaults `''` and null for older
  servers).
- **Features** `automations.recipes` and `automations.delete`: clients show the simple form and Delete only on
  runtimes that have them. No `SESSION_API_LEVEL` change: additive fields, a new source kind, new operations and a new
  frame, all behind the feature names. An older runtime refuses a definition with `recipe`, a `github_comment` step or
  the new trigger fields, which only a newer client sends.

Every package is 0.66.0.

## CT-323 Contracts 0.67.0: automations that fix the bugs they find (2026-10-09)

John, 2026-10-09, on the recipes of CT-322: when Banjo's assessment finds a bug that needs fixing, Banjo should fix it
— but only with some certainty that it is a bug and that it matters, and with fixing on its own an explicit opt-in,
never on by itself. Whombat `docs/decisions/automation-recipes.md` (AR-24…), whombat-app the same file.

- **Assessments**: `AutomationAssessment` (`kind` bug/feature/question/not_a_bug/duplicate/unclear, `importance`
  critical…low, `confidence` low/medium/high, `size` small/large, `summary`, `fixPlan`, `duplicateOf`), reported with
  the agents' tool `report_assessment` in the turn of a `dispatch_agent` step with `assessment: true` (not together with
  `verdict`); conditions read `steps.<id>.assessment.*` and its `line` (`assessmentLine`: “Bug · high importance · sure
  · small fix”). A turn that reports none gives `unassessed()`: `unclear`, so nothing follows from a missing answer.
- **`AutomationRecipe.fix`** (`RecipeFix`: `mode` ask/auto, `minImportance` default high, `developerId`, `reviewerId`,
  `maxPerDay` default 5), GitHub recipes with new issues only; absent = only assess (`RECIPE_FIX_MODES`' `off`, the
  form's default). `recipeDefinition` adds `worth_fixing` (an issue, a bug, important enough), with `auto` a
  `needs_yes` condition that skips to the fix only when the agent is sure (high confidence), the fix is small,
  `trigger.trusted` (the author is the repo's owner, a member or a collaborator), nobody is `trigger.assigned`, no
  `trigger.linkedPr`, not `run.test` and `run.today.fix` is under `maxPerDay` — else `approve` (a person's yes) — then
  `fix` (the developer on `feat/issue-<n>`, a failing test first; no commits fails the step), `review` (another agent's
  verdict), `pr` (“Fixes #n”) and, when it answers on GitHub, `linked` (the issue hears about the pull request).
  Merging stays with a person. The assessment's line heads the GitHub comment.
- **Conditions read `run.*`** (`run.number`, `run.test`, `run.today.<step>`: runs of the automation in the 24 hours
  before that started the step), beside `trigger.*` and `steps.*`.
- **Feature `automations.fixes`**; no `SESSION_API_LEVEL` change (additive fields, a new tool, behind the feature).
  An older runtime refuses a definition with `assessment` or a recipe with `fix`, which only a newer client sends.

Every package is 0.67.0.

## CT-324 Contracts 0.68.0: an assessment in plain words (2026-10-09)

John, 2026-10-09, on a real run of 0.67.0 (Banjo assessing a Fusebox issue: “not a bug”, correct): the output was too
technical — file paths with line ranges, `cargo test --locked`, “provisionally small scope”, the labels repeated in
words, and the run page showing the conditions' expressions. Whombat `docs/decisions/automation-recipes.md` (AR-37…),
whombat-app the same file.

- **`AutomationAssessment.details`** (Markdown, at most 4000): the technical part — files and lines, what was checked,
  how to test it. `summary` is one plain sentence without file names, code or commands. `report_assessment`'s
  description says so.
- **A recipe that assesses** (GitHub, job `assess`, or with `fix`) has `assessment: true` (0.67: only with `fix`). Its
  prompt asks for the assessment with summary and details first, then an answer for someone who doesn't read code: two
  to four short sentences, no file names, line numbers, code or commands, no repeated labels. The default Assess words
  no longer ask for “(files and lines)”.
- **`assessmentMarkdown`**: a comment's `heading` (“**Bug · high importance · sure · small fix**”, empty when not
  assessed) and `detailsBlock` (the details folded in `<details><summary>Technical details</summary>`, empty without
  any); the server adds both to the step's `assessment` output. A recipe's comment is
  `{{steps.ask.assessment.heading}}{{steps.ask.reply}}{{steps.ask.assessment.detailsBlock}}`.
- **`recipeConditionStory`**: what a recipe's check decided in plain words (“No: Banjo says it’s not a bug.”, “Yes, a
  person decides: Banjo isn’t sure enough and someone is assigned to it.”); the server keeps it in the condition step's
  output (`story`).
- **`recipeOf` compares the shape** (triggers, steps, agents, rooms, checkouts, limits), not the words a version writes
  (prompts, messages, conditions, step names, `assessment`), so an automation made with older words keeps its simple
  form; **`recipeIsCurrent`** tells whether it has this version's words, and **`refreshRecipe`** swaps an older
  version's unchanged default instructions for today's (“Update its wording”).
- A patch-sized minor: no feature name and no `SESSION_API_LEVEL` change. An older runtime ignores `details` it doesn't
  know only if it strips unknown fields — it doesn't (strict), so a 0.68 agent's report fails there; runtimes and their
  prompts ship together.

Every package is 0.68.0.

## CT-325 Contracts 0.69.0: The tracker reports through automations (2026-10-10)

John, 2026-10-10: “We have support for the ticket system of the tracker … I think we should use automations instead. I think
this would be a better fit.” The feedback module kept a second copy of every tracker report and synced it both ways
(CT-288, CT-292); automations leave an item where it lives and make the run's thread the conversation about it. The tracker
becomes a connection, a new report an automation trigger, and the assessment is written back by a step. Whombat
`docs/decisions/report-trackers.md` (TA-01…TA-21), whombat-app the same file.

- **The connection** (TA-01…TA-03): `CatalogEntry.use` (`CATALOG_USES`: `agents`, `automations`; absent: agents) and the
  entry `tracker` — shared only, an address (`url`) and a BEARER API token whose steps name `reports:read`,
  `reports:write`, `reports:assess` and `reports:platform`, checked with `GET /v1/integrations/reports`, transport `rest`
  without tools, `request` or discovery, handle `tracker`, `use: 'automations'`. **`isAgentConnection(entry | id)`** is
  false for it: never listed or callable through `connection_tools`/`connection_call`, never in
  `DispatchContext.connections`; an id the catalog doesn't know counts as an agents' entry. `caretakerRoleFor` gives
  nobody for it (no agent could use it). **`ConnectionView.poller`** (`checkedAt`, `succeededAt`, `problem`; default
  null): the poller's state, set only for an automations entry while an automation listens to it.
- **The trigger** (TA-04): `TrackerTrigger` `{kind: 'tracker', connectionId, event: 'report_opened'
  (`TrackerTriggerEvent`), reportKinds?}` (`TrackerItemKind` bug/feature; absent: both; each kind once); `TriggerFacts`
  `{kind: 'tracker', event, connectionId, reportKind}`. `triggerSummary` takes a third resolver, `connectionLabel`: “New
  reports in Acme dev”, “New bug reports in …”, “New feature requests in …”, “… in a tracker connection” when the
  viewer can't see it. `AutomationTriggerInfo.kind` and `TRIGGER_KIND_LABELS` (“A report arrives in the tracker”).
- **The step** (TA-11, TA-13): `TrackerUpdateStep` `{kind: 'tracker_update', connectionId, report (template), from,
  otherwise: skip|fail}`; `from` must name an earlier `dispatch_agent` step with `assessment: true`. It is in
  `EXTERNAL_STEP_KINDS` (the engine's external pass) and in the new **`REPEATABLE_EXTERNAL_STEP_KINDS`**: after a crash
  it is sent again with the request id kept on the attempt instead of becoming `uncertain`. `trackerWriteOf` (bug →
  `likely_bug`, feature → `feature_request`, question/unclear → `needs_information`, duplicate → `duplicate`, not a bug
  or not assessed → skip; priority for bugs and features, critical → urgent … low → low), `trackerWriteLine` (“Acme dev
  #15: Likely bug · high priority”), `trackerNothingToWriteText`. `AutomationRunStep.kind`, `STEP_KIND_LABELS` (“Write
  back to the tracker”).
- **The key** (TA-12): `report.update` (“Update the tracker reports”, group support) in `KEY_IDS` and `AUTOMATION_KEYS`.
  `KeyDef.automationsOnly` (`AUTOMATION_ONLY_KEYS`): no agent tool needs it, so it is never an always-on key, a
  switch or a row; its `agentMaxTier` is `can` because an automation's principal decides as an agent does.
  **`AutomationGrant.connections`** maps to the new `KeyScope.connections` and `RequestScope.connection`, a dimension
  `scopeMatches` checks like repos (fail closed).
- **The organization** (TA-10): `DispatchAgentStep.trackerAccess` (only when every trigger is `tracker`, else a
  problem). **`DispatchContext.tracker`** (`TrackerDispatchContext`: the connection's label, the report's number and
  the step's `FeedbackSourceAccess`, null when it didn't ask): set for every agent turn of a tracker run.
- **Tools** (TA-09, TA-10; `mcp-tracker.ts`): `tracker_item {diagnostics?}` → `{status: 'ok', text, cut}` (16 000
  characters, a package 64 KB) and `tracker_read {path}` → `{status: 'ok', httpStatus, body, cut}` (a `/v1/…` path, 256
  KB, 120 reads); read only, no key. **`TRACKER_RUN_TOOL_NAMES`**: listed only in a tracker run's turns (`tracker_read`
  only when granted), like `report_assessment` only in an assessing turn. `report_assessment` says “an issue, a pull
  request or a report”.
- **Operations**: `tracker.item` (`GET /burrows/:burrow/trackers/runs/:runId/report`, `READ`) → `{report:
  TrackerItemView, can: {update}}` (TA-14: the reporter's name and email for people, the screenshot as a data URL up to
  2 MB, the conversation as `reporter`/`team`, the release); `tracker.update` (`POST` the same path, `TrackerUpdateBody`
  `{requestId (UUID), message?, status?}` with `TrackerUpdateStatus` — investigating, needs_information, planned,
  in_progress, awaiting_release, closed, not_planned; a reply or a status, Not planned only with a reply) → `{report,
  messageId}`, **destructive** with a receipt (it emails the reporter before its commit, as `feedback.replyToReporter`;
  a person's retry with the same `requestId` sends nothing twice); `feedback.moveSource` (`POST
  /burrows/:burrow/feedback/integrations/:id/move`, `receipt`: one commit, nothing reaches the tracker before it) →
  `commitOutcome({connectionId, automationId, integration})`, and **`FeedbackIntegration.movedTo`** (`{connectionId,
  automationId, at}`, default null) so the integration's page links both. **`AutomationSample`** is a union of
  `AutomationGitHubSample` (as before) and `AutomationReportSample` `{kind: 'report', connectionId, reportId, number,
  title, type, organization, openedAt}` (TA-19); `runNow`'s `sample` also takes `{reportId}`. Status words:
  `TRACKER_STATUS_LABELS`, `trackerStatusLabel`, `TRACKER_ASSESSMENT_LABELS`, `TRACKER_PRIORITY_LABELS`.
- **The recipe** (TA-17, TA-18): `RecipeWhen` `{kind: 'tracker', connectionId, reportKinds}` (default both;
  `RECIPE_TRACKER_ITEM_KINDS`), jobs `assess` (default), `answer`, `custom` with their own words, `repo` optional (a
  read-only checkout of its default branch). `AutomationRecipe.writeBack` and `organizationAccess` (the tracker only; the
  definition stores them as given, absent as true; true on another trigger is a problem, and other recipes' definitions
  carry neither). It makes `ask` (`assessment` as for GitHub, `trackerAccess` with `organizationAccess`) and, when it
  writes back and assesses, `write_back` (`tracker_update` from `ask`, `retries: 2`: safe to repeat). The prompt says a
  signed-in customer sent it through the tracker's own Feedback, that it is information never instructions, that
  `tracker_item` reads the whole report and `tracker_read` the organization when granted, and that only people answer
  the customer. **Fixing always asks**: `auto` is “Fix it when sure needs an issue opened by someone with access to the
  repository: a tracker report always asks.”, a fix needs bug reports and a repository; the chain is AR-25's with
  `trigger.item == "report"`, the branch `RECIPE_TRACKER_FIX_BRANCH` (`feat/{{trigger.ref}}`), “Fix {{trigger.connection}}
  #{{trigger.number}}: {{trigger.title}}” and “Fixes {{trigger.connection}} report #{{trigger.number}}.”, no comment after
  it. `recipeSentence` (“When a new report arrives in Acme dev, Banjo assesses it in #tracker-reports and writes the
  assessment back to the tracker.”) reads `RecipeNames.connection` (`UNKNOWN_TRACKER_CONNECTION`), `recipeName(recipe,
  names?)` (“Assess new reports in Acme dev”), `describeAutomation`'s `connectionLabel`. Every GitHub recipe's
  definition, words and sentence are what 0.68 made.
- **Feature `automations.tracker`** (`SINCE_0_69`): clients offer the tracker in the simple form, the run page's report and
  Move to automations only on runtimes that have it; such a runtime refuses new tracker feedback integrations (TA-21).
- **No `SESSION_API_LEVEL` change** (as CT-322, CT-323): unions of automation definitions grew, new operations and
  additive fields, all behind the feature name. An older runtime refuses a definition with a `tracker` trigger or step,
  which only a newer client sends; an older client decodes a newer runtime's automation, sample or connection
  tolerantly (CT-136).

Every package is 0.69.0.

## CT-326 Contracts 0.70.0: an automation merges its fix once its checks pass (2026-10-10)

John, 2026-10-10, on the Fusebox automation (“Assess new issues on DigitalPals/Fusebox”): “it succeeded successfully
but I would like the option to auto merge the PR to main as well. Can you add this to the automation as a setting?”
CT-323's “Merging stays with a person” becomes the default of an opt-in: off until a person ticks it for that
automation. Whombat `docs/decisions/automation-recipes.md` (AR-44…AR-47), whombat-app the same file.

- **`RecipeFix.merge`** (`z.enum(['checks']).optional()`): `checks` merges the fix's pull request into the default
  branch once its checks pass, after the review approved it. Absent (no default): the pull request is left for a person,
  so every recipe made before 0.70 parses to the same JSON and `recipeIsCurrent` stays true for it. The form's words are
  **`RECIPE_FIX_MERGE`** `{label: 'Merge the fix into main once its checks pass', hint: 'After the review approves it.
  If checks fail or someone changes the pull request, it waits for you.'}`, shown under “When it’s a bug” once fixing
  is on.
- **`MergePullRequestStep`** `{kind: 'merge_pull_request', repo, number (template), method (MergeMethod, default
  squash), waitMinutes (5…10080, default 1440: how long it waits for checks), otherwise: skip|fail (default fail)}`,
  strict, in the `AutomationStep` union, `AutomationRunStep.kind` and `STEP_KIND_LABELS` (“Merge a pull request”, the
  agents' tool's title). `number` is a template of up to **64** characters, not 20 as `github_comment`'s: the recipe's
  `{{steps.pr.prNumber}}` is 21, and any step id (32) fits. It is in `EXTERNAL_STEP_KINDS` and not in
  `REPEATABLE_EXTERNAL_STEP_KINDS` (a merge with no answer is `uncertain`, AR-47). It acts in the run's room
  (`stepActsIn`: its approval card when the key asks and its “Merged PR #10 into main.” line), reads what its template
  reads (`stepReads`), and validation checks its template like any other. The waiting for checks, the key
  decision and the merge itself are the server's (AR-45…AR-47).
- **Keys**: `AUTOMATION_KEYS` gains `merge` and `merge.main` (appended; labels from `KEY_CATALOG`: “Merge”, “Merge
  into main”), so `AutomationGrant` and `automations.setKeys` take them, limited to repos as `pr.open` is.
- **The recipe**: `recipeDefinition` appends `{id: 'merge', name: 'Merge the fix', kind: 'merge_pull_request', repo,
  number: '{{steps.pr.prNumber}}', method: 'squash', otherwise: 'fail', retries: 0}` last — after `pr`, and after
  `pr_open`/`linked` when the recipe answers on GitHub; without them a pull request that wasn't opened renders nothing
  and the step is skipped. The approval card's details end “… a pull request is opened that closes the issue, and it is
  merged into main once its checks pass.” instead of “Nothing is merged: that stays with a person.”, and
  `recipeSentence` adds “, and merges the fix once its checks pass”. The issue's “A fix is ready for review” comment
  keeps its words.
- **GitHub issues only**: a tracker recipe with `merge` is refused (“Merging on its own is only for GitHub issues: a fix
  for a customer’s report waits for a person.”), and should one get past `recipeProblem` its definition has no merge
  step and its sentence and card say nothing of merging (`recipeDefinition` keeps the field as given; the form shows the
  checkbox only for GitHub recipes). A GitHub recipe without new issues is already refused fixing (“Fixing bugs needs
  new issues: tick New issues.”), merging with it.
- **Feature `automations.merge`** (`SINCE_0_70`): a client offers the checkbox only on runtimes that have it. **No
  `SESSION_API_LEVEL` change** (as CT-322, CT-323, CT-325): a union of automation definitions grew and a recipe field
  was added, behind the feature name. An older runtime refuses a recipe with `merge` or a `merge_pull_request` step,
  which only a newer client sends; an older client decodes a newer runtime's run step tolerantly (CT-136).

Every package is 0.70.0.

## CT-327 Contracts 0.71.0: the agent's suggestions get a card, and the tracker access follows the token (2026-10-10)

John, 2026-10-10, after a real tracker run (report #16: Banjo rated it a usability bug of medium importance and
recommended a compact, recent-first Diagnostics view; the automation fixes bugs of high importance or more, so the run
stopped with one line on the run page): “If this happens, I would like it to show me a card where I can go ahead and
implement the fix.” And on the same run, where Banjo couldn't look inside the reporting organization (the moved
automation had organization access off, and its token was one organization's): “We should not create API tokens per
organization / environment, I need Banjo to be able to assess every environment for bug assessments.” Whombat
`docs/decisions/automation-recipes.md` (AR-51…AR-54) and `report-trackers.md` (TA-22, TA-23), whombat-app the same
files.

- **`AutomationAssessment.recommends`** (`AssessmentRecommends`: `change` | `nothing`), optional on the stored shape:
  absent (a report before 0.71) is `nothing`, so older rows parse to the same JSON; `unassessed()` says `nothing`.
  **`ReportAssessmentInput`** is `report_assessment`'s input: the same, strict, with `recommends` required and
  described in plain words (`change` when the agent recommends changing the code — a fix, an improvement or a feature —
  with the fix plan saying what; `nothing` for a question, a duplicate, something unclear or a report that needs no
  change). Every recipe that assesses asks for it, and one that fixes tells its agent that a change it recommends may
  be worked on next.
- **The card's words**: `assessmentQuestion` (“Fix this bug?” for a bug, “Make this change?” otherwise) and
  `assessmentOffer` (“Fix”, “Suggested change for”); the server adds both to a step's `assessment` output (`question`,
  `offer`, beside `line`, `heading` and `detailsBlock`; documented on `DispatchAgentStep.assessment`). The approval
  card's title is `{{steps.ask.assessment.offer}} #{{trigger.number}}: {{trigger.title}}` (the tracker: with
  `{{trigger.connection}}` before the number); the pull request's title stays “Fix …”. Its details are three short
  paragraphs, each well under the 280 characters the server shows as one item (AR-34), also with a 40-character
  repository: `{{steps.ask.assessment.question}} {{steps.ask.assessment.summary}}`; “If you say yes, the agent works on
  feat/issue-12 in acme/web: for a bug, a failing test first; for another change, tests that cover it.”; and the review
  and pull request, with CT-326's merge sentence or, for the tracker, “nothing is sent to the customer”.
- **The fix chain** (AR-52, AR-53): `worth_fixing` is `trigger.item == "issue" && ((kind == "bug" && importance ≥
  minImportance) || recommends == "change")` (`report` for the tracker); with `auto`, `needs_yes` puts the bug-and-importance
  part in front of the gates, so only a bug important enough is fixed without asking and everything else asks. Step
  names: “A bug worth fixing or a suggested change?”, “Approve it”, “Fix it or make the change”, “Review the work”. The
  developer's prompt covers both (a bug: a failing test first; another change: the change with tests that cover it;
  neither done safely: no commits and why), and it and the reviewer's read the assessment's line, summary and fix plan.
  `recipeConditionStory` says “Yes: Banjo suggests a change.”, “Yes: Banjo suggests fixing this bug of medium
  importance.”, “No: Banjo says it’s a question and recommends no change.”, “No: it’s a bug of medium importance and
  Banjo recommends no change.” and, for `needs_yes`, “Yes, a person decides: Banjo suggests a change, and only bugs of
  high importance or more are fixed without asking.” A change recommended but not taken up happens only on a chain made
  before 0.71, so there it keeps 0.70's words. The recipe's sentence and the form's fix modes keep theirs.
- **Older automations** (AR-54): conditions, step names, titles and prompts are wording `recipeOf` ignores, so a
  recipe made before 0.71 is still its recipe; `recipeIsCurrent` is false for every recipe that assesses (its prompt
  doesn't ask for `recommends`, and one that fixes has the older chain), and rebuilding it (`refreshRecipe`,
  `recipeDefinition`) gives today's chain. A test keeps four definitions 0.70.0 made as a fixture.
- **The organization follows the token** (TA-23): `recipeDefinition` no longer writes `DispatchAgentStep.trackerAccess`
  nor reads `AutomationRecipe.organizationAccess` (left out of the recipe it stores, and `refreshRecipe` drops it); both
  stay in the schemas for older clients, documented as ignored from 0.71. `recipeOf` leaves both out of the shape, so a
  the tracker automation of 0.69–0.70 is still a recipe. Every the tracker recipe's prompt says Whombat asks for the
  organization. Validation no longer refuses `trackerAccess` on any trigger, and `recipeProblem` refuses only
  `writeBack` outside the tracker (“Only a tracker trigger writes back to the tracker.”). **`trackerAccessAsked(step)`**
  (`automations/tracker.ts`): true for a `dispatch_agent` step without a `write` checkout and without `verdict` — the
  steps of a run started from a report that the server asks the tracker's grant for.
- **The tracker connection** (TA-22): its sign-in help and steps say first that one token per tracker installation, made
  by a platform admin in Admin Settings → Automation with `reports:read`, `reports:write`, `reports:platform` and
  `reports:assess`, reads every organization's reports, and that an organization's own token works for that
  organization only.
- **Feature `automations.suggestions`** (`SINCE_0_71`): a client hides the organization checkbox and offers “Update”
  for an older recipe only on runtimes that have it (an older runtime would rebuild it with its own chain). **No
  `SESSION_API_LEVEL` change** (as CT-322, CT-323, CT-325, CT-326): an additive field and new helpers, behind the
  feature name. An older runtime's `report_assessment` doesn't list `recommends`, so its agents don't send it; an older
  client reads a run step's output as JSON (`output: JsonObject`), so `recommends`, `question` and `offer` reach it
  unparsed.

- **The recipe's sentence** says what the card offers: *Ask me before fixing* “…, and fixes bugs or makes the changes Banjo suggests once a person says yes”; *Fix it when sure* “…, and fixes bugs of high importance or more on its own when it’s sure; anything else Banjo suggests waits for a person’s yes”.

Every package is 0.71.0.

## CT-328 Contracts 0.72.0: the Automations list at a glance (2026-10-10)

John, 2026-10-10, on the Automations page: “I would like to improve the Automations page visually … perhaps we can add
the logo of the GitHub repo for example?” He approved a mockup — a tile per source with the GitHub owner's picture,
what starts it → the agent → the room, tags for what it may do, the run history, a line when a run waits on someone,
an On/Off switch — and said “implement this fully”. Whombat and whombat-app `docs/decisions/automation-list.md`.

- **`Automation.glance`** (`AutomationGlance`): `source` (the first trigger's kind: `github`, `tracker`, `schedule`,
  `message`, `reaction`, `webhook`, `manual`), `repo` (a GitHub automation's `owner/name`, for the owner picture),
  `trigger` (a few words: “New issue · Fusebox”, “Weekdays at 09:00”, “Message with “bug”…”), `agentId`, `room` and
  `does`, tags for what it may do (`AutomationGlanceTag`: id, label, `tone` `plain` | `changes` | `merges`), mildest
  first. `automationGlance(definition, names)` makes it, from the recipe while the definition still is one (the job;
  comments on GitHub; writes back to the tracker; fixes after a yes or when sure; merges when checks pass), else from the
  triggers and steps (a tag per kind of step that does something). The runtime names rooms and the tracker connections as it
  does for `summary`; the room is named once (a trigger “in #bugs” that answers in #bugs is “Message”, the next chip
  says where). The words live in core (`AUTOMATION_DOES_LABELS`) so web, Android and the server say the same. Null
  (default) from older runtimes and for a draft that doesn't validate.
- **`Automation.recentRuns`**: the latest `AUTOMATION_RECENT_RUNS` (10) runs, newest first, default empty;
  **`AutomationRunSummary.waitingOn`** (`approval` — a step waits for a person's yes, a `request_approval` step or any
  step whose key asks; `review` — the run needs review; null otherwise, also while it waits for an agent, checks or
  time), default null.
- **`automations.list` → `canManage`** (default false): whether the viewer may switch them on and off from the list.
- **`github.avatar`** (`GET /burrows/:burrow/github/owners/:owner/avatar`, READ, members): a GitHub owner's picture
  as a `data:` URL (`GitHubAvatar`; PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, never SVG; at most `GITHUB_AVATAR_MAX_BYTES`, fetched at
  `GITHUB_AVATAR_SIZE` 88), null when the Whombat couldn't fetch it. Only for owners of repos the burrow has or an
  automation watches (404 otherwise), so the Whombat is no open image proxy. A `data:` URL in JSON rather than a byte
  stream: it works the same over the appliance session and same-origin, needs no new resource kind, and the CSP
  already allows `img-src data:`.
- **Feature `automations.glance`.** `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 38, as for 0.69–0.71: a bump would put level-21 runtimes
  outside the client's window (the conformance suite's legacy check), and every field here has a default an older
  client ignores and a newer client reads as “not there”.

## CT-329 Contracts 0.73.0: Fix it when sure may trust the repo's GitHub Actions (2026-10-10)

John, 2026-10-10, on two approval cards in Needs you (Fusebox #12 and #13, “Claude Code 2.1.296 is out”, “Codex CLI
0.162.1 is out”): “Can you explain why these were not automatically approved?” Banjo rated both a bug of high
importance, sure, small fix; the only gate that failed was “someone with access to the repo opened the issue”, because
the repo's own version-check workflow opens them as `github-actions[bot]`, whose `author_association` is `NONE`
(AR-27). A third run (#14) sat queued because the two waiting for a yes filled both places. He said yes to both
changes proposed. Whombat `docs/decisions/automation-recipes.md` AR-55, AR-56.

- **`RecipeFix.trustActions`** (optional boolean, “Also fix issues opened by this repo’s GitHub Actions”,
  `RECIPE_FIX_ACTIONS` has the form's words): `needs_yes` reads `(trigger.trusted == true || trigger.author ==
  "github-actions[bot]")` instead of `trigger.trusted == true`. `GITHUB_ACTIONS_LOGIN` names the login: only GitHub
  Apps have a `[bot]` login and the `github-actions` app is GitHub's, so no person can open an issue as it, and a
  `GITHUB_TOKEN` only writes to its own repo. The trigger already carries `author`, so the gate needs no new fact and
  the runtime nothing new to read. Opt-in and narrow: `recipeProblem` refuses it without `auto` (“Fixing issues GitHub
  Actions opened on its own needs Fix it when sure.”), on anything but GitHub, and while bots are skipped (“Issues
  GitHub Actions opens start nothing while bots are skipped: untick Bots.”); `recipeDefinition` keeps it only when
  true, so off makes exactly what 0.72 made (`recipeOf` and `recipeIsCurrent` unchanged for every existing recipe).
  The hint says the one risk: a workflow that copies what other people write into an issue.
- **The check says it by name**: `recipeConditionStory`'s `needs_yes` says “GitHub Actions opened the issue, and fixing
  those on its own is off” instead of “someone without access to the repo opened the issue” when the author is GitHub
  Actions, so the person knows what to turn on. The sentence adds “(also in issues GitHub Actions opens)”.
- **`AutomationLimits.maxConcurrentRuns`, documented**: a run waiting for a person's yes on its approval card doesn't
  count, and a run that gets its yes while the others fill every place waits its turn (`queued`) again (runtime only,
  AR-56).
- **Feature `automations.trust_actions`.** `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 38 (as CT-326…CT-328): an older client never sends
  the field, and a newer client offers the checkbox only where the runtime advertises it (an older runtime's strict
  `RecipeFix` refuses it).

## CT-330 Contracts 0.74.0: link previews on or off per channel (2026-10-10)

John, 2026-10-10, on #fusebox-style automation posts whose GitHub preview card repeats the line above it: “I would like
the option to switch off the previews of the URLs in a message … So turn off the preview cards”, then “Make it
configurable per channel”. Whombat `docs/decisions/essentials-conversations.md` EC-23.

- **`Conversation.linkPreviews`** (optional boolean): absent or true = on, as the burrow says (`Burrow.linkPreviews`,
  CT-174, still the owners' switch for the whole burrow); false = the server fetches none for the conversation's
  messages and clients don't show those already there (turning it back on shows them again, and new messages get
  theirs). `conversationLinkPreviewsOn(conversation, burrow?)` is the one rule clients use.
- **`conversations.update` takes `linkPreviews`**: people who are members of the conversation change it (an agent is
  refused, like any setting that changes what everyone sees); a signed `conversation.updated` “Turned link previews
  off in #name”. Allowed for every kind of conversation; the apps offer it on channels.
- **`CHANNEL_LINK_PREVIEWS_COPY`**: the row's words for web and Android (“Link previews”, the hint, the toasts).
- **Feature `conversations.link_previews`.** `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 38 (as CT-326…CT-329): the field is optional both
  ways; a client offers the switch only where the runtime advertises it (an older runtime would ignore the field).

## CT-331 Contracts 0.75.0: replying to a tracker report's customer (2026-10-10)

John, 2026-10-10: “Is it possible to make Banjo reply with it's assesment … in a way that makes sense for the customer
that reported it? I would also like it to tell when the bugfix or feature request was implemented”, and for production
reports “the customer should be notified that the bug has been fixed, but it's not on production yet”. Then: replies go
out on their own from day one, signed “Banjo - AI Developer”, and a merged report fix deploys development on its own.
This reverses Whombat report-trackers.md TA-15's “never an agent”, TA-18's “no comment follows” and RN-03 (John's
call); Whombat report-trackers.md TA-25…TA-35.

- **The reply is part of the assessment**: `AutomationAssessment.reply` (≤ `TRACKER_CUSTOMER_REPLY_MAX`, 1 500
  characters, default empty), `replyAsks` (it asks the customer something) and `language` (ISO 639-1, default empty).
  Older stored assessments parse unchanged; `report_assessment` describes the fields and says they are only for turns
  whose instructions say the customer is answered.
- **Step `tracker_reply`** `{connectionId, report, from, otherwise}`: sends step `from`'s reply, signed
  (`customerSignature(name, role)` → “Banjo - AI Developer”, the role's short word; `signedReply`), with
  `trackerReplyStatus`'s status (“Needs information” when it asks, else “Investigating” for a new report or one that waited
  for the customer). External and safe to repeat, as `tracker_update`.
- **Key `report.reply`** (“Reply to customers”), automations only, scoped to connections like `report.update`.
- **`customerReplyProblem`**: what a customer mustn't read — too long, a link off the tracker origin, code, a commit hash,
  a file of the code, a pull request, an @mention, another organization's name. The runtime sends a reply only when it
  finds nothing; otherwise the step asks a person whatever the key says.
- **Trigger event `reporter_replied`** on the `tracker` trigger: the reporter wrote back or reopened a report an automation
  already ran for. `triggerSummary` says “Customer replies in Acme dev”.
- **The recipe's `replyToCustomer`** (the tracker only, needs an assessing job; `recipeProblem` says so otherwise): adds the
  `reply` step after `write_back` and the `reporter_replied` trigger, tells the agent what the customer reads, and the
  fix card says the customer hears once the fix is live. Absent means off, so every existing definition is still its
  recipe; `refreshRecipe` turns it on for a tracker recipe that assesses, so “Update” offers it (`recipeIsCurrent` is
  false until then). `recipeReplyCopy` has the form's words. The tracker fix's pull request gains the line
  `Tracker report: {{trigger.host}} #{{trigger.number}}`, which the tracker's automatic development deploy looks for.
- **Fix notices**: `trackerFixNotice` — a development report hears “fixed, live now” once the fix is live on development
  (`available`, with the release record's evidence “Live on dev.tracker.example since 12 October 2026.”), a production report
  “fixed, it comes with the next update” then (`awaiting_release`) and “live now” once production runs it (`available`).
  English and Dutch (`TRACKER_NOTICE_LANGUAGES`, `noticeLanguage`, `guessLanguage` when the agent didn't say).
  `TrackerFixState`/`TrackerFixView` and `TrackerItemView.fix` (default null) show it on the run page.
- **Which installation**: `TrackerEnvironment` and `trackerEnvironmentOf(health.environment, address)` (the address's first
  label when the tracker doesn't say); `ConnectionView.poller.environment` and `version` (default null).
- **List tag `reply`** (“Replies to customers”, tone `changes`) and `STEP_KIND_LABELS.tracker_reply`.
- **Feature `automations.tracker_replies`.** `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 38: every new field is optional or defaulted;
  a client offers the checkbox only where the runtime advertises it.
- **0.75.1 (same day)**: `AutomationRunStep.kind` lists `tracker_reply` too. 0.75.0 added the step kind to the
  definition but not to the run view, so a client's tolerant decoder dropped the step from a run (found while building
  the app). A test now checks that the run view knows every step kind.

## CT-332 Contracts 0.76.0: Claude Code and Codex through an AI gateway (2026-10-10)

John, 2026-10-10: “add a new connection: Fusebox … we should be able to route all our traffic from Codex and Claude …
through Fusebox. We should be able to turn this on / off. I also would like to see the remaining usage of the
subscriptions.” Whombat `docs/decisions/ai-gateway.md` AIG-01…AIG-21 (the contract list is AIG-20).

- **Catalog use `gateway`** and two entries, `fusebox` (“Fusebox”: address and management key, check `GET /api/accounts`
  200, found on 8317 https and http by `<title>Fusebox</title>`, handle `fusebox`) and `ai_gateway` (“AI gateway”: address
  and a key, check `GET /v1/models` 200, handle `gateway`). Shared, developer, `rest`, no tools, no `request`. Both also
  take the certificate fingerprint field, as the other home-network entries do: the relay pins it (AIG-09).
  `isAgentConnection` is false for them (never an agent's tool or `DispatchConnection`, looked after by nobody);
  `isGatewayConnection` and `gatewayKindOf` tell them apart. **A gateway's default label is the entry's name**
  (“Fusebox”, not “Fusebox · 10.100.0.235:8317”): it goes into sentences (“Send Claude Code through Fusebox”) and a burrow
  has only one.
- **Connecting and removing**: connection errors `gateway_exists` (a second gateway, AIG-01) and `gateway_too_old` (a
  Fusebox that refused `named-clients`, AIG-02); `connections.disconnect` answers an optional `notice` (“Fusebox didn’t
  answer, so remove the client “Whombat · Cybex BV” there yourself.”, AIG-03). `gatewayClientId(slug)`,
  `gatewayClientLabel(name)` and `GATEWAY_CLIENT_KEY_PREFIX` name Whombat's client in Fusebox.
- **The switches**: `Burrow.aiGateway` (`BurrowAiGateway {connectionId, name, kind, claude, codex}`, null without a
  gateway, absent from older runtimes), `aiGatewayFor(burrow, provider)` (the gateway while that tool's switch is on),
  `aiGatewayProviders`, `aiGatewayOn`. `burrows.setAiGateway` (`PUT /burrows/:burrow/ai-gateway`, strict body
  `{claude?, codex?}`, at least one; owners) signs `burrow.ai_gateway_changed` (Keys) per switch it changes, so its
  `eventId` is the last of them; `not_found` without a gateway. Retry class `receipt`.
- **The runner**: `DispatchContext.gateway` (`GatewayDispatchContext {v: 1, provider, connectionId, name, kind}`) and
  the heartbeat response's `gateway` (`AiGatewaySwitches`, AIG-16). The relay's paths are shared so the runner's
  forwarder and the server agree: `AI_GATEWAY_RELAY_PREFIX`, `aiGatewayRelayPath(provider)`, `AI_GATEWAY_RELAY_PATHS`,
  `aiGatewayRelayRoute(provider, path)` (`forward` / `hello` / `refuse`).
- **Usage**: `GatewayAccountUsage` and `GatewayPool` as AIG-20 lists them (windows are `UsageWindow`s, at most 64
  accounts), `UsageListOutput.gateway` for everyone in the burrow, and `usage.gateway_updated {connectionId}` on the
  `burrow` topic. The event carries no usage: clients refetch `usage.list`, so account emails still reach only owners
  and admins. `GATEWAY_POLL_MS` and the other watch constants are AIG-11's and AIG-14's numbers.
- **Refusals**: `GATEWAY_REFUSAL_CODES` (`gateway.missing`, `gateway.unreachable`, `gateway.used_up`), also in the
  session's `APP_ERROR_CODES`.
- **Copy** (`text/gateway.ts`): `AI_GATEWAY_COPY` (switch, hint, Fusebox's confirmation, Runs on, usage lines, connect
  and remove messages), `formatGatewayUntil` (“today 18:40”, “tomorrow 09:00”, the weekday within six days, else “12 Oct
  09:00”), `gatewayRefusalText`, `gatewayAlertText`, `gatewayKeysText`, `gatewayAccountStatusText`,
  `gatewayUpdatedText`, `gatewayAccountLabel`, `gatewaySwitchConfirms` (Fusebox only). Words the spec didn't give,
  decided here: the usage section's switch line “Claude Code turns go through Fusebox” / “… don’t go through Fusebox”,
  “Fusebox is answering” for the generic kind, “Not read yet”, “Used up” and “Busy” without a time, “Busy until 14:05”
  with the clock alone on the same day, and an alert without a reset “… Claude Code turns won’t start until it has room
  again.”
- **Feature `ai.gateway`.** `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 38 (as CT-326…CT-331): a new operation, a new event older
  clients skip, and optional fields; a client offers the connections, the switches and the pool only where the runtime
  advertises the feature.

Every package is 0.76.0.

## CT-333 Contracts 0.77.0: an agent's model and effort (2026-10-10)

John, 2026-10-10: “We have different agents that we can configure with a provider (Claude or Codex), but we cannot set
the model and we cannot set the effort. I would like to be able to configure this per agent.” Then: “Yes, give Claude
agents medium by default and high for coding. For the rest use your recommendations, implement it.” Whombat
`docs/decisions/model-effort.md` ME-01…ME-07.

- **`AgentEffort`** (`AGENT_EFFORTS`: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, `ultra`, least first) and
  **`AgentModelRuntime.effort`** (optional; absent = automatic). `model` was already there (a tool's model id); nothing
  set it before. Both go through `agents.update`'s `runtime`, as the provider does.
- **`ProviderModel`** (`id`, `label`, `description` without prices, `efforts`, `isDefault`) and `ProviderModels` (at most
  `PROVIDER_MODELS_MAX` 40): **`ProviderCheck.models`** (the runner reads them from the tool itself, without a sign-in:
  Claude Code's `initialize` `models`, Codex's app-server `model/list`) and **`ProviderSetup.models`** for clients.
  Absent: not known; a client then offers only the default model and every effort.
- **`turnEffort(setting, kind, supported)`**: the agent's effort, else `AUTOMATIC_EFFORT` (`work` → `high`, `chat` →
  `medium`, now for Claude Code as for Codex), kept within what the model takes — the nearest lower, else the nearest
  higher; null for a model that takes none. `modelOf`, `effortsFor` (every effort while the list is unknown).
- **Falling back** (ME-05): **`CompleteBody.modelFallback`** (`ModelFallbackReport {model, detail}`) when the agent's model
  refused the turn on its sign-in or gateway and the runner ran it again on the tool's default; **`AgentProfile.modelFallback`**
  (`AgentModelFallback {model, where {kind: account|org|gateway, name}, at}`, null when the last turn ran on the agent's
  model) for Configure → Model's quiet note. Never in a conversation.
- **Copy** (`text/models.ts`): `EFFORT_LABELS` (“Extra high” for `xhigh`), `MODEL_EFFORT_COPY` (sections, “Automatic”
  and its hint “Medium for conversations, high for code work.”, the fixed-effort hint), `defaultModelLabel` (“Default
  (Opus)”), `modelLabel`, `effortLabel`, `agentModelSummary` (“Sonnet · High effort”), the Keys lines
  `agentModelChangeText` / `agentEffortChangeText` (“Set Banjo’s effort to High”) and `modelFallbackText` (“Fable wasn’t
  available on Sara’s sign-in, so Banjo used the default model for that turn.”).
- **Feature `agents.model_effort`.** `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 38 (as CT-326…CT-332): optional fields both ways; a
  client offers the pickers only where the runtime advertises it (an older runtime would drop `effort`).

Every package is 0.77.0.

## CT-334 Contracts 0.78.0: how the box is doing (2026-10-11)

John, 2026-10-11: “I would like to see how the appliance is doing … CPU usage and the history, disk space usage,
network utilization, so bandwidth, how much data has been sent and received today … perhaps a complete overview with
token usage even.” He approved the mockup (Settings → This Whombat → “How it’s doing”) with “Yes please”. Whombat
`docs/decisions/box-status.md` BS-01…BS-12.

- **`HostMetrics`** (`@whombat/protocol/session`, `session/host.ts`): `now` (the latest sample: `cpuPermille`, `cores`,
  memory total/used, the computers' memory, the uplink's interface names), `disks` (`data` = `/persist` with `parts`
  `computers`/`whombat`/`work`/`database` — never more than `usedBytes`, null while quotas are recounted —, `system` =
  `/`, `backup` when mounted), `series` (one range's points: `start`, `stepS`, points oldest first, null for a gap; each
  `cpuPermille`, `cpuPeakPermille`, `memoryUsedBytes`, uplink `inBytes`/`outBytes`, the computers' bridge
  `computersInBytes`/`computersOutBytes`), `days` (30 days of traffic in `timeZone`, today last) and `measuringSince`.
  Ranges `hour`/`day`/`week`/`month` at 10 s / 5 min / 30 min / 2 h steps (`HOST_METRICS_STEP_S`, `HOST_METRICS_POINTS`).
  Processor shares are **tenths of a percent** (integers cross languages exactly). `TimeZoneName` (an IANA name).
- **Local IPC:** `MANAGER_PATHS.hostMetrics` = `POST /v1/host/metrics`, `HostMetricsRequest {v, range, since?, timeZone}`
  → `HostMetricsResponse {v, metrics}` (runtime → manager; an older manager answers 404). Go types in `go/local` and
  `go/protocol`.
- **Session op `host.metrics`** (`HostMetricsInput {range, since?}` → `HostMetricsOutput {metrics, reason}`; READ): owners
  only; `reason` `not_managed` on a self-hosted server, `unavailable` when the manager doesn't answer.
- **`spend.daily`** (`GET /burrows/:burrow/spend/daily` → `SpendDaily {scope, generatedAt, timeZone, days[]}`,
  `SpendDay {date, turns, input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite tokens}`, `SPEND_DAILY_DAYS` 30, every day present, today
  last; the scope rule of `spend.overview`).
- **Copy** (`text/host.ts`): `HOST_STATUS_COPY`, `HOST_RANGE_LABELS`, `HOST_DISK_PART_LABELS`, `HOST_CHART_DAYS` 14,
  `formatBytes` (decimal: `41 MB`, `2.2 GB`, `87 GB`), `formatMbits`, `bitsPerSecond`, `hostDiskUsedPct` (as `df`),
  `cacheReadPct`, and the owners' disk alert: `hostDiskAlertDue` (85 % then 95 %, a level re-arms 5 points below it)
  and `hostDiskAlertText` (“The Whombat’s disk is 86 % full, with 12.4 GB left. Most space goes to agents’ computers
  (22.9 GB).”).
- **Feature `host.metrics`** (covers `spend.daily` too). `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 38: new ops and fields only.

Every package is 0.78.0.

## CT-335 Contracts 0.79.0: backup files (2026-10-11)

John, 2026-10-11: “We need a way to create a backup which we can simply download and restore via an upload as well.
Perhaps we should be able to check what we want to include in the backup and set a default setting what a user should
backup?” After the proposal: “Implement this fully”. Whombat `docs/decisions/backup-file.md` BF-01… (the settled
decisions; not reopened here). New subpath **`@whombat/core/backup`** (pure: server, web, Android and the offline CLI)
and **`api.backups`**.

- **Categories** (`categories.ts`): `BACKUP_CATEGORY_IDS` in panel order (`agents`, `memories`, `automations`,
  `connections`, `skills`, `people`, `vault`, `messages`, `files`, `repositories`), `BACKUP_DEFAULT_CATEGORIES` (the
  first seven), `BACKUP_CATEGORY_LABELS`, `BACKUP_SECRET_CATEGORIES` (`connections`, `vault`: `includesSecrets` and the
  other owners' notice), `BackupCategoryEstimate {id, count, bytes, channels, othersPrivate}` and
  `backupCategoryMeta(estimate)` with the mock's lines. Decided here: one/none forms (“1 agent with its role, model and
  keys”, “No agents yet”, “Your 1 entry”, “Nothing of yours yet”), “· other people’s stay private” whenever
  `othersPrivate > 0` (vault and connections; never in a one-person burrow), repositories “3 repositories, with all
  their history”. `formatBackupSize` follows the mock, not `formatBytes`: decimal units, whole KB (at least 1), one
  decimal below 10 MB / 10 GB, a no-break space before the unit; `backupDownloadLabel` “Download · 1.8 MB”.
- **Container** (`container.ts`), decided: a 110-byte header (PNG-style magic `\x89WBK\r\n\x1a\n` to catch text-mode
  transfers, container version 1, KDF and its parameters, salt, cipher, chunk size, nonce prefix, a 16-byte key check,
  and a SHA-256 checksum of the rest) and nothing else in plaintext. **Argon2id** (RFC 9106, not scrypt: the current
  recommendation, and Node 24 has it natively) with **m = 128 MiB, t = 3, p = 1** (`BACKUP_KDF_DEFAULT`): measured 1.0 s
  with `@noble/hashes` and 0.15 s with Node's native `crypto.argon2` on the build machine (64 cores; scrypt N=2¹⁷ took
  0.23 s and Argon2id at 64 MiB 0.55 s, too little), so the CLI and a runtime without native Argon2 stay usable and slower
  boxes take 2–3 s; the server may pass the native one as `kdf` (vectors prove the bytes match). A reader bounds an
  untrusted header (≤ 1 GiB, ≤ 16 passes and lanes, chunks 1 KiB–16 MiB) and accepts Argon2's own minimums so vectors
  stay small. Keys: HKDF-SHA256 from the Argon2id output gives the stream key and the **key check**, so a wrong
  password is told apart from a damaged file (`wrong_password` before any chunk); the password is NFC-normalized UTF-8
  (≥ 10 code points). Body: **XChaCha20-Poly1305 STREAM**, 64 KiB chunks, nonce = prefix (16) ‖ counter (7 bytes) ‖
  last flag, AAD = SHA-256 of the whole header, so truncation, reordering, dropped or repeated chunks, swapped files and
  header edits fail. Because the prefix is fixed per file, `backupChunkSubkey` (HChaCha20) turns every chunk into IETF
  ChaCha20-Poly1305 under one subkey (`backupChunkIetfNonce`): a server may seal and open natively, byte for byte.
  `BackupFileEncoder` / `BackupFileDecoder` / `BackupFileReader` work incrementally and hold at most one chunk; the
  decoder releases only authenticated plaintext, and truncation is known only at `finish`, so **`backups.inspect` reads
  the whole file to its end before it answers**, and a restore only runs on a file that did.
- **Tar** (`tar.ts`): a minimal streaming POSIX ustar writer and reader — regular files only, ≤ 8 GiB per entry, paths ≤
  255 bytes with the ustar prefix, safe paths only (no `..`, absolute paths, backslashes or controls; the CLI unpacks
  with it), no pax/GNU extensions. Checked both ways against GNU tar.
- **Body** (`manifest.ts`): `manifest.json` first, `directory.jsonl` second, then `<category>.jsonl` in category order,
  then bytes — `files/<sha256>` (one blob namespace for message attachments, Files and pack files, each blob once),
  `canvases/<id>.yjs`, `repositories/<name>.bundle` (`git bundle --all`). `BackupEntryOrder` refuses anything else, so
  a preview stops after the last `.jsonl`. `BackupFileManifest` (`format: whombat.backup-file/1`, `schemaVersion`,
  `createdAt`, `timeZone`, `whombatVersion`, `source {burrowId, name, slug}`, `madeBy {name, email}`, categories with
  counts and bytes, `includesSecrets`), `BackupJsonlReader` (lines ≤ 4 MiB), `backupFileName` (`cybex-bv-2026-10-11.wbk`,
  the day in the burrow's time zone), `backupMadeText` (“Made 11 Oct 2026 on Cybex BV · Whombat 0.83”, major.minor as
  the mock), `.wbk`, `application/vnd.whombat.backup`, `BACKUP_FILE_MAX_BYTES` 10 GiB (the session's upload ceiling).
- **Records** (`records.ts`), decided: records name things by their **source ids**, and `directory.jsonl` (always
  written) maps every id the records use onto a portable key (person email; agent handle, a personal assistant by its
  person's email; automation name; conversation kind and slug, a DM by agent and person; connection service, scope,
  address or account and owner; repository name; Vault owner, kind and name; pack name, version, target; canvas slug).
  Compact, one remapping path (the restore map) for both restored and existing things, and references into a category
  that isn't in the file still resolve. Raw JSON the server stores as is (automation definitions and drafts, feedback
  settings, cards, previews) stays raw and is rewritten with `remapBackupIds` and validated by the current rules on
  restore (a definition that no longer validates comes back as a draft). Key ids, catalog ids and sign-in kinds are
  text (old grants parse; restore checks them). Secrets are unsealed inside (`secret`, `token`, `refreshToken`,
  `clientSecret`); never signing keys, sealed blobs, device ids, sessions, provider sessions, runs, usage. Per category:
  agents (`agent` with runtime, a portable `credential` — an org credential falls back to `requester` with a note —,
  channels, grants, skills off, connections it looks after; `schedule`, the maker's `briefing`), memories (active
  `memory` items, `note`, the maker's `profile` and `learning`), automations (`automation`, `destination`), connections
  (`connection` with its `credential`, the maker's `connector_account`, `connector_app`, `feedback_source`, `github`
  with the token only when the connection is the maker's), skills (`pack`, `pack_version` with its files or bundled by
  name and version, `pack_attachment` with approvals and secret bindings, `learned_skill`), people (`person`, `invite`,
  `channel`, `settings` — the burrow's name and slug never change on restore —, `repo`), vault (`vault_entry` with
  secret, tools, keys by agent, SSH servers and trusted host keys), messages (a `conversation` record per conversation
  first so the category restores alone, `message` with attachments, reactions and pin, `canvas`), files (`file`),
  repositories (`repository`). `BACKUP_COUNTED_TYPES` says what a count counts. **Versions**: changes stay additive
  with defaults; a reader refuses a higher format or `schemaVersion` (`newer_format`) rather than drop what it doesn't
  know; a record that doesn't parse is skipped with a note, never the restore.
- **Restore** (`restore.ts`): `BackupRestorePreview {fileName, size, manifest, sameBurrow, categories, notes}` with
  `BackupRestoreCategoryPreview {count, new, here, different, invite, channels, notes}`; `backupRestoreChips` (“130
  new”, “12 already here”, “3 different” in amber; people “2 people to invite”, “11 channels”). Decided: one chip order
  everywhere, new → already here → different (the sketch's Agents row has them the other way round). `backupRestoreHint`
  (the automations and connections lines), `BackupOnDifferent` `keep` (default) / `replace` with the mock's labels,
  `BackupNote` codes with `backupNoteText`, `BackupRestoreSummary` (per category added, updated, unchanged, kept,
  skipped; connections to sign in again, automations off, schedules paused, people invited, notes),
  `backupRestoreSummaryLines`, and the signed event's `backupRestoredText` (“Restored 9 automations from a backup made on
  11 Oct”, three categories then “and more”).
- **Words** (`copy.ts`, `errors.ts`): `BACKUP_COPY` (both panels), `backupFileNoticeText` for the other owners (“Mara
  made a backup file that includes connection sign-ins.”; Vault only: “… that includes their Vault.”; null without
  sign-ins), `backupFileMadeText`, `backupMakingText` / `backupRestoringText`, `BACKUP_FILE_ERROR_CODES` with a sentence
  and REST status each (the spec's three verbatim) in `error.details.code` as `backup_file.<code>`, `BackupFileError`.
- **REST** (`contracts/backups.ts`): `backups.defaults`, `setDefaults`, `estimate`, `list`, `create`, `get`, `remove`,
  `stage`, `getUpload`, `removeUpload`, `inspect`, `restore`, `getRestore`; `BackupFileView`, `BackupUploadView`,
  `BackupRestoreView`, `BackupProgress`. Decided: a file, an upload and a restore are their maker's alone (other owners
  get the DM notice, not the file); limits `BACKUP_FILE_TTL_S` / `BACKUP_UPLOAD_TTL_S` 24 h, `BACKUP_FILES_MAX` 5 per
  burrow, `BACKUP_UPLOADS_MAX` 3 per person. Raw transfers beside the JSON API (`BACKUP_FILE_TRANSFER`, as attachments):
  the download with `Range`/`If-Range`, 206/416, ETag = sha256; the upload as `PUT` chunks with `Content-Range` (8 MiB,
  at most 16 MiB), resumed from `backups.getUpload`'s `received`, 409 `upload_mismatch` with `received`
  (`BackupUploadMismatchDetails`). `sha256` at stage is optional over REST (a browser shouldn't read a GB twice) and
  always sent over the session.
- **Session**: `DownloadResource {type: 'backup-file', burrow, backupFileId}` (resumable by range), `UploadTarget {type:
  'backup-file', burrow, stagedBackupId}` staged by the api op `backups.stage` (no session-native stage op: the REST
  one serves both), `stream_done.output` `BackupFileStagedUploadOutput`. `SECRET_API_OPS` gains `backups.create`,
  `backups.inspect`, `backups.restore` (the password). Operation safety: those three `never` (secret); `restore` not
  destructive (it only adds and updates) but never resent; `remove` and `removeUpload` destructive (receipt);
  `setDefaults` and `stage` `receipt`; the reads `safe`. `backup_file.*` in `APP_ERROR_CODES`. Event `backups.changed
  {kind: file | restore, id}` on the maker's `me` topic (no content; progress at most once a second). Ids `bkf_`,
  `bku_`, `bkr_`.
- **The server enforces** what the contracts can't: owners and people only; only what the maker may see (and no
  reference to anything else); the staging directory under `WHOMBAT_HOME` with `CACHEDIR.TAG`; the disk check before
  making, staging and restoring; the password never stored, logged or kept; inspect reads to the end; restore through
  the commit pipeline, never deleting, idempotent through its restore map, automations off, schedules paused, webhook
  secrets only when switched on, invitations, connection checks; the signed events and the notice; the TTL sweeps.
- **Vectors**: `vectors/backup-file.json` (Argon2id small and at the defaults, whole files of 0, 1, 1024 and 2500 bytes
  with keys, subkey and header, ten altered files with their codes, a ustar body), checked against Node's native
  Argon2id and ChaCha20-Poly1305 too; session vectors for both streams and the ops' inputs.
- **Feature `backup.file`.** `SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 38: new ops, stream resources a client opens only where the
  feature is, and an event older clients skip. `@noble/ciphers` (MIT, already in the lockfile) is now a dependency of
  core.

Every package is 0.79.0.

## CT-336 Contracts 0.80.0: one Whombat — Home, Watch, Done recently, widgets (2026-10-17)

John, 2026-10-17: Whombat becomes one Whombat per person, connected to servers, Home Assistant, network gear, mail and
services, with dashboards (Whombat `docs/decisions/one-whombat.md` ONE-01…ONE-22, the settled decisions; not reopened
here). Built against `docs/implementation/one-whombat/assignment.md` §3; the released names are in Whombat
`docs/implementation/one-whombat/contracts-0.80.md`. Everything is additive: optional fields, new ops, new events older
clients skip, a new card kind older clients null (tolerant decoding).

- **Home** (`domain/home.ts`): `HomeOverview {summary {needsYou, working, problems}, needsYou, working, things,
  automationsToday, widgets, doneRecently, generatedAt?}`; `NeedsYouItem` (kind approval · alert · question · connection
  · device_skill · enrollment; severity bad · warn · info; `actions` with kinds approve · approve_later · decline · snooze
  · open · investigate; optional `subject` and `approvalNumber`); `WorkingTask` with steps done · active · waiting ·
  todo; `ThingSummary` (status ok · warn · bad · learning · offline · unknown, `facts`, `href`); `AutomationToday`;
  `ChangeEntry` with `undo {state, until?}`; `Widget`, `WidgetSource`; `WatchItem`.
- Decided: **links are `href` strings** (burrow-relative app paths: `/things/server%3Apve-02`, `/chats/cnv_…`, `/watch`)
  rather than new `LinkRef` members, so a newer server points at screens without a union change; `thingId(kind, id)` =
  `server:pve-02`, `parseThingId`, `thingHref`, `chatHref`. `HomeRef.kind` is open text (known values in
  `HOME_REF_KINDS`). **`WidgetSource` has a `kind`** (`connection_tool` | `server_metric`) the assignment's shape lacked,
  to make it a discriminated union. Limits: refresh 60 s – 1 day, default 300 s (`WIDGET_REFRESH_*`), 24 h of points
  (`WIDGET_HISTORY_S`), at most 3 series and `WIDGETS_MAX` 12 per person; Undo offered for 24 hours
  (`CHANGE_UNDO_WINDOW_S`), Home shows `DONE_RECENTLY_MAX` 8. `JsonPointer` and `jsonPointerGet` (RFC 6901).
- **REST** (`contracts/home.ts`): `home.overview` `GET /burrows/:burrow/home`; `watch.list` `GET …/watch`;
  `needsYou.snooze` `POST …/needs-you/snooze {ref, until}`; `changes.list` `GET …/changes` (cursor `before`, `thing`);
  `changes.undo` `POST …/changes/:changeId/undo` → `{change, state: undone | asked, approvalNumber?}`; `widgets.list`,
  `widgets.remove` (DELETE), `widgets.move` `POST …/widgets/:widgetId/move {position}` (each answers the widgets).
- **Events**: `home.changed {parts}` and `widget.updated {widgetId}` on `me`; no content, the client refetches.
- Ids `chg_` (change), `wdg_` (widget), `dvp_` (device skill proposal).

## CT-339 Servers: the hosts service through Whombat (2026-10-17)

ONE-11…ONE-15. `domain/hosts.ts` translates the hosts service's (Rackoon's) JSON to camelCase `Host*`: `HostServer`
(status ok · warn · bad · offline · pending, `platform` proxmox · standard, os, cpu, uptime, cpu %, memory, storage,
hottest sensor vs its limit, guests running/total per platform, agent, last seen, `cpu24h` ≤ 48 points, remote-control
switches), `HostFleet`, `HostServerDetail` (+ `HostServerInfo`, `HostLive`, sensors, disks with SMART, `HostHealth`,
`HostVirtualization`, hints, standard `workloads`, `proxmox {cluster, storages, backups, guests}`), `HostGuest`,
`HostGuestDetail`, `HostGuestPage`, `HostSeries`, `HostAlert`, `HostHint`, `HostMaintenance`, `HostCheck`,
`HostEnrollment`/`HostPendingEnrollment`, `HostTask`, `HostManageRequest`/`HostManageResult`, `HostManageReadResult`,
`HostGuestConfig`, `HostChoices`, `HostFirewall`, `HostBackupVolume`, `HostSnapshot`, `HostInspectResult`,
`HostConsoleSession`, `HostsStatus`. Rarely used nested parts are typed and optional.

- Decided: **op names are two-part.** Session op names are `api.<area>.<action>` and equal the endpoint ids, so the
  assignment's `hosts.servers.get` style becomes one area `hosts` with verb-noun keys: `status`, `fleet`, `getServer`,
  `serverMetrics`, `serverSettings`, `updateServer`, `removeServer`, `serverAction`, `listGuests` (fleet-wide, `server`
  filters one), `getGuest`, `guestMetrics`, `guestAction`, `manage`, `manageRead`, `getTask`, `listAlerts`, `ackAlert`,
  `unackAlert`, `listMaintenance`, `createMaintenance`, `removeMaintenance`, `listChecks`, `createCheck`, `updateCheck`,
  `removeCheck`, `createEnrollment`, `listEnrollments`, `approveEnrollment`, `rejectEnrollment`, `createConsole`,
  `closeConsole`, `inspect`, all under `/burrows/:burrow/hosts`. Beyond §3: `serverSettings` (the settings form needs a
  read), `serverAction` (host reboot/shutdown), `updateCheck`, `closeConsole`. **`hosts.manage` only changes**; the
  manage reads (configuration with its digest, choices, backups, storage content, appliances, tasks, firewall,
  snapshots) are `hosts.manageRead` `GET …/servers/:serverId/manage?op=…`, answered by op, so reads stay `GET` (safe to
  repeat) and writes `POST`. `guest.migrate` is one of the manage ops.
- `HostRange` was taken (`text/host.ts`, the box's own metrics), so the ranges are `HostSeriesRange` (1h … 90d).
- Consoles: `hosts.createConsole` answers `{sessionId, path, token, protocol, expiresAt, idleTimeoutS}`; the browser
  opens `path` (`HOSTS_CONSOLE_WS_PATH` = `/burrows/:burrow/hosts/consoles/:sessionId/ws` under `/api/v1`) offering
  `whombat.console.v1` and `whombat.token.<token>`; frames are the hosts service's. Whombat speaks the service's own
  subprotocol behind it.
- Realtime: a new topic kind **`hosts:<burrowId>`** (frequent server updates reach only clients showing servers) with
  `hosts.server {serverId, server | null}`, `hosts.guest`, `hosts.alert`, `hosts.task`, `hosts.enrollment`,
  `hosts.resync`.
- Session: every write is a call to the service outside the receipt's transaction, so `never` resent; removals, power,
  manage, enrollment decisions and `DELETE`s destructive. `hosts.createEnrollment` (the install command's token) and
  `hosts.createConsole` (the console token) are secret ops.
