## CT-345 A device action's unit, a reading's words (2026-10-17)

Whombat one-whombat-devices.md ONE-DD18/DD19 worked around both. `DeviceAction.unit?` (≤ 16, `°C`): shown with the value
and the owner's limits (“only between 16 and 24 °C”) instead of borrowing the unit of a reading with the same key.
`DeviceReading.choices? [{value, label}]` (the action's `DeviceChoice`, ≤ 32): a coded reading shows its words (“Mode ·
Heating”); a value without a choice shows as it is. Both optional: profiles written before keep parsing.

## CT-346 REST `unavailable` (503) (2026-10-17)

A service Whombat relies on that is down or still starting (the hosts service today) was a 503 `conflict` with
`details.code: hosts_unavailable` (Whombat ONE-DH11). **`ErrorCode` gains `unavailable`, `ERROR_STATUS` 503**, the app's
code still in `details.code`. The session already had a protocol `unavailable` with the same meaning (retryable), so
`SessionErrorCode` lists it once. `APP_ERROR_CODES` documents `hosts_unavailable`.

## CT-347 A connection call in the server's words (2026-10-17)

ONE-DH21 overrode the stored copy of a Servers call's approval on the server (`ApprovalDraft.callWords`), so the stored
title (“Restart web on pve-02”) and the copy clients derive from the action (“Use guest_power on servers”) disagreed
(`approvalCopy.matchesStored` false). **`ConnectionCallAction.params.words?`** (≤ `CONNECTION_CALL_WORDS_MAX` 150):
the call in plain words, written by the server from exactly this call's arguments, never by an agent (the action is
server-only), signed with the action like its other params. `actionCopy` says them — title “Restart web on pve-02”,
question with “?”, WHAT HAPPENS “Restart web on pve-02 once, then say how it went where it was asked” — and
`describeAction` (“Asked to restart web on pve-02”) for a shared connection; a personal one still names nothing in the
log. Absent: the generic words.

## CT-348 A link to a task chat (2026-10-17)

`DmLink` names only the agent, so a link into a task chat (a message, an approval's `in`, a plan) opened the default DM.
**`ChatLink {type: 'chat', id: ConversationId}`** is a `ConversationLink` (so `MessageLink.in`, `ApprovalLink.in`,
`PlanLink.in` take it) and a `LinkRef`; `linkPath` → `/:burrow/chats/:id`; `conversationLink(c)` answers it for a DM with
`chat` set; `auditLinkLabel` “Open the chat”. An older client leaves an item with an unknown link type out
(`decodeTolerant`).

## CT-349 Acknowledge in Watch; unarchive a chat (2026-10-17)

- **`watch.acknowledge`** `POST /burrows/:burrow/watch/acknowledge {ref: HomeRef, acknowledged = true}` → `{ref, state:
  acknowledged | open}`: “I've seen it” until it changes, or (`acknowledged: false`) “Bring it back”. A server alert's
  acknowledgement is the hosts service's (until it resolves, shared, as `hosts.ackAlert` with `minutes: 0`); anything
  else is the caller's own view. Session safety `never` (the alert's case is a hosts call outside the receipt, CT-339).
  Clients that split it themselves (`hosts.ackAlert` / `needsYou.snooze`, app AP-1259, AP-1362) can switch to it.
- **`chats.unarchive`** `POST /burrows/:burrow/chats/:conversationId/unarchive` → `{conversation}` (its person; the chat
  comes back to the list). Receipt.

## CT-350 Consoles through the session (2026-10-17)

A browser that reaches its Whombat through the relay (dev.whombat.com → relay → box) had no way to a console: the
console is a WebSocket on the box's own origin (CT-339). The session gets a **`console` stream**, following the
bidirectional collab stream (CT-22):

- `open{stream, spec: {kind: 'console', burrow, sessionId, token}}` with what `hosts.createConsole` answered (a `secret`
  op, so the token is never kept in a receipt). The appliance checks it as its WebSocket proxy does (the session's
  person, still an owner of the burrow that sees servers, the same session, single use, 30 seconds), opens the hosts
  service's console, and answers `opened{meta: {kind: 'console', protocol}}` **once that is connected**; a refusal is
  `error{stream_refused}` with `details.code` `console_refused` (token used, old or someone else's; the service said no)
  or `hosts_unavailable`, so a client tells “open it again” from “try later”.
- DATA both ways: the console's messages unchanged (`kind | channel (u16 BE) | payload`), each framed `[u32 len]
  [message]` like collab, ≤ **`CONSOLE_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` 2 MiB** (the hub's payloads are ≤ 1 MiB; Whombat's proxy
  reads 2 MiB). `@whombat/protocol/console`: `encodeConsoleMessages`, `consoleDataPayloads`, `ConsoleMessageDecoder`
  (the collab encoder and decoder take a bound now; collab's stays 16 MiB).
- **Back-pressure is credit**: each side grants it as it hands messages on (the appliance after the service's socket
  took them, the client as they reach the screen), so a slow browser slows the console and the other way round.
- **Closing**: END from either side ends the console (the hub's `{"type":"closed","reason"}` control comes in DATA
  before the appliance's END, as over the WebSocket); RESET aborts (`cancelled` from the client, `internal` when the
  service's socket failed). The hub's idle timer counts the client's `activity` controls, which it sends while a person
  types, as before.
- Negotiated: capability **`stream.console`** (`CAPABILITIES.console`); a client offers consoles on the session only
  when `welcome.capabilities` has it, so an older runtime keeps its “consoles open on the local network for now”.

## CT-351 Contracts 0.80.2: a host page with only the platforms it has (2026-10-17)

A patch over 0.80.1 (no level or feature change). `HostServerDetail.workloads` was `z.record(z.enum(['docker', 'incus',
'libvirt']), …)`, and Zod 4 makes a record over an enum require **every** key: a Docker host's page (only `docker`)
failed response validation. It is a **`z.partialRecord`** now (TS type `Partial<Record<…>>`). No other record in the
hosts, Home, devices or tool-limit shapes is keyed by an enum (they key by `z.string()` or a string pattern).

Not added: allocated-disk totals for a storage (“overbooked”, app AP-1311). The hosts service reports a storage's used
and total size and each guest's used disk, not the size guests' disks are provisioned at, so the field would have no
source; it waits for the hosts service to report it (a change to the hosts service first).

Every package is 0.80.2.

## CT-352 Contracts 0.80.3: Ignore a Needs you item (2026-10-17)

John asked for “Ignore” in Needs you: an old approval from an agent nobody uses any more stayed there with only Approve,
Tonight at 03:00 and Not now (which brings it back the next morning). **`needsYou.ignore`** `POST
/burrows/:burrow/needs-you/ignore {ref: HomeRef, ignored = true}` → `{ref, ignored}`: the item leaves the caller's
Needs you for good and their Watch shows it as seen (`acknowledged`); `ignored: false` takes it back (the toast's
Undo). Nothing else changes: an approval stays undecided (Decline is the decision), a server alert stays open for
everyone else and in the hosts service. The caller's own view only, like snoozes; session safety receipt.

Ignore is a button every client draws on every item (not a `NeedsYouActionKind`): an action kind an older client
doesn't know would be dropped and counted as “needs a newer version of the app”. No feature name, as `watch.acknowledge`
(CT-349): a runtime without the op answers `unknown_op` and the client says it didn't work.

Every package is 0.80.3.

## CT-353 Backup jobs (2026-10-17)

Whombat proxmox.md PX-03: a server's Backups tab lists Proxmox's scheduled backup jobs and creates, edits, pauses,
deletes and runs them, and a guest without a job gets “Add to a backup job”. `domain/hosts.ts`:

- **`HostBackupJob`**, the camelCase mirror of the hub's `BackupJob` (build brief §2.1): `id`, `enabled`, `schedule`
  (Proxmox's calendar event), `storage`, `node?` (null: every node), `selection` `all | guests | pool`, `guests?` and
  `exclude?` (hub guest ids), `pool?`, `mode` `snapshot | suspend | stop`, `compress?`, `keep?`
  (`HostBackupKeep {last, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, yearly}`, each a non-negative integer and optional; null: the
  storage's own retention), `notesTemplate?`, `comment?`, `nextRun?`, `digest?`. Read tolerantly: everything but the
  first seven is optional and nullable, and `compress` is text (Proxmox also knows `1`), so a leaner or newer hub
  parses.
- `HOST_MANAGE_READ_OPS` + **`backupjob.list`** → `{op: 'backupjob.list', items: HostBackupJob[]}`.
- `HOST_MANAGE_OPS` + **`backupjob.create`**, **`backupjob.update`**, **`backupjob.delete`**, **`backupjob.run`**;
  `backupjob.delete` is in `HOST_MANAGE_DESTRUCTIVE_OPS` (and takes `confirm: true`), `run` isn't (it backs up, like
  Back up now).
- Their `params` are **`HostBackupJobParams`**: `jobId` (every op but create), `enabled`, `schedule`, `storage`, `node`,
  `selection`, `guests`, `exclude`, `pool`, `mode`, `compress` (an enum here: `zstd | lzo | gzip | 0`), `keep`,
  `notesTemplate`, `comment`; an update sends what changes, `null` clears a nullable field. It is **strict**, so a field
  Whombat doesn't pass is refused naming it (PX-08) instead of being dropped. An update sends the job's own `digest` as
  the request's `digest` (`digest_mismatch` when it changed meanwhile). Create answers the job's id as
  `HostManageResult.newId`, run a `task`.
- Feature **`hosts.backup_jobs`**: a client shows the jobs and “Add to a backup job” only on runtimes that advertise
  it, since an older runtime refuses the op as invalid rather than answering `unknown_op`.

## CT-354 A sensitive rule that tests one argument (2026-10-17)

`SensitiveRule.argValue` matched every string anywhere in a call's arguments, so with the new Servers tools a backup's
notes, a file name or a job's comment that said “delete” would have made an everyday call ask. **`SensitiveRule.arg?`**
names the one top-level argument `argValue` tests (every string inside it); absent, every string anywhere as before, so
Home Assistant's rules over nested entity ids are unchanged. Additive: an older matcher ignores the field and asks
more, never less. `SERVERS_SENSITIVE` rules all test `action`.

## CT-355 The Servers tools for full Proxmox support (2026-10-17)

Whombat proxmox.md PX-02, PX-08. `SERVERS_TOOLS` has 34 tools (build brief §2.2), so `CatalogEntry.tools` takes up to
**48** (was 32; the catalog is a constant, never parsed off the wire, and `ConnectionToolView` lists have no bound).

- **Fixed:** `guest_power` takes `pause` and `resume`; `guest_config_set` takes `revert` (keys) and `confirm` (deleting an
  unused disk); `guest_migrate` takes `storage` (the target node's storage for local disks) and no longer `online` (the
  service decides); `server_diagnose` takes `args` (strings, at most 16, as the hub's diagnose takes them);
  `server_metrics` names `cpu_pct, mem_pct, temp_max_c, net_rx_mbps, net_tx_mbps` (a server's history has no
  `net_mbps`; that is only the fleet overview's sum).
- **New reads:** `guest_snapshots`, `guest_backups {guest?}`, `guest_firewall`, `server_choices`, `backup_jobs`,
  `storage_contents {storage?, content?, appliances?}`, `server_tasks {guest?, task?}`.
- **New writes:** `guest_create`, `guest_clone`, `guest_template`, `guest_delete {purge?}`, `guest_disk`, `guest_backup`,
  `backup_job_set`, `storage_content`, `task_stop`, `guest_firewall_set`, `guest_ha`, `guest_replication`,
  `server_power`. Arguments are snake_case like the existing tools'; the server maps them to the manage ops.
- **Always ask:** `guest_delete`, `guest_template`, `server_power` (with `guest_migrate` and `server_command`) are
  `sensitive: true`; by `action` (`SERVERS_SENSITIVE`, CT-354): `guest_power` stop · shutdown · reboot · pause,
  `guest_snapshot` restore · delete, `guest_disk` move, `guest_backup` restore · delete, `storage_content` delete,
  `backup_job_set` delete. Everything else follows the tool's tier.
- Decided where the brief left it open: `backup_job_set` also takes **`pool`** (without it `selection: pool` couldn't
  name one); `guest_firewall_set`'s `rule` has `HostFirewall`'s rule fields; stated defaults follow Rackoon's dialogs
  and Proxmox: `start` false, `purge` true, `delete_source` false (the old copy stays as an unused disk), `as_new` false,
  `full` linked from a template and a full copy otherwise, HA `started` with one restart and one relocation,
  replication every 15 minutes. `guest_create`'s `id` and the others' new-guest ids are Proxmox numbers (100 and up).
- The connection's guide says to read before changing (digests, choices, ids), that long work runs as a task Whombat
  reports on in the chat (PX-05), and what always asks.

## CT-357 The assistant's name: Dusty first, “Whombat” reserved (2026-10-17)

Whombat assistant-name.md AN-02, AN-03. In the assistant shell an assistant gets a person's name, not “Whombat”:
`pickAssistantName(taken, {prefer, seed, skip})` tries a `prefer`red name (the account's assistant elsewhere) when it
is well-formed, free and not reserved, then the first free of **`ASSISTANT_NAMES`** (Dusty, Pippa, Banjo, Hazel, Ace,
in that order), then `pickPersonalAgentName`'s pool from the seed. `skip` passes over names as if taken, so “Suggest a
name” offers another each press. **`RESERVED_AGENT_NAMES`** = `['Whombat']` (`isReservedAgentName`, case-insensitive):
`agents.update` refuses it with `AGENT_NAME_RESERVED_TEXT` (“Whombat is the name of this box, so pick another one.”);
`AGENT_NAME_FORM_TEXT` (“…, like Dusty.”) replaces the server's “like Hazel” hint. `pickPersonalAgentName`, Hazel's
`PERSONAL_AGENT_DEFAULT_NAME` and `assistantName` are unchanged: the crew shell still uses them.
`ASSISTANT_RESET_TAKEN_TEXT` is deprecated (the crew shell's “Reset to Hazel”). Additive.

## CT-358 An agent's face: `Agent.look` drawn again, `agents.update` `look` (2026-10-17)

Whombat assistant-name.md AN-04. **`Agent.look`** is the face the agent wears: the character an assistant was given
with its name or that its owner picked. The schema stays `AgentRole.nullable().optional()` (a team agent migration 0061
moved still holds its old legacy role there), and **`agentFace(agent)`** = `canonicalRole(agent.look ?? agent.role)`
draws it, so those team agents keep their role's face. **`assistantLookFor(name)`**: the character whose
`defaultName` it is (Dusty → `operator`), else `assistant` (Hazel's drawing). **`ASSISTANT_FACES`**: the five keys in
`AGENT_CHARACTERS` order, for the picker. **`agents.update` takes `look`**: `z.enum(CANONICAL_ROLES)`, optional; a team
agent's is refused (`validation_failed` on `look`, `ONLY_ASSISTANT_FACE_TEXT`); a rename never changes it. Additive: an
older runtime strips the unknown field (the face just doesn't change), an older client never sends it.

## CT-361 An assistant may hold a team agent's keys in the assistant shell (2026-10-17)

Whombat assistant-name.md AN-10. Once the crew retires (AN-06), each person's assistant is the only agent and does
what the crew did: code on branches, CI, merges and deploys at their tiers. **`personalAgentMayHold(id, {assistantShell})`**
and **`grantFitProblem(name, personal, keyId, {assistantShell})`** take the runtime's shell (`PersonalKeyOptions`); with
`assistantShell` a personal agent may also hold every key a team agent may, never one only automations hold
(`agentMaxTier` still caps the tier). **`KeyRequestAgent.assistantShell`** lets it ask for one there.
**`assistantShellGrants(agentId)`**: its own defaults (`PERSONAL_DEFAULT_GRANTS`) and a team agent's
(`ROLE_DEFAULT_KEYS.developer`); a key in both keeps the assistant's tier. Without the option every rule is as before
(the crew shell, older callers). Pure and additive: no wire change.

## CT-363 Incus and unRAID server kinds, the self guest (2026-10-17)

Whombat incus-unraid.md IU-02, IU-03 (build brief `docs/implementation/incus-unraid/assignment.md` §2.1).

- **`HostServerPlatform`** gains `incus` (Incus without Proxmox VE or unRAID) and `unraid` at the end; a client maps a
  value it doesn't know to `standard`. **`HostManagePlatform`** gains `unraid`.
- **`HostGuest.self?`** (only when true): one of the guest's MAC addresses is the hub machine's own, so it is this
  Whombat. The MACs stay inside the hosts service (not in the contract). **`HostServer.hostsThisWhombat?`** and
  **`HostServerInfo.hostsThisWhombat?`**: one of its guests is `self`.
- **`HOST_SELF_GUEST_ALLOWED`** is an allowlist, not the brief's refusal list turned round: `actions` `start`, `resume`,
  `snapshot_create`, `snapshot_delete`; `ops` `backup.create`, `backup.update`, `backup.delete`, `guest.clone`,
  `replication.add`, `replication.delete`, `task.stop`; `asNewOnly` `backup.restore` (an Incus restore is always new, a
  Proxmox one with `newId`). Reads and consoles are always allowed. Everything else that changes the guest is refused
  with `self_guest` — the brief's list, plus firewall and HA changes (a rule or an HA state `stopped` cuts the Whombat
  off as surely as a stop), so a client that hides by this list never offers more than the hub allows. **`selfGuestAllows
  (change)`** answers it for an action or an op.
- Words: **`HOST_SELF_GUEST_LABEL`** “This Whombat”, **`HOST_SELF_SERVER_POWER_TEXT`** “This Whombat goes down too.”
  (the question before restarting or shutting down its host; that stays allowed).

## CT-366 The Servers tools for Incus and unRAID (2026-10-17)

IU-04…IU-06 (brief §2.5). `SERVERS_TOOLS` has **49** tools, so `CatalogEntry.tools` takes up to **64** (was 48).

- **Widened for Incus:** `server_detail` (Incus and Unraid parts, the self server), `guest_config` (profiles, devices,
  restricted keys), `guest_config_set` (`devices` — a map of name → `{key: value}` or null to remove — and `profiles`),
  `guest_create` (`project`, `profiles`, `pool`, `network`, `cloud_init` ≤ 64 KiB, `template` = image alias),
  `guest_clone` (`storage` = pool, `project`, `instance_only`), `guest_delete`, `guest_disk` (resize `root`),
  `guest_backup` (`name`, `expires_days` default 7, `start`; restore is always new on Incus), `guest_backups`,
  `server_tasks` (Incus operations and Unraid commands), `task_stop`, `server_choices` (`project`). Their descriptions
  say which platform each argument is for.
- **New reads:** `incus_overview`, `incus_profile`, `network_leases`, `guest_log {lines?}`, `unraid_overview`.
- **New writes:** `guest_rename`, `guest_move`, `guest_publish {alias?, description?, snapshot?}`, `incus_image`,
  `incus_profile_set`, `storage_volume`, `unraid_array`, `unraid_plugins`, `container_update`, `guest_autostart`.
- **Deviations from the brief, decided here:** `incus_profile_set` takes **`digest`** (`profile.update` needs it;
  `incus_profile` gives it); `container_update`'s **`action` (`update | check`) is required**, because a sensitive rule
  on an absent argument never matches, so an update without it would not have asked; `guest_publish` also takes
  `description`. `guest_rename`'s `name` carries `INCUS_NAME_PATTERN` as a JSON Schema pattern.
- **Always ask:** `guest_move` whole (`sensitive: true`); by `action`: `incus_image` delete, `incus_profile_set` delete,
  `storage_volume` delete, `unraid_array` stop · parity_cancel, `unraid_plugins` update, `container_update` update.
  `SERVERS_SENSITIVE` has 12 rules, all on `action` (CT-354). The self guest's refusals and the self server's
  power question are the server's (CT-363 words), not rules.
- Copy: “Unraid” in every description (the vendor's spelling, as the UI writes it); the guide (1 102 characters) names
  `incus_overview`, `unraid_overview`, `incus_profile`'s digest, Unraid commands as tasks and the self guest.

## CT-368 Contracts 0.83.0: full Incus and unRAID support (2026-10-17)

CT-363…CT-367. Additive: new enum members at the end, optional fields, new ops and read variants, new tools, two new
features. No new op id (`hosts.manage` and `hosts.manageRead` carry the new ops), so no `OPERATION_SAFETY` change;

## CT-374 Pre-approved enrollments (2026-10-18)

SI-07 (brief §2.3). **`hosts.createEnrollment`** takes **`body: HostCreateEnrollmentBody.optional()`** —
`{control?, name? (1–63)}`, strict. The contract library's way of an optional body is the schema's own `.optional()`:
`apiOperationInput` already makes a body that accepts `undefined` optional in the session input, and on REST an empty
POST (no body) or `{}` both pass. Absent `control` means `full`. There is no `approve` member: Whombat always
pre-approves (the server sends `approve: true` to the hub), so a client can't ask for an enrollment that waits.

  `preApproved?`; **`HostPendingEnrollment`** gains `control?` (nullable: what an approval by hand applies) and `name?`
  (nullable). All optional, so an older Whombat's answers still parse.

## CT-375 Install jobs: Sign in once (2026-10-18)

SI-02…SI-05, SI-08, SI-09, SI-11 (brief §2.3). Exactly the brief's shapes:

- **`HostInstallState`** `connecting | installing | waiting | ready | failed`; **`HostInstallErrorCode`** (twelve codes,
  `not_allowed` … `failed`); **`HostInstall`** `{id, address, username, control, state, hostKey {algorithm,
  fingerprint} | null, hostKeyNew, serverId, serverName, system, already, keptKey, error {code, message} | null,
  detail, startedAt, updatedAt, finishedAt}`; **`HostInstallBody`** `{address (1–255), username (1–64), auth: password
  {password} | vault {entryId, password?}, control, name?, keepKey?: {entryId} | {create: true}}`.
- **Ops**, at the end of the enrollment group: **`hosts.startInstall`** `POST /burrows/:burrow/hosts/installs` →
  202 `HostInstall` (owners) and **`hosts.getInstall`** `GET /burrows/:burrow/hosts/installs/:installId` →
  `HostInstall` (owners).
- Tighter than the brief's sketch, decided here: the `auth` variants and the `keepKey` objects are strict too (the body
  already is), so `{entryId, create: true}` or a password variant with an `entryId` is refused instead of being
  stripped to the first matching variant; and `detail` is capped at **`HOST_INSTALL_DETAIL_MAX`** (4096), the brief's
  4 KiB (the server trims the installer's last lines to it).
- **`parseHostInstallAddress(text)`** → `{host, hostKind, port}` or null: a host name or IP (core's
  `parseVaultSshHost`, so the same rule as a Vault SSH server), `:port` optional (**`HOST_INSTALL_SSH_PORT`** 22),
  IPv6 bare without a port and in brackets with one. One parser for the server's check and both clients' forms; the
  body's `address` stays a plain string so the server answers a bad one in words.
- **`hostInstallErrorText(code, {address, name?, whombat?, withKey?, installed?})`**: the words of SI-11 for each code,
  as `HostInstall.error.message` carries them (“Couldn’t sign in to 10.100.0.14: the user name or password isn’t
  right.”, “pve-03 can’t reach this Whombat at 10.100.1.160:8443. Is it on another network?”, “This server reports to
  another Whombat. Remove its agent there first.”, and for `timed_out` with `installed` “It’s installed, but its first
  report hasn’t come in yet. It shows up once it does.”). Hosts errors have a words table here (`HOST_ERROR_WORDS`,
  CT-367), so these words live next to it; the server may still give `not_allowed` the destination rule's own words
  (core's `vaultSshDestinationProblem`). Clients show `error.message` as it comes.

## CT-405 GraphQL read paths (2026-10-18)

CT-400's audit: Unraid's guide reads through `POST /graphql`, where the path can't tell a query from a mutation, so every
Unraid read counted as a change; GitLab's `POST /api/graphql` read path counted its mutations as reads. **`ReadPath.graphql`**
(optional): the call reads only when its body is GraphQL queries (**`graphqlReadsOnly`**: one operation or a batch, an
object or its JSON text or a raw document, every `query` a non-empty string that names no `mutation` or `subscription`
anywhere; a persisted query without its text is not a read). **`isReadRequest(entry, method, path, body?)`** takes the
body (without it such a call is a write) and `callAccess` passes `args.body`. Unraid gets `POST ^/graphql$` (graphql),
GitLab's read path becomes graphql and its prefixes gain `/api/graphql` (the endpoint is outside `/api/v4/`, so the guide's
call was refused). Cloudflare's analytics GraphQL has no mutations and keeps its plain read path. The guides say queries
read.

## CT-406 Undo asks the agent (2026-10-18)

HR-03 (stream S). **`DispatchTrigger`** gains **`undo_requested`**: a person pressed Undo on a change reported with
`report_change` and `undo`; the turn runs in the change's chat for that person, its trigger message their “Please undo
this: …”. **`DispatchContext.undoRequest`** (`UndoRequestContext` `{changeId, title (1–200), undo (≤ 1000)}`, nullable,
optional): the private note goes to the agent here, never into the chat. **`UndoChangeResponse.state`** gains
**`requested`** (`UNDO_STATES`) with **`conversationId`**: the agent was asked to put it back there.

Apps up to 0.87 parse `DispatchSummary.trigger` strictly (`dispatch.updated`, and the answer of Stop, `dispatches.cancel`).
So the new trigger stays between server and runner: **`DispatchSummary.trigger`** is **`SummaryTrigger`** (every trigger
up to `passed`) and the server fills it with **`summaryTrigger`** (`undo_requested` → `mention`: the turn answers a
person's message). An older app that presses Undo on a reported change can't read `requested` and shows its generic
error, although the request went through; that beats the words of an older state (“Undone.”, “needs an approval”).

## CT-407 An approved call answers in words (2026-10-18)

HR-04 (stream S). **`DispatchContext.grantedResult`** (`GrantedResultContext` `{outcome done | error | failed, text ≤
GRANTED_RESULT_TEXT_MAX 4000, truncated}`, nullable, optional): with `grantedApproval` after an approved `connection_call`
or pack call, what the call returned, so the agent answers in its own words instead of Whombat posting the raw output.

## CT-410 What a skill needs (2026-10-18)

Whombat all-skills.md SK-04. **`PackSkillRef.needs`** (**`SkillNeeds`**, strict) `{connections ≤ 8, servers ≤ 8}`,
default empty (a function default, so parses never share arrays). Connections are catalog ids by **`SkillConnectionId`**,
`CatalogIdText`'s slug pattern (not imported: the catalog imports the Vault, which imports packs, and the cycle left a Vault
constant undefined at load); servers are **`SkillServerKind`** slugs: a server's platform but `standard` (`proxmox`,
`incus`, `unraid`, `libvirt`), `docker`, or the mark of its system (`osMark`: `truenas`, `openmediavault`, `debian` …),
because TrueNAS and OpenMediaVault are systems, not platforms. **`serverSkillKinds({platform, os, docker})`** gives a
server's kinds and **`missingSkillNeeds(needs, have)`** what a burrow lacks, so server and tests agree. Unknown shapes,
duplicates and more than eight are refused; unknown ids are not (a newer catalog may know them, an older Whombat treats
them as missing). `validatePack`'s skills carry `needs`. Front matter stays name and description (BP-D20).

## CT-411 One name, one skill (2026-10-18)

SK-03. **`SkillOrigin`** `shipped | imported | own` (`SKILL_ORIGINS`) and **`SKILL_ORIGIN_PRECEDENCE`** (own > imported >
shipped). The brief called it `SkillSource`; core already exports `SkillSource` (the https link a skill came from, RA-25),
so the enum is named apart while the field on `PackContext.skills`, `SkillLibraryItem` and `SkillMatch` stays `source`.
**`skillWinner(skills)`** answers one `SkillPick {name, winner, replaced}` per name in first-seen order: the closest origin
wins, copies of the same origin keep the order given (attachment order), `replaced` is closest first so `replaced[0]` is
what Compare diffs against and Reset leaves. The caller decides which copies take part.

## CT-412 The index (2026-10-18)

SK-05. **`SkillListing`** `full | short | unlisted`; **`SKILL_LISTING_FULL_MAX`** 160, **`SKILL_LISTING_SHORT_MAX`** 60,
**`SKILL_LISTING_BUDGET_DEFAULT`** 10,000, **`SKILL_LISTING_LINE_OVERHEAD`** 24 (a listed line costs name + description +
24: the CLI's bullet, separators and line). **`planSkillListing(items, budget)`** over `{key, name, description, rank}`
answers `{byKey: Map<key, {listing, description}>, used, unlisted}`, in rank then name order: full while every skill
after it could still be listed short, or while full listings stay within **`SKILL_LISTING_FULL_SHARE`** (half) of the
budget; then short while it fits; the rest unlisted (their description is the short cut, for the front matter). A plain
“full while it fits” spends the whole 10,000 on ~45 full lines and leaves the short tier empty; the share keeps the top
skills full and lists as many others short as fit. Never a less important skill above a more important one.
**`skillListingRank`** gives SK-05's tiers (0 pinned, 1 used in **`SKILL_RANK_RECENT_DAYS`** 30, 2 own or imported, 3
tied to a connected thing, 4 the rest). **`cutSkillDescription(text, max)`**: white space folded, cut at the last word
boundary (unless that drops more than half), trailing punctuation dropped, `…`.

## CT-414 find_skill, read_skill, skill_write (2026-10-18)

SK-06, SK-09, SK-10, SK-12. In `SKILL_MCP_TOOLS`:

- **`find_skill`** `{query 1–200, online = false, limit 1–10 = 5}` → ok `{matches: SkillMatch {pack, name, description,
  source, status listed | unlisted | resting, folder}[], online?: SkillHubResult[], unreachable?: SkillHub[]}`. No key,
  read-only.
- **`read_skill`** `{name, pack?, file?}` → ok `{pack, name, version, folder, text, files {path, bytes}[]}` or
  `not_found {suggestions ≤ 5}`. `file` is any path inside the skill (`SkillFilePathText`, `packPathProblem`'s rules):
  imported skills carry folders like `assets/` that `SkillFilePath`'s three folders would refuse. No key, read-only.
- **`skill_write`**: MCP inputs are objects, so **`SkillWriteInput`** is one object (`action` + every action's fields,
  each optional) checked against **`SkillWriteChange`**, the discriminated union on `action` (`create`, `patch`,
  `rewrite`, `add_file`, `remove_file`, `rest`, `install`) the server's `writeSkill` takes; **`skillWriteChange(input)`**
  narrows a parsed input. `add_file` paths follow `SkillFilePath`; `remove_file` takes any path inside the skill.
  **`SkillWriteOutput`**: `commitOutcome({pack, name, version, replaces?: {pack}, messageId?})` (a key at `ask` waits like
  any keyed tool), `invalid`, `refused`, `not_found`, `waiting {messageId}`. Key `skills.propose`. **Not** in
  `MCP_POSTING_TOOLS`: most calls (patches) post nothing; the server stamps `postedAt` itself when a create or install
  posts its card.
- `propose_skill` stays; its description starts “Older form of skill_write (use that)”. `skill_result` and `memory`
  point at `skill_write` instead of `propose_skill`.

## CT-421 A password in a URL, found fast (2026-10-18)

Stream L: `literalSecretKind` took about 7 s on a 130 KB run without spaces (a base64 blob in a skill file), so
`validatePack` stalled on such an import, which the larger import limits (CT-417) make likely. The URL-password pattern,
in `TOKEN_PATTERNS` and in `redactSecrets`, was unanchored with an unbounded scheme and backtracked quadratically: it now
starts at a word boundary with a scheme of at most 31 characters (`\b[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]{0,30}://`). A unit test runs a
130 KB run through both in well under a second and still finds a URL with a user and password in it.

## CT-423 Contracts 0.92.1: skill archives over the session (2026-10-18)

The lead found Add skills → upload a zip broken on managed appliances: `skills.importPreview` carried the archive as
base64 JSON and a CONTROL message holds 64 KiB (`SESSION_MAX_CONTROL_BYTES`), so any zip over ≈ 48 KB failed. Skill
archives now travel like pack archives (CT-55), reusing that machinery instead of a second staging path:

- **`packs.stage`** takes an optional **`purpose`** (`StagedArchivePurpose`: `pack`, the default, or `skills`). `skills`
  allows up to `SKILL_IMPORT_MAX_BYTES` (25 MiB) instead of `PACK_ARCHIVE_MAX_BYTES`; `STAGED_ARCHIVE_MAX_BYTES` names
  both and `maxBytes` in the answer is the cap of the purpose. `size` in the schema allows the larger cap and a
  refinement keeps packs at 4 MiB; `PackStagedUploadOutput.size` allows 25 MiB. Who may stage `skills` is the
  runtime's to decide (any member, for their own assistant; Whombat SK-S).
- **`skills.importPreview`**'s body union gains **`{ stagedArchiveId, agentId? }`**: an archive the caller staged and
  uploaded through the `pack-archive` stream; the preview consumes it and reads it under its staged file name.
- **`StagedArchiveId`** moves to core (`contracts/packs.ts`), where the preview body needs it; `@whombat/protocol/session`
  re-exports it under the same name.
- Feature **`skills.import_staged`**: a client stages skill archives only on runtimes that advertise it (a 0.92.0 runtime
  refuses `purpose`, its `packs.stage` input being strict) and sends small ones as base64 elsewhere.

Additive: old clients send no `purpose` and get packs as before; old runtimes don't advertise the feature. A patch, so
`SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 39. Every package is 0.92.1.

## CT-456 Fast replies on a model and an agent (2026-10-19)

John, 2026-10-19: “In the chat with Dusty, we should be able to change: the provider (e.g., OpenAI or Claude), the
effort, fast mode, if applicable.” After the mockup: “I love it. Implement this fully.” Whombat
`docs/decisions/chat-runtime.md` CR-01…CR-11. **`ProviderModel.fast`** (`ModelFast`, `MODEL_FAST`: `off` — offered, off
unless asked; `on` — offered and on by default; absent or null: none): Claude Code's `supportsFastMode`, Codex's
`priority` service tier and `defaultServiceTier`. **`AgentModelRuntime.fast`** (optional boolean; absent: the model's own
default), through `agents.update`'s `runtime` like `effort`. **`modelFast(models, id)`** → `off` | `on` | null, the
default model's without an id.

## CT-457 Whether a turn asks for fast replies (2026-10-19)

CR-06. **`turnFast(setting, offered)`** → boolean | null: the setting when the model offers fast replies; null — send
nothing, the model's own default applies — when the setting is absent or the model has none. `false` is a value the
runner sends (Codex `serviceTier: "default"`, Claude Code `fastMode: false`), so a model whose default is `on` can be
turned off. Kept that simple on purpose: an unknown list (`offered` absent) sends nothing, as a model without fast
replies. `effortsFor` and `turnEffort` are unchanged.

## CT-458 What a turn actually ran on (2026-10-19)

CR-07, CR-08. **`CompleteBody.ran`** (`TurnRanReport {model (null: the tool's default), effort (null: none sent), fast,
fastSkipped?}`), from runners of 0.96; older runners leave it out. **`FastSkippedReason`** (`FAST_SKIPPED_REASONS`:
`busy` — the fast tier's own limit or cooldown; `credits` — no usage credits on the Claude account, Codex: the plan's
usage; `org` — turned off for the Claude organization or ChatGPT workspace; `unavailable` — anything else). A model the
sign-in refused stays `modelFallback` (ME-05); in a Chat thread it doesn't touch the assistant's own (CR-08, the
server's to keep apart). Both live in `domain/models.ts` beside `ModelFallbackReport`: they are about any turn.

## CT-459 A choice of what answers (2026-10-19)

CR-02, CR-05. New `domain/chat-runtime.ts`. **`ChatProvider`** (`CHAT_PROVIDERS`: `claude`, `codex`) and **`ChatRuntime`**
`{provider, model? (ModelId), effort?, fast?}`, absent fields meaning the same as `AgentModelRuntime`'s. Pure helpers
clients share: **`chatRuntimeOf(runtime)`** (the assistant's runtime as a choice; null on ACP or scripted, so no button),
**`chatRuntimeWithProvider(runtime, provider)`** (another provider: model, effort and fast reset; the same provider changes
nothing), **`chatRuntimeWithModel(runtime, id, models)`** (the effort kept within the model's by `turnEffort`'s rule,
dropped for a model that takes none, automatic stays automatic; fast dropped when the model has none; a model the list
doesn't have keeps both), **`chatRuntimeEquals(a, b)`** (absent and null alike; field by field, so `{claude}` and
`{claude, model: 'opus'}` differ even when Opus is the default — CR-02's “equal choice is stored as null” compares with
`chatRuntimeOf` of the assistant's runtime). **`ChatThread.runtime`** (nullable, optional): the caller's choice; null
follows the assistant's own.

## CT-461 `chats.runtime`, `chats.setThreadRuntime`, `chats.start` `runtime` (2026-10-19)

CR-01…CR-05, CR-09. **`GET /burrows/:burrow/chats/runtime`** (`api.chats.runtime`), query **`ChatRuntimeQuery`**
`{thread? (MessageId)}` → **`ChatRuntimeView`** `{assistantId, assistantName (1–80), default (ChatRuntime | null),
thread? (ChatRuntime | null; absent: none asked), canSetDefault, providers (≤ 2 ChatRuntimeProvider)}`, where
**`ChatRuntimeProvider`** is `{provider, ready, models (ProviderModels), fastBlocked ('gateway' | null), usage
(ChatProviderUsage {usedPct 0–100, resetsAt | null} | null)}`. Operation safety `READ`. **`PUT
/burrows/:burrow/chats/threads/:rootId/runtime`** (`api.chats.setThreadRuntime`), body **`SetChatThreadRuntimeBody`**
`{runtime: ChatRuntime | null}` → **`ChatThreadRuntimeResponse`** `{thread: ChatRuntime | null}` (as stored: null when it
equals the assistant's own); `RECEIPT`, setting the same choice twice is harmless. A `PUT` under `/chats/threads/`: no
other route sits there. **`StartChatBody.runtime`** (optional): the top-level box's choice, stored with the new thread;
a runtime without the feature ignores it. These types sit in the domain module, not in `contracts/home.ts`, so the text
helpers (`chatUsageLine`) read them without importing contracts.

## CT-465 What answered, what switched, what was skipped (2026-10-19)

CR-07, CR-08. **`ranOnText(ranOn)`** (“Claude · Opus · High effort · Fast”). **`runSwitchText(prev, next)`**: null for the
first reply and when nothing asked for changed; else “Switched to ” and the parts — another provider by its label, else
another model by its label; another effort “High effort”; fast “fast replies on/off”, alone “Fast replies on/off”.
Decided here: it compares what each reply asked for — a reply with `fastSkipped` counts as fast, one with `modelSkipped`
as that model — so a skipped fast reply or model gives its own quiet line and no divider before it or after it; a model
change to a skipped model shows no model part. **`fastSkippedText(reason, provider)`** (busy, credits, org,
unavailable; Claude account / organization, ChatGPT plan / workspace) and **`modelSkippedText(asked, used)`** (“Fable
wasn’t available, so this one came from Opus.”).

## CT-470 A session sign-in: a token whose `auth` is `session` (2026-10-19)

John, 2026-10-19: “Implement group 1 and pi-hole + Nginx Proxy Manager + IMAP/SMTP + TrueNAS, ESPHome.” Whombat
`docs/decisions/connections-more.md` CM-01…CM-30 has the decisions; this is their contract. Pi-hole 6 and Nginx Proxy
Manager have no keys to paste, only a password that signs in for a session. No new sign-in kind (CM-10): **`TokenAuth`
gains `session`** `{login {method POST|PUT, path, body (string templates over {secret} and the fields)},
tokenJsonPath, expiresJsonPath?, ttlSeconds (60…86 400, default 1800), apply (SessionApply: bearer, a header template
over {token}, a query parameter), logout?, missing?}`, so `SignInKind`, `ConnectionView` and every older app's rows stay
as they are. `missing` is decided here: the check's words when the sign-in path answers 404 (“This Pi-hole is older than
version 6: update it, then connect it.”), next to `SocketSpec.missing`. **`tokenCredential`** answers null for it (the
server makes the credential, CM-11). Pure helpers for the server: **`fillLoginTemplate(entry, template, secret,
fields)`** (every string in an array or object, the secret put in last as `tokenCredential` does), **`sessionCredential
(apply, token)`**, **`sessionToken(auth, answer)`**, **`sessionExpiresAt(auth, answer, now)`** (seconds or an ISO time,
else the ttl; never past a day, never before now). **`tokenAuthProblem`** checks a session: `{secret}` in the sign-in,
known fields only, `{token}` in a header, no forbidden header.

## CT-471 A socket transport (2026-10-19)

CM-13, CM-15, CM-17. **`CONNECTION_TRANSPORTS` gains `socket`**; such an entry has **`CatalogEntry.socket`**
(**`SocketSpec`** `{dialect jsonrpc|esphome, path, login {method, params (JSON with templates), when always|asked} |
null, reads, streams, refused, missing}`, default null) and `request: null`. `missing` (asked for by the server stream)
is the check's sentence when the socket isn't there. **`CatalogCheck` gains `socket`** `{method, params?, version?}`:
`version` is a dotted path into the result (TrueNAS `system.info` → `version`); absent, the server takes a string
result, else `result.version`, else the dialect's first message (ESPHome's `esphome_version`). Constants
**`SOCKET_CONNECT_DEADLINE_MS`** (10 s), **`SOCKET_STREAM_SECONDS_DEFAULT`** (10) and **`SOCKET_STREAM_SECONDS_MAX`**
(25); the whole call keeps `CONNECTION_CALL_DEADLINE_MS`. An entry's token sign-in `auth` is not used by a socket (the
server sends no credential on the handshake; signing in is the `login` message): TrueNAS's bearer and ESPHome's basic
are placeholders the form still reads its labels from.

## CT-472 The `call` tool (2026-10-19)

CM-14, CM-16. **`SOCKET_TOOL_NAME = 'call'`**, input `{method, params?, seconds?}`. **`socketReads(entry, method)`**
(a whole-name match of `reads`, without case; never a refused one), **`socketStreams`**, **`socketRefused`** (also true
for an entry without a socket), **`socketRefusedText`**, **`hasSocketTool(entry, kind)`** and **`socketToolDef(entry,
baseUrl)`** (the tool's definition, stored and hashed like `request`'s; it lives in core because it is built only from
the entry; it names the streams, and leaves the reads, which are patterns, to the entry's guide). **`callAccess`** decides a `call` by its method; **`sensitiveReason`** asks for a socket method named for
deleting (`deletesByName`: `pool.dataset.delete`, `devices/delete`, `disk.wipe`) and applies an entry's rules on the
method with `tools: ['call'], arg: 'method'` as written; a read's argument rules are skipped as before.

## CT-473 Reads by a query parameter (2026-10-19)

CM-18. **`RequestSpec.queryReads`** (**`QueryRead`** `{name, values, writes}`, at most 4, default empty). Decided here:
`writes` sits on each rule (`{name, values}[]`), not beside `queryReads`, so SABnzbd's rule reads “`mode` is a read
mode unless `name` is `delete`, `pause` …”. A call that carries a rule's parameter reads only when every value of it is
one of `values` (compared exactly: `Queue` isn't `queue`) and none of that rule's `writes` holds (compared without case);
without any rule's parameter the method and read paths decide, as before. **`queryReadDecision(entry, query)`**;
**`isReadRequest`** takes the query as a fifth argument and **`callAccess`** passes the `request` call's `query`.

## CT-474 A url field's own rule (2026-10-19)

CM-05. **`fieldProblem` applies `validation` to `url` fields too**, after the address is usable (asked for by the
server stream): TrueNAS's field refuses `http://` — TrueNAS turns a key off when it is used over plain http. No other
url field has a rule, so nothing else changes.

## CT-475 A rule on a request's body (2026-10-19)

CM-03 asks for switching protection off on Pi-hole (`POST /api/dns/blocking {"blocking": false}`) and AdGuard Home
(`POST /control/protection {"enabled": false}`), not for switching it on, and for killing a Pterodactyl server
(`{"signal": "kill"}`), not for stopping it. `argValue` only sees strings, so **`SensitiveRule.body`** `{path, equals?}`
is added: the `request` call's JSON body (an object, or its JSON text) holds `equals` at that dotted path (a string
compared without case, a number, a boolean, null), or any value at all without `equals` (a Pi-hole config change that
touches `config.webserver`). Like `methods` and `path` it applies to `request` calls only, and `toolAlwaysAsks` doesn't
mark a tool for it.

## CT-476 Group 1: keys people paste (2026-10-19)

CM-01, CM-02, CM-03, CM-04, CM-30. Each entry checked against the vendor's current documentation and source on
2026-10-19 (the doc's own words, menus and paths; what a doc leaves open is in the guide). Every token sign-in has
numbered steps and, where the key has a shape, a paste pattern.

- **UniFi Access** (`unifi_access`, handle `access`, Home): bearer token from Access → Settings → General → Advanced →
  API Token, base `{url}` on port 12445 (its own self-signed certificate, `certificateField`), prefix
  `/api/v1/developer/`; the check reads `/doors` with `okJsonPath: 'data'` (a refusal can come back 200 with an error
  code); `POST /system/logs` and `/system/logs/export` read. Asks: unlocking, lock rules, lockdown and evacuation,
  people, visitors and credentials (cards, PINs, touch passes, which cost money to buy), policies, device settings,
  webhooks, deleting. Found by the 401 `CODE_UNAUTHORIZED` on 12445.
- **SABnzbd** (`sabnzbd`, Home): `apikey` query; `GET /api?mode=…` decided by `queryReads` (CT-473): the read modes,
  unless `name` is one of the queue, history, status and warnings actions. The check is `mode=queue` with
  `okJsonPath: 'queue'` (a wrong key answers 200 `{"status": false}`). Asks: deleting from the queue or history,
  shutting down or restarting, and reading or changing its settings (`get_config` shows its keys). `showlog` stays out of
  the reads (a download, and an admin call). Found by `mode=version` with SABnzbd's `Server: CherryPy`. The address help
  names SABnzbd's hostname check (an IP address, or `host_whitelist`).
- **NZBHydra2** (`nzbhydra`, Home): `apikey` query on the Newznab API (`t=` reads by `queryReads`; `t=get` downloads and
  counts against the indexers, so it is a write) and the external API of NZBHydra2 9 (`/externalapi/v1/`, a wrong key
  answers a bare 404); the check is `/externalapi/v1/ping` (`okJsonPath: 'version'`), so it needs NZBHydra2 9. Reading
  its log (which isn't anonymised) asks.
- **Plex** (`plex`, Home): sign in once first (CM-06; `secondFactor: 'asked'`, `serviceLimits: false`, stored as the
  `X-Plex-Token` header token), the token from View XML second (paste pattern for the 20-character token and the newer
  JWT); `Accept: application/json` on every request and the check. Prefixes: library, status, hubs, playlists, `/:/`,
  butler, activities, updater, identity (not `/security`, which makes tokens). Asks: deleting (Plex deletes the files),
  emptying a library's trash, the server's settings, installing an update. Found by `/identity` and its
  `X-Plex-Protocol` header.
- **Overseerr** (`overseerr`, Home; Jellyseerr and Seerr answer the same): `X-Api-Key` (it acts as the first admin;
  `X-Api-User` is allowed); asks for settings (also a new key), adding users and their permissions, deleting. Found by
  `/api/v1/status`'s `commitTag`.
- **Pterodactyl** (`pterodactyl`, Infrastructure): a `ptlc_` client key, `Accept: application/json` (without it the
  panel redirects to its login page). Asks: kill (`body.signal`), reinstall, restoring a backup, deleting files (a POST),
  backups, databases and schedules, a database's new password, sub-users, and the account's keys, email, password and
  two-step sign-in (`GET /account/two-factor` writes a new secret). Found by the panel's JSON 401 and its
  `SiteConfiguration` page.
- **Airtable** (`airtable`, Productivity, personal by default): a `pat…` token; `listRecords` POSTs read; deleting asks.
- **HubSpot** (`hubspot`, Business): a service key (HubSpot's replacement for private apps, which can't be made after
  2026-10-26; their `pat-` tokens work too); dated paths and `/crm/v3/` both under `/crm/`; search and batch reads read;
  asks for deleting, batch archives, GDPR deletes and merges.
- **Pipedrive** (`pipedrive`, Business): `x-api-token`; `/api/v2/` and `/v1/`; asks for deleting and merging (`PUT
  …/merge`).
- **Plausible** (`plausible`, Business): a Stats API key; `POST /api/v2/query` reads. Decided here: a **`site`** field
  (one site's domain), because nothing else proves a Stats key on both plausible.io and the community edition (the Sites
  API is Enterprise-only and absent from the community edition): the check is `GET
  /api/v1/stats/realtime/visitors?site_id={site}`. Deleting a site or a goal asks.

## CT-477 Pi-hole, AdGuard Home and Nginx Proxy Manager (2026-10-19)

CM-08. **Pi-hole** (`pihole`, Home): the app password signs in for a session (CT-470: `POST /api/auth`, `session.sid`
in `X-FTL-SID`, `session.validity`, `DELETE /api/auth` so its 16 seats don't fill up, and the too-old sentence for v5).
An app password can't change Pi-hole's settings unless `webserver.api.app_sudo` is on; the steps and the guide say so.
Asks: blocking off (`body.blocking` false; on is allowed), restoring a Teleporter backup, emptying logs, config changes
under `webserver` (passwords, the API), deleting (also `:batchDelete`). Found by `/api/auth`'s session answer, so only
Pi-hole 6 is found. **AdGuard Home** (`adguard`, Home): basic auth with the web username and password (no keys exist);
version, update checks, upstream tests and client search POSTs read. Asks: protection off (`body.enabled` false, also
`dns_config`'s `protection_enabled`), safe browsing or parental off, deleting (its removals are POSTs), clearing
statistics, the log or DHCP, access and TLS settings, updating. Found by its login page's colour and the 401 of
`/control/status`, on 80 and 3000. **Nginx Proxy Manager** (`nginx_proxy_manager`, handle `npm`, Infrastructure): email and
password for a token that lasts a day (`POST /api/tokens`, bearer, `expires`); the steps make a user for Whombat with
only its permissions and without two-step sign-in (the server says “Turn off two-step sign-in for the user Whombat signs
in as.” when the answer asks for a code). Prefixes leave `/api/tokens` out, so a refreshed token never reaches an agent;
`certificates/test-http` and `validate` read. Asks: users, permissions, passwords and two-step sign-in, signing in as
someone, deleting. Found by `/api/` on port 81.

## CT-478 TrueNAS and ESPHome (2026-10-19)

CM-05, CM-07, CM-16. **TrueNAS** (`truenas`, Infrastructure): JSON-RPC at `/api/current`, signed in with
`auth.login_with_api_key [key]` (it answers `false` for a refused key; TrueNAS marks it for removal in v27, and
`auth.login_ex` would also need the username, so it stays until then). The url field takes only `https://` (CT-474);
the certificate is pinned. Reads: every `*.query`, `*.get_instance` and `*.config` but certificates', SSH keychains' and
cloud credentials' (they hold private keys), plus `system.info` and the rest as listed; refused: `auth.*` except
`auth.me`, `core.subscribe`/`unsubscribe`/`set_options` (it would change how jobs answer)/`download`/`upload`,
`user.setup_local_administrator`, `system.debug`, `config.save`. Asks: exporting a pool or taking disks out, rolling
back, rebooting or shutting down, updates (`update.update` installs on 25.04 and only changes settings on 25.10; both
ask), users, groups, privileges and API keys, SSH (`ssh.update`, and any write naming `ssh`), certificates, private keys
and stored credentials, a dataset's encryption, `filesystem.*` writes, resetting the configuration, network interfaces;
deleting and wiping by name. Snapshots are `pool.snapshot.*` on 25.10 and `zfs.snapshot.*` on 25.04, both covered. Found
by `/api/versions`. **ESPHome** (`esphome`, Home): Device Builder's `/ws`, no sign-in or its username and password
(`auth/login` when the server's first message says `requires_auth`); reads, streams (`devices/logs`,
`devices/validate`, `firmware/follow_job`) and refused commands (logins, subscriptions, `firmware/follow_jobs`,
`devices/stop_stream` — a call has one socket — and the download tokens) from its `docs/API.md` and source. Asks:
flashing, renaming (it flashes again), deleting, resetting the build files, secrets and Wi-Fi credentials, restoring an
older version, reading a device's encryption key, updating, and anything naming `secrets.yaml`, also the read
`devices/get_config` (**`SensitiveRule.onReads`**, decided here: an `argValue` rule that asks for reads too). Found by
`/version` (the old dashboard answers it too; the check then says it is too old).

## CT-500 The host's package ops (2026-10-19)

John, 2026-10-19: “I want to be able to install software updates via Whombat on, for example, Proxmox or Debian, etc.”
Whombat `docs/decisions/server-updates.md` SWU-01…SWU-15 has the decisions; this is their contract.
**`HOST_MANAGE_OPS`** gains **`packages.check`** and **`packages.install`** at the end, and **`HostManagePlatform`**
gains **`host`** at the end (the server's own operating system), as 0.84 appended `libvirt` (CT-369). `host` widens the
enum `HostGuestConfig` and `HostChoices` also use; no runtime answers it there. **`HOST_PACKAGE_MANAGE_OPS`** and
**`isHostPackageManageOp`** name the two. `packages.install` takes **`params.packages?`**: **`HostPackageNames`**, 1 to
**`HOST_PACKAGES_MAX`** (200) names matching **`HOST_PACKAGE_NAME_PATTERN`** `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9+._:@~-]{0,127}$`;
left out, everything waiting. Decided here, as a refinement on **`HostManageRequest`** (it was a plain object): the
package ops take `platform: host` or none and never a `guestId`; `host` is refused on every other op but **`task.stop`**,
which stops a Check (`pkg:…`); `packages` only on Install, and an empty list is refused rather than meaning “all”.
**`packages.install` joins `HOST_MANAGE_DESTRUCTIVE_OPS`**, as `plugin.update` and `container.update` did (CT-365): it
has a `SERVERS_SENSITIVE` rule like them. Not in `HOST_SELF_GUEST_ALLOWED`: the ops are the server's, never a guest's.
**`HostPackageOp`** (`check` | `install`, `HOST_PACKAGE_OPS`) is the short name the report and the tool use.

## CT-501 The package task and the server's report (2026-10-19)

SWU-04, SWU-10. **`HostSystem.packageTask`** (**`HostPackageTask`** `{id, op, startedAt}` | null) while one runs, and
**`HostSystem.packageLast`** (**`HostPackageLast`** `{op, status ok|failed, finishedAt, installed (null for Check),
message (a failure's reason, or on ok SWU-06's one-sentence warning; null: none), code}` | null), both optional for
older hubs and agents. **`HostTask.packages?`** `{installed, keptBack, warning (null: none)}` once a package task ended
(`pkg:<16 hex>`, `platform: host`; Check `cancellable`, Install not). `hosts.getTask` and `task.stop` take
`platform: host` through `HostManagePlatform`; `hosts.manage`'s summary names the server's own updates.

## CT-502 Why a package task ended early (2026-10-19)

Asked for by stream H. **`HostTask.code?`** (a string, set only when a package task ended early) and
**`HostPackageLast.code`** (string | null): **`HOST_PACKAGE_TASK_CODES`** `busy` (the package lock still held after two
minutes) and `timeout` (past Check's 10 minutes or Install's 2 hours). Open strings on the wire, so a later code doesn't
break an older client; it shows the task's `message`.

and 0.84 (CT-368, CT-372): no new op id (`hosts.manage` and `hosts.getTask` carry the new ops), so no

## CT-504 Asking before installing updates (2026-10-19)

SWU-08, SWU-09 (asked for by stream S). **`serverAsksApply`** keeps the rules for **`server_update`** on the server this
Whombat runs on even when its Asks you first is Never, like `server_power` (SA-03): an upgrade there can restart
Whombat's own database. Its rule asks only for `install`, so Check never asks. **`HOST_ASKS_FIRST_WORDS`**: `hint.risky`
“Commands, power, updates, deleting and restoring wait for your yes.”, `selfNote` “It still asks before restarting,
shutting down or updating {server}, which runs this Whombat.”, and, decided here so the confirm stays true,
`confirmBody` “Whombat will run commands, install updates, restart guests and delete things on {server} without asking
you first. You can switch it back any time.”

## CT-505 The Servers tools for updates (2026-10-19)

SWU-08. `SERVERS_TOOLS` has **53**, the two before `server_add` (which stays last): read **`server_updates {server}`**
(the waiting updates: manager, counts, checked when, the error, restart needed and why, the packages with name, installed
and new version, security and source, at most 500; the running package task and the last result) and write
**`server_update {server, action check|install, packages?, reason}`** (`packages` as `HostPackageNames`: the pattern,
1 to 200 items, in its JSON schema). Its description says it installs as a task, never restarts the server, changes its
repositories or upgrades to a new release, and asks unless the server is set not to ask. Not `sensitive` whole: Check
never asks. **`SERVERS_SENSITIVE`** gains `{tools: ['server_update'], arg: 'action', argValue: '^install$', reason:
'Installing updates always asks'}`. The guide gains the updates paragraph (check, install, say plainly what changed,
offer a restart with `server_power`, one node of a cluster at a time, never a new major release). It was 1 435 of
`CONNECTION_GUIDE_MAX` 1 500, a wire limit older clients check, so instead of raising the limit the guide was tightened
to 1 477: the read-first and asking sentences say the same in fewer words (“Deleting, restoring or moving something, …”).

AU-03…AU-05, AU-07, AU-08. `HostServerSettings.agent.update` is named **`HostAgentUpdate`** and gains, all optional

## CT-512 Keep server agents up to date (2026-10-20)

AU-06. **`HostAgentSettings {autoUpdate, halted}`**, kept by the hosts service (on by default there):
**`hosts.agentSettings`** GET and **`hosts.updateAgentSettings`** PATCH (**`HostAgentSettingsPatch {autoUpdate}`**) at

## CT-513 Update the agent now (2026-10-20)

AU-05, AU-07, AU-08. **`hosts.updateAgent`** POST `/burrows/:burrow/hosts/servers/:serverId/agent/update`, no body,
owners: Update now, Try again and Update the agent. It answers **202** with **`HostAgentUpdateAccepted {state: updating |
installing}`** (`HOST_AGENT_UPDATE_STARTS`; `installing` is the one last install), decided here as `hosts.serverAction`
and `hosts.startInstall` do: the update goes on after the answer, and how it goes comes with the server's settings.
Refusals (`needs_install`, `update_running`) are the Whombat server's `conflict` with words, as other hosts refusals.

## CT-514 Their operation safety (2026-10-20)

`hosts.agentSettings` READ; **`hosts.updateAgentSettings`** NEVER, as `hosts.updateServer` (the hosts service keeps the
setting, outside the receipt); **`hosts.updateAgent`** NEVER, not destructive: it restarts the agent on the server (as
root for the last install) outside any receipt, so no client sends it again by itself, but it is neither irreversible
nor high-impact (the agent rolls back a version that doesn't come back), unlike `hosts.serverAction`. None is secret.

## CT-517 The desk screen's settings, and what Settings sees (2026-10-20)

John, 2026-10-20: “it would be awesome if we can actually do something with the screen when we have this on our desk.”
Whombat `docs/decisions/desk-display.md` DK-01…DK-15 has the decisions, `docs/implementation/desk-display/assignment.md`
§2 the shapes; this is their contract. Core `domain/desk.ts`: **`DeskLockedView`** (`time` · `summary` ·
`everything`), **`DeskNight`** (`dim` · `black`), **`DeskQuietHours {enabled, start, end}`** and **`DeskSettings
{lockedView, quietHours, night, voice}`** with Zod defaults (`summary`, 23:00–07:00 on, `dim`, on;
`DEFAULT_DESK_SETTINGS`), so a screen nobody paired and an older runtime's answer read the same. **`DeskSettingsPatch`**
is `desk.update`'s strict input, each member whole. **`DeskScreen {paired: {personId, name, pairedAt} | null, settings,
pairing: {expiresAt} | null, unlockRequest: {id, expiresAt} | null, hasDisplay, hasMicrophone, hasSpeaker, hasBattery,
voiceAvailable}`** is what Settings reads. **`DESK_PIN_RE`** is `^[0-9]{6}$`, not the brief's `^\d{6}$`: the same
digits (no `u` flag), written so the PIN crosses to Go (`DeskUnlockRequest`), where the subset refuses shorthand
classes. The numbers of DK-02 and DK-04 are constants (`DESK_PAIRING_TTL_S` 600, `DESK_TRIES` 5,
`DESK_UNLOCKED_IDLE_S` 120, `DESK_PHONE_UNLOCK_TTL_S` 120, `DESK_TALK_CONTINUE_S` 120) with **`deskTriesLeft`** and
**`deskPinBackoffS`** (none below five wrong PINs, then 60 s doubling with each further wrong PIN, at most 3 600 s), and
**`deskToneOf`** turns a person's tone into the screen's 1…5 (`HUMAN_TONES` order).

## CT-519 What the desk screen may answer (2026-10-20)

DK-05. **`deskMayDecide(approval, call?)`** → `{ok: true}` or `{ok: false, reason: DeskPhoneReason}`
(**`DESK_PHONE_REASONS`**: `vault`, `money`, `release`, `delete`, `keys`, `outside`). On the phone: `vault_use`
(vault); `refund` (money); `deploy`, `merge_pr`, `push_shared_branch` to `main`/`master` and `run_command` deploying,
reaching production, merging or pushing to main (release); `files_trash`, a destructive `run_command` and a
`connection_call` that deletes or destroys (delete); `grant_key` (keys); `message_external`, `mail_send`,
`calendar_invite`, `files_share` and an outside-messaging `run_command` (outside); and any ask whose key is a risk row
(`keyTierRowOf`) or one of `mail.send`, `calendar.invite`, `files.share` (outside), `files.delete` (delete),
`agents.manage` (keys). Every `run_command` category is consequential today, so no command is answered on the screen.
**`connectionCallDestroys(params, args?)`**: a tool named for deleting (`deletesByName`: `guest_delete`), a tool that
destroys whatever it's called with (`guest_template`), the server's words for the call (CT-347) saying it deletes or
restores over something, and — with the deferred call's arguments — a `DELETE` request, a socket method named for
deleting, or an `action` that deletes or restores (`guest_snapshot`, `guest_backup`, …). The approval's action has no
arguments (they stay with the deferred call, CX-21), so `deskMayDecide` takes them as an optional second argument
`{args}`, beyond §2's signature; without them a call is judged by its tool and words. Restoring counts as destroying:
it overwrites what is there. An ordinary call (`server_command`, “Restart Plex”), a new channel or a `custom` ask about
another key stays answerable.

## CT-523 The desk's session ops (2026-10-20)

DK-02, DK-04, DK-12. Session-native on the `app` channel, in `SESSION_SPECS`: **`desk.get`** `{}` → `DeskScreen`;
**`desk.startPairing`** `{}` → `{expiresAt}`; **`desk.pair`** `{code: ClaimLetters, pin: DeskPin}` → `DeskScreen`
and **`desk.setPin`** `{pin}` → `DeskScreen`, both secret (CT-44: a PIN never lands in a receipt); **`desk.update`**
(`DeskSettingsPatch`) → `DeskScreen`; **`desk.unpair`** `{}` → `DeskScreen`; **`desk.answerUnlock`** `{id, unlock}` →
`{ok: true}`. Who may call which (owners; the paired person) is the runtime's check, written on each op.
`SECRET_OPS` (`session.json`) names the two PIN ops.

## CT-524 Their operation safety (2026-10-20)

`desk.get` READ. `desk.startPairing` NEVER and `desk.answerUnlock` NEVER: the letters and the unlock live in the
runtime's memory, outside any receipt. `desk.pair` and `desk.setPin` NEVER (secret). **`desk.update` RECEIPT**, where the
brief said never: it is one commit (`update_desk`) and everything after it is a rebuild, so the table's rule
(mutations are `receipt` unless something acts outside the commit) makes it so, like `me.updatePreferences`.
**`desk.unpair` DESTRUCTIVE** (receipt): it takes the screen from its person, so a person decides.

and the console server connect, as the admin socket (MR-15). **`DESK_PATHS`**: `state` (GET → **`DeskState`**),
`unlock` (**`DeskUnlockRequest {v, pin}`** → **`DeskUnlockAnswer {v, result, triesLeft?, retryAt?}`**), `unlockPhone`
(**`DeskRequest {v}`** → **`DeskPhoneUnlockAnswer {v, expiresAt}`**), `lock` (`DeskRequest` → **`DeskAck {v}`**),
`touch` (`DeskRequest` → **`DeskTouchAnswer {v, until}`**), `decide` (**`DeskDecideRequest {v, number, decision}`** →
`DeskAck`), `talk` (**`DeskTalkRequest`** → **`DeskTalkStarted {v, id}`**), `talkGet` and `talkAudio`
(**`DeskTalkRef {v, id}`** → **`DeskTalk`**, or `audio/wav`). The brief's anonymous `{v:1}` bodies got names: one
`DeskRequest` for the three bodiless calls, one `DeskAck`, one `DeskTalkRef`. `talk/get` answers `DeskTalk` itself
(without `v`), as the brief has it, the same shape as `DeskState.talk`. `DeskState {v, now, paired, pairing, lock,
glance, power, talk}` and its parts (`DeskPaired`, `DeskPerson`, `DeskAssistant`, `DeskPairing`, `DeskLock`,
`DeskGlance`, `DeskStatus`, `DeskNeedsYou`, `DeskAsk`, `DeskWorking`, `DeskStep`, `DeskDone`, `DeskServer`,
`DeskMeter`, `DeskTile`, `DeskPower`) are §2.3's, with these refinements: `DeskServer.note` may be empty; `DeskMeter.value`
is a whole number −100…1 000; `mark` is a lower-case slug (`DeskMark`); `DeskAsk.number` 1…10⁹; counts 0…10⁶.
**`DeskPower`** has `HostPower`'s shape as its own schema, so Go has `local.DeskPower` (registering `HostPower` under a
local name would make Go `protocol` import `local`). Limits: **`DESK_REQUEST_MAX_BYTES`** 1 KiB,
**`DESK_TALK_REQUEST_MAX_BYTES`** 1.5 MiB, **`DESK_STATE_MAX_BYTES`** 64 KiB. Errors: `LocalError` with
**`DESK_SOCKET_ERRORS`** (`bad_request`, `too_large`, `not_paired`, `locked`, `on_phone`, `not_found`, `decided`,
`backoff`, `busy`, `voice_unavailable`, `bad_audio`).

## CT-529 Display text on the desk (2026-10-20)

The desk shows people's words — names, titles, the status, an ask, tile values, a question and its answer — so its
text is any script on one line, not CT-23's ASCII: **`DESK_TEXT_RES`**, `^(?:[^\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Cs}\p{Z}]| ){min,max}$`
with flag `u` at the twelve lengths the desk uses (2 … 600 code points), the push previews' form (CT-286) and
`ConsoleDisplayText`'s categories (CT-116), admitted into the cross-language subset by name (`UNICODE_PATTERNS`).
**`deskTextSchema(max, min?)`** builds a member from them (an unknown length throws). A no-break space is a separator,
so `deskText` turns it into a space. RE2 takes the 600 (its limit is 1 000); `desk_test.go` checks Unicode, line
breaks, invisible characters and code point lengths in Go.

## CT-535 The command a connection call runs, on the desk (2026-10-20)

DK-05; a verified review finding on 0.100.0 (high). `deskMayDecide` and `connectionCallDestroys` never read the shell
command a connection call runs, so a Servers `server_command` whose deferred arguments were `{command: "rm -rf
/srv/backups"}` or `"git push origin main"` was `{ok: true}`: the screen could approve what DK-05 keeps on the phone.
Now, when the deferred call's arguments carry a string `command` (`server_command`'s, and any other connection tool's
that runs one), `deskMayDecide` reads it as running on the server, in two steps.

**Deleting first, the desk's own reading.** The guard's `destructive` is narrow on purpose (an agent's computer is
disposable, AC-40), so the desk reads the command's simple commands itself — through `sudo`, `env`, `timeout`,
`xargs`, after `&&`, inside `bash -c`, an ssh remote command or `$(…)` — and keeps on the phone as **`delete`** any of:
`rm`, `rmdir`, `shred`, `unlink`, `truncate`; `find … -delete` or `-exec rm`; `dd of=…`; `mkfs*`, `wipefs`, `sgdisk`,
`sfdisk`, `fdisk`, `parted` (any use); `zfs destroy|rollback`, `zpool destroy|labelclear`; `lvremove`, `vgremove`,
`pvremove`; `btrfs subvolume delete` (and its prefixes, `btrfs sub del`); `docker|podman rm|rmi` and `container|image|
volume|network|system rm|prune`; compose (`docker compose`, `docker-compose`, `podman-compose`) `rm`, or `down` with
`-v`, `--volumes` or `--rmi`; `kubectl delete`; `helm uninstall` (and its aliases); `pct destroy`, `qm destroy`;
`virsh undefine`; `incus|lxc … delete` (also `snapshot delete`, `storage volume delete`); `pvesm free`; `psql`, `mysql`
or `mariadb` with DROP or TRUNCATE anywhere in the command (a pipe into the client too); `redis-cli` with FLUSHALL or
FLUSHDB; and a redirection that writes a file over (`>`, `>|`, `>&` with a file, `&>`; not `>>`, a file descriptor,
`/dev/null`, `/dev/zero` or a standard stream). Deleting is named first: whatever else the command does, it is what
can't be undone, so `kubectl delete` and `helm uninstall` say “It deletes something.”, not the guard's `deploy`.
`docker restart|ps|logs`, `systemctl restart|status`, `journalctl`, `apt list`, `df`, `du`, `docker run --rm …`,
`find` without `-delete`, an append and `> /dev/null` stay answerable.

**Then the guard's reading.** **`classifyCommand`** with the new **`ClassifyContext.runsOn?: string | null`**: the
machine the command runs on, read as ssh's remote command there — its destructive commands count, and a `runsOn` naming
a production server of the context is `deploy_production`. Absent, null or blank is the agent's own computer, so every
existing caller reads as before (tested against the ssh reading). The desk passes the server the call names
(`params.server.name`, else `args.server`) and no production servers (it doesn't know them, and every category already
stays on the phone), and maps the category as for `run_command`: `destructive` → `delete`, `message_external` →
`outside`, `deploy`, `deploy_production`, `merge` and `push_main` → `release` (`git push origin main`, `gh pr merge`,
`kubectl apply`, `sendmail`).

The simple commands come from the classifier's own reader, exported as **`shellSimpleCommands(command):
ShellSimpleCommand[]`** (`{name, args, stdin, truncates}`; `@whombat/core/computer`) so the two readings split a
command the same way; the classifier's tokenizer now keeps the files a truncating redirection writes over, which
`classifyCommand` ignores (its results are unchanged, the classifier tests pass as they were). The list lives in the
desk (`desk.ts`), not in the classifier: a stricter rule for a screen anyone at the desk can touch, not for the guard.
**Fail closed:** a `server_command` whose arguments the caller couldn't give (none, or no string `command`) stays on
the phone as **`delete`**: the screen can't rule out a command that deletes, the likeliest harm of an unread command
run as root, and “It deletes something.” says that more honestly than `release` or `outside`; a new `DeskPhoneReason`
would not be a patch (it crosses to Go and the console page). Other tools without a `command` are judged by their tool,
words and arguments as before (`connectionCallDestroys` unchanged).

## CT-536 Whose screen it is (2026-10-20)

A verified review finding on 0.100.0 (medium). `DeskScreen.paired.personId` is the paired person's principal in the
burrow the screen was paired in, while a session is an account's (`welcome.principal`, a principal per burrow), so a
client looking from another burrow couldn't tell the screen is its own. **`DeskScreen.paired.you?: boolean`**: the
session's account is the paired account. Optional, for runtimes before 0.100.1: clients use `you` and, when it is
absent, compare `personId` with the account's principals (`welcome.principal.principals`). An older client strips it.

## CT-538 What the screen is (2026-10-20)

John, 2026-10-20: “When we install a Whombat appliance I want the appliance to detect if it has a real monitor and
automatically pair the monitor if it has one. … the default should be that the monitor works immediately.” Whombat
`docs/decisions/desk-display.md` DK-16…DK-25 has the decisions, `docs/implementation/desk-display/auto-pair.md` §2 the
shapes; this is their contract. DK-16. Core **`DeskDisplay {connected, real, builtIn, name}`**: `connected` is today's
`DeskScreen.hasDisplay` (a DRM connector reads `connected`); `real` a monitor or a laptop's own panel — connected, not a
virtual machine's driver, an EDID whose maker isn't a virtual display's; `builtIn` an eDP, LVDS or DSI panel; `name` the
EDID's monitor name (1…60, plain text: Settings shows it, the screen doesn't) or null. **`DeskScreen.display?`**:
absent from runtimes before 0.101. `hasDisplay` stays.

## CT-540 Turning the screen on and off (2026-10-20)

DK-20. **`desk.setScreen {on: boolean}`** → `DeskScreen` (owners), session-native on the `app` channel, strict input.
On pairs the screen to the caller without letters or a PIN when a screen is connected (a VM's too: they asked), else
`no_screen` (CT-541); off ends the pairing and its PIN, and nothing pairs itself while it is off. **DESTRUCTIVE**
(receipt), as `desk.unpair`: off takes the screen and its PIN from its person, so a person decides; on is one commit.
Not secret: no PIN crosses. **`desk.unpair`** keeps its shape and now means `desk.setScreen {on: false}` (its doc
comment), so an older app's Unpair turns the screen off instead of being undone by the screen pairing itself a minute
later. *Pair to me instead* is `desk.startPairing` and `desk.pair` as before.

## CT-546 `deskBox`: This Whombat from the manager's measurements (2026-10-20)

DK-22, DK-24. Core **`deskBox(input: DeskBoxInput): DeskBoxPanel`**, pure. **Where the type lives:** core is the base
package (control-contracts imports it, never the other way), so core has the TypeScript shape `DeskBoxPanel` (with
`DeskBoxFigure` and `DeskBoxTone`) and control-contracts the Zod `DeskBox` that builds on it; `desk.test.ts` there
assigns `deskBox(…)` to `DeskBox` (typecheck) and checks `DeskBox.parse(deskBox(…))` at its widest (every figure at its
longest, an empty series). **`DeskBoxInput`** is structural — `now {cpuPermille, cores, memoryTotalBytes,
memoryUsedBytes, cpuTempC?, uptimeS?}`, `disks.data {totalBytes, usedBytes, freeBytes, parts}`, `series {stepS,
points}` — so the manager's `HostMetrics` (range `hour`) is one as it is, without core importing protocol.

- **The hour.** `deskBox` downsamples itself: points of `round(60 / stepS)` steps (6 for the manager's 10 s), aligned
  to end with the last point, each the mean of what was measured in it (null when nothing was), at most
  `DESK_BOX_POINTS` (60) and never more than an hour; a step of a minute or more stays as it is (300 s: 12 points).
  It is **always the whole hour**, padded with nulls before measuring began, so the chart's time axis (“1 h ago” …
  “now”) doesn't move on a box that started 5 minutes ago. Processor percent is `cpuPermille / 10`, memory the mean
  used bytes over `now.memoryTotalBytes`, both whole.
- **Sizes** as Settings → “How it’s doing” (**`formatBytes`**, decimal: “11.2 GB”, “812 GB”, “1.6 TB”; one decimal
  under 100 GB, whole KB and MB), split at its no-break space by **`deskBoxFigure`** (“812” “GB”) or with a plain space
  by **`deskBoxSize`** (“937 GB”). **Memory** as computers count it (the lead, 2026-10-20): **`deskMemoryFigure`**
  writes GiB as “GB” (“11.2” “GB”, MB below 1 GiB) and **`deskMemoryTotal`** rounds `MemTotal` up to the size the
  machine was sold as when it is within 10 % of it (62.6 GiB → “64 GB”), else as the figure (a VM given 10 GiB: “10 GB”).
  *Why:* a decimal `MemTotal` made a 64 GB machine read “68.7 GB”, and the kernel's share made a binary one “62.6 GB”;
  people know their machine by the size it was sold as.
- **Rates**, new: **`formatDeskRate(bytesPerSecond)`** — “0 B/s”, “850 B/s”, “310 kB/s”, “2.4 MB/s”: decimal, SI
  `kB` as the mockup writes it, one decimal under 100 (none when .0) and none from 100, whole bytes. Not
  `formatBytes`'s whole KB and MB: a rate under 10 MB/s needs its decimal. The network is the last point's in and out
  bytes over its step; null when the series is empty or its last step wasn't measured (an old rate shown as now would
  mislead).
- **Uptime**, new: **`formatDeskUptime(seconds)`** — “up 12 min”, “up 2 h 14 min”, “up 5 h”, “up 41 d”: the desk's
  server cards' note (`uptimeNote` in Whombat `desk/glance.ts`: “up 41 d”, one unit from a day) with the minutes under
  a day, as §2 and the mockup write it (`formatPowerLeft`'s form). Plain spaces (CT-529). Empty `up` without `uptimeS`.
- **Storage** percent is used ÷ (used + free) as `df` and “How it’s doing” count it (`hostDiskUsedPct`). The parts:
  **`whombat`** = the manager's `whombat` + `database` (the Whombat's own data, its conversations and history),
  **`agents`** = `computers` + `work` (the agents' computers and their work folders, BS-02); a part shows when any of
  its sources was measured, none when `parts` is null; each part's percent of used + free, whole.
- **Tones** (**`DESK_BOX_TONES`**), compared with the number the panel shows (rounded) so the colour always fits it:
  processor warn ≥ 75, bad ≥ 90 and memory warn ≥ 80, bad ≥ 90 — DK-24's “as the server cards”, read as the **desk's
  own server cards** (`deskServer`'s meters in Whombat `desk/glance.ts`), the cards this panel stands in for on the same
  screen, not the app's dashboard tiles (80/95, 85/95); storage warn ≥ 85, bad ≥ 95 (`HOST_DISK_ALERT_LEVELS`, BS-09,
  tested equal); temperature warn ≥ 80, bad ≥ 90 °C (DK-24). The runtime may move `deskServer` onto these constants.
