## CT-550 Release ids after PI-23 in the version vectors (2026-10-20; unreleased)

The appliance names its releases `whombat-YYYYMMDD.N` and `whombat-dev-YYYYMMDD.N` (appliance PI-23; were
`pve-…`). Host versions are those ids, ordered by `compareVersions`; nothing in it changes: the part before the first
`-` compares as text and `whombat` sorts after `pve`, so every box takes the new ids as newer. Three vectors pin that in
both languages (`host: whombat- after pve-, whatever the day`, its dev twin, and counter 10 after 9 in the new family),
and the doc comment names both forms. No package version changes: no consumer needs it before the next release, which
carries it.


## CT-560 Display text in the hardware report and the network (2026-10-20)

John, 2026-10-20: “I installed a whombat appliance and the mic is not working, also WiFi is not working by default. Is
there a way to implement better hardware support, including WiFi?” Whombat `docs/decisions/hardware-support.md`
HD-01…HD-11 has the decisions, `docs/implementation/hardware-support/assignment.md` §2.1–2.5 the shapes; this is their
contract. Device names, vendors, models, interface names, SSIDs and the kernel's lines are what the machine says, in any
script, so they are display text: **`HOST_TEXT_RES`** (`@whombat/protocol/session`, `session/hardware.ts`), the desk's
form `^(?:[^\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Cs}\p{Z}]| ){min,max}$` (flag `u`, CT-529) at the lengths the report uses (1…15, 1…32, 1…64,
1…80, 0…120, 1…120, 1…240 code points), admitted into the cross-language subset by name (`UNICODE_PATTERNS`).
**`hostTextSchema(max, min?)`** builds a member (an unknown length throws). They live in `protocol` rather than reusing
`DESK_TEXT_RES` because `@whombat/control-contracts/local` imports `protocol`, not the other way round. Producers clean
rather than fail: **`hostText(text, max)`** (Go **`local.HostText`**, the same steps as core's `deskText`: separators and
white space become one space, control and format characters go, trimmed, cut with `…`; Go also drops bytes that aren't
UTF-8), checked against each other by `local.json` → `hostTexts`. **`InterfaceName`** is display text of 1…15 code
points, as §2 says, not `HostNow.uplink`'s ASCII pattern (a superset of it: Linux names never hold a space).

## CT-561 The hardware report (2026-10-20)

HD-01, HD-03. **`HostHardware {collectedAt, kernel (1…64), machine, cpu, memoryBytes, devices ≤ 256, log ≤ 40 (each
1…240)}`** with **`HardwareMachine {vendor?, model?, family?, firmware?, virtual, hypervisor?}`**, **`HardwareCpu {model,
cores 1…4 096, threads 1…4 096}`** and **`HardwareDevice {kind, name (1…120), vendor?, bus, id?, driver (≤ 64) | null,
status, interface?, link?, speedMbps?, capture?, playback?, card?, connected?, sizeBytes?}`**; enums **`HardwareKind`**
(`HARDWARE_KINDS`), **`HardwareStatus`** (`ok`, `no_driver`, `no_firmware`, `disabled`), **`HardwareBus`** (`pci`, `usb`,
`platform`, `virtual`) and **`HardwareLink`** (`up`, `down`). §2.1's shape, with these refinements: the inline machine and
processor got names (Go needs them); `cpu.model` may be empty (an ARM machine that doesn't say), since a word in its
place would be the producer's (HD-11); `cores` and `threads` start at 1 like `HostNow.cores`; `speedMbps` is at most
10 000 000. `HOST_HARDWARE_DEVICES_MAX`, `HOST_HARDWARE_LOG_MAX`, `HOST_HARDWARE_LOG_LINE_MAX`. No serial numbers and no
MAC addresses: there is no member for either, and an answer that carried one is stripped (`z.object`, tested on both).

HD-03. **`hardwareProblems(h)`** → `HardwareProblem {kind, name, status}[]`: the devices whose status isn't `ok`,
**`HARDWARE_PROBLEM_KINDS`** (`wifi`, `wired`, `sound`, `graphics`) first in that order, then the rest, each kind in the
report's order. TypeScript only: the app and the phone list them; the words stay theirs (HD-11).

## CT-563 `host.hardware` (2026-10-20)

Session-native on the `app` channel, owners (the runtime's check): **`HostHardwareInput {}`** → **`HostHardwareOutput
{hardware: HostHardware | null, reason?: not_managed | unavailable}`**, `host.metrics`'s meaning (`not_managed`: no
manager; `unavailable`: it didn't answer or is too old). `reason` is optional as §2.3 has it; `host.metrics` keeps its
nullable one.

## CT-564 A network's name and its password (2026-10-20)

HD-05. **`Ssid`** is display text of 1…32 code points (`SSID_RE`, from `HOST_TEXT_RES`). §2.2's “1…32 bytes UTF-8” can't be
one cross-language pattern (a pattern counts code points), so **`ssidValid(s)`** (Go **`local.SsidValid`**, constant
**`SsidMaxBytes`**) checks the pattern and **`SSID_MAX_BYTES`** (32) bytes; `host.wifi.join`'s input refines its `ssid` with
it, and the manager answers 400 `bad_request` to a join or a forget whose name fails it. Producers leave networks whose
name isn't displayable out of every list (a name with a zero-width joiner or a no-break space among them). Vectors:
`local.json` → `ssids`. **`WifiPassphrase`**: `^([\x20-\x7e]{8,63}|[0-9A-Fa-f]{64})$`, a secret wherever it goes.
**`NetworkChangeId`** `^c-[a-z0-9]{8,32}$`.

## CT-565 The networks around the box (2026-10-20)

**`WifiSecurity`** (`open`, `psk` for WPA2/WPA3 Personal, `enterprise`, `other` for WEP and the like), **`WifiSignal`**
0…4 and **`wifiSignalFromDbm(dbm)`** (Go **`local.WifiSignalFromDBm`**, §2.2's thresholds; `local.json` → `wifiSignals`),
**`WifiNetwork {ssid, security, signal, saved, connected}`**, **`WifiScan {networks ≤ 64, strongest first, scannedAt}`**.
Hidden networks aren't in a scan; they are joined by name.

## CT-566 How the box is connected (2026-10-20)

HD-05, HD-10. **`HostNetwork {online, checkedAt | null, wired ≤ 8, wifi | null, wifiMissing?, change | null}`** with
**`HostWired {interface, connected, address?}`**, **`HostWifi {interface, state, ssid?, signal?, address?, saved ≤ 32}`**,
**`WifiSaved {ssid, security}`**, **`WifiState`** (`disconnected`, `connecting`, `connected`), **`WifiMissing`**
(`no_adapter`, `no_driver`, `disabled`). §2.2's inline parts got names. An address is **`IpAddress`**, IPv4 or IPv6
without a prefix length (ASCII, ≤ 45). **`hostNetworkValid(n)`** (Go **`local.HostNetworkValid`**) checks what one schema
can't: `wifiMissing` only without `wifi`; `ssid` exactly while connecting or connected, `signal` and `address` only while
connected; a consistent change. Vectors: `local.json` → `hostNetworks`.

## CT-567 A guarded change (2026-10-20)

HD-06, MG-15. **`NetworkChange {id, kind, ssid, phase, deadline, previous?, failure?}`**, **`NetworkChangeKind`** (`join`,
`forget`), **`NetworkChangePhase`** (`applying`, `confirming`, `committed`, `reverting`, `reverted`, `failed`;
**`networkChangeDone`**: the last three) and **`NetworkChangeFailure`** (`wrong_password`, `not_found`, `no_address`,
`no_internet`, `failed`). Refinements of §2.2: the phase is a new enum, not local's `NetworkPhase`: that one stays the
wired guard's as it is (no `failed`; §2.4 keeps `networkCandidates`/`networkStatus` unchanged) and `protocol` can't import
`local`; **`previous`** is optional and never null (the subset has no optional-nullable): absent when the box used no
Wi-Fi network before; **`failure`** exactly in `reverting`, `reverted` and `failed` (**`networkChangeValid`**, Go
**`local.NetworkChangeValid`**; `local.json` → `networkChanges`), so “Joined Home, but Whombat couldn’t reach the internet
there, so it went back to Office.” is `reverted` + `no_internet` + `previous: Office`.

## CT-568 The network's session ops (2026-10-20)

HD-06. Session-native on the `app` channel, owners: **`host.network`** `{}` → **`HostNetworkOutput {network | null,
reason?: not_managed | unavailable}`**; **`host.wifi.scan`** `{}` → **`HostWifiScanOutput {scan | null, reason?:
not_managed | unavailable | no_wifi}`**; **`host.wifi.join`** **`HostWifiJoinInput {ssid, passphrase?, hidden?}`** →
**`HostWifiChangeOutput {change}`**, secret (CT-44: the passphrase never lands in a receipt; `SECRET_OPS` in
`session.json`); **`host.wifi.forget`** **`HostWifiForgetInput {ssid}`** → `HostWifiChangeOutput`. Inputs are strict.
No realtime event: the app polls `host.network` every 2 s while a change runs. On a runtime without a manager neither
feature is advertised, so a client never sends the changes there (the runtime refuses them `not_allowed`).

## CT-569 Their refusals (2026-10-20)

**`WIFI_ERROR_CODES`** in `error.details.code` (**`WifiErrorDetails {code}`**) on **`WIFI_ERROR_STATUS`**'s generic code:
`no_wifi` (`not_allowed`), `busy` (`conflict`), `in_use` (`conflict`), `not_saved` (`not_found`), `invalid_passphrase`
(`validation_failed`). `in_use` existed (the hosts service's; its description now names the Wi-Fi too); `no_wifi`,
`busy`, `not_saved` and `invalid_passphrase` are new in `APP_ERROR_CODES`. A non-owner gets the generic `forbidden`.
The same codes are the manager's and the desk's `LocalError` codes (Go **`local.WifiError*`**). A wrong password is no
refusal: the change fails with `wrong_password`.

## CT-570 Their operation safety (2026-10-20)

`host.hardware`, `host.network` and `host.wifi.scan` READ. **`host.wifi.join`** and **`host.wifi.forget`** NEVER, not
destructive: they act on the box (iwd's networks, through the manager) outside any receipt, and the join is secret, but
the guard undoes a join that cuts the box off and a forgotten network can be joined again.

## CT-571 Wi-Fi in the audit log (2026-10-20)

Asked for by stream S so Wi-Fi changes can be audited. **`APPLIANCE_EVENT_TYPES`** gains **`network.wifi_joined`** (a join
that committed) and **`network.wifi_forgotten`**, payload **`NetworkAuditPayload {ssid, via: app | screen, changeId}`**
(`NETWORK_AUDIT_VIA`). Never a passphrase: the schema strips any other member, so a writer that parses before writing
can't carry one (tested). No vectors: appliance events have none.

Network only on runtimes that advertise them (managed runtimes). **`SESSION_API_LEVEL` 40** (window 38…41), as the
brief for this release asked, following CT-284: by the precedent of CT-467, CT-515 and CT-526 (new ops behind a feature,

## CT-573 The manager's hardware and network routes (2026-10-20)

`@whombat/control-contracts/local`, cross-language; the runtime's uid only, as every manager route. **`MANAGER_PATHS`**
(Go `ManagerPath*`): `hostHardware` `POST /v1/host/hardware` (**`HostHardwareRequest {v}`** → **`HostHardwareResponse {v,
hardware}`**), `networkState` `POST /v1/network/state` (**`NetworkStateRequest {v}`** → **`NetworkStateResponse {v,
network}`**), `wifiScan` `POST /v1/network/wifi/scan` (**`WifiScanRequest {v}`** → **`WifiScanResponse {v, scan}`**, at most
10 s for a fresh scan), `wifiJoin` `POST /v1/network/wifi/join` (**`WifiJoinRequest {v, ssid, passphrase?, hidden?,
confirmTimeoutSec 30…600}`** → 202 **`WifiChangeResponse {v, change}`**), `wifiForget` `POST /v1/network/wifi/forget`
(**`WifiForgetRequest {v, ssid}`** → 202 `WifiChangeResponse`). The brief's anonymous `{v}` bodies got a name each.
Errors are `LocalError` with `WIFI_ERROR_CODES`: 409 `no_wifi`, `busy`, `in_use`, 404 `not_saved`, 400
`invalid_passphrase` (and `bad_request`, 503 `unavailable`); an older manager answers 404, which the runtime reports as
`unavailable`. The wired `networkCandidates` and `networkStatus` stay as they are; a `wl*` interface stays refused by
`NetworkCandidate` (schema cases `wlan0` and `wlp194s0`): Wi-Fi has its own shapes.

## CT-574 The network on the desk socket (2026-10-20)

HD-07. **`DESK_PATHS`** (Go `DeskPath*`) gains `network` `GET /v1/desk/network` (**`DeskNetworkAnswer {v, network,
mayChange, why?: locked}`**, **`DeskNetworkWhy`**), `wifiScan` `POST /v1/desk/network/wifi/scan` (`DeskRequest` →
**`DeskWifiScanAnswer {v, scan}`**), `wifiJoin` (**`DeskWifiJoinRequest {v, ssid, passphrase?, hidden?}`** →
**`DeskWifiChangeAnswer {v, change}`**) and `wifiForget` (**`DeskWifiForgetRequest {v, ssid}`** → `DeskWifiChangeAnswer`).
`mayChange`: the box isn't claimed, or `network.online` is false, or the screen is unlocked; `why` exactly when it is
false (the runtime's rule; no helper, the console only shows it). Join and forget when it is false: 409 `locked`. Scans
work whenever `network` answers, on an unpaired screen too. The runtime adds the guard's confirm time; the screen can't
choose it. **`DESK_SOCKET_ERRORS`** gains `no_wifi`, `in_use`, `not_saved`, `invalid_passphrase` and `unavailable`
(`busy` and `locked` were there).

## CT-590 A PIN of 4 to 6 digits (2026-10-20)

John, 2026-10-20: “Allow a four-digit PIN at the appliance monitor. Also, can we detect if the user is present? …
Use the camera for this.” Whombat `docs/decisions/desk-display.md` DK-26…DK-35 has the decisions,
`docs/implementation/desk-display/presence.md` §2 the shapes; this is their contract. DK-26. Core **`DESK_PIN_MIN`** (4),
**`DESK_PIN_MAX`** (6), **`DESK_PIN_RE`** `^[0-9]{4,6}$` (was `^[0-9]{6}$`; ASCII digits written out, CT-529) and
**`DeskPinDigits`** (`int`, 4…6). `desk.pair`'s and `desk.setPin`'s `pin` (`DeskPin`) and the desk socket's
`DeskUnlockRequest.pin` follow the pattern, so 4, 5 and 6 digits pass and 3, 7 and other scripts' digits don't (schema
cases in both languages). PINs chosen before are six digits and stay valid. Go gets **`local.DeskPinMin`** and
**`DeskPinMax`** beside the desk's other constants, so the console's Go server needs no number of its own.

## CT-591 PINs too easy to guess (2026-10-20)

DK-27. Core **`deskPinTooEasy(pin)`**, pure: one digit repeated (0000, 11111); a run where each digit is one more, or
each one less, than the one before, **9 and 0 next to each other** read as a step either way (1234, 7890, 8901, 4321,
0987, 123456); **a pair or three digits repeated**. The brief's examples (1212, 6969, 123123) leave five digits and a
partial repeat open; decided: the PIN has the same digit every 2 (or every 3) places throughout, and the block fits
**at least twice** — so 12121 and 121212 are too easy (a pair repeated, five or six digits), 123123 is, and 1231 or
12312 aren't (three digits that don't fit twice are just a PIN). Anything that isn't a PIN (`DESK_PIN_RE`) answers
false: the schema refuses it, this judges only how guessable a PIN is. The schema doesn't refuse easy PINs (PINs
chosen before stay, DK-27); the runtime does with `easy_pin` (CT-594) and Settings before it sends anything. TypeScript
only: the console never chooses a PIN, it only types one.

## CT-592 Stay unlocked while you're here (2026-10-20)

DK-28…DK-30. **`DeskSettings.presence`** (`boolean`, default false: off until the paired person turns it on; an older
runtime's settings read as off), **`DEFAULT_DESK_SETTINGS.presence`** false, **`DeskSettingsPatch.presence?`**, so
`desk.update {presence}` turns it on and off. The timing as constants, the runtime's to apply: **`DESK_PRESENCE_GONE_S`**
30 (locks this long after the last face or touch, once a face was seen since this unlock), **`DESK_PRESENCE_MAX_S`**
14 400 (at most 4 hours unlocked in a row this way) and **`DESK_PRESENCE_CHECK_S`** 2 (the runtime asks the presence
service this often while it wants the camera). DK-04's `DESK_UNLOCKED_IDLE_S` stays the rule until a face is seen and
whenever the camera can't tell. A face never unlocks (DK-29): nothing in the contract lets one.

## CT-593 Where the camera works, and the words (2026-10-20)

DK-28, DK-30, DK-31. **`DeskScreen.presenceAvailable?`**: the presence service answers and has a camera it can read
(`PresenceHealth.camera && detector`), so Settings shows the switch; absent from runtimes before 0.103, where a client
shows no presence row. **`DESK_WORDS`** gains §2's keys and words exactly: `unlockedHere` (“Unlocked as {name} · stays
unlocked while you’re here”, the lock chip while the camera sees someone), `cameraOn` (the camera mark's label and
title), `settings.presence`, `settings.presenceHint`, `errors.easy_pin`; `settings.choosePin` is now “Choose a PIN of 4
to 6 digits” (was “Choose a 6-digit PIN”). No new hole. The console page copies the words (CG-40).

## CT-594 The refusal of an easy PIN (2026-10-20)

DK-27. **`DESK_ERROR_CODES`** gains **`easy_pin`** on **`validation_failed`** (`DESK_ERROR_STATUS`): the PIN is
well-formed and Whombat won't take it, as `invalid_passphrase` (CT-569) and the backup file's `password_too_short` are
mapped; `bad_request` is for what the schema refuses, `not_allowed` for what the caller may not do. In `APP_ERROR_CODES`
and `DESK_WORDS.errors` (“That PIN is too easy to guess. Choose another.”). The runtime refuses in `desk.pair` before the
letters are used up, and in `desk.setPin`. Not a desk socket code: unlocking never judges a PIN.

## CT-595 The PIN's length on the desk socket (2026-10-20)

DK-26, DK-34. **`DeskPaired.pinDigits?`** (`DeskPinDigits`, Go `*int64`): the pad shows that many dots and unlocks at
the last; absent means 6 (a PIN from before, or an older runtime), and the runtime leaves it out while there is no PIN
(`hasPin: false`). An older console strips it and draws six dots: a shorter PIN can't be typed there until the box's
candidate brings the new console with the runtime (DK-34). **`DeskUnlockRequest.pin`** takes 4 to 6 digits.

## CT-596 The camera on the lock chip (2026-10-20)

DK-28, DK-30. **`DeskLock.camera?`** (the camera is on now: the chip shows the camera mark) and **`DeskLock.present?`**
(it sees someone: the chip reads `unlockedHere`, and `until` is at most `DESK_PRESENCE_GONE_S` ahead), both booleans.
**`deskStateValid`** (Go **`DeskStateValid`**) refuses `camera` or `present` **true** on a lock that isn't `unlocked`, and
`present` true without `camera` true. Decided: the rule reads the values, not the members — `false` says nothing wherever
it is — so a producer that writes `camera: false` on a locked screen doesn't blank the console; the times keep their
member rule. Vectors: `local.json` → `deskStates` gains a four-digit PIN, unlocked with the camera on and someone there,
the camera on and nobody seen yet, the camera on while locked, on the phone, someone there while in backoff, someone
there without the camera (absent and false), and the false members locked and unlocked.

## CT-597 The presence socket (2026-10-20)

DK-31, DK-33. `@whombat/control-contracts/local`, new **`local/presence.ts`**, exported from the local index (its doc
list names it): the runtime → the appliance's camera service `whombat-presence`, HTTP/1.1 JSON over a unix socket at
**`PRESENCE_SOCKET_ENV`** `WHOMBAT_PRESENCE_SOCKET` (**`PRESENCE_SOCKET_DEFAULT`** `/run/whombat-presence/presence.sock`;
unset: no presence), as the voice socket (CT-532). **`PRESENCE_PATHS`**: `GET /v1/presence/health` → `PresenceHealth`,
`POST /v1/presence/watch` `PresenceWatchRequest {v}` → `PresenceWatch`, `POST /v1/presence/stop` `PresenceStopRequest
{v}` → `PresenceAck {v}`. **`PRESENCE_KEEP_S`** 6: the camera closes this long after the last watch by itself (DK-30),
so two missed watches at `DESK_PRESENCE_CHECK_S` don't close it and a runtime that stops asking can't keep it open.
**`PRESENCE_REQUEST_MAX_BYTES`** 1 024: §2's “at most 1 KiB” as a constant (Go `PresenceRequestMaxBytes`), as the desk's
`DESK_REQUEST_MAX_BYTES`. Errors are `LocalError` with **`PRESENCE_ERRORS`** (`bad_request`, 413 `too_large`, 503
`unavailable`). Requests strict, answers tolerant.

## CT-598 What the camera service says (2026-10-20)

DK-28, DK-31. **`PresenceHealth {v, camera, detector}`** (a capture camera exists; the model loads and runs).
**`PresenceWatch {v, state, face, seenAt?, frameAt?}`** with **`PresenceState`** (`PRESENCE_STATES`: `starting`,
`watching`, `dark`, `failed`, `no_camera`): `face` a face in the latest checked frame, `seenAt` the last frame with a face
since the camera came on, `frameAt` the last frame checked (`Rfc3339`). §2's inline `z.enum(PRESENCE_STATES)` got a
name, as CT-544 did for the box's parts, so Go has `local.PresenceState` rather than a bare string. Only a boolean and
two times cross: a newer service's score or a picture would be stripped before the runtime sees it (tested), and there
is no member for either. Schema cases for each state, a score for `face`, epoch times, unknown members.

## CT-601 This Whombat beside servers and tiles (2026-10-20)

John, 2026-10-20: one glance that lays itself out by what there is (“make it dynamical, so it adjusts on the content
available”). Whombat `docs/decisions/desk-display.md` DK-37…DK-43 has the decisions; this is their contract. DK-39:
This Whombat shows on every glance but *Only the time*, as a panel or a card. **`DeskGlance.self?`** (`DeskBox`): This
Whombat beside servers or tiles. `box` keeps its meaning (a glance without servers and tiles, CT-545) rather than
being widened: an older console's `deskStateValid` refuses a `box` beside servers, and a console that fails validity
shows no desk, so a runtime sending it there would blank every older screen. A new member an older parser strips
can't (DK-42). So a 0.104 runtime sends `box` on a new box and `self` beside servers or tiles; a 0.104 console draws
whichever is there, and on an older runtime shows This Whombat only on a new box, as before. **`deskStateValid`** (Go
`DeskStateValid`) adds: a `self` never together with `box`; only on a glance with at least one server or tile; not
while locked (any lock state but `unlocked`) in *Only the time*, as `box`; its history's two series the same length.
Absent when the manager doesn't answer, as `box` (DK-22). No new words: the card and the panel use `DESK_WORDS.box`
(`title`, `cpu`, `memory`, `temp`, `box.storage`).

## CT-602 Servers and tiles five to eight (2026-10-20)

DK-38, DK-41. **`DeskGlance.extraServers?`** and **`DeskGlance.extraTiles?`**, each at most four (`DeskServer`,
`DeskTile`): servers five to eight, worst first after `servers` (DK-S08), and tiles five to eight. `servers` and
`tiles` keep `.max(4)`: an older console's schema refuses a fifth, and a state that fails the schema shows no desk
(DK-42). **`moreServers`** keeps counting every server not in `servers`, those in `extraServers` too, so an older
console still shows “+n more” right, and a 0.104 console shows `moreServers` less the extra servers it drew.
**`deskStateValid`** adds: `extraServers` only beside four `servers`, and `moreServers` at least as many as
`extraServers`; `extraTiles` only beside four `tiles`. Decided: like CT-596's “false says nothing”, the rules read the
length, not the member — **an empty list says nothing, wherever it is** — so a runtime that always writes
`servers.slice(4, 8)` doesn't blank the console beside two servers, and Go's nil and empty slices (`omitempty`) can't
disagree. Tiles beyond eight are left out without a count, as beyond four before. The screen decides what fits.

## CT-612 Listen: `desk.voiceSample` (2026-10-20)

`desk.voiceSample {voice}` (`DeskVoiceSampleInput`, strict; the paired person) → `DeskVoiceSample {audioWav}`: the

(64 KiB), and clients read it through `open{spec: {kind: 'export', op: 'desk.voiceSample', input}}` as UTF-8 JSON. Not a
download resource or a `sessionExport`: those are for stored files and audited changes. The text is the runtime's, not
the caller's: *Listen* can't make the box say anything else.

## CT-620 The screen sign-in's letters (2026-10-20)

Whombat signin-at-box.md BX-02, BX-04 (John, 2026-10-20: no recovery kit at enrollment; physical access to the box is
enough to let a device in). `@whombat/protocol/claim` (`claim/screen.ts`): **`SCREEN_SIGNIN_LETTERS_LENGTH`** 6,
**`ScreenSignInLetters`** (`^[ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRTVWXY]{6}$`, the claim alphabet: 20⁶ = 64 million),
**`generateScreenSignInLetters(randomBytes)`** (CT-58's byte rule for six letters: bytes < 240 give `b % 20`, the rest
are skipped, then as many bytes as letters are missing), **`normalizeScreenSignInLetters(input)`** (ASCII upper-case,
drop the claim code's White_Space set, U+FEFF and `-`; six alphabet letters or `null`, nothing repaired) and
**`formatScreenSignInLetters(letters)`** (`KXQMTR` → `KXQ MTR`, display only; throws on anything but six letters, as
`formatClaimCode` does). Six, not the claim's four: the sign-in stays possible for the box's whole life, and with the
claim's backoff a patient guesser gets about 24 tries a day. Vectors: `claim.json` `screenCodes`, `screenFormats`,
`screenLetters`.

## CT-621 The screen sign-in PAKE, sharing the claim's code (2026-10-20)

BX-03: the claim's exchange (CC-06, CT-59) with its own inputs. `PRS` = UTF-8 of the six letters;
**`CI = lv_cat(SCREEN_SIGNIN_CI_TAG, deviceId, appliancePeerId, clientPeerId)`** with `SCREEN_SIGNIN_CI_TAG`
`whombat-screen-signin/1` and both PeerIds as each side sees them in Noise; `sid` = UTF-8 of the sign-in id; `ADa` =
`ADb` = empty; tags as the claim's with **`SCREEN_SIGNIN_CONFIRM_INFO`** `whombat-screen-signin-confirm/1`.
`ScreenSignInPakeContext {password, deviceId, appliancePeerId, clientPeerId, signinId}`; **`screenSignInPakeInitiator`**,
**`screenSignInPakeInitiatorFinish`**, **`screenSignInPakeResponder`**, plus `screenSignInPakeCi` and
`screenSignInPakeInputs`; the same share and tag shapes (`ClaimPakeShare`, `ClaimConfirmTag`, `ClaimConfirmTags`), the
same error (`ClaimPakeError`: `invalid_share`, `invalid_password` for anything but six letters) and `claimConfirmEqual`.
No method in the CI (there is one way), and a CI tag of its own, so a claim transcript can't stand in for a sign-in.
The shared part is factored out, not copied: `claim/alphabet.ts` (the byte rule for n letters, the typed-code fold) and
`claim/confirmed.ts` (shares, tags, the error, the initiator and responder for any inputs and info), both internal (not
exported from the index); the claim's exports and its vectors are unchanged. Vectors: `cpace.json` `screenSignIn` (same
inputs agree; wrong letters, a relay's key on either side, swapped PeerIds, another sign-in id or device id don't),
TypeScript only: the console (Go) never runs the PAKE.

## CT-622 `enroll.screen.request`, `enroll.screen.begin`, `enroll.screen` (2026-10-20)

`@whombat/protocol/session` (`enrollment.ts`), channel `enroll`. **`ScreenSignInId`** (8–64, `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`).
**`enroll.screen.request`** `EnrollScreenRequestInput {email, endpoint: NewEndpoint}` (strict) →
`EnrollScreenRequestOutput {signinId, expiresAt}`; **`enroll.screen.begin`** `EnrollScreenBeginInput {signinId,
share}` → `EnrollScreenBeginOutput {share}`; **`enroll.screen`** `EnrollScreenInput {signinId, confirm}` →
**`EnrollScreenOutput`** = `EnrolledOutput + {confirm}`. Request and begin are ephemeral like `enroll.claim.begin`
(`session(…, 'enroll', true, true)`: no receipt, never resent); `enroll.screen` is like `enroll.claim`. Safety: all
three `never`, not destructive (the device lets itself in, as `enroll.claim`, `recovery.enroll` and `enroll.passkey`;
`enroll.pair.approve` is destructive because a trusted device lets another one in). Not `secret`: the letters never
cross the wire, and the tags prove nothing after the exchange. They join the unenrolled lists (the module comment,
`OperationChannel`, the allowlist test). The begin lives `ENROLL_CLAIM_BEGIN_TTL_S` (120 s); the code shows
**`SCREEN_SIGNIN_TTL_S`** (300 s); at most **`SCREEN_SIGNIN_REQUESTS_PER_KEY`** (5) per device key and
**`SCREEN_SIGNIN_REQUESTS_TOTAL`** (30) per box an hour (BX-05). Beyond the brief: the request is refused with
`screen_backoff` too while the backoff runs (not only the begin, as for the claim), so the device says so before the
person types the letters.

## CT-671 Devices and looking (2026-10-20)

**`BluetoothDevice {address, name, kind, connected, battery? 0…100, signal?}`**, one shape for paired and found devices
(`connected` false in a scan). **`BluetoothScan {until, devices ≤ BLUETOOTH_SCAN_MAX (64)}`**: not paired, named only,
strongest first (the producer's order; no rule checks it). Paired devices are at most **`BLUETOOTH_DEVICES_MAX`** (32),
connected first then by name.

## CT-672 A pairing (2026-10-20)

**`BluetoothPairing {id, address, name, kind, phase, deadline, code?, typed?, failure?}`**: `BluetoothPairingId`
`^p-[a-z0-9]{8,32}$` (as `NetworkChangeId`'s `c-`), `BluetoothCode` 4…6 ASCII digits, `typed` 0…6.
**`BLUETOOTH_PAIRING_PHASES`** `pairing` · `code` · `confirm` · `connecting` · `done` · `failed`,
**`BLUETOOTH_PAIRING_FAILURES`** `rejected` · `timeout` · `not_found` · `canceled` · `failed` (a device that wants a
code typed into the box ends `failed`, BT-04). **`bluetoothPairingDone`** (`done` or `failed`) and
**`bluetoothPairingValid`** (TS and Go): `code` exactly in `code` and `confirm` (the brief's “phase `code` or
`confirm`” read as both ways: neither question makes sense without it), `typed` only in `code` and at most the code's
length, `failure` exactly in `failed`.

## CT-673 The state (2026-10-20)

**`BluetoothState {adapter: {name, powered} | null, missing?, devices, scan | null, pairing | null}`**,
**`BLUETOOTH_MISSING`** `no_adapter` · `no_driver` · `disabled`. **`bluetoothStateValid`** (TS and Go
`local.BluetoothStateValid`): `missing` exactly when `adapter` is null or not powered (the brief's “when”, read as
exactly, so the app always knows which words to show); every address once among the paired devices and once in the
scan, and no paired device in the scan (rows are keyed by address); no scan while a pairing runs (BT-07: a pairing stops
looking; looking again after it ended is fine); a consistent pairing. The value of `missing` isn't tied to whether
there is an adapter: what the kernel shows for a missing driver or firmware differs by adapter. Vectors `local.json` →
`bluetoothStates`, `bluetoothPairings`.

## CT-674 Timing (2026-10-20)

**`BLUETOOTH_SCAN_S`** 60 (asked again, it runs on 60 s from then), **`BLUETOOTH_PAIRING_S`** 90, **`BLUETOOTH_POLL_MS`**
1 000 (clients read the state this often while `scan` is there or a pairing runs), **`BLUETOOTH_RESULT_KEEP_S`** 60. One
the brief left as words: **`BLUETOOTH_CONNECT_S`** 15, the most a connect waits (the service's limit and the runtime's
timeout for it).

## CT-675 Refusals (2026-10-20)

**`BLUETOOTH_ERRORS`** `no_bluetooth` · `busy` · `not_found` · `not_paired` · `unavailable` in `error.details.code`
(**`BluetoothErrorDetails {code}`**) on **`BLUETOOTH_ERROR_STATUS`**'s generic code, as `host.wifi.*` did (CT-569):
`no_bluetooth` → `not_allowed` (as `no_wifi`), `busy` → `conflict`, `not_found` → `not_found`, `not_paired` →
`conflict` (the device is there, in the wrong state), `unavailable` → `unavailable` (the session's own code, retryable,
which a change op is never resent on anyway: CT-676). `no_bluetooth` is new in `APP_ERROR_CODES`; `busy` and
`not_paired` existed (Wi-Fi's, the desk screen's) and their descriptions now name Bluetooth; `not_found` and
`unavailable` ride on their namesakes and need no entry. A non-owner gets the generic `forbidden`.

## CT-676 The session ops and their safety (2026-10-20)

BT-02…BT-05. Session-native on the `app` channel, owners: **`host.bluetooth`** `HostBluetoothInput {}` →
**`HostBluetoothOutput {bluetooth | null, reason?: not_managed | unavailable}`**; **`host.bluetooth.scan`**
`HostBluetoothScanInput {}` → **`HostBluetoothScanOutput {scan | null, reason?: not_managed | unavailable |
no_bluetooth}`**; **`host.bluetooth.pair`**, **`.connect`**, **`.disconnect`**, **`.forget`** take
**`HostBluetoothDeviceInput {address}`**; **`.confirm`** **`HostBluetoothConfirmInput {pairingId, accept}`**, **`.cancel`**
**`HostBluetoothCancelInput {pairingId}`**; pair, confirm and cancel answer **`HostBluetoothPairingOutput {pairing}`**,
connect and disconnect **`HostBluetoothDeviceOutput {device}`**, forget **`OkOutput {ok: true}`** (the brief's `{}`:
every answer-less session op answers `OkOutput`). Inputs are strict; none is secret. No realtime event (the app polls).
Safety: `host.bluetooth` and `.scan` READ (looking again only runs on); pair, confirm, cancel and connect NEVER (they act
on BlueZ outside any receipt); **disconnect and forget DESTRUCTIVE_NEVER**, where the brief had NEVER: CT-194's rule
that the table is at least as strict as the old op-name heuristic makes every `disconnect` destructive, and a forget is a
removal by the table's own words (it has to be paired again, BT-05). Both are still never resent; a client may ask before
sending them, as Settings does for Remove.

## CT-680 The Bluetooth socket (2026-10-20)

BT-09. `@whombat/control-contracts/local`, `local/bluetooth.ts`, cross-language: the runtime → the appliance's
`whombat-bluetooth`, HTTP/1.1 JSON over a unix socket at **`BLUETOOTH_SOCKET_ENV`** `WHOMBAT_BLUETOOTH_SOCKET`
(**`BLUETOOTH_SOCKET_DEFAULT`** `/run/whombat-bluetooth/bluetooth.sock`; unset: no Bluetooth, `not_managed`), the presence
socket's model (CT-597). **`BLUETOOTH_PATHS`** (Go `BluetoothPath*`): `state` `GET /v1/bluetooth/state`, `scan`, `pair`,
`confirm` `/v1/bluetooth/pairing/confirm`, `cancel` `/v1/bluetooth/pairing/cancel`, `connect`, `disconnect`, `forget`.
**`BLUETOOTH_REQUEST_MAX_BYTES`** 1 KiB.

## CT-681 Its requests and answers (2026-10-20)

The brief's anonymous bodies got a name each, as the manager's did (CT-573): **`BluetoothStateAnswer {v, bluetooth}`**;
**`BluetoothScanRequest {v}`** → **`BluetoothScanAnswer {v, scan}`**; **`BluetoothDeviceRequest {v, address}`** (pair,
connect, disconnect, forget); **`BluetoothConfirmRequest {v, pairingId, accept}`**; **`BluetoothCancelRequest {v,
pairingId}`**; **`BluetoothPairingAnswer {v, pairing}`** (pair answers it with 202, confirm and cancel with 200);
**`BluetoothDeviceAnswer {v, device}`**; **`BluetoothAck {v}`** (forget, as `PresenceAck`). Requests strict, answers
tolerant. Looking while a pairing runs is refused `busy` (BT-07: looking slows pairing down), which the brief didn't say.

## CT-682 Its errors (2026-10-20)

**`BLUETOOTH_SOCKET_ERRORS`** = `bad_request`, `too_large` and `BLUETOOTH_ERRORS` (a new name: `BLUETOOTH_ERRORS` is the
session's list, CT-675), each at **`BLUETOOTH_SOCKET_ERROR_STATUS`**'s HTTP status (Go `local.BluetoothSocketErrorStatus`,
a generated map, so the service and the runtime can't disagree): 400 `bad_request`, 413 `too_large`, 409 `no_bluetooth`,
`busy`, `not_paired`, 404 `not_found`, 503 `unavailable`. An older appliance without the service has no socket, so the
runtime never asks it.

## CT-700 Found on your network on the desk: `DeskGlance.found` (2026-10-20)

John, 2026-10-20: “When we just installed a new appliance and we have a screen, it would be nice to see what the
Whombat appliance found on the network that we can connect to.” Whombat `docs/decisions/desk-found.md` DF-01…DF-14 and
NS-01…NS-08 have the decisions; this is their contract. **`DeskGlance.found`** (optional, additive): **`DeskFound`**
`{scanning, progress {done, total} | null, items (at most DESK_FOUND_ITEMS, 8), count, finishedAt | null}` with
**`DeskFoundItem`** `{catalogId, name, tagline, address}`. Decided here:

- `catalogId` is `CatalogIdText` (any slug), not `CatalogId`: a newer runtime's entry parses on an older console, which
  draws the name's first letter for a mark it lacks (DF-12).
- `name` is desk text of at most 60 code points (a new `DESK_TEXT_LENGTHS` length, `[1, 60]`): an entry's name is at
  most 40, a device find's own name (DF-03, the server's) may be longer. `tagline` 40, `address` 120, shown as given.
- Present exactly when the panel or the strip shows (DF-06); the console decides which, as it does for `box` and `self`,
  so `box` is unchanged and may come with it. **`deskFoundValid`** (TS and Go `DeskFoundValid`) says what the schema
  can't: no more `items` than `count`; `finishedAt` null only while `scanning` (the first scan, DF-07); `progress` only
  then, `done` at most `total` (null before the scan knows how many addresses it looks at); `count` 0 only while the
  first scan looks (a finished result with nothing new doesn't show). **`deskStateValid`** adds: `found` never while
  locked in *Only the time* (DF-06; unlocked it may show). Nothing ties it to `servers`, `tiles` or `box`.
- The widest glance with eight found items still fits `DESK_STATE_MAX_BYTES` (64 KiB), so the limit stays.

## CT-703 A session sign-in as a form or a query (2026-10-20)

NS-03. Synology's and QNAP's sign-ins are CGI calls, not JSON. The `session` `TokenAuth` grows, every new member optional
without a default, so Pi-hole's and Nginx Proxy Manager's entries (and every stored connection's `auth`) parse byte for
byte as before (checked: the whole catalog's sign-ins serialise identically):

- **`login.method`** also `GET`, whose values go in **`login.query`** (templates, as `body`'s; also allowed with a POST)
  and whose `body` is `{}` (`body` stays required, so older code that reads it still compiles; `tokenAuthProblem`
  refuses a `GET` with a body).
- **`login.encoding`** `json` (absent: as before) or `form` (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`).
- **`{id:base64}`** in the sign-in's templates: the value's UTF-8 in standard base64 with padding (core's own encoder,
  no `btoa`), for QNAP's `pwd`. `{secret}` may be either form; `tokenAuthProblem` looks through both.
- **`logout.method`** also `GET`, with a fixed **`logout.query`** (no templates: the password never goes on a sign-out);
  the session goes on it as `apply` says (Synology's `method=logout` with `_sid`).

## CT-704 A token from XML (2026-10-20)

NS-03. **`tokenXmlTag`**: the element whose text is the session token (QNAP's `authSid`). **Exactly one** of
`tokenJsonPath` (now optional) and `tokenXmlTag` (a refinement of the session shape, and `tokenAuthProblem`).
**`xmlElementText(xml, tag)`**: the first element of that name, CDATA unwrapped, the five entities and numeric
references decoded, trimmed; `''` for an empty one, null for none. A small reader, not a parser: the answers it reads are
the services' own flat documents. A token with a control character is no token (it goes into a header or a query).

## CT-705 Answers that mean the session ended (2026-10-20)

NS-03. **`stale`** (at most 4 **`SessionStale`**): an answer with a 2xx status that says the session ended — a value at a
JSON path or in an XML element (**`SessionAnswerMatch`** `{json | xml, values}`, values compared as text, so the JSON
number 119 is `"119"`) — optionally only for calls whose path matches `path`. The server signs in again once and repeats
the call, as on a 401 (CM-11). Repeating is safe because such an answer means the call wasn't carried out: only codes
that say so go in `stale` (Synology's 106/107/119/150, QNAP's `authPassed` 0 and File Station's `status` 3 under
`/cgi-bin/filemanager/`, CT-708, CT-709).

## CT-706 Why a sign-in was refused, in the person's words (2026-10-20)

NS-04. **`failures`** (at most 12 **`SessionFailure`** `{json | xml, values, reason, text?}`): sign-in answers that refuse,
the first that holds deciding, whatever the status (Synology and QNAP answer 200). **`SESSION_LOGIN_FAILURES`**:
`refused` (the name or password), `disabled` (the account is switched off), `denied` (it may not sign in there),
`two_step` (it asks for a two-step code), `locked` (the service blocked Whombat's address after too many tries),
`expired` (the password expired). `text` is the entry's own sentence; absent, **`SESSION_LOGIN_FAILURE_WORDS`** over
`{name}` (the `two_step` one ends with the server's existing “Turn off two-step sign-in for the user Whombat signs in
as.”). The server keeps its own reading of 400/401/403/404/429 for entries without `failures`.

## CT-707 Pure helpers for the server (2026-10-20)

**`sessionLoginRequest(entry, auth, secret, fields)`** → `{method, path (with the query), headers (content-type,
accept), body (JSON text, a form, or null)}` or null when the secret or a field it names is empty — for Pi-hole it is the
same JSON the server sent before; **`sessionLogoutRequest(auth, token)`**; **`sessionAnswerToken(auth, text)`** and
**`sessionAnswerExpiresAt(auth, text, now)`** (from the answer's text, JSON or XML; `sessionToken` reads XML too when
given the text); **`sessionIsStale(auth, status, text, path?)`**; **`sessionLoginFailure(entry, auth, text)`** →
`{reason, text}` or null, and **`sessionLoginFailureText(entry, reason)`**; **`fillSessionTemplate`**,
**`sessionTemplateFields`**, **`sessionAnswerMatches`**. They take the answer as text so the server reads JSON and XML
the same way. No `URL` or `URLSearchParams` (core stays usable on Hermes): names and values are percent-encoded.

## CT-708 Synology DSM (2026-10-20)

NS-01…NS-07. **`synology`** (“Synology DSM”, Infrastructure, after TrueNAS, handle `synology`, tagline “Storage,
shares and backups”). Checked on 2026-10-20 against Synology's DSM Login Web API Guide (2023-04-19,
https://global.download.synology.com/download/Document/Software/DeveloperGuide/Os/DSM/All/enu/DSM_Login_Web_API_Guide_enu.pdf)
and File Station API Guide
(https://global.download.synology.com/download/Document/Software/DeveloperGuide/Package/FileStation/All/enu/Synology_File_Station_API_Guide.pdf);
where they are silent, against the clients Home Assistant and others use (py-synologydsm-api 2.11.0,
https://github.com/mib1185/py-synologydsm-api; N4S4 synology-api, https://github.com/N4S4/synology-api).

- **Found** on 5001 (https) and 5000 (http) by `GET /webapi/query.cgi?api=SYNO.API.Info&version=1&method=query&query=
  SYNO.API.Auth`, which answers before sign-in with `SYNO.API.Auth`'s path and versions. DSM shows no version there;
  the probe takes none.
- **Sign-in**: a session (`token`, CT-703): `POST /webapi/entry.cgi?api=SYNO.API.Auth&version=6&method=login` (version 6
  is the guide's recommended one; the routing in the query as py-synologydsm-api sends it), a form `{account, passwd,
  session: webui, format: sid}` — a form keeps the password out of URLs and logs; the guides show only GET, which also
  works. `session=webui` because N4S4 found that it lets users who aren't administrators use the APIs. Token
  `data.sid`, sent as `_sid` (the guide: with `format=sid` every request carries `_sid`). No `SynoToken`: the guide asks
  for it only with *Improve protection against cross-site request forgery attacks*, which guards the cookie session,
  not `_sid` (unverified on a NAS, NS-08). Sign-out `GET …method=logout` with `_sid`. Lifetime 30 minutes, renewed
  sooner by `stale`.
- **`stale`** `error.code` 106 (timeout), 107 (interrupted by a duplicate sign-in), 119 (invalid session, “SID not
  found”) and 150 (a request from another address than the sign-in's): the guide's common codes; 105 (no permission)
  isn't one.
- **`failures`** (the guide's table): 400 `refused`, 401 `disabled`, 402 `denied` (its own words: allow DSM for the user
  under Applications), 403/404/406 `two_step` (a code needed, a code refused, two-step enforced), 407 `locked` (blocked
  address; its own words name the Allow/Block List) and 411 `locked` (account locked after too many tries, from the
  clients only), 408/409/410 `expired`.
- **Steps**: a user named whombat, administrators for Manage; for Look only it may stay a plain user, but the steps
  say that DSM then hides storage and system health from it (DSM's control-panel APIs answer 105 to non-administrators;
  Whombat refuses writes on Look only either way). Decided here against NS-02's plain wording, so Look only still sees
  what it is for. Two-step sign-in off for it, also where Security → Account enforces it for a group.
- **Fields**: address, `username` (“Account”), certificate fingerprint (as TrueNAS). **Check**: `SYNO.FileStation.Info
  get` (version 2) with `okJsonPath: data` — any user File Station is allowed for may read it, and an error answer has
  no `data`.
- **`request`**: prefix `/webapi/`, **GET only** (a POST's body could name another method than its query),
  `readMethods: []` and `queryReads` on `method`: `get`, `list`, `info`, `getinfo`, `get_info`, `load_info`,
  `list_share`, `query`, `status`, `check`, `stats`, `get_health_info`, `get_smart_info`, `download`. A call without
  `method` is a write.
- **`sensitive`** (on a write's query, so reads never ask): `shutdown`/`reboot`; deleting (`delete…`, `remove…`,
  `secure_erase`, `erase_all_data`, `prune`, `uninstall`); `SYNO.Core.User`, `Group`, `NormalUser`, `OTP`, `AppPriv`,
  `Share.Permission`; any write to `SYNO.Storage.*` (pools, volumes, disks, erasing); `SYNO.Core.Upgrade*` (DSM
  updates restart the NAS); `SYNO.Core.Terminal` (SSH); `SYNO.API.Auth`.
- **Guide**: the health calls (`SYNO.DSM.Info getinfo`, `SYNO.Core.System info`, `…Utilization get`,
  `SYNO.Storage.CGI.Storage load_info`, `SYNO.Core.Upgrade.Server check`), shares and snapshots, packages, Container
  Manager (`SYNO.Docker.Container`, `…Log`), Hyper Backup tasks, File Station, the error shape and codes. docsUrl the
  Login guide; tokenUrl `{url}/?launchApp=SYNO.SDS.AdminCenter.Application` (Control Panel).

## CT-709 QNAP (2026-10-20)

NS-01…NS-07. **`qnap`** (“QNAP”, Infrastructure, after Synology DSM, handle `qnap`, tagline “Storage, shares and
snapshots”). Checked on 2026-10-20 against QNAP's API for QTS Authentication v4.2
(https://download.qnap.com/dev/API_QNAP_QTS_Authentication.pdf), File Station HTTP API v5
(https://download.qnap.com/dev/QNAP_QTS_File_Station_API_v5.pdf), QTS 5.1's user guide
(https://docs.qnap.com/operating-system/qts/5.1.x/en-us/), and where they are silent the clients Home Assistant and
QNAP itself use (qnapstats, https://github.com/colinodell/python-qnapstats; OpenStack Manila's QNAP driver,
https://github.com/openstack/manila/blob/master/manila/share/drivers/qnap/api.py).

- **Found** on 443 (https) and 8080 (http, QTS's default system port) by `GET /cgi-bin/authLogin.cgi`, which answers
  before sign-in with a `<QDocRoot>` holding the model and, unless hidden, `<firmware><version>` (QuTS hero's starts
  with `h`): the probe's version.
- **Sign-in**: a session: `POST /cgi-bin/authLogin.cgi`, a form `{user, pwd: {secret:base64}, serviceKey: 1}` (the
  guide's GET carries the same; qnapstats posts the form). `pwd` is QNAP's `ezEncode`, base64 of the UTF-8 password;
  it differs from UTF-8 only for characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane (emoji), which Whombat sends as real
  UTF-8. Token `<authSid>` (CT-704), sent as `sid`. Sign-out `GET /cgi-bin/authLogout.cgi?logout=1&sid=…` (the
  clients'; QNAP's own doc is vague).
- **`stale`**: XML `authPassed` 0 (what qnapstats signs in again on) and, under `/cgi-bin/filemanager/`, JSON `status`
  3 (`WFM2_AUTH_FAIL`, File Station's own code).
- **`failures`**: `need_2sv` 1 → `two_step` (first: it comes with `authPassed` 0), `PermissionDeny` 1 → `denied`,
  `authPassed` 0 → `refused` with words that also name a disabled account and Access Protection: QTS answers those
  the same way (`errorValue` -1), so they can't be told apart.
- **Steps**: a user named whombat; administrators for Manage, everyone for Look only with the same note as Synology's;
  2-step verification off for it.
- **Fields**: address, `username`, certificate fingerprint. **Check**: File Station's `utilRequest.cgi?func=check_sid`,
  `{"status": 1}` for a working session. A value's presence can't tell 1 from 3, so **`CatalogCheck.okAnswer`**
  (`SessionAnswerMatch`, decided here; **`checkAnswerOk(check, body)`**) says which values a check needs, at a JSON
  path or in an XML element. Additive: the server ignores it until it reads it.
- **`request`**: GET only, prefixes `/cgi-bin/management/`, `disk/`, `sys/`, `filemanager/`, `application/`,
  `devices/`, `priv/`, `accessrights/` and `wizReq.cgi` (not the sign-in and sign-out CGIs); `readMethods: []` and
  `queryReads` on `func` (`get_tree`, `get_list`, `stat`, `search`, `download`, `get_thumb`, `check_sid`, `extra_get`,
  `all_hd_data`, `getExternalDev`, `external_get_all`), `subfunc` (`sysinfo`, `firm_update`, `qpkg`), `chart_func`
  (`disk_usage`, `QSM40bandwidth`, `bandwidth`) and `apply` (`10`, listing apps; 3 and 4 start and stop one). A call
  naming none of them is a write (fail closed: QTS's CGIs name their function in many ways).
- **`sensitive`** (on a write's query): power (`power_mgmt`, `shutdown`, `restart`, `reboot`); deleting (`delete`,
  `del_*`, `*_delete`, `*_remove`); volumes and pools (`volume_mgmt`, `pool_mgmt`) and anything naming `format` or
  `init_disk`; every write under `/cgi-bin/priv/` and `/cgi-bin/accessrights/`, and `user_*`, `group_*` or `password`
  values (users, groups, passwords, permissions); firmware (`firm_update` as a write).
- **Guide**: system information and health, disks (`qsmart.cgi`), volumes (`chartReq.cgi`), pools and snapshots
  (`disk_manage.cgi`, `snapshot.cgi`), firmware, apps, File Station, the XML and JSON shapes. Container Station and
  HBS 3 have no documented API; the guide leaves them out.

## CT-711 Contracts 0.110.0: found on your network on the desk, Synology and QNAP (2026-10-20)

CT-700…CT-710, on top of 0.109.0 (merged from main). Additive for older apps, consoles and runtimes: an optional glance
member and a desk path with their Go types, optional catalog and session members (the existing entries parse byte for
byte as before), two entries, two event types, pure helpers. No session op, frame or answer union changes:
**`SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 42**, no runtime feature (an older app skips catalog ids it doesn't know, `CatalogIdText`). Every package is 0.110.0, tag `contracts-v0.110.0`.

## CT-730 Signing in on the service's own page: `service_login` (2026-10-21)

John, 2026-10-21: “We have lots of connections, but some of them don't work correctly regarding the sign-in process.
For example Plex auth is not working when it has 2FA.” Whombat `docs/decisions/connection-signin.md` SG-01…SG-22 has the
decisions; CT-730…CT-769 are their contract. SG-01, SG-03. **`SIGN_IN_KINDS`** gains **`service_login`**: the person
opens the service's own sign-in page in a new tab, signs in there however their account does (two-step, Google, Apple,
a passkey), allows Whombat, and the form polls until Whombat holds the token. **`CatalogSignIn`** variant `{kind:
'service_login', label, transport?, note (1…200, the radio card's sentence), tokenMethod (0…3, default 0)}`. Generic on
purpose: the server has one adapter per catalog id, so the entry carries no URLs. Decided here:

- Stored as the token it gives: the connection is saved with `signIn: 'token'` and the `token` sign-in at `tokenMethod`
  (by index among the entry's token sign-ins, as `password`'s). Checks, tools, Replace token and every call work
  unchanged, and `ConnectionView.signIn` never carries `service_login`, so older clients (whose `SignInKind` lacks it)
  still parse every connection. Older clients never see the kind at all: the catalog ships in the package.
- `CreateConnectionBody.signIn` does not take it (the sign-in has its own endpoints, CT-738).
- **`storedTokenSignIn(entry, method)`** (new): the token sign-in a `password` or `service_login` sign-in is stored as,
  or null; a test holds every such sign-in to one.
- **`SERVICE_LOGIN_POLL_MS`** 2000, **`SERVICE_LOGIN_MAX_MS`** 10 minutes and **`SERVICE_LOGIN_USER_CODE_MAX`** 32
  (Nextcloud's two, and the longest `userCode`).

## CT-731 A challenge handed back (2026-10-21)

SG-06 (amends CS-03 for challenges, not passwords). **`ConnectionErrorDetails.challenge`** (optional, at most 4096,
**`ConnectionChallenge`**): on `second_factor_needed`, and on `sign_in_refused` with reason `code` when the service made
a new one (UniFi's `UBIC_2FA`). **`CreateConnectionBody.login.challenge`** (optional, the same shape): sent back as it
came, with `login.code`. Opaque on the wire: the server seals it (`provision-challenge`) with the entry, the origin, the
account and an expiry, and ignores one that doesn't open (the sign-in starts fresh). No feature: an older runtime never
sends one, and strips it from a body (`z.object` drops unknown members).

## CT-732 A session's two-step code, asked once: `twoStep` (2026-10-21)

SG-09. The session `TokenAuth` gains optional **`twoStep`** (**`SessionTwoStep`**): `asked` (`SessionAnswerMatch`, the
answer that asks for a code), `wrongCode?` (the answer to a code that didn't work), `code {name}` (where the code goes),
`remember? {body, tokenJsonPaths (1…3), name, with?}` and, decided here, `again?` (1…300: the words when a stored
connection is asked for a code again; absent: **`SESSION_TWO_STEP_AGAIN_WORDS`** over `{name}`, through
**`sessionTwoStepAgainText(entry, auth)`**). Every existing session parses byte for byte as before. Decided here:

- The code and the remembered token go **beside** the sign-in's values: in `body`, or in `query` for a `GET` sign-in
  (where the login's own values go). `tokenAuthProblem` refuses a name that is already one of the sign-in's, the same
  name twice, and a template in `remember.body`/`with` (they are sent as they are; never the password).
- **`sessionLoginRequest(entry, auth, secret, fields, extras?)`**: `extras` **`SessionLoginExtras {code?, remembered?}`**
  (optional, so 0.110 callers are unchanged). With a code: `code.name` and `remember.body`; else with a remembered token:
  `remember.name` and `remember.with`. **A code replaces a remembered token**: it is asked exactly when the token no
  longer works. **`sessionTwoStepValues(auth, extras)`** gives those values alone; nothing without `twoStep`.
- **`sessionTwoStepAsk(auth, body)`** → `wrong_code` (checked first) | `asked` | null, looked at **before**
  `sessionLoginFailure`, so an entry with `twoStep` keeps those answers out of its `failures`.
- **`sessionRememberedToken(auth, body)`**: the first usable string at `remember.tokenJsonPaths` (no control
  characters), or null. JSON only: the one service that needs it answers JSON.
- The remembered token is a credential: the server seals it in its own column (Whombat migration 0128), never shows
  it, and drops it with the connection or a new password. Nothing on the wire carries it.

## CT-733 A two-step code on connect and Replace password (2026-10-21)

SG-09. **`CreateConnectionBody.code`** and **`SetConnectionSecretBody.code`** (optional, **`TwoStepCode`**: trimmed,
4…64, as `login.code`): a code for a token sign-in whose session has `twoStep`, sent again with the same body after
`second_factor_needed`. `login.code` stays sign in once's. No feature: an older runtime strips `code` and answers the
refusal it always did.

## CT-734 A session failure names its statuses (2026-10-21)

SG-10. **`SessionFailure.status`** (optional, 1…10 statuses of 100…599; absent: any). **`sessionLoginFailure(entry,
auth, body, status?)`** takes the answer's status: a failure with `status` holds only when the caller gives one of them
(a 0.110 caller that passes none never matches such a rule and reads the status as before). Pi-hole needs it: 200 with
`session.validity` −1 is a Pi-hole without a password; 401 with the same value is a wrong one.

## CT-735 A check names its refusals: `failures` (2026-10-21)

SG-11. The request **`CatalogCheck`** gains **`failures`** (at most 8 **`CheckFailure`** `{status (1…10), bodyPattern?,
refused, text (1…300)}`), matched in order before the server's own reading. `refused` true marks the credential refused
(the connection needs a new one); false keeps it (an address, a network or a plan is in the way). **`checkFailure(check,
status, body)`** → `{refused, text}` or null; the pattern is case-insensitive and unanchored unless it anchors itself.

## CT-736 A check per secret shape: `forSecret` (2026-10-21)

SG-12. The request **`CatalogCheck`** gains **`forSecret`** (at most 4 **`CheckForSecret`** `{pattern, method, path,
headers?, okJsonPath?, okAnswer?}`). **`catalogCheckFor(entry, secret)`**: the first whose pattern the secret matches
(case-insensitively) is the check — its method, path and answer rules, its headers or else the check's, the check's
`failures`, no `body`, no `okStatus` (any 2xx); else the entry's check. **`resolveCheckPath(entry, fields, secret?)`**
takes the secret too (optional: unchanged without it). Decided here: `okJsonPath`/`okAnswer` are not inherited (they
describe another answer), `failures` are (they describe the service).

## CT-737 A field filled from the check: `fromCheck` (2026-10-21)

SG-15a. **`CatalogField.fromCheck`** (optional `JsonPathText`): filled from the check's JSON answer at that path after
every check that passes, never asked. **`fieldsFor`** leaves such a field out for every method, so a form that lists
`fieldsFor` hides it and **`fieldsProblems`** never asks for it; **`fieldProblem`** never calls one needed. A value a
client sends (an edit form sending back `ConnectionView.fields`) is no “unknown field”: it is kept until the next check
replaces it. **`fieldsFromCheck(entry, answer)`**: each such field's first string or number at its path, trimmed, when
it fits a field (at most `CONNECTION_FIELD_VALUE_MAX`, no control characters); absent ones are left out, so an older
connection keeps what it has. A test holds every such field optional, apart from `fromService`, on an entry with a
request check.

## CT-738 The service-login endpoints (2026-10-21)

SG-02. **`connections.startServiceLogin`** POST `/burrows/:burrow/connections/service-login/start`
**`StartServiceLoginBody {catalogId, scope, label?, fields (default {}), access (default manage), connectionId?}`** →
**`StartServiceLoginResponse {loginUrl, flowId (OAuthStateId), pollEveryMs (500…60 000), expiresAt, userCode (at most
32) | null}`**; **`connections.pollServiceLogin`** POST `/connections/service-login/:flowId/poll` →
**`PollServiceLoginResponse`**, the very schema `PollNextcloudLoginResponse` is (“exactly as Nextcloud's”: one union, so
the two can't drift). `access` is in the start (unlike Nextcloud's), so the level is set on save. `userCode` is required
and nullable: the form always knows whether to show a code. A flow that ended answers `login_expired` (its doc grows),
no new error code. **Operation safety** `NEVER` for both (the start asks the service for a flow before its row, a poll
that connects takes a one-time token), as Nextcloud's. Neither is a secret op: the start carries fields, the poll a flow
id.

## CT-743 Pi-hole, SABnzbd, NZBHydra2, Plausible and Mollie in their own words (2026-10-21)

SG-10…SG-12, the spec's words verbatim. **Pi-hole** `failures`: `error.message` “No 2FA token found in JSON payload” /
“Invalid 2FA token” / “Reused 2FA token” → `two_step` (make an app password), `error.key` `api_seats_exceeded` →
`locked` (seats), `status` 200 with `session.validity` −1 → `denied` (no password set). **SABnzbd** check `failures`
(403, plain text): “Access denied - Hostname verification failed” and “External internet access denied” not refused,
“API Key Incorrect|Required” refused; an empty 403 (`api_warnings` off) stays the server's refused key. Its wrong
comment (“A wrong key answers 200 …”) now says every refusal is a plain-text 403. **NZBHydra2**: 404 with an empty body
→ refused (“…or it’s older than version 9.”). **Plausible**: 402 → not refused (the Business plan). **Mollie**:
`forSecret` `^access_` → `GET /v2/permissions` (any advanced or OAuth token, no scope needed); API keys keep `GET
/v2/methods`; its steps follow its one page (“+ Create access token”, a Standard API key to manage, an Advanced access
token with read permissions to look only, copied right away), the secret's label and placeholder name access tokens.
Patterns allow leading white space (`^\s*`).

## CT-744 Feature `connections.service_login` and level 43 (2026-10-21)

**`connections.service_login`** (`SINCE_0_111`): a client offers a `service_login` sign-in only on runtimes that
advertise it, and otherwise the entry's token. **`SESSION_API_LEVEL` 43** (window 41…44): new ops and their outputs
(CT-136's rule). New clients no longer serve level-40 runtimes (0.102…0.105). Go's `SessionAPILevel` follows. The other
additions need no feature: older runtimes ignore `code`, `login.challenge` and the catalog's new members, and never send
`details.challenge`.

## CT-745 What 0.111 doesn't change (2026-10-21)

No enum a `ConnectionView` or another answer older clients parse carries gains a value: `CatalogReauthReason`,
`CatalogConnectionState`, `ConnectionErrorCode`, `ConnectionErrorDetails.reason` and `ConnectionConnectError` are as they
were (a service-login flow that ended is `login_expired`; SG-13's single-sign-on refusals use the existing reasons with
`method`). `SESSION_LOGIN_FAILURES` and their words are unchanged. Left to the server: each `service_login` adapter
(Plex's PIN, its headers and client id), sealing the challenge and the remembered token, the words of `asked`
(`second_factor_needed`'s message), and when a `fromCheck` value replaces a stored one.

## CT-780 The assistant saves a login it is sent: `vault_save` (2026-10-21)

John, 2026-10-21: “When we use a vault, we shouldn't have to hand a key to the agent … I also want the agent to be able
to store login details and passwords in the vault.” Whombat `docs/decisions/vault-self-serve.md` VS-01…VS-14 has the
decisions; CT-780…CT-799 are their contract. VS-04…VS-06. **`vault_save`** in `VAULT_MCP_TOOLS`: `personal: true`,
`requiredKey: null`, `readOnly: false`. **`VAULT_SAVE_KINDS`** `['login', 'token', 'basic']` (**`VaultSaveKind`**): a
website signed in to in the browser (`login`, `form`), an API token sent as Bearer (`http` + `bearer`), an API with a
username and password (`http` + `basic`). **`VaultSaveInput`** `{kind, name?, description?, address? (VaultUrl, ≤ 2000),
username?, secret (VaultSecretValue), entry? (VaultEntryRef), made (default false)}`, each field described for the
model. Refinements: without `entry`, `name` and `address` are required and `username` for `login`/`basic`; with
`entry`, no `address` (“…the person can, in the Vault.”), no `name`, `made` false. Decided here:

- The secret is never trimmed (the server matches it against the person's words, VS-05); a `username` with `token` is
  not refused (the server ignores it), nor a `description` with `entry`: neither can send anything elsewhere, and a
  refusal would cost the model a call.
- **`VaultSaveOutput`** `ok {entryId, name, created, blanked ≥ 0} | VaultToolRefusal`. No new `VAULT_FAILURES`: a secret
  not in the person's message is `failed` `invalid_request` with the server's words (VS-05), an address the Vault refuses
  `not_allowed`, a room others read or a turn that isn't the owner's `blocked`. The enum older runners parse stays as it
  is.

## CT-781 Servers for an SSH key: `vault_add_server` (2026-10-21)

VS-09…VS-11. **`vault_add_server`** in `VAULT_MCP_TOOLS`, `personal: true`, `requiredKey: null`, `readOnly: false`.
**`VaultAddServerInput`** `{entry?, address, username? (VaultSshUsername), name? (VaultSshServerName), password? (1…1024,
VAULT_SSH_SERVER_PASSWORD_MAX, never trimmed)}`. **`VaultAddServerOutput`** `ok {entryId, entryName, server, target
(user@host:port), outcome, publicKey} | VaultToolRefusal`, **`VAULT_ADD_SERVER_OUTCOMES`** `signed_in | key_added |
key_refused | already` (**`VaultAddServerOutcome`**); a refinement holds `publicKey` (the `authorized_keys` line) to
`key_refused` and null otherwise. Decided here:

- **`parseVaultSshAddress(text)`** → `{host, hostKind, port} | null` (pure, `vault/ssh.ts`): a host name or IP literal
  as `parseVaultSshHost` reads it, with an optional `:port` (1…65535, else 22, `VAULT_SSH_DEFAULT_PORT`); IPv6 with a
  port in brackets, a bare IPv6 address without one. A user (`root@…`), a scheme or a path is refused.
  **`vaultSshAddressProblem`** words it (`VAULT_SSH_FIELD_TEXT.address`, `.addressUser`: “Put the user in username…”),
  and **`VaultSshAddress`** (1…260, `VAULT_SSH_ADDRESS_MAX`) is the input's field, so the server gets a host and port it
  can check with `vaultSshDestinationProblem` as for a person's server.
- `host_key_changed` is the existing failure reason (VS-10); `key_refused` is an outcome, not a refusal: the server is
  added (and its key trusted) though the key isn't on it yet.

## CT-782 Personal tools, the Vault's activity, not uses of an entry (2026-10-21)

VS-12, VS-14. **`VAULT_SELF_SERVE_TOOL_NAMES`** `['vault_save', 'vault_add_server']` (**`VaultSelfServeToolName`**,
`vault/tools.ts`). `isVaultActivityTool` is true for both, bare or prefixed (neutral rows, no evidence, no input kept,
VT-D07); `isVaultToolName` stays false (they aren't a use of an entry, like `request_vault_key`). Both are
`PERSONAL_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES` and not `WHOMBAT_TOOL_NAMES`, so a server lists them to personal agents only;
`VaultDispatchContext.tools` says a personal assistant's turn for its owner carries them with the SSH tools (VS-12).
Until a runtime serves them it must leave them unlisted (as Whombat's `NOT_YET_SERVED_TOOL_NAMES` did for 0.80's tools).

## CT-785 What the assistant is told (2026-10-21)

VS-09, VS-12, VS-13. Every variant is an option whose default is a team agent's words, so a runtime that passes nothing
reads what it did (except the first trust, below):

- **`VAULT_SAVE_RULES`** (five, in VS-13's order): save what the person sends in a room only they read with
  `vault_save` right away, never repeat it; in a room others read ask for it in their own chat or the Vault; a new
  password goes to its entry; `made: true` for one the assistant made; SSH passwords used once with `vault_add_server`.
- **`VAULT_SSH_ADD_SERVER_RULE`** (personal) and **`VAULT_SSH_UNLISTED_HOST_RULE`** (the team rule, VT-G04, its own
  export now). `VAULT_SSH_AGENT_RULES` keeps it last, unchanged; **`vaultSshAgentRules({personal})`** swaps it.
- **`vaultSshSetupSteps(agentName, {personal})`**: personal → **`VAULT_SSH_SETUP_STEPS_PERSONAL`** (three: add the key;
  add the server or tell {agent} the address, trusted the first time; the public key line, or the server's password
  once in your chat). `VAULT_SSH_SETUP_STEPS` (team) loses “Check, compare the fingerprint … Trust this server” for
  everyone (VS-10: a first key is trusted), so it has four steps and “Give a key to…” is step 4 (a runtime that says
  “step 5” must say 4). “Add server” stays step 2 (`VAULT_SSH_UNLISTED_HOST_RULE` names it).
- **`vaultUnheldAskLine(facts, {personal})`**: “{Owner} switched you off for it: they can switch “{agent} can use this”
  back on in the Vault → “{entry}”.” (the title is `vaultAssistantAccessCopy`'s); **`VAULT_UNHELD_NOTE_OFF`** “switched
  off for you” for the block's tag.
- **`vaultAccessRules({personal})`**: the second rule says “never ask for a secret in a room other people read” for a
  personal assistant. Decided here, unlike the assignment's wording: `VAULT_ACCESS_RULES` itself keeps “in chat”,
  because VS-13 keeps team agents' wording (a team agent can't save a secret, so one pasted in its DM would stay there).
- `vault_request` and `request_vault_key` descriptions: “Never ask for a password or token in a room other people
  read.” (one description serves every agent).
- **`vaultNoServerText(names, {canAdd})`**: “That host isn’t one of this key’s servers yet: add it with
  vault_add_server{, or use one of: a, b}.”

## CT-800 Skills without packs: the `skills/` module (2026-10-21)

Whombat skill-store.md SST-01…SST-17 (John, 2026-10-21: “remove packs”). A skill is a folder with `SKILL.md` and its
files; packs are gone. Core gets **`skills/`** (subpath **`@whombat/core/skills`**, also in the root export), pure, with
what skills still need from `packs/`: `skill.ts` (`SkillName`, `SKILL_REQUIREMENTS`/`SkillRequirement`/
`SkillRequirements`, `SkillPrerequisites`, `SkillNeeds`, `SKILL_NEEDS_MAX`, `SkillConnectionId`, `SkillServerKind`,
`SkillMeta`, `SkillCategory`, `SkillCategoryInfo`, `SkillOrigin`), `meta.ts` (front matter, CT-801), `files.ts` (paths,
sizes, UTF-8, the check of a skill folder, the content hash, CT-804), `scan.ts`, `secrets.ts`, `readiness.ts` and
`library.ts` (moved, CT-805). The names that only described packs went with them: `PackManifest` and its parts, the
manifest's MCP servers, tools, secrets, permissions and runtime suggestions, `validatePack`/`PackValidation`/
`PackLimits`/`packLimitsFor`/`OWN_PACK_LIMITS`/`IMPORTED_PACK_LIMITS`/`PACK_LIMITS`, `normalizePack`/`normalizeEntries`,
`packContentHash`, `stdioArgProblem`, `parseHttpUrl` (unused), `diffPacks`/`packTools`/`toolHash`, the instruction
precedence (`orderPackInstructions`, `PACK_PRECEDENCE`), role packs (`rolePacks`, `rolePackSuggestionText`,
`packSkippedReason`), semver, `skillWinner`/`SKILL_ORIGIN_PRECEDENCE`/`SkillPick` (one skill per name is the server's,
SST-02; its pack-era backfill keeps its own copy) and their tests. Renamed on the way: `PackScan` → **`SkillScan`**,
`scanPackContent` → **`scanSkillContent`**, `packPathProblem` → **`skillPathProblem`**, `PackEntry` → **`SkillEntry`**,
`LIBRARY_SKILL_LIMITS` → **`SKILL_LIMITS`** (now with `fileBytes` and `depth`).

## CT-801 The `whombat:` line: `parseSkillMeta` / `renderSkillMeta` (2026-10-21)

SST-01. Besides `name` and `description`, a stored `SKILL.md` may carry one front-matter key, **`whombat:`**, whose value
is one line of JSON: `{"requires": [...], "needs": {"connections": [...], "servers": [...]}, "prerequisites": {...}}`
(**`SkillMeta`**, the manifest entry's schemas: `SkillRequirements`, `SkillNeeds`, `SkillPrerequisites`; every part may
be left out). It is valid YAML for any other tool, and the flat parser (`skillFrontMatter`, which now also unquotes a
JSON-quoted value) reads it. The pair: **`parseSkillMeta(text)`** → `{name, description, meta, body, dropped,
problems}` and **`renderSkillMeta({name, description, meta?}, body)`**, which writes name and description JSON-quoted
and the line only when it says something (**`skillMetaLine`**: canonical order `requires`, `needs`, `prerequisites`,
`", "` and `": "` separators), so the same meta gives the same bytes and content hash and `parseSkillMeta` reads back
exactly what was written. Decided here: keys inside the line this release doesn't know are dropped (a newer release may
add one); a known key its schema refuses, or a line that isn't one JSON object, is a problem and `meta` stays the
defaults (a skill that says what it needs wrongly is better refused than run without it); other front-matter keys are
named in `dropped` (the importer leaves them out, SST-01). `skillFrontMatterExtra` allows `whombat`;
`sanitizedSkillMarkdown` (what the runner writes for a CLI) still keeps only name and the listed description, so the
CLIs never see the line (BP-D20). `SKILL_FRONT_MATTER_KEYS`, `SKILL_META_KEY`, `skillBody`, `emptySkillMeta`.

## CT-802 Categories (2026-10-21)

SST-03. **`SkillCategory`**: a slug of 3–32 characters, the former `PackName` rule, so the shipped categories are the
former pack names (`homelab`, `developer-craft`) and stored references keep working. **`SkillCategoryInfo`**
(`skills/<category>/category.json`, `SKILL_CATEGORY_FILE`): `{title, description}`, strict. Decided here: the skills an
agent wrote are in category **`LEARNED_SKILL_CATEGORY`** (`learned`), listed as **`learnedSkillsTitle(name)`** (“Learned
by Dusty”); imports keep their group's slug (`hermes-smart-home`).

## CT-803 Origins (2026-10-21)

SST-02. **`SKILL_ORIGINS`** = `shipped`, `imported`, **`learned`** (was `own`). An agent's own copy of a shipped or
imported skill keeps that skill's origin and is marked changed (`DispatchSkill.changed`, `SkillLibraryItem.changed`).
`skillListingRank` takes `{origin, changed?}`: learned, imported or changed rank 2.

## CT-804 A skill folder's check, its content hash and the scan (2026-10-21)

SST-01, SST-04. **`validateSkill(entries, read, {name?, limits?})`** checks one skill folder and answers the skill
(`name`, `description`, `meta`, `files`, `sha256`, `scan`) or every problem (`SkillProblem` codes `path`, `entry_type`,
`limits`, `encoding`, `skill`, `hooks`, `secret`, `duplicate`, `scan`): paths (`skillPathProblem`, six folders deep),
plain files only, no hook/plugin/provider files (**`SKILL_PROVIDER_FILE`**, now shared with `SkillFilePath`), one
`SKILL.md` at the top, **`SKILL_LIMITS`** (128 KiB `SKILL.md`, 64 other files of at most 256 KB, 2 MiB together, SST-01's
library limits for every skill, shipped ones too; a file read larger than its limit is refused too), UTF-8, front matter with a valid
name (and the expected one) and a description of at most 1024 characters, no keys besides `name`, `description` and
`whombat`, a valid `whombat:` line, no literal secret in a text file (prose rules: known shapes, not entropy), and the
content scan (`dangerous` refused). The folder rule of `SkillFilePath` (`references/`, `templates/`, `scripts/`) stays
for what agents write; shipped skills have other folders. **`skillContentHash(files)`** (sha-256 over `path`, NUL, file
sha-256, newline, sorted; was `packContentHash`) is a version's identity: its folder in the content store
(`$WHOMBAT_HOME/skills/<sha256>/`), the hash `runner.skillFiles` answers and what the runner caches by (TE-09). The scan
no longer treats `whombat-pack.json` as prose; it still flags an imitated `[[pack` delimiter.

## CT-806 What stays of packs (2026-10-21)

SST-09, SST-12, SST-15. `packs/` keeps only **`PackName`**, **`PackVersionString`** and **`PACK_MANIFEST_FILE`**
(`packs/legacy.ts`, subpath `@whombat/core/packs` kept): what the journal's `pack.*` events, old approvals and a
pre-0.113 `.wbk` carry. The ids `pck_`, `pkv_`, `pka_`, `pkt_`, `pks_`, `vlb_` stay parseable; nothing makes new ones.
Decided here: no manifest schema for the importer. An archive with a `whombat-pack.json` is one layout of Add skills

schema would refuse archives the loose read takes, for nothing. A restore of a pre-0.113 backup reads a pack version's
files the same way (its skills through `validateSkill`).

SST-15. `skills.jsonl` gains **`skill`** `{id: skl_, agent, name, category, origin, original (an own copy of a shipped

SST-04, SST-06. `libraryReset {agentId, name}` removes the agent's own copy of a shipped name (the shipped skill applies

## CT-822 Older phones keep working for a release (2026-10-21)

SST-16. Checked against whombat-app main (0.113.0; the 0.114 branches don't touch these files): the phone calls
`skills.library`, `librarySkill`, `librarySwitch`, `libraryAdd`, `libraryPin` and `libraryReset`, `skills.proposals`,
`decide`, `removeLearned`, `packs.agentPacks` (the chat `/skill` hint) and, only from PacksScreen, `packs.inspect`,
`updateAttachment`, `approveTool`, `revokeTool`, `setSkill`; it validates its requests against its own schemas (`pack`
a `PackName`) and decodes `skills.*` tolerantly (a release build falls back to the raw JSON when a field is missing or
an id has the wrong prefix) and `packs.*` strictly. Kept, and why:

- **Library rows in the 0.111 shape**: `key` = **`legacySkillKey(category, name)`** (`<category>:<name>`; the phone looks
  rows up and flips switches by `pack:name`), `pack` = category (a valid `PackName`), `packTitle` = group, `source` =
  **`legacySkillSource`** (`own` for learned or changed), `changedAt`/`changedBy` from `changed`, `replacedBy` always
  null. **`legacySkillItemFields(row)`** fills them; they are required in the schema so the server can't leave one out
  (a release phone reads the raw JSON, without defaults). `SkillVersion.version` stays required; `original` keeps
  `{pack, packTitle, text}`.
- **Requests take `pack` and ignore it** (`SkillRefQuery`, the panel bodies; `libraryAdd` by `pack`, CT-820).
- **`SkillProposalSummary.versionId` stays `pkv_` | null and is always null since 0.113**: the phone reads it in
  message cards and realtime frames, where a `skv_` would drop the frame or the whole page's defaults. The skill version
  is **`skillVersionId`** (optional).
- **`VaultEntryDetail.packs`** stays required and always `[]` (CT-823).
- **The `packs.tool.read`/`packs.tool.write` key ids** stay in `KeyId`: the phone echoes held grants in `agents.setKeys`
  and reads grants strictly.

Not kept: **`packs.agentPacks`** (an error makes the phone send `/name …` as typed, without a hint, after one retry; it
doesn't fail; the server may read a leading `/name` itself, `parseSkillCommand`), PacksScreen's ops (it shows “Packs
didn't load.” with Retry, reachable only from a team agent's profile), every other `packs.*` endpoint, `packs.stage` and
`pack-archive` (web only), `skills.uses`, `libraryRestore`'s `pkv_` (web only; the phone never calls it), the `packs`
feature (unread), `SkillImportCommitResponse.packs` (unread). Known cost: a debug build of an older phone shows “This
skill didn't load.” on a skill's page, because its `versions` carry `skv_` ids; release builds read the raw JSON and
work. Remove the compat fields in 0.114.

## CT-823 No new `secret` Vault entries (2026-10-21)

SST-09. The `secret` kind stays in `VAULT_ENTRY_KINDS` and `VAULT_TEMPLATES` so existing entries list and can be removed;
`vaultEntryShapeProblems` (and so `CreateVaultEntryBody`) refuses it on create (`kind`: “Whombat doesn't make this kind
of entry any more. Save it as an API token.”); an existing one takes neither URL nor sign-in, and can be edited and
removed (Whombat's insertEntry and own-keys still read the kind).
**`VAULT_NEW_TEMPLATES`** is what Add to Vault offers (no `secret`). The template is “Secret”, “A single value kept for
an older Whombat feature. Nothing uses it now.”; `vaultEntryMeta` says “Secret · nothing uses it”. `VAULT_COPY.packs`

## CT-862 A server's id of its own: `DeskServerId` (2026-10-21)

The brief had the desk's `Id` (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$`), which refuses the hosts service's ids: they are slugs of the
host name (`Slug` in whombat-hosts: lower-case letters, digits and dashes, at most 63), often shorter than eight (`nas`,
`pve-01`), and older hubs' ids have dots. **`DESK_SERVER_ID_RE`** = `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}$` and
**`DeskServerId`** (the lead's pattern): a letter or a digit first, so never `.`, `..` or a leading dash, no slash, no
space, at most 128. Used in all four places: `DeskServer.id`, `DeskServerRequest.id`, `DeskTalkRequest.server` and
`DeskDispatchContext.server.id`. It lives in core (`@whombat/core/domain`, beside the desk's other constants) because
the runner contract uses it and core can't import control-contracts; `@whombat/control-contracts/local` re-exports it.
Go: **`DeskServerIDPattern`** and the hand-written **`ValidDeskServerID`** for the console server, which checks the id
before it asks; vectors `local.json` → `deskServerIds` (short ids, an older hub's with dots, and empty, a leading dot,
dot-dot, a slash, a space, a trailing line break, a non-ASCII letter, 129 characters refused).
