hosts service didn't answer) are the socket's. A POST, like the other paths that take only the version.

## CT-864 A server's own screen: `server`, `DeskServerRequest`, `DeskServerPage` (2026-10-21)

DK-83, DK-84, mockup 2. **`DESK_PATHS.server`** = `POST /v1/desk/server`, **`DeskServerRequest`** (strict) `{v, id,
range}` with **`DESK_SERVER_RANGES`** `1h`, `24h`, `7d` → **`DeskServerPage`** as the brief's §2, plus `not_found` for a
server not in the fleet. Decided here:

- Its parts are named schemas (`DeskServerCpu`, `DeskServerMemory`, `DeskServerDisk`, `DeskServerTemp`,
  `DeskServerHistory`, `DeskServerVolume`, `DeskServerGuest`, `DeskServerGuestList`, `DeskServerAlert`,
  `DeskServerAlertList`) so Go gets the same names. The two lists are `…List`, not `DeskServerGuests`/`DeskServerAlerts`:
  those are the Go constants of `DESK_SERVER_GUESTS` and `DESK_SERVER_ALERTS`, and one Go package can't have both.
- Limits: `DESK_SERVER_POINTS` 96 (a quarter of an hour over 24 hours), `DESK_SERVER_VOLUMES` 6, `DESK_SERVER_GUESTS` 6,
  `DESK_SERVER_ALERTS` 3, `stepS` 1…86 400 (a point a day over 7 days at most). **`DESK_SERVER_MAX_BYTES`** 32 KiB: the
  widest page is about 9.5 KiB, three times that if every character were escaped.
- Three desk text lengths join `DESK_TEXT_LENGTHS`: `[0, 8]` (the load), `[0, 16]` (a guest's memory, empty when off)
  and `[0, 60]` (the OS).
- `temp {value, limit}` in whole °C with `DeskMeter`'s range (−100…1 000); the tone is the card's temperature tone.
- `disk.used` may leave out its unit when it is the total's (“1.2” of “3.6 TB”, the mockup's “1.2 of 3.6 TB”); the
  runtime decides, `DESK_WORDS.server.diskOf` joins them.
- `DESK_GUEST_STATES` are the hosts service's (`HostGuestState`), in core beside the words that name them;
  `DESK_GUEST_KINDS` `vm`, `container`; `DESK_SERVER_ALERT_TONES` `warn`, `bad`.
- `alerts.count` always, its `items` only while unlocked or with *Everything* (DK-84, DK-03); the runtime trims them, as
  it trims an ask's words. The schema can't know the lock, so it doesn't check it.

## CT-880 A followed server task's card: `task` (2026-10-21)

John, 2026-10-21 (Whombat `docs/decisions/task-feedback.md`, “Implement fully”): asked by voice to update the Home
Assistant server, Neo started the install, and nothing said afterwards that it had worked. TF-10…TF-18 are the
decisions; CT-880…CT-899 their contract. TF-10: a server task Whombat follows is a live card in its thread. Card kind
**`task`** (`domain/task-card.ts`, **`TaskCard`**): `{followedTaskId, serverId, server, title, state, startedAt, endedAt,
result}`, in `MessageCard`, `StoredCard` (the same shape: the runtime updates it in place as the task runs and ends) and
`CARD_KINDS`, never in `PostableCard` (an agent can't forge one). Decided here:

- **`followedTaskId`** is Whombat's own row (TF-11's `followed_tasks`), a new id **`FollowedTaskId`** (`ftk_`,
  `ID_PREFIXES.followedTask`), not the hub's task id (`pkg:…`, `incus:…`, a Proxmox UPID): the card is about Whombat's
  following, and a hub id is neither unique across servers nor a safe key.
- `serverId` is the hosts service's id as `HostServer.id` takes it (1…200, not `DeskServerId`: a stored card must parse
  whatever hub id it was made with); `server` the name as the card shows it (1…80), `title` the running words (1…200,
  “Installing 23 updates on Home Assistant”), `result` the outcome words (1…600, the runtime's `taskOutcomeText` and
  `installedText`), null while running.
- **`TASK_CARD_STATES`** `running`, `ok`, `warning`, `error`, `lost` (the hub's task states and TF-11's `lost`);
  **`TASK_END_STATES`** the four ends. `endedAt` null exactly while running and a `result` only once ended
  (**`taskCardValid`**): a helper, not a refinement, so a client decoding a card a runtime got slightly wrong still shows
  it.
- No server mark or agent on the card: the server's id finds its mark, the message's author is the agent.

## CT-881 The card's line and its time (2026-10-21)

card-settle: active is a card, done is a line. **`taskCardLine(card, now)`**, shared by web, Android and the desk:
running, the title and the time it has run (“Installing 23 updates on Home Assistant · 12 s”); ended, the first sentence
of `result` without its full stop and how long it took (“Home Assistant is up to date: 23 updates installed · 4 min”,
“Backing up web on pve-02 didn’t work: the storage is full · 2 min”), or the title and the state's label when there is no
result; lost, the title and “lost track”, with no time (the time to giving up says nothing). The full result is what the
card opens to. The brief's “Installed 23 updates on Home Assistant” isn't a word the runtime writes: the line takes the
outcome as `installedText` says it rather than asking the runtime for a second, shorter text. **`taskResultLine`**: the
first line with text, up to the first `.`, `!`, `?` or `…` followed by a space or the end (so “v2.1.3” stays whole), a
closing full stop dropped. **`formatTaskDuration(ms)`**: “0 s”, “12 s”, “4 min”, “1 h”, “1 h 5 min”, “1 d 3 h” —
whole units rounded down, plain spaces as `formatDeskUptime`; not `formatDuration` (“2m 14s”, the run log's).
**`taskCardElapsedMs(card, now)`** (start to end, or to now; never negative) and **`taskCardActive`** (running).

## CT-882 The card's own words (2026-10-21)

**`TASK_CARD_WORDS`**: `states` (Running, Done, Done with warnings, Didn’t work, Lost track; `satisfies Record` of the
states: a badge, a status dot's label, the desk's row), `lostLine` (“lost track”) and `lost` (“Whombat lost track of this
task. {server}’s Tasks tab has it.”, TF-11), which the runtime writes as a lost card's `result` with
**`taskLostText(server)`**. **`taskCardText(card)`** (`[task: {title}, {state} — {result}]`) is the card as text for the
inbox, search and other agents' windows, as `deployCardText`. Everything else the card says is the runtime's.

## CT-883 The agent hears its tasks end: `task_finished` (2026-10-21)

TF-12. **`DispatchTrigger`** gains **`task_finished`**: the agent that started the task is woken in its thread, for the
same person, with **`DispatchContext.taskFinished`**: 1…**`TASK_FINISHED_MAX`** (10) **`TaskFinishedContext`**
`{followedTaskId, serverId, server, what, result, words, rebootRequired, startedAt, endedAt}`, in the order they ended
(tasks ending while such a turn is queued join it). `result` is `TaskEndState` (`ok`, `warning`, `error`, `lost`);
`what` the card's title and `words` its result (≤ 600, data, never instructions; empty is allowed for a lost task the
runtime has no words for); `rebootRequired` (the hosts service's name for it, `rebootRequired`) when the server's report
after the task asks for a restart, the next step the agent may offer; the times so it can say how long. No dispatch of
the turn that started it (`notify` has `fromDispatchId`): the followed task row doesn't keep it, and the thread is the
link. The runner reads it in the claim's `DispatchContext` (runner contract), as `notify`; nothing else carries it.

Clients: **`SummaryTrigger`** leaves `task_finished` out and **`summaryTrigger`** names it `notify` (a background job
that reported back, which is what it is), so `DispatchSummary`'s union is unchanged for every app. Not added to
`REFLECT_LONG_TURN_SKIPPED_TRIGGERS`: a turn that acts on its task's end (a restart, a retry) is a person's work like
`notify`'s. Every exhaustive use of triggers in the contracts is `summaryTrigger` and that list; both stay total.

The only union a session answer carries that grows is a server-made card kind, which apps before 0.116 drop with CT-136's
tolerant decoding (`card: null`) while the message's text stays — so the runtime writes the card's line as the message's
text. CT-193's precedent: **`SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 44**. No `RUNTIME_FEATURES` name: nothing in an app waits for the
card, it shows when one comes; `task_finished` is between the server and its runner, which ship together.

TF-14 (amends desk-display.md DK-05). **`DeskAsk.choices`** (optional, 1…**`DESK_ASK_CHOICES`**) of **`DeskAskChoice`**
`{scope: DeskChoiceScope, label ≤ 120}`, **`DESK_CHOICE_SCOPES`** `task`, `agent`: `approvalView().scopeChoices` for the
paired person without `once` (Approve is the ask's own button, with `approveLabel`), in its order, each scope once
(“Don’t ask again on Home Assistant”, “Always allow Banjo to merge into main”, the computer's and the Vault's “for this
task”). The labels come from the runtime, so web and desk can't differ. Every choice needs the PIN (TF-14); the rule is

ask offers nothing here), not on a screen without a PIN (`hasPin` false), each scope once. At most two: `once` is the
Approve button and there are two scopes besides; a third scope would be a new enum value anyway.

## CT-891 Deciding with a scope: `DeskDecideRequest.scope`, `not_offered` (2026-10-21)

**`DeskDecideRequest.scope`** (optional, **`DeskDecideScope`**, **`DESK_DECIDE_SCOPES`** = core's `COMMAND_SCOPES`:
`once`, `task`, `agent`, as `approvals.decide` takes it; absent is once). **`deskDecideRequestValid`** (TS and Go): a
scope only with `approve` (else `bad_request`). **`deskDecideNeedsPin(ask, request)`** (TS and Go): an approve of an ask
with `approveWithPin`, or an approve with a scope wider than once; deny and *Not now* never. Without the PIN the runtime
answers `pin_needed`, on a screen without a PIN `no_pin`, a wrong one `wrong`/`backoff` as before (`DeskDecideAnswer`).
A scope the ask doesn't offer the paired person now (they may not change the agent's keys or the server's asks, the ask
has no such choice, it changed) is a new error code, **`not_offered`** (403), nothing decided: an error, not a
`DeskDecideAnswer` result, because it is a refusal the page didn't expect (the state offered it), like `on_phone`; and not
`on_phone`, which keeps meaning “answer this on your phone”. Words `DESK_WORDS.choiceWithPin` (“Type your PIN for
“{choice}”.”, a new hole `{choice}`) and `DESK_WORDS.notOffered`.

**`REMOTE_HELP_DURATIONS`** `hour`, `day`, `week`, `forever` (`RemoteHelpDuration`), **`REMOTE_HELP_DURATION_S`** and
**`remoteHelpDurationSeconds`** (null for forever), **`REMOTE_HELP_LOOK_COMMANDS`** (`LookCommand`, twelve),
**`REMOTE_HELP_STEP_KINDS`**, **`REMOTE_HELP_REFUSALS`**, **`REMOTE_HELP_UNIT_RE`** (Look's unit grammar) and

space, tab, no-break space, `·`, `.`, `-`, U+2010…U+2015 and the minus sign; upper-cases ASCII letters only; `O` → `0`,
`I`/`L` → `1`; six characters or null), **`formatHelpCode`** (`KQ7·2MX`) and **`helpCodeFromBytes`** (low 5 bits, so
unbiased). Only ASCII is upper-cased so that Go and JavaScript agree: `ſ` and `ı` upper-case to `S` and `I` in both, but
a ligature expands in JavaScript only; they refuse instead (vectors).

## CT-932 What support did: steps and visits (2026-10-21)

**`RemoteHelpStep`** `{at, kind, command?, units? ≤ 8, line? (display text ≤ 500), seconds?, target? (printable ASCII ≤
200), bytes?, reason?}` and **`remoteHelpStepValid`** (TS and Go): a `look` names its command and only `logs` names units,
`exec` its line, `shell` its seconds, `restart` exactly one unit, `forward` its target, `refused` its reason, `bytes`
only on a forward. `refused` may also carry the `command` that was refused. **`RemoteHelpVisit`** `{id, who, level,
startedAt, endedAt | null, steps ≤ REMOTE_HELP_STEPS_SHOWN, truncated, transcriptBytes}`. Tolerant (`z.object`): an
older app drops a newer step kind and keeps the visit (tested). `line` is one line: the service cleans it with
`HostText` rather than recording newlines, so one odd command can't break a list.

## CT-933 Session ops, the feature and the level (2026-10-21)

`remoteHelp.get` (read), `remoteHelp.confirmBegin` (ephemeral, as `passkey.register.begin`: mutating, no receipt,
`never`), `remoteHelp.start`, `remoteHelp.stop`, `remoteHelp.visits` (read), `remoteHelp.transcript`
(`sessionExport`, text; **`REMOTE_HELP_TRANSCRIPT_CONTENT_TYPE`**, **`remoteHelpTranscriptName`**). Safety:
`remoteHelp.start` is **secret, destructive and `never`** where the brief said `receipt` — secret because its answer
holds a prod box's help code, and a secret op's result is never kept in a receipt (`Outcome.redacted`, CT-44; the lead);
destructive because it lets someone into the box (as `enroll.pair.approve` is); `never` because it acts on the support
service before anything commits and consumes the begin's one-time nonce (as `passkey.register`): a client never sends it
again by itself, a person checks the state. `remoteHelp.stop` `receipt` (only takes access away; idempotent; its answer
has no grant, so no code). `remoteHelp.get` answers the code too, but reads keep no receipt. The transcript is `never`:
an export op is mutating (`sessionExport`, like `diagnostics.download`; text bytes need it), and only non-mutating ops
may be `safe`, so the brief's “READ” isn't possible. Feature **`remote_help`** (`SINCE_0_120`; the
brief's `remoteHelp` fails `FeatureName`). **`SESSION_API_LEVEL` 45** (window 43…46), as the brief and the lead asked
(CT-678's precedent; 0.117 and 0.119 kept 44 by CT-615's): new clients no longer serve level-42 runtimes (0.109…0.110).
Go's `SessionAPILevel` follows.

## CT-934 Confirming with a passkey (2026-10-21)

RH-04, changed by the lead from the brief on W's request: **`remoteHelp.confirmBegin`** takes **`{level, duration}`** and
answers **`{nonce: PasskeyNonce | null, options: WebAuthnRequestOptions | null}`** (both null when the owner has no
passkey on this Whombat). **`PASSKEY_REMOTE_HELP_PURPOSE`** `whombat-remote-help/1`; **`passkeyRemoteHelpChallenge`** /
**`passkeyRemoteHelpChallengeBase64url`** `({nonce, endpoint, level, duration})` = SHA-256(utf8(canonicalJson({purpose,
nonce, endpoint, level, duration}))), `endpoint` the caller's session PeerId, exactly as PK-03's enroll challenge; the
client recomputes it and refuses a mismatch. **`WebAuthnRequestOptions`** `{challenge, rpId, allowCredentials [{id,
type, transports?}], userVerification, timeout?}` (tolerant) is the box's own `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON`
(the brief's `PasskeyRequestOptionsJSON`); the assertion is the existing `WebAuthnAuthenticationResponse` (the brief's
`PasskeyAssertionJSON`). **`REMOTE_HELP_CONFIRM_TTL_S`** 300. `remoteHelp.start {level, duration, passkey?}` is
unchanged. Vectors `session.json` → `passkeys.remoteHelp`.

## CT-1005 Controls (2026-10-21)

Panel **`controls`** `{…panel, title, meta, hint? ≤ 200, buttons?, groups ≤ 16, empty?}`; **`ThingControlGroup`** `{id,
title ≤ 60, items ≤ 48}`; **`ThingControl`** `{id, label ≤ 60, icon?, state? ≤ 60, on?, tone?, toggle?, buttons? ≤ 4,
stepper?, image?}`; **`ThingControlStepper`** `{value, min, max, step > 0, unit? ≤ 8, button}`; **`THING_CONTROL_ICONS`**
(16). Tightened here, with reasons: a stepper's `value` lies within `min`…`max` (and `min ≤ max`), so a client never
draws a figure it can't step from; a `toggle` comes with `on`, since the client sends `value: !on`. The server keeps
both (it clamps a thermostat that reports a target outside its range, and leaves the switch out when the state is
unknown).

## CT-1009 The catalog: Sonarr, Radarr and Seerr (2026-10-21)

SD-21, SD-24, SD-S07. **`sonarr`** and **`radarr`** (Home, after `nzbhydra`): an API key in `X-Api-Key`, base `{url}`,
check `GET /api/v3/system/status` (`okJsonPath` `version`), `request.prefixes` `/api/v3/` and `/MediaCover/` only,
`tokenUrl` `{url}/settings/general`, docs sonarr.tv / radarr.video, a guide each (series or movies, calendar, queue,
wanted/missing, history, commands `MissingEpisodeSearch` / `MissingMoviesSearch`, health, disk space, posters). Checked
against Sonarr 4.0.20 and Radarr 6.4.4 in throwaway containers: every `/api/` path answers an empty 401 without a key
or with a wrong one; `/ping` answers `{"status": "OK"}` for both alike; **`/initialize.json` answers the API key to
anyone on a fresh install**, so nothing outside the two prefixes is reachable through the connection; `/login` answers
200 with `<meta name="description" content="Sonarr">` (Radarr: `"Radarr (Preview)"`) both fresh and with Forms sign-in,
so discovery probes that page (ports 8989 and 7878, http). What asks a person (`arrSensitive`): deleting, changing
settings (config, indexers, download clients, notifications, lists, profiles, root folders, tags…), reading
`/api/v3/config/host` (it holds the API key), restart, shutdown and backup restore, and the commands `ApplicationUpdate`
and `ResetApiKey`; other commands (searches, refreshes, RSS sync) don't. **`overseerr`** is shown as **Seerr** (id and
handle unchanged), “Movie and TV requests in Seerr, Overseerr or Jellyseerr.”, docs https://docs.seerr.dev/, its words
naming Seerr first; `CATALOG_ROUTING_WORDS` keeps `overseerr` and `jellyseerr` pointing at it, and gives Sonarr and
Radarr theirs. Pictures the service pages read through their connections, all reads within their prefixes: Plex
**`/photo/:/transcode`** (new, posters through Plex's resizer; the tenth prefix), Home Assistant `/api/camera_proxy/`,
UniFi Protect `/v1/cameras/<id>/snapshot`, Immich `/api/assets/<id>/thumbnail`, Paperless-ngx `/api/documents/<id>/thumb/`,
Sonarr and Radarr `/MediaCover/` (a test holds each).

queue with meters and Pause / Pause 30 min / Half speed, Failed with Retry and a confirmed Retry all, a speed chart,

Whombat quiet-notices.md QN-01…QN-17 (John: UniFi said “Access point offline” for one he took offline on purpose, and
the only way out was “Look into it”; “give me controls to ignore certain things Whombat is monitoring”). New
`domain/quiet.ts`, the brief's shapes: **`NOTICE_NATURES`** `problem` · `you` · `fyi` (Problem · Only you · Heads-up)
as **`NoticeNature`**; **`QUIET_LIFTS`** `fixed` · `newer` · `period` as **`QuietLifts`**; **`NoticeCheck`** (≤ 80,
**`NOTICE_CHECK_RE`** `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z0-9_]+)+$`: two parts or more, so `host.disk.space_high` and

**`NoticeRef`** `{check, subject?}`; **`NoticeIgnore`** `{lifts, words 1…60 (a sentence), until?}`; **`NoticeQuiet`**
`{state: ignored | snoozed, words 1…60 (lower case), until?, by?, at}`, with **`QuietBy`** `{id: PrincipalId, name}`
shared by the quiet line, an exception and a check switched off. **`noticeNature(n)`**: `n.nature`, else `info` a
heads-up, an `ask` link a problem, any other only-you (an older server's line). **`QUIET_WORDS`** as the brief has them,
plus `snoozedBare` (“Snoozed {words}”, beside `ignoredBare`: a hosts service's acknowledgement without a person Whombat

until it’s back online”), **`stopWatchingLabel`** (“Stop watching Hallway AP” / “Stop watching this”) and
**`quietWordsOf`** (Ignore's “Until it’s back online.” → the quiet line's “until it’s back online”, so the server words

isn't tied to `period` by a refinement: a reader only shows `words`, and the server decides.

`thingEndpoints` += **`things.quiet`** (POST `/burrows/:burrow/things/:thing/quiet`, **`QuietNoticeBody`** `{notice:
NoticeRef, how: ignore | snooze | undo (QUIET_HOWS), until?}` → **`QuietNoticeResponse`** `{notice, quiet | null}`),
**`things.watch`** (GET `…/watch` → `ThingWatch`) and **`things.setWatch`** (POST `…/watch`, **`SetThingWatchBody`**
`{check, subject?: NoticeSubject, watched}` → `ThingWatch`). Tightened here: `until` only with `snooze` (a refinement;
an ignore's end is the check's own). `setWatch` takes the item with its name, so an exception still reads “Attic AP” once
the item went. Refusals: `not_allowed` (403) for who may not manage the thing, `not_found` for a line the thing doesn't
have now (`undo`: nothing to take back) or a check it doesn't have. Session: `things.watch` `safe`; `things.quiet` and
`things.setWatch` `never`, not destructive (a server's is a call to the hosts service outside the receipt, QN-23; Undo
and Watch again take either back). Feature **`things.quiet`** (`SINCE_0_122`): a client offers the ⋯ menu and What
Whombat watches only where the runtime has it. **`SESSION_API_LEVEL` stays 45** by CT-615's and CT-994's precedent (new
ops a feature names, optional members a tolerant client skips).

## CT-1064 Home (2026-10-22)

`NeedsYouItem.nature?` and `WatchItem.nature?` (`problem` or `you`; heads-ups reach neither, QN-02, QN-22).
`needsYou.ignore`'s note: on `alert` and `connection` items it is the shared Ignore of `things.quiet` (QN-21: for the
whole Whombat until it changes, a server alert the hosts service's acknowledgement until it resolves, the toast
`QUIET_WORDS.toastIgnored`); on approvals and questions the person's own, as before (ONE-24). The body and answer are

## CT-1065 The desk (2026-10-22)

QN-20. `DeskLook` += optional `notice {check: NoticeCheck, subject?: text(160)}`, `nature` (`NoticeNature`; absent a
problem, as in 0.118; the runtime never sends a heads-up), `ignoreWords` (text 60) and `question` (text 300, the line's
own question for *Ask*). **`DESK_PATHS.lookQuiet`** `/v1/desk/look/quiet`: **`DeskLookQuietRequest`** (strict) `{v,
key, notice {check, subject?} (strict), how: ignore | snooze (DESK_LOOK_QUIET_HOWS)}` → `DeskAck`; 409 `not_paired`,
`locked`, 403 **`not_allowed`** (new in `DESK_SOCKET_ERRORS`: the paired person may not manage the thing), 404
`not_found`. `DESK_WORDS.looks.fix` is now “Ask {assistant} to look into it”, and `looks` gains `ignore`, `notNow`,
`ignored` and `snoozed` (the same words as `QUIET_WORDS.toastIgnored`/`toastSnoozed`, tested). The subject is display
text (a desk pattern, so the console server's cleaning leaves it as it is), not core's `NoticeSubjectId`, which the
cross-language subset couldn't carry; two new desk text lengths, 160 and 300. `NoticeNature`, `NoticeCheck` and
`NOTICE_NATURES` are re-exported from `local` so Go names the enum (`local.NoticeNature`).

Limits, decided here: five looks with these members at their widest (four-byte characters everywhere) make the widest
glance 70.8 KB, above `DESK_STATE_MAX_BYTES` (64 KiB, 59.6 KB before), so it is **96 KiB** now; and the widest
`look/quiet` (a key of 120 and an item of 160 four-byte characters) is about 1.25 KB, so **`DESK_REQUEST_MAX_BYTES`** is
**2 KiB**. Real states and requests stay a few kilobytes; the runtime and the console ship in one host release and read
both from the contracts (the console's `local.DeskStateMaxBytes`, the runtime's `DESK_REQUEST_MAX_BYTES`). Shortening the
question or the item instead would have cut lines the page carries whole. Go: `DeskLook.Notice`, `.Nature`,
`.IgnoreWords`, `.Question`, `DeskLookQuietRequest`, `DeskLookQuietHow`, `NoticeNature`, `DeskPathLookQuiet`,
`DeskErrorNotAllowed`; JSON Schema, vectors and schema cases.

## CT-1066 Servers (2026-10-22)

`HostAlert` += `entity?` (≤ 200, the hosts service's entity: `fs:/mnt/data`, `pool:tank`, `host`) and `key?` (≤ 300,
`<rule>:<entity>`, the same while the condition recurs); `HostHint` += `id?` (≤ 200, `<kind>:<entity>`). Absent from
older hubs. New `domain/host-watch.ts`: **`HOST_WATCH_CHECKS`**, one **`HostWatchCheck`** `{check, rule? | hint?, name,
nature, warnNature?, lifts, words, perItem}` per alert rule (29: `host.<rule>`) and hint kind (40 of the hosts service
and Whombat's own `agent.update_failed` and `agent.needs_install`: `host.hint.<kind>`), every rule and kind checked
against `hosts/internal/rules`, `internal/hub/checks.go`, `internal/hub/api_alerts.go` and
`internal/hub/model/hints.go` (30c4985). Natures as the catalogue (catalogue-cross-cutting.md C.3, C.4): alerts 19
problems, 8 only-you, 2 heads-ups; the hub's hints 7 · 7 · 26; Whombat's two only-you. Added to the brief's shape:
**`warnNature`**, the kind of a hint at `warning` where it differs (`incus.pool_full` and `libvirt.pool_full` a problem
at 95 %, `unraid.notification` only-you for an alert note), read with **`hostHintNature(check, severity)`**. Words
describe when you hear again under the way Ignore works for each: an alert is acknowledged until it resolves (“Until
there’s room again.”, “Until a backup works again.”), a hint lifts by the check's own `lifts`; where the catalogue's
words were vague (“Until it changes.”) they say what changes (“Until it’s back to normal.”, “Until another guest is
affected.”). No `period`: the hosts service has no windows. Lookups **`hostAlertCheck(rule)`** and
**`hostHintCheck(kind)`** answer a rule or kind a newer hub has with its own `host.<rule>` (or `host.other` /
`host.hint.other` when that isn't a valid check id), a problem or a heads-up about one item. **`hostNoticeSubjectId(check,
entity)`** keys a server line's item the same in the runtime and the client: the hub's entity as it is, for per-item
checks only, never `host`; **`hostEntityName(entity)`** a name without the hub's prefix when nothing better is known.

## CT-1068 Quiet on a server's detail, and the banner's alert (2026-10-22)

Asked by stream S4 through the lead. **`HostBanner`** += `rule?` (≤ 80) and `alertId?` (≤ 200): the hosts service sends
the banner's `rule` and `alert_id`, which the runtime dropped, so a client matched the banner to its alert by title;
now by id. **`HostAlert.quiet?`** and **`HostHint.quiet?`** (`NoticeQuiet`): the runtime fills them on a server's detail
(`hosts.getServer`) — an alert from the hosts service's acknowledgement (ignored “until it’s back online”, the check's own
words, or snoozed “until tomorrow 09:00”, `by` the person who did it), a hint from Whombat's own store. A hint whose check
is switched off for the server or its item is left out of the detail altogether (QN-13), so there is no `stopped` state
here. The client draws quiet ones greyed at the bottom of Worth a look and counts only the rest. Absent from older
runtimes; an older client strips them.

for compatibility (HE-27). The export list for the streams is `docs/hermes-engine-api.md`.

  CLI on the person's own sign-in (Hermes's Claude Code mode and Codex mode) or Hermes's own loop on an organization key

## CT-1200…CT-1249 Hermes keeps memory and skills; its browser and the Vault without relays (2026-10-23)

Whombat hermes-engine.md step 3 (HE-16…HE-21, HE-38…HE-45): Hermes owns memory, skills, sessions and the browser;
Whombat shows, edits and backs them up through the runner's Hermes-home service. Nothing is kept for compatibility
(HE-27). The export list for the streams is `docs/hermes-engine-api.md` (“Step 3”).

- **CT-1200** Each person's memory is Hermes's two files in their own profile (`domain/memory.ts`): `MEMORY_FILES`
  `memory` (`MEMORY.md`, what the agent learned working with them) and `user` (`USER.md`, about them), by Hermes's own
  target names. `MEMORY_FILE_LIMITS` 2,200 and 1,375 characters and `MEMORY_ENTRY_SEPARATOR` `\n§\n` are Hermes's
  (`tools/memory_tool_store.py`): entries split on the whole separator, trimmed, empty ones dropped, a repeat kept once
  (`memoryEntries`, `normalizeMemoryFile`), counted as code points of the entries joined (`memoryChars`). A file is
  `MemoryFileView {text, used, limit, version, updatedAt}`; a person's is `PersonMemory {memory, user}`.
- **CT-1201** `memory.write` (PUT `/memory/:file`, `{text, ifVersion?}`) replaces one file: over its limit in Hermes's
  count is `validation_failed` `details.reason: too_long` (`memoryFileProblem`); a file the agent changed since
  `ifVersion` is `conflict`; while a turn holds the person's profile, `conflict` `details.reason: busy`. A view carries up
  to 65,536 characters (`MEMORY_VIEW_TEXT_MAX`): Hermes keeps a file written outside it that runs over its limit, and so
  does the view; a write takes at most 8,000 before it is counted.
- **CT-1202** `memory.mine` (GET `/memory`) and `memory.clear` (DELETE `/memory`, both files or `?file=`): only the

## CT-1250…CT-1299 One product shape: the direct connection, Tailscale, no compatibility — contracts 1.0.0 (2026-10-24)

Whombat hermes-engine.md step 4 (HE-22, HE-23, HE-27; HE-48…HE-56): the appliance's runtime mode is the only one, web
and Android reach the box through the relay or directly, and the contracts drop every compatibility shape for a clean
major version. The export list for the streams is `docs/hermes-engine-api.md` (“Step 4”).

- **CT-1250** The box's direct listener (`@whombat/protocol/direct`, cross-language, Go `protocol.Direct*`):
  `DIRECT_PATH` `/v1/direct`, subprotocol `whombat-direct.v1`, `DirectHello {t, v: 1, class}` (text, within 10 s) →
  `DirectWelcome {t, v: 1, heartbeatMs, maxMessage}`, then binary only: Noise XX and the session, as through the relay.
  Close codes are the relay's numbers where the meaning is the same (`badHello` 4400, `forbidden` 4403,
  `messageTooLarge` 4413, `rateLimited` 4429, `draining` 4503 with `{retryAfterMs}`). One port, `DIRECT_PORT` 4480, on
  the LAN addresses and the Tailscale name (HE-51's one firewall port); the listener answers the page and the socket
  on it. Clients use the routes the box reports, never the constant.
- **CT-1251** No ticket on the direct path: the hello has no `ticket`, `session` or `chn`. The box admits from the
  client's Noise static key (MA-04): enrolled → `app`, unknown → `enroll` (the unenrolled budget), revoked → `revoked`.
  The relay's ticket only ever admitted traffic; the box rate-limits handshakes by source address instead. The PeerId
  pin is unchanged, so a LAN address now held by another box fails in message 2 and the client moves on
  (secure-channel SC-12).
- **CT-1252** The ways in, learnt over the session: `Welcome.direct` (`DirectAddresses {port, lan, tailscale,
  routes}`, required, null on the enrollment channel and when the box takes no direct connections). A route is
  `{way: lan | tailscale, socket, web}` with full URLs (`ws://…/v1/direct` + `http://…/` on the LAN, `wss://` +
  `https://` on the Tailscale name), best first. `directRoutesFor(addresses, {secureOnly})`: an `https://` page (the
  hosted app, the Tailscale page) keeps the `wss://` routes only. A welcome, not an op: every connection refreshes the
  client's copy, and nothing else needs asking. `IpAddress` moves to `session/direct.ts` (no import cycle).
- **CT-1253** Tailscale for This Whombat: `TailscaleStatus {state, loginUrl, name, addresses, tailnet, https,
  problem}`, flat so Go reads it (`protocol.TailscaleStatus`); states `off`, `starting`, `needs_sign_in` (with
  Tailscale's own `loginUrl`), `needs_approval` (the tailnet's admin approves the device), `on` (`name`, `addresses`,
  `tailnet`, `https`: a certificate for the name works, which needs HTTPS turned on in the tailnet), `error`
  (`problem`: `not_running`, `unreachable`, `failed`); `tailscaleStatusValid` says what the schema can't. Kinds cross
  the wire, the app makes the words (HD-11).
- **CT-1254** Owners' ops: `host.tailscale` (read; `{tailscale | null, reason?: not_managed | unavailable}` as
  `host.network`), `host.tailscale.on`, `host.tailscale.off` (`{signOut?}`: off keeps the sign-in, sign out leaves the
  tailnet; destructive: clients on Tailscale lose that way) and `host.tailscale.signIn` (a fresh login link). None is
  resent by a client (the manager acts outside the receipt). The app polls `host.tailscale` every `TAILSCALE_POLL_MS`
  while it waits; refusals `tailscale.unavailable`, `tailscale.busy`.
- **CT-1255** The manager drives Tailscale and is the only caller of its local API (it is root, and Tailscale's local
  API can do far more than the runtime needs): `MANAGER_PATHS.tailscaleState|On|Off|SignIn|Cert`
  (`/v1/tailscale/state|on|off|sign-in|cert`), Go `local.Tailscale*`. `tailscaleCert` hands the runtime the
  certificate chain and key for the box's Tailscale name (`tailscale cert`), which the direct listener serves HTTPS with;
  the key is a secret, never logged.
- **CT-1256** Browsers on the direct ways: the box serves the web app on every route (`DirectRoute.web`). A plain-HTTP
  LAN page has no secure context: no WebCrypto `subtle` (so a software identity), no passkeys, notifications or
  clipboard; each page origin is its own browser storage, so a browser enrols once per origin (SC-12).
- **CT-1257** `enroll.dev` (HE-49): a development runtime lets a browser on the machine itself in, without claim,
  control or relay: `{account: {name, email}, endpoint}` → `EnrolledOutput`, the account found by email or made, the
  first one the owner; `ENDPOINT_ENROLLED_VIA` `dev`. Every other runtime, and any connection not from the machine
  itself, refuses with `forbidden` / `dev_only`. On the enrollment channel; never resent.
- **CT-1260** One version rule: `SESSION_PROTOCOL` is `{major: 2, minor: 0}`. A box answers only its own major
  (`negotiateVersion(offered, ours)`), else `unsupported_version` with `UnsupportedVersionDetails`; `whoMustUpdate` and
  `VERSION_REFUSAL_COPY` (“Update the app to use this Whombat.” / “This Whombat needs an update to work with this
  app.”). Major 2, not 1: every 0.x app and box speaks major 1 and has the same check, so a 0.x app meeting a 1.0 box
  says “update the app” and a 1.0 app meeting a 0.x box says the box needs an update, with no code for either. The
  session major moves only with a breaking contracts major (publishing.md). `hello.versions` stays a list so a box can
  read any app's hello and refuse it in words.
- **CT-1261** Gone: `session/features.ts` (`RUNTIME_FEATURES`, `LEGACY_FEATURES`, `WelcomeRuntime`,
  `runtimeHasFeature`), `SESSION_API_LEVEL`, `LEGACY_API_LEVEL`, `apiLevelWindow`, `runtimeSkew`,
  `SUPPORTED_SESSION_VERSIONS`, `Welcome.runtime`, core's `FeatureName` and `ApiLevel`, `ReleaseManifest.apiLevel` and
  `.features`, control's `ReleaseRecord.apiLevel` and `.features` and `FleetSummary.releases[].apiLevel`. A box's
  version for people is `appliance.status.appliance.runtimeVersion`.
- **CT-1262** Kept: tolerant decoding (`decodeTolerant`). Within one major a box and an app may differ by minors (the
  hosted web app ships apart from boxes) and a minor may add a union member; leaving the item out beats failing the
  answer. The client security floor (`client_below_security_floor`, `clientFloor`, CT-53) stays too: it is a security
  control, not compatibility. Schema rollback classes are the release package's and stay (HE-52).
- **CT-1270** No HTTP sign-in (HE-48): `auth.*` (sign-in links and codes, invites by link, Tailscale identity,
  sessions, API tokens) and their bodies, `SESSION_COOKIE`, `AuthOptions`, `SignUpPolicy`, `ClientKind`, `Session`,
  `ApiToken`, `SessionId`, `TokenId` go (the `ses`/`tok` prefixes stay taken). `me.*` stays, in `contracts/me.ts`;
  `Account` and `Preferences` in `domain/account.ts`. `Account.title`, `.isAdmin` and `.canCreateBurrows` are required
  (the runtime always sends them). `SESSION_EXCLUDED_API_OPS` is `devices.vapidKey` only.
- **CT-1271** The agent works on its computer only: `AgentAccess`, `AgentCheckout`, `TurnSandbox`, `TurnCommands`,
  `TurnAccess`, `turnAccessLabel`, `AGENT_CHECKOUT_COPY`, `AGENT_ACCESS_COPY`, `AgentRuntimeChange`,
  `diffAgentRuntime`, `describeRuntimeChange`, `describeDefaultWorkdirChange`, `AgentRuntimeInput`, `domain/workdir.ts`
  (`Workdir`, `normalizeWorkdir`, `parseWorkdirRoots`, `expandHome`, …), `WorkdirInput`, `agent.setRuntime`
  (`SetAgentRuntimeBody`, `…Response`), `burrows.setWorkdir` (`SetBurrowWorkdirBody`), `Burrow.defaultWorkdir`,
  `Run.access`, `ProgressBody.access` and the backup agent record's `workdir`, `checkout`, `access` and settings'
  `defaultWorkdir` go. `AgentRuntime` = the model plus `credentialSource`; `DEFAULT_AGENT_RUNTIME` `{provider:
  'claude'}`. The audit type `burrow.workdir_changed` stays for the log's history (CT-1247's rule).
- **CT-1272** `host.info` (`HostInfo`) is `{deployWorkflow, computers}`, both required: `home` and `workdirRoots` were
  the self-hosted host's.
- **CT-1273** GitHub runs on a person's own GitHub sign-in: `GitHubStatusResponse.via` goes, `signInNeeded` is required;
  `fix` is a short action (“sign in to GitHub”). `GitHubMode` keeps `gh` for GitHub itself (through `gh` on that
  sign-in), `fake` and `off`.
- **CT-1274** AI clients come from the box's manager only: `ClientStatus.installed` is `{version, installedAt}`
  (`source` and the host CLI's null `installedAt` go).
- **CT-1275** `/ws` goes with the HTTP transport (HE-50): `WS_PATH`, `ClientMessage`, `ServerMessage`,

- **CT-1276** The self-hosted `managed.*` refusals go: `managed.trusted_access`, `.sandbox_fallback`, `.api_tokens`,

- **CT-1278** What 0.39 deprecated goes: `AvatarMotionPreference`, `DEFAULT_AVATAR_MOTION`, `Preferences.avatarMotion`.
- **CT-1279** Old-version fixtures go: `__fixtures__/recipes-0.70.ts`, its tests, and a recipe chain's pre-0.71 words

## CT-1300…CT-1349 The community edition — contracts 1.1.0 (2026-10-24)

Whombat hermes-engine.md step 5 (HE-24, HE-25; HE-56, HE-58…HE-64): one image, two editions. A community box has no
control, relay, licence or remote help: it is claimed, joined and reached over its direct ways only, sends Web Push
itself and mail through the owner's own server, and may sign in to the owner's own Tailscale coordination server. Every
change is an addition within session major 2 (CT-14, CT-1262). The export list for the streams is
`docs/hermes-engine-api.md` (“Step 5”).

- **CT-1300** The edition (`@whombat/protocol`, also from `/session`; Go `protocol.Edition`): `EDITIONS`
  (`commercial`, `community`), `Edition`, `DEFAULT_EDITION`, `editionOf`, and `editionHas(edition, part)` over
  `EDITION_PARTS` (`relay`, `control`, `remote_help`, `licence`, `phone_push` — commercial only; `local_claim` —
  community only). **`Welcome.edition`**, optional on every channel: absent is `commercial`, which every 1.0 box is, so a
  1.1 client reads a 1.0 box right and the welcome stays tolerant. Not in `appliance.status`: the welcome comes with
  every connection. A part list is product shape, not the runtime feature flags HE-52 removed: it never varies within an
  edition and no version gates it.
- **CT-1301** Which box answers before a session: **`DirectIdentity {v: 1, appliance, edition?, claimed?}`**, the JSON of a
  plain GET of `/v1/direct` (the runtime already answered `{v, appliance}`; now a contract, cross-language for the
  image's install test). The box's page reads it first: the PeerId to pin on that origin, and the first screen (a
  community box nobody claimed shows the claim). Nothing in it is secret: the console shows as much.
- **CT-1302** The claim on the box's own page (HE-59), enrollment channel: **`enroll.claim.local.start {}`** →
  `{claimId, expiresAt}` (ephemeral; `LOCAL_CLAIM_TTL_S` 300; also says whether a claim can start: `claim_used`,
  `claim_not_ready`, `claim_backoff`), **`enroll.claim.local.begin {claimId, share}`** → `{share}` (ephemeral) and
  **`enroll.claim.local {claimId, confirm, account, endpoint}`** → `EnrollClaimOutput`. CPace as CC-06 with
  `CI = lv_cat("whombat-claim-local/1", appliancePeerId, clientPeerId)` (no device id: a community box has none and its
  PeerId names it), `sid` = the box's claim id, `info = "whombat-claim-local-confirm/1"` (`localClaimPake*`, vectors in
  `cpace.json` `localClaim`, TypeScript only like the screen sign-in). The box chooses the claim id (not the client) so
  it binds it to the starting key and answers the claim's state before anyone types. The `code` method only: the
  community ISO has no card. Letters, rotation and backoff are the claim's (one set, one counter). A commercial box
  refuses with `claim_local_unavailable`: it is claimed through control, which records the organization. New codes
  `claim_local_unavailable`, `claim_start_missing`. `appliance.status.claimReported` stays false on a community box.
- **CT-1303** The first owner is made by the claim with `account {name, email}`, as `enroll.claim`; the burrow follows
  with `burrows.create` as on any box. No new op: the commercial claim does the same in two steps.
- **CT-1304** Links the box makes (HE-60; `session/local-links.ts`): `<first way's page><path>#s=<secret>&p=<PeerId>&l=<page>&t=<page>…`,
  `LOCAL_LINK_PATHS` `/join` (invite), `/get-back-in` (re-enrolment), `/add-device` (device link); `l`/`t` are the
  pages on each local-network and Tailscale way, best first (`DirectAddresses.routes`' order), the sockets derived from
  them. The box writes them (`localLinkFor`, from its current ways), browsers and the Android app read them
  (`parseLocalLink`, hand-parsed without `URL` so it runs the same on Hermes; unknown keys ignored for a later minor;
  `LocalLink`, ≤ 2000 characters). `p` is the pin: the link came from someone already in over a session, so it vouches
  for the box better than the page can. `EnrollInviteCreateOutput.link` and `EnrollReenrollCreateOutput.link`, optional
  (absent without a direct way; a commercial box's clients may keep the hosted link). `enroll.invite.accept` and
  `enroll.reenroll.accept` are unchanged and work over the direct path (the box gives unknown keys the enrollment
  channel there, CT-1251). An invite still names an email: it is the account's name on the box, and mail is optional.
- **CT-1305** Device links (HE-60, “devices enrolled locally”): **`enroll.link.create {}`** → `{linkId, secret, expiresAt,
  link}` (app channel, secret; `link_unavailable` without a direct way; one live link per account) and
  **`enroll.link.accept {secret, endpoint}`** → `EnrolledOutput` (enrollment channel, secret; `via: 'link'` in
  `ENDPOINT_ENROLLED_VIA`; `link_invalid`, `link_expired`, `link_used`). A bearer secret for `DEVICE_LINK_TTL_S` 300,
  used once — the same trust as an invite link, shown on the person's own screen. Pairing by code (`enroll.pair.*`)
  stays and also works directly: its fingerprint comparison catches a key swapped on the local network.
- **CT-1306** Tailscale's own login server (HE-64): **`TailscaleLoginServer`** (`http`/`https`, a host, optional port and
  path; no credentials, query, fragment or character a command line could misread; normalized —
  `normalizeTailscaleLoginServer`, `TAILSCALE_LOGIN_SERVER_PROBLEMS` for the app's words). Plain `http://` is allowed for
  a Headscale on the owner's network (Tailscale's control protocol is encrypted inside; the image's install test uses
  one). **`host.tailscale.on {loginServer?}`**: absent keeps the box's, `null` is Tailscale's own, a different one signs
  the box out of its tailnet first. `TailscaleStatus.loginServer` (optional: absent is Tailscale's own); the manager's
  `TailscaleOnRequest.loginServer` is always the wanted one (optional, no optional-nullable in the cross-language
  subset). `TailscaleLoginUrl` admits `http://`; `tailscaleLoginUrlTrusted` (also in `tailscaleStatusValid`) lets an app
  open a login link only on the login server's origin, or on `https://*.tailscale.com` without one. The signed appliance
  log gains **`tailscale.on`**, **`tailscale.off`** and **`tailscale.sign_in`** (`TailscaleAuditPayload {byAccountId,
  loginServer, loginServerChanged, signOut}`), step 4's missing event (direct-connection.md).
- **CT-1307** Web Push from the box (HE-61): `devices.vapidKey` comes over the session (app channel;
  `SESSION_EXCLUDED_API_OPS` is empty) and answers `VapidKeyResponse {publicKey: VapidPublicKey}` (87 base64url
  characters); a box without a key of its own refuses with `push.web_unavailable` (`not_allowed`).
  `Bootstrap.capabilities.webPush` says whether to ask; a browser also needs a secure page (the Tailscale page). No
  phone push on community (`editionHas(…, 'phone_push')`): it goes through control and the box has no Firebase key.
- **CT-1308** The owner's own mail server (HE-61; `session/mail.ts`), owners: **`host.mail`** → `{mail: MailSettings |
  null}`, **`host.mail.set`** (`MailSettingsInput`; secret), **`host.mail.test {draft?}`** → `{test: MailTest}` (secret,
  never resent) and **`host.mail.remove`** (destructive). `MAIL_SECURITY` `tls`, `starttls`, `none`
  (`MAIL_DEFAULT_PORTS`); no login without encryption (`mailSettingsProblem`); the password is write-only (`hasPassword`;
  absent on set keeps it, `null` removes it). A test goes to the asking owner's own email only, so the op can't send mail
  to anyone else. `source: 'config'` (development's Mailpit) is read-only (`mail.in_config`); `mail.not_set`,
  `mail.busy`. `MAIL_TEST_STATES` with `MAIL_TEST_TEXT`, and the test message's words (`MAIL_TEST_MESSAGE`) — the box
  sends them itself. Signed events **`mail.set`**, **`mail.removed`** (`MailAuditPayload`: server and from address, never
  the login).
- **CT-1309** Passkeys on a community box's Tailscale page (HE-60) need no new shape: `PasskeyRpId` admits the box's
  Tailscale name. `passkeys_unavailable_here` (the runtime's refusal since step 4) is in `APP_ERROR_CODES` now.
- **CT-1310** `SESSION_PROTOCOL` is `{major: 2, minor: 1}`: the minor counts additions; a 1.0 app and a 1.1 box (or the
  reverse) meet at minor 0, and an op one side lacks is `unknown_op`.
- **CT-1349** Contracts 1.1.0, every package; schema, vectors and Go regenerated (`DirectIdentity`, `Edition`, the login
  server fields). Built provisionally into `dist-release/1.1.0` on `he5-c` (no tag; the lead tags, pushes and merges).

each person and the learned skills owners share. Ops go and the library's answer changes meaning, so this is a new

  `added`, `learned`) goes; the field is `origin` so nobody reads the old values into it. `SkillScope` stays.

  lines (“Needs NOTION_API_KEY”, “Needs the curl and jq commands”, “Can use USDA_API_KEY”). Lists on the wire, words

  none), `host.agents`, `host.recheckAgents`, `usage.list` and `burrows.setAiGateway`. Claude keeps “Claude Code” and
  “Claude”. Comments that quoted the old words follow; comments about Codex's own wire names (`windowDurationMins`,
  `cached_input_tokens`, a Codex access token) stay true and stay. `chatgpt-name.test.ts` checks that every label map
  names `codex` ChatGPT and that no endpoint summary or catalog entry says Codex. Once vendored, the app's own maps
  (`PROVIDER_NAMES`, `USAGE_NAMES`, `providerSetupLabel`, AP-5611…AP-5617) can go.
- **CT-1451** **ChatGPT's row needs nothing installed and shows no version.** `providerStateLabel` takes an optional
  `provider` (a `ProviderSetup` already carries it): for `codex`, `ready` is “Ready” (the runner's `version` is
  `Hermes <v>` since HN-C07, which names the engine people never read), `missing` and `logged_out` are “Not ready”
  (there is nothing to install or log in to on the machine: the runner says `missing` only while Hermes isn't ready);
  `error` and `unknown` as for Claude Code. Without `provider`, or for `claude`, unchanged (“Ready · 2.1.278 (Claude
  Code)”). `providerFix` for `codex` `missing`/`logged_out` is “ChatGPT needs nothing installed. It works once this
  Whombat is running; restarting this Whombat usually fixes it.” with no command (`npm i -g @openai/codex` and `codex
  login` are gone). Same rule as the app's AP-5613, now in one place.
- **CT-1452** **The AI gateway says ChatGPT.** `GATEWAY_TOOL_LABELS.codex` is “ChatGPT”, so the switch is “Send ChatGPT
  through Fusebox”, its hint, the confirmation's title, “Runs on”'s note, the Usage lines, the refusal (“Fusebox has no
  ChatGPT room left…”), the owners' alerts and the signed Keys line (“John now sends every ChatGPT turn through Fusebox
  (an override: OpenAI’s terms don’t allow sharing a ChatGPT sign-in)”) say it; the pool's account groups already did.
  The catalog's `fusebox` and `ai_gateway` entries (description, tagline “One gateway for Claude Code and ChatGPT”, key
  help, the agent-visible guide) say “Claude Code and ChatGPT”; the gateway address help is true for Hermes's loop: a
  ChatGPT turn calls `{url}/v1` as an OpenAI-compatible Responses API (the relay's `codex` paths, AIG-09, unchanged).
  A `burrow.ai_gateway_changed` already in a log keeps its signed `text`: only new lines say ChatGPT.
- **CT-1453** **`sessions.list`**, a Hermes-home step (`HERMES_HOME_METHODS`, runner-internal, not a session op):
  `{account: HermesProfileRef}` → `{sessions: HermesSessionListing[], more}`, `HermesSessionListing {id, source,
  lastActiveAt}`. One entry per conversation, by the logical id an editor holds (ACP's `session/new` id, what Whombat
  stores after `hermes:`; Hermes's compression and reset segments and sub-agent sessions are inside it, and
  `sessions.delete` with that id removes all of them), Hermes's `source` (`acp` for Whombat's turns) and `last_active`
  (latest over the segments). Least recently active first; at most **`HERMES_SESSIONS_LIST_MAX` 5 000** — half of
  `sessions.pending`'s 10 000 because each entry carries more, so the longest answer stays near 1.2 MB under the runner
  answer route's 2 MiB — and `more` when the profile has more (the newest are left out, which a prune keeps anyway).
  The runner lists them the Hermes way (Hermes's own session store, as its ACP `session/list` reads it), never by
  reading `state.db` or session files; a read without the profile's lock, so a turn neither waits for it nor makes it
  `busy`; `unavailable` without a real Hermes. A safe prune (the server's, HN-K03's “left”) keeps every conversation a
  thread names, anything active lately (a turn starts its session before it reports it) and anything not `acp`, and
  deletes the rest with `sessions.delete`. Last activity is all it needs: no start time, title or message count.
- **CT-1499** Contracts 2.1.0, every package. No schema, vector or Go change: nothing here is in the cross-language
  subset (`pnpm gen:check` clean). Built provisionally into `dist-release/2.1.0` on `hn-ct` (no tag; the lead tags,
  pushes, merges and vendors).


## CT-1500…CT-1599 One person per Whombat, no computer — contracts 3.0.0 (2026-10-25)

Whombat one-person.md OP-01…OP-19: a Whombat is one person's device, and the agent's computer goes (Hermes runs commands
itself, each in a thin wrapper on the appliance; what stays up is a container). Ops go and answers change meaning, so
this is a new contracts major and a new session major (publishing.md rule 1, OP-14). Nothing is released: deleted, not
deprecated (HE-27). Streams: C (this repository, with forks for connections, control and skills); the export list for
the other streams is `/home/me/.cache/wb-tmp/one-person/C-READY` and `docs/hermes-engine-api.md` “Step 8”.

### People (CT-1500…CT-1529)

- **CT-1503** **One sign-in per provider, no source to pick** (OP-09; the lead with S1): `CredentialSource`,
  `MemberCredentialSource`, `OrgCredentialSource`, `OrgCredentialId`, `DEFAULT_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE`,
  `AgentRuntime.credentialSource` (`AgentRuntime` is `AgentModelRuntime`), `agent.setCredentialSource`, the organisation
  credentials (`signins.orgList`, `.orgLoginStart`, `.orgRemove`, `OrgCredential`, `OrgCredentialProvider`) and
  `ProviderSignIn.ownerAccountId/credentialId/label` go. The person's API key is the existing key entry
  (`signins.loginStart` with `authMode` `api_key`) in the one credential home per provider. `DispatchCredential` is
  `{v, provider, authMode}`. The runner's sign-in executor drops `owner` and `label`: `list {}` → `[{provider, meta}]`
  (at most 3), `logout {provider}`, `githubToken {}`, `usageProbe {provider}`, `consoleStart` without `owner`;
  `CredentialOwner` goes and `CredentialMeta` loses `owner`, `accountId`, `credentialId`, `label`. `ProviderSignInState`
  loses `owner_departed`; `ProviderStatus` (appliance status) and the `provider.signed_in/out` payload lose the
  organisation variant.
- **CT-1504** **Whose turn** (OP-17): `DispatchContext.outside: boolean`, true exactly for a turn outsiders' input
  starts (a feedback assessment, a reply to a tracker customer, incoming mail); the runner routes on it (the `_feedback`
  or `_outsiders` Hermes profile, CT-1576). `onBehalfOf` is the person (null exactly when `outside`) and loses
  `accountId`; the Vault, connections and logins docs say “the person's”.
- **CT-1505** **No invites or re-enrolment**: `enroll.invite.create/.accept/.revoke`, `enroll.reenroll.*` and their
  shapes, `InviteSecret` (the device link's secret is `DeviceLinkSecret` itself, the same shape), `ENDPOINT_ENROLLED_VIA`
  `invite`/`reenroll`, `LocalLinkKind` `invite`/`reenroll` (`/join`, `/get-back-in`; `device` stays), the codes
  `invite_*`, `invite_account_exists`, `reenroll_*`, the burrow invites (`members.invite`, `.revokeInvite`, `Invite`,
  `InviteState`, `InviteId`; the `inv` prefix stays taken). The appliance event types `invite.*`, `owner.*`,
  `reenroll.*` stay in `APPLIANCE_EVENT_TYPES`, marked as written until 3.0: it is a closed enum, so a signed appliance
  log that has them stays readable (CT-1247's rule); nothing writes them. The recovery kit, passkeys, pairing, device
  links, screen sign-in, the claim and `enroll.dev` stay.
- **CT-1506** **Onboarding has three steps** (OP-11): `ONBOARDING_STEP_COUNT` 3, `OnboardingState.invites`,
  `CompleteOnboardingBody.invites` and `CompleteOnboardingResponse.invites` go.
- **CT-1507** **No roles**: `PersonRole`, `Person.role` and `.removedAt`, `isActivePrincipal`, `FORMER_MEMBER_LABEL`,
  `principalStatusLabel`, `MemberRef`, `canRemoveMember`, `canSetMemberRole`, `members.*` (`MembersResponse`),
  `Account.isAdmin` and `.canCreateBurrows`, `Membership.role`, `ownerAdminLockedReason`, the key `members.invite`,
  `KeyDef.personRole`, the keys engine's `owner_only` and `Actor.personRole`: the person may use every key
  (`burrow.manage` is “People only”).
- **CT-1508** **Audit**: `EVENT_TYPES` (what the server writes) loses `member.invited`, `.joined`, `.added`, `.removed`,
  `.invite_revoked`, `.role_changed`, `agent.computer`, `vault.swept` and `skill.shared`; `member.updated` is
  `person.updated`; `service.stopped` is new (Keys). A signed event keeps its own type and kind (`EventType` is any
  dotted name), so a log that has the old ones stays readable — unlike CT-1247 and CT-1416, which kept such names in the
  writer's list.
- **CT-1509** **Devices are the person's**: `enroll.screen.request {endpoint}` (no email; `screen_no_account` goes),
  `enroll.pair.request {endpoint}` (no email), `EndpointsListInput {}` (no `all`), `admins.*` and `Admin` go,
  `ApplianceStatusOutput.owner` and `.recovery.ownerAccountId` go, the codes `not_owner` and `last_owner` go and
  `last_owner_endpoint` is `last_endpoint` (“This is your last device …”), `recovery_not_owner` goes.
- **CT-1510** **The desk is the person's**: `DeskScreen.paired.you` goes, `DESK_ERROR_CODES` lose `not_owner` and
  `not_paired_person` (and their words); docs say the person.
- **CT-1511** **The Vault without privacy between people**: entries are the person's; `VaultListResponse.showHostNote`,
  `VaultNetworksResponse.canManage` and `admins_only` go; `vaultUseRow` loses `forWhom`; `vaultUnheldAskLine` takes
  `personFirstName`; the Vault's failure words don't name an owner or admin. The signed text stays neutral (“a private
  Vault entry”): a log can be read by support while remote help is on.
- **CT-1512** **Backups of one person** (OP-11): `BACKUP_SCHEMA_VERSION` 6; the `people` category is **`settings`**
  (“Settings”; `settings`, `repo`, `widget`, `account_profile` records; `person` and `invite` records go); the directory's
  person loses `role` and `left`, a Vault entry and a connector account lose `owner`; `BackupCredentialSource` and the
  agent runtime's `credential` go; `hermes_home` is the person's (no `person`), `agent_notes` loses `updatedBy`; a
  schedule loses `forEmail`, a conversation `members`; `othersPrivate`, `BACKUP_STAYS_PRIVATE`, the restore's `invite`
  count and `invited` list, the notes `org_credential` and `personal_elsewhere` go; `backupFileNoticeText(categories)`
  tells the person (no maker, no other owners); the error `owners_only` is `people_only`. An older file doesn't restore
  (HE-27).
- **CT-1513** **Spend and usage without whose**: `SpendOverview` loses `scope` and `byPerson` (`SpendPersonRow`,
  `SPEND_NOBODY` go), `SpendDaily` its `scope`, `SpendAgentWeek` is `{week}`; `UsageListOutput.everyone` and
  `USAGE_LIST_MAX` go, `SubscriptionUsage` loses `principalId` and `name`, `usageAlertKey` is
  `<provider>:<window>:<resetsAt>:<level>`.
- **CT-1514** **Rooms are the person's**: `Conversation.memberIds` and `.dmPersonId`, `ConversationSummary.memberCount`,
  `ConversationDetail.memberCount`, `FeedbackIntegrationChat.personId` and `AgentSchedule.forAccountId` go.
- **CT-1515** **No presence**: `presence.set`, `presence.typing`, `PresenceSetInput`, `PresenceTypingInput`,
  `Bootstrap.presence`, `PresenceEntry`, `PresenceState`, `PRESENCE_IDLE_AFTER_MS` and the `presence` event go; the
  `typing` event is the agent's thinking line only (its `mode` goes). The desk's camera presence is another thing and

- **CT-1516** **The mock world is Mara's**: `@whombat/fixtures` and core's test world have Mara and Dusty only; Mara
  reviews PR #482, the mention in the branch room is Dusty's, the search answers, audit rows, canvas and messages that
  named Joris, Priya or Tom name Mara (or nobody). The seed world has no `invites`.
- **CT-1517** **Deciding and deleting**: `canDecide` lets the person decide any approval (no approvers to pick, no owner
  override, no `private` approvals: `PersonApprovesCondition.private`, `privateApprovers`, `privateApprovalVisibleTo`
  and the error `not_an_approver` go; `Decider` and `MessageViewer` lose their role); the person undoes any decision and
  deletes any message. `AutomationDetail.canManage/canEditDraft`, the list's `canManage`, `ClientsListOutput.canManage`
  and `HostsStatus.canManage` go. A thing's `canManage` (look-only access) stays.
- **CT-1518** **Words**: what people and the agent read says “you”, “the person” or the agent's name, never owners,
  members, admins, a team or the computer (endpoint summaries, MCP tool descriptions, the gateway's and remote help's
  messages — `remoteHelpTurnedOnText(level, duration)` says “You turned on …” —, the Vault, the keys catalog, turn
  failures, onboarding fixtures).

### No computer (CT-1530…CT-1549)

- **CT-1530** **`@whombat/core/commands`** replaces `@whombat/core/computer`: the guard (`classifyCommand`,
  `shellSimpleCommands`), the categories and their keys, `CommandAllowance`, the `run_command` copy. Gone: `AgentComputer`,
  `ComputerState`, `ComputerKind`, `COMPUTER_*`, `computerMemoryMiB`, `PublishedPort`, `KEEP_AWAKE_MAX_DAYS`,
  `COMPUTER_COPY`, `COMPUTER_PORTS_COPY`, `COMPUTERS_NOT_HERE`, `computerCopy`, `computerSizeText`,
  `computerStatusLine`, `computerActions`, `computerKeepAwakeLine`, `publishedPortLine`; `computers.*` (the api area);
  the activity rows `whombat.computer_setup`/`computer_wait`; the approval copy “on Dusty’s computer”.
- **CT-1531** **`DispatchContext.commands`** (was `computer`; the lead): `DispatchCommandsContext {productionServers,
  homeNetworks, lan}` with `CommandProductionServer` (the inner shapes as before), on every turn of the person's, null
  exactly when `outside`. `ComputerOpening` is `CommandOpening`. `ProgressBody.computerBegun` and `runner.computerReport`
  (`ComputerReportBody`) go. `runner.authorizeCommand` and `runner.authorizeWait` stay.
- **CT-1532** **`runner.turnKeys`** (was `runner.computerKeys`; the lead), `GET /dispatches/:id/turn-keys` →
  `TurnKeys {files, env, mcpServers, entries}`: `needles` and `entries[].ownerName` go (no sweep: the keys folder is each
  command's tmpfs). `ComputerKeyPath` is `CommandKeyPath`, `ComputerMcpServer` is `VaultMcpServer`. The Vault side:
  `vault/computer.ts` is `vault/keys.ts` — `vaultKeyDeliverable`, `vaultKeyEnvNames`, `VAULT_KEYS_DIR`
  (`VAULT_COMPUTER_SWEEP_MARK` goes) —, `VAULT_COMPUTER_COPY` is `VAULT_KEYS_COPY` without `swept`, `vaultTurnUseWhat`
  says “in Dusty’s commands for this turn”, `vaultRotateNotice` “in its commands”.
- **CT-1533** **The agent's services** (OP-19, I-2): `api.services` — **`services.list`** `GET
  /burrows/:burrow/agent/services` → `ServicesListResponse {available, reason, services}` and **`services.stop`** `POST
  /burrows/:burrow/agent/services/stop {id}` → `StopServiceResponse {service, eventId}`. `AgentService {id, name, port,
  url, state, startedAt, image}`: `id` the container's id (12–64 hex), `port` in `AGENT_SERVICE_PORTS` 20000–20099,
  `state` `starting` | `running` | `stopped` | `failed`, at most `AGENT_SERVICES_MAX` 5, the label
  `AGENT_SERVICE_LABEL` `whombat.service`. Settings → Agent lists them with Stop (“Running on your Whombat”).
- **CT-1534** **`HostInfo.services`** (`ServicesHostStatus {available, reason}`) replaces `HostInfo.computers`: whether
  the container engine is there; `SERVICES_NOT_HERE` “This Whombat can’t run containers.” in development without Podman.
- **CT-1535** **Host metrics** (the lead, matching the appliance): `HOST_DISK_PARTS` `containers` (was `computers`; “The
  agent’s containers”), `HostNow.containersMemoryBytes` (was `computersMemoryBytes`), `computersIn/OutBytes` go from
  points and days with no containers equivalent (no bridge to count). `HOST_STATUS_COPY.memoryContainers` replaces
  `memoryComputers`, `byComputers` goes. The desk's agent part sums `containers` and `work`.
- **CT-1536** **`services.changed`**, a realtime event (topic `burrow`, no payload: refetch `services.list`) when a
  service starts, stops, fails or comes back; `services.stop` signs `service.stopped` (`{id, name, port}`, Keys).
- **CT-1537** Operation safety, as the computer's: `services.list` read, `services.stop` destructive with its receipt
  (stopping a stopped container changes nothing, but it takes away what someone may be using).
- **CT-1538** **`runner.notify`** (the lead): `POST /notify` `RunnerNotifyBody {fromDispatchId, attempt, runnerId,
  eventId, text}` → `{dispatchId}` (201), fenced by the runner and the starting turn's attempt and idempotent on
  `eventId` (`NotifyEventId`); it replaces the path through computerd. `DispatchContext.notify` and the `notify` trigger
  stay.
- **CT-1539** `DeploymentHow` `cli` (“Command line”) replaces `computer`; `record_deploy`'s words follow. A stored
  `computer` is Whombat's data migration's to rename.
- **CT-1540** **`SESSION_PROTOCOL` `{major: 4, minor: 0}`**: a 2.x app or box (major 3) and a 3.0 one refuse each other
  with `unsupported_version`; the session vectors' hello and version error moved to major 4.

### Skills, memory and the Hermes profiles (CT-1570…CT-1589)

Whombat one-person.md OP-08 (one Hermes profile in Hermes's own layout, one skills list, `_feedback` beside it) and
OP-17 (outsiders' turns in their own profile). Export list: `docs/hermes-engine-api.md` “Step 8”.

- **CT-1570** **One skills list.** The agent's skills are the person's Hermes profile's `skills/` as Hermes lays it out:
  Hermes's built-ins (its own sync), hub installs (its hub lock) and what the agent learned (Hermes's agent-created). No
  shared directory, no `external_dirs`, no learned copy in front of another. `SKILL_ORIGINS` `builtin` | `hub` |
  `learned`; `shared` goes. `SKILL_SCOPES`/`SkillScope` go: “For everyone” and “Learned with you” are one list.
- **CT-1571** One skill per name: `SkillRefQuery {name}` (so `SkillRemoveBody`); `SkillLibraryItem` loses `scope`,
  `overrides` and `shareRequest`; `enabled`, `changed`, Restore, Compare mean the same for every skill (Compare only a
  changed or removed built-in against Hermes's version). `SkillLibraryResponse` loses `canAdd`: the person always may.
- **CT-1572** **Sharing goes**: `skills.libraryShare`, `skills.shareRequest` and their shapes (`SkillShareBody`,
  `SkillShareResponse`, `SkillShareRequest`), `SkillCan.share`; `EXPORT_READ_OPS` and `OPERATION_SAFETY` lose them.
  Every remaining op keeps its id and safety class. Endpoint summaries drop “owners” and “for everyone”.
- **CT-1573** The `skill_share` approval (`SkillShareAction`, its verbs, copy, `SKILL_SHARE_CTA`, desk phone reason
  `share`, `undoBlock`'s case) goes, and with it the one approval without a key: `Approval.keyId` is `KeyId` again and

  one when absent); `OwnAddressCtResponse.hosts?` (every host the watch covers; absent from an older manager); errors
  `own_address.label_reserved`, `.rename_limit`, `.link_off`. Go: `local.ManagerPathOwnAddressCheck`,
  `ManagerPathOwnAddressRename`, `OwnAddressErrorLabelReserved`, `OwnAddressErrorRenameLimit`, `OwnAddressErrorLinkOff`
  and the types. An older manager answers 404 on the new paths.
- **CT-1799** The session, minor 6 (`OWN_ADDRESS_NAMES_MINOR`): `ownAddress.check` (read) and `ownAddress.rename`
  (owners, never resent: it acts at control first), `OwnAddressSummary.leaving?`, application codes `label_invalid`,
  `label_reserved`, `label_taken`, `rename_limit`, `link_off`, `own_address_off` (`OWN_ADDRESS_RENAME_ERROR_CODES`) and
  `address_moved` (`boxPasskey.register.begin` at the leaving host). `OWN_ADDRESS_ZONE_CERTIFICATES` and
  `ownAddressZoneCertificate(spki, at)` name Cloudflare's two certificates for `*.whombat.app`, which a box doesn't
  call foreign within their dates.

## CT-1800 More names nobody gets — contracts 4.17.0 (2026-11-23)

Names that pass for a sign-in or payment page, or that devices look up by themselves under a domain, are reserved
(Whombat own-address.md OWA-54). A minor: `ownAddressNameProblem` refuses more names; no shape changes.

- **CT-1800** `OWN_ADDRESS_RESERVED_NAMES` gains sign-in and payment words (`secure`, `verify`, `wallet`, …) and the
  names mail programs and devices look up (`autodiscover`, `autoconfig`, `wpad`, `mta-sts`, …);
  `OWN_ADDRESS_RESERVED_PREFIXES` gains distinctive company names (`paypal`, `google`, `microsoft`, …); the new
  `OWN_ADDRESS_LOOKALIKE_WORDS` refuses a name that is a company's name or has one as a hyphen-part (`apple-support`),
  except a drawn label. A name already given stays its box's. Control's own list of operator-reserved names comes on
  top and is control's alone.

## CT-1801…CT-1804 Reports to the Whombat Team — contracts 4.18.0 (2026-11-25)

A Whombat Link person tells the team behind Whombat about a problem or an idea from inside Whombat and follows the
answer there (Whombat team-reports.md). A minor: new device ops, manager paths and session operations.

- **CT-1801** `@whombat/core/domain` `team-reports.ts`: the shapes the box, the apps and control share (`TeamReport`,
  `TeamReportSummary`, `TeamReportDraft`, `TeamReportReply`, `TeamReportList`, `TeamReportContext`), the tracker's
  status vocabulary (`TeamReportStatus`), the limits (6 000 characters a description or reply, 1 500 for what the
  person expected, 200 messages a report) and the person's words (`TEAM_REPORT_STATUS_WORDS`, the four-step track).
- **CT-1802** Device ops `team.reports.list`, `.get`, `.create`, `.reply`, `.act`: the first ops that carry what the
  person wrote, readable at control (John, 2026-11-25: the form says the Whombat Team reads it). The words travel as
  base64url JSON (`TeamRequestPayload`, at most 40 KiB; `TeamAnswerPayload`, at most 4 MiB), checked on both ends with
  the core shapes, so the cross-language schemas stay ASCII and the manager forwards them unread. Refusal codes
  `TeamReportRefusalCode` in control's `details.code` (`team_reports_unavailable` for the team's switch,
  `not_invited`, `link_off`, `too_many_open`, `report_unknown`, `report_closed`, `validation_failed`, `rate_limited`).
- **CT-1803** Manager paths `/v1/runtime/team-reports/{list,get,create,reply,act}` (`MANAGER_PATHS.teamReports*`), the
  device ops' bodies and answers exactly. An older manager answers 404.
- **CT-1804** The session, minor 10 (`TEAM_REPORTS_MINOR`): `teamReports.list`, `.get`, `.draft` (reads),
  `teamReports.create` and `.reply` (never resent: they act at control first) and `teamReports.act` (destructive and
  never resent: a withdrawn report is deleted). The three are secret ops, so the person's and the team's words stay
  out of receipts and logs. Their bodies take an optional `requestId` (`TeamRequestId`) the app keeps for every try of
  one send; an answer with a whole report says how many of its oldest messages it left out (`earlier`), so it fits one
  CONTROL message. People only; the assistant reaches none of them.
